Closes #106.

## The pin was not the problem

The project required `upToNextMajorVersion` from **0.2.0**. For a pre-1.0 version that resolves to `< 0.3.0`, so *Update to Latest Package Versions* could never have reached 1.x no matter how often it ran. Raising the requirement is the actual fix, not re-resolving.

The system is also at **1.6.0**, not the 1.2.1 the issue recorded on 2026-08-12.

## Safer than the issue feared

The issue suspected the app had drifted into local constants that happen to match. It has not: `DesignTokens.swift` still does `@_exported import IAMJARLDesignTokens`, and there is not one hardcoded colour anywhere outside it.

The only breaking change on the path from 0.2 to 1.6 is the v1.0 rename of `typography.lineHeights`. **The app never references a line-height token**, so it does not apply. Everything else on the path is additive for a SwiftUI consumer; the v0.3 break hit web and CSS only.

## One visible change, measured not assumed

v0.4 darkened the error colour from `#FF3B30` to `#D70015` for WCAG AA contrast against white text, and `SharedTimerViews.swift:342` uses it as the Cancel button background. Sampled from a running timer on device:

| | Cancel button |
|---|---|
| 0.2.0, as shipped in 1.7 | `#FF3B30` |
| 1.6.0 | `#D70015` |

So the 1.7 App Store screenshots no longer match the binary exactly. That costs nothing today, since screenshots are version-locked and will be regenerated for 1.8 anyway.

issues.body:
`Package.resolved` pins `iamjarl-design` at **v0.2.0**. The design system is at **v1.2.1**.

This is the largest gap in the portfolio, and WODrounds is the app it matters most for.

v0.2.0 predates the entire v1.0 token layer, so this app is missing:

- `state.*` text colours
- `primaryHover` / `primaryPressed` interaction tokens
- the disabled tokens
- the z-index scale

It also predates the v1.0 `lineHeights` rename, so any typography token names in use here are
the pre-rename ones.

Worth checking whether the app is actually reading tokens from the package or has drifted into
local constants that happen to match; a gap this wide usually means the dependency stopped being
consulted a while ago.

Suggested: bump to `from: 1.2.1`, resolve, and read `MIGRATION.md` in iamjarl-design for the
`lineHeights` rename before assuming it is a no-op. This one probably is not a no-op.

Separately, and much smaller: the marketing site in `docs/` uses hand-rolled CSS with no
`--ij-` tokens at all. That is tracked in the strategy hub as part of the shared-component work
and does not need solving here, but it is worth knowing the app and the site are on two
different visual sources of truth.

## Why this arrived as an issue

The strategy hub now derives design-system adoption from the repos themselves rather than
tracking it by hand (`tools/design_adoption.py`), after a review of iamjarl-design found that
the marketing sites did not share tokens even though every document said they did. The first
full run found **one of fifteen projects on the current version**.

Every defect it found was invisible from inside the repo that had it, which is why this is
reported from outside. The fix is yours to make or to decline; if you decline, say why here so
the reason is recorded rather than rediscovered next month.

agent_prs.title: Fuse operators in newly extracted functions within the same optimization pass

issues.body:
## Problem

When partition extraction and fusion patterns run in the same optimization pass, newly created local functions are not optimized during that pass. `GraphGraph::OptimizeImpl` snapshots existing local functions before optimizing the parent (`onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_graph.cc`, around lines 2095-2105). Since `PartitionGroup` has higher priority than `MatMulAdd`, a `MatMul -> Add` graph becomes a partition function whose body still contains both operators; a second optimization pass fuses them to `Gemm`.

## Evidence

Reproduced with `PartitionGroupPattern()` and `MatMulAddPattern()` together, and with the documented `all` pattern set. Fusion alone produces `Gemm`; combined optimization requires a second pass.

## Expected

Schedule or revisit newly introduced function bodies so compatible fusion patterns can run in the same optimization invocation. Preserve deterministic priority behavior, replay/undo invariants, and termination. Add a regression test asserting the combined pass fuses `MatMul + Add` inside the extracted function.

## Problem

Converting a model to a newer default-domain opset drops all `ModelProto.functions`, even when the graph calls one of them. The converted model no longer contains the called function and cannot represent the original graph faithfully. This blocks automatic opset alignment for model comparison in onnx-light-viewer, independently of the installed-header issue #5897.

The 0.2.7 source and current main both construct a new model in `PrepareOutput` without copying `functions`. Reproduced with the 0.2.8 development Python bindings:

```python

import onnx_light.onnx.helper as oh
from onnx_light.onnx import checker, version_converter
from onnx_light.onnx.defs import register_onnx_operator_set_schema

register_onnx_operator_set_schema()
function = oh.make_function(
    "custom", "MyRelu", ["X"], ["Y"],
    [oh.make_node("Relu", ["X"], ["Y"])],
    [oh.make_operatorsetid("", 17)],
)
graph = oh.make_graph(
    [oh.make_node("MyRelu", ["x"], ["y"], domain="custom")],
    "local_function",
    [oh.make_tensor_value_info("x", onnx.TensorProto.FLOAT, [2])],
    [oh.make_tensor_value_info("y", onnx.TensorProto.FLOAT, [2])],
)
model = oh.make_model(
    graph,
    opset_imports=[oh.make_operatorsetid("", 17), oh.make_operatorsetid("custom", 1)],
    functions=[function],
)
checker.check_model(model)
converted = version_converter.convert_version(model, 18)
assert len(converted.functions) == len(model.functions)
```

Observed: one local function before conversion, zero afterward. Expected: retain the function definitions and a valid reference to the called function, converting their own opsets as needed.

`onnx-light-viewer` currently uses the onnx-light 0.2.7 C++ SDK. When an ONNX file has large inline tensor payloads, the viewer initially skips them for display, but must re-read and materialize them before calling `GraphGraph::Optimize`, including `RepeatedLayer` and `PartitionGroup`, to preserve optimization and save/undo behavior.

On one warm-cache synthetic model with a 64 MiB inline float initializer shared by eight MatMul/Relu blocks, each operation read 64 MiB and increased peak RSS by about 69 MiB: `RepeatedLayer` 247 ms, `PartitionGroup` 220 ms, and `TransposeTranspose` 213 ms. agent_prs.title: Inline If nodes with equivalent branches

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a built-in pattern that replaces an `If` node with the body of one branch when `then_branch` and `else_branch` are equivalent, because the result does not depend on the condition.

```
If(cond) { then: Neg(x) } else { else: Neg(x) }   ->   Neg(x)
```

No pattern currently matches `If` in `onnx_light/onnx_extensions/patterns`.

## Matching rules

- Compare the branches structurally and allow local intermediate names to differ (alpha-equivalence).
- Require identical names for values captured from the outer graph, because `Neg(x)` and `Neg(z)` are not equivalent.
- Compare node op types, domains, overloads, attributes (including tensor payloads), output order, and the branch output types.
- Compare graph-valued attributes in nested `If`/`Loop`/`Scan` subgraphs recursively.
- Treat branch-local initializers and `Constant` nodes as part of the body and compare them by value.

## Rewrite

- Inline one branch into the parent graph, giving its local values fresh names, and map the branch outputs to the `If` outputs.
- When a branch output directly forwards a captured or outer value and has no producing node, emit `Identity`.
- Remove the `If` node. `cond` may become dead and is left to the existing dead-code cleanup.
- Respect existing optimizer constraints, such as values used by subgraphs, graph outputs, and configured or device-assigned nodes.

## Tests (C++)

- Positive cases:
  - Identical branches with different local names.
  - A branch with multiple outputs.
  - A branch that only forwards a captured value.
  - Nested identical subgraphs.
  - An `If` inside a `Loop` body.
- Negative cases:
  - Branches that capture different outer values.
  - Branches whose attributes or constants differ.
  - Branches whose output order differs.

The pipeline format already declares `top_k` and `top_p`; `PipelineOptions` explicitly rejects their use. This is a missing runtime feature, not a request for new serialized fields.

- Expose the settings through `GenerationOptions` and honor the existing pipeline fields, consistently across applicable generation overloads and public bindings.
- Preserve current greedy and temperature-only behavior when filtering is disabled. Follow the existing format contract: `top_k = 0` disables top-k; top-p is optional and its valid range is `(0, 1]`, with `1` leaving the candidate distribution unfiltered.

Follow-up to xadupre/onnx-light-cpu#1079 and the upstream integration discussion in xadupre/onnx-light-cpu#1127.

During generation prefill, a model can compute logits for every prompt token even though native `Generate` only samples from the final position. Selecting the required hidden-state row before the LM head avoids the unused projections:

```text
Current: hidden[B,S,D] -> MatMul(W[D,V]) -> logits[B,S,V] -> select final position
Target:  hidden[B,S,D] -> select final position[B,1,D] -> MatMul(W[D,V]) -> logits[B,1,V]

`GatherUpstreamPropagation` already exists, but its MatMul handling currently propagates Gather only across batch dimensions. Selecting the sequence/row dimension of `[B,S,D] @ [D,V]` is not covered. Reuse or extend existing native patterns where appropriate rather than introducing a separate Python preparation/generation API.

agent_prs.title: Exclude discarded function proposals from replay caller analysis

issues.body:
## Problem

`GraphBuilder::ReplayRewritings` computes `FunctionOnlyCallers` from both the existing definitions and every proposed `rewrites.added_functions()` body before deciding which proposals are retained. A proposal that is subsequently discarded can therefore disable registered-operator precedence for another declaration and cause an otherwise valid replay to fail with a conflicting-definition error.

## Reproduction scenario

- Register `custom::F` since opset version 2 and import `custom:2` in the model.
- Keep existing local overloads A and B of `custom::F`.
- Propose a conflicting definition of A whose body imports `custom:1` and calls local overload B. Operator precedence means this A proposal should be discarded in favor of the existing declaration.
- Also propose a conflicting definition of B.

The discarded A proposal marks B as function-only, so the B proposal is rejected even though no retained caller selects local B.

## Expected behavior

Analyze caller scopes using the effective retained/replaced definitions. Exclude discarded proposals, preserve genuinely added callers and explicit replacements, and continue rejecting conflicts when a retained caller actually selects a local function.

Add a regression covering the discarded-A/colliding-B scenario while preserving the existing caller-scope and explicit-replacement tests.

## Affected code and origin

- `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_graph.cc`: `FunctionOnlyCallers` and its use in `GraphBuilder::ReplayRewritings` (around line 3286 in the PR).
- Remaining review finding in #5851, tracked separately from the original #5850 work.
- Original review comment: https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5851#discussion_r4507924684

Independent kernel and estimator registration can leave accounting attached to the wrong implementation, including when an override is refused. This change pairs registration and retains accounting with resolved kernels.

- **Shared registration contract**
  - Adds `KernelRegistration{factory, peak_memory}` for global and context-local registration.
  - Successful global replacement selects both; `overwrite=false` refusal changes neither.
  - An omitted estimator explicitly means zero additional memory, never inherited accounting.

  ```cpp
  KernelRegistration implementation{factory, estimator};
  RegisterKernelFn(domain, op_type, device, implementation);
  context.RegisterKernelFn(domain, op_type, device, implementation);
  ```

- **Built-in registration and collection**
  - Associates built-in factories with their portable estimators.
  - Exposes side-effect-free factory and estimator collection.
  - Prevents lazy defaults from replacing explicit backend selections, including zero-memory selections.

- **Session consistency**
  - Retains estimators on resolved kernels and exposes per-node `RuntimeSession::ComputePeakMemory`.
  - Keeps local registration isolated from global accounting; later registry changes do not affect resolved sessions.

- **Estimator scope**
  - Documents that shape-only bounds must cover all supported dtypes and executor configurations, or explicitly report an unknown bound.

agent_prs.title: Associate peak-memory estimators with kernel registration

issues.body:
## Problem

Kernel factories and peak-memory estimators are registered independently: `core::runtime::RegisterKernelFn` accepts a factory and an overwrite policy, while `core::shapes::RegisterComputePeakMemoryFn` installs the estimator separately.

A backend replacing an operator can therefore leave the previous implementation's estimator active, or install its own estimator even when its kernel registration was refused. The built-in and optimized implementations can have different temporary-memory requirements.

In xadupre/onnx-light-cpu#1110, this required a backend-local `detail::InstallKernel` helper which calls `RegisterKernelFn` and, only on success, installs the native MatMul estimator. This duplicates the association policy across backend registration entry points and hard-codes an operator-specific side effect.

## Expected behavior

Provide a shared registration contract associating a kernel factory with its matching peak-memory estimator, so consumers can register an implementation and its memory accounting together without backend-specific glue.

The contract should define and test:

- Successful replacement selects the matching estimator; a refused `overwrite=false` registration leaves existing accounting unchanged.
- Metadata/factory collection does not mutate either registry.
- Lazy built-in registration does not replace an explicitly selected backend implementation or its estimator.
- Session-local registration and already-created sessions remain consistent with the implementation they actually execute; registering a session-local kernel must not silently change unrelated sessions' global accounting.
- Behavior when an implementation supplies no estimator is explicit, rather than silently retaining an incompatible one.

The API design should also clarify how implementation-specific accounting interacts with the current shape-only estimator signature, which lacks dtype and executor metadata.

## Origin

Architectural follow-up to xadupre/onnx-light-cp

issues.body:
## Problem

Composing a symbolic maximum with a sum can produce an expression string whose interpretation differs from the intended arithmetic. This can underestimate peak-memory profiles.

## Reproducer

```python
from onnx_light.onnx_core.expressions import (
    dim_add,
    dim_max,
    evaluate_expression,
)

workspace = dim_max(1234, "scratch")
expression = dim_add(8240, workspace)
print(workspace)   # 1234^scratch
print(expression)  # 1234^scratch+8240
print(evaluate_expression(expression, {"scratch": 128}))  # 8368
```

Here `^` denotes maximum. The intended computation is:

```text
8240 + max(1234, scratch)
```

However, the serialized expression is interpreted as:

```text
max(1234, scratch + 8240)
```

For `scratch=128`, the correct result is **9474**, not **8368**.

## Expected behavior

Simplification and serialization must preserve expression grouping and evaluation semantics. A composed maximum must retain the necessary parentheses, for example `(1234^scratch)+8240`, or an equivalent expression.

## Affected code and validation

- `onnx_light/onnx_core/expressions/expressions.cc`: dimension arithmetic, simplification, and expression serialization.
- `onnx_light/onnx_core/compute/compute_context.cc`: composition of tensor memory with symbolic worst-case scratch estimates.
- In draft PR #5769, `GraphBuilder.LocalFunctionMemoryIncludesBodyActivationsAndWorkspace` exposes the resulting incorrect `during_bytes` and `released_bytes` profiles. The standalone workspace maximum evaluates correctly.

Add a focused arithmetic round-trip regression covering the reproducer, validate subtraction of released bytes as well, and rerun the affected profiling test. This is a blocker for merging #5769.

issues.body:
## Observed end-to-end regression

Default native optimization in xadupre/onnx-light-viewer remains very slow on the public `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` model exported with mobius. The bottleneck is external-weight materialization **before** the optimizer, not pattern matching.

Measured on the current viewer `main` (`66ff25a`), using the published onnx-light **0.2.3** C++ SDK on Linux/WSL2:

- ONNX graph: 574 nodes, 57 outputs, 256 external initializers.
- External weight file: **1,202,571,264 bytes** (1.12 GiB).
- Initial model load: 6.4 ms; graph snapshot: 15.8 ms.
- Default optimization selects 133 `enabledByDefault` patterns.
- First run: **31.991 s** wall time, versus **150.6 ms** in `OptimizationReport::TotalTimeNs()`.
- Another run: **26.826 s** wall time, versus **95.8 ms** in the SDK report.
- The latter run consumed **168,624,912,990 logical read bytes** and **160,824 read syscalls**, measured from `/proc/self/io` immediately before and after `model.optimize()`.
- The sum of the 256 external initializer offsets is **167,381,237,760 bytes**, explaining almost all of the excess reads. The sum of their lengths is exactly the weight-file size above.
- A `/usr/bin/time -v` run reports 1.62 s user CPU and **32.07 s system CPU**; peak RSS approximately 1.22 GiB. These timings are individual runs, not statistical benchmarks.

`rchar` measures logical bytes returned by read-like calls, not physical disk traffic; caching does not remove the repeated read/syscall work.

## Root cause

The viewer's external-weight reader safely opens each weight file, constructs the supported `utils::FdReadStream`, and calls `stream.skip_bytes(offset)` before reading that tensor's payload:

https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light-viewer/blob/66ff25add78dab9932550dd171e0427637cd7aad/native/model_storage.cc#L59-L79

Despite its API documentation saying that `skip_bytes()` advances using `lseek`, `FdReadStream::skip_bytes()` repeatedly calls `EnsureAvailable()` and discards the intervening buffers.

issues.body:
## Observed
The existing native GraphBuilder::DeduplicateInitializers uses TensorProto::ContentHash(false). For same-shaped unloaded external tensors, that hash includes the count of external metadata entries but not their keys or values. Distinct offsets in a shared missing weight file therefore land in one bucket and require pairwise comparisons.

This is reproducible directly through GraphBuilder.remove_duplicate_initializers(), without the new optimize CLI and without reading external weights. On the existing native build, one run measured 1,000 tensors in 0.029 s, 2,000 in 0.158 s, and 4,000 in 0.671 s (zero duplicates removed). These are focused single-run timings, not end-to-end optimizer benchmarks. Ten thousand unique tensors produce approximately 50 million candidate comparisons.

## Expected
Unloaded external metadata identities should discriminate hash buckets without loading payloads, while preserving equal-tensor hash/equality invariants and existing inline-payload behavior.

## Locations
- onnx_proto/src/onnx.cc: TensorProto::ContentHash(false)
- onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc: GraphBuilder::DeduplicateInitializers

Reported in #5718: https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5718#discussion_r4419069113 . The generic deduplication/hash algorithm predates that CLI and is tracked separately to keep its repair in a dedicated PR.

PR #5682 canonicalizes imported domain aliases, including `onnx.ai`, but the explicit-context compatibility check in `RuntimeSession::Run` still normalizes only the empty domain.

agent_prs.title: Version quantization reconstruction precision independently of output dtype

issues.body:
## Problem

The generic quantization decoder currently uses `double` as a universal reconstruction type:

- `DecodeBlock` performs affine/codebook reconstruction into `std::vector<double>`.
- `DecodeValues` retains the full reconstructed tensor in that representation.
- `DequantizeTensor` and `DequantizeTensorProto` convert to the requested output dtype afterwards.

Relevant code:
- https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/blob/c3d16a69a5e66bf4ddefb2d49ed94f170b222632/onnx_light/onnx_core/runtime/quantization.cc#L597-L635
- https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/blob/c3d16a69a5e66bf4ddefb2d49ed94f170b222632/onnx_light/onnx_core/runtime/quantization.cc#L2018-L2068

This unifies the implementation but does not establish the correct numerical contract for every codec. Binary64 intermediate operations followed by a FLOAT conversion can differ from reconstruction with binary32 rounding at each specified operation. The full double workspace also costs eight bytes per logical element, in addition to the output tensor and other workspace.

The discussion of onnx/onnx#8677 makes the distinction concrete: its GGUF decoding contract specifies FLOAT arithmetic even when the requested output is DOUBLE. Existing onnx-light portable profiles are not GGUF binary layouts, so that contract must not silently be assumed for all existing profiles.

The public C++ memory-analysis path and registered peak-memory estimators validate products and aggregate sums before arithmetic. | --- | --- | --- |
| Tile | X=[4294967296], repeats=INT64 tensor [4294967296] | output dimension is 2^64 |

| DepthToSpace | X=[0,4,4611686018427387904,1], blocksize=2; also swap H/W | spatial product overflows despite zero batch |

issues.body:
## Origin

Previously missed issue in PR #5571, review https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5571#pullrequestreview-5644974692. Deferred for separate follow-up at the maintainer’s request.

## Problem

In `onnx_light/onnx_core/compute/compute_context.cc`, `EstimateFunctionBodyMemory` seeds missing descriptors from function `value_info` with `SymTensorFromValueInfo` whenever a type exists. Tensor annotations without an explicit shape are converted into rank-zero descriptors.

With an `Outer -> Product -> MatMul` function chain and FLOAT arguments of unknown rank, recursive memory estimation can therefore feed fabricated scalars to MatMul and raise:

```
ComputeShapeMatMul: input A must have rank >= 1, got rank 0.
```

Unknown-rank arguments must remain deferred; they must not be interpreted as genuine scalar tensors.

## Expected change

- Require an explicit tensor shape before seeding this fallback, consistently with `SeedDeclaredValueInfo`.
- Extend `GraphBuilder.LocalFunctionMemoryDefersRankUnknownTensorInputs` to cover nested calls with values that actually carry a FLOAT type but no known rank, including round-trip import.
- Preserve rejection of genuine scalar MatMul inputs and existing known-shape memory estimates.

## Reproduction notes

Plain `GraphBuilder.MakeInput` declarations without a shape may not populate `ShapesContext.HasType`, allowing memory estimation to return early and masking the bug. `SequenceAt` on a sequence with rank-unknown FLOAT elements produces genuinely typed, unknown-rank values suitable for the nested regression. Check both dtype availability and absence of a tensor shape before the call.

Local exploratory changes have not been committed or pushed; this issue does not claim the fix is complete.

issues.body:
## Goal

Load an ONNX model's structure without materializing its weights, then load or unload individual weights by name on the same model object. Support this in both Python and C++, for inline weights in a single `.onnx` file as well as ordinary external weights.

## Current limitations

- `load(..., skip_raw_data=True, raw_data_threshold=0)` skips inline raw payloads but does not retain the source information needed to load them later into the same model.
- `TensorProto.load_external_data(base_dir)` supports individual external tensors and preserves their external metadata, but requires callers to find the tensor themselves.
- `load_external_data_for_model` eagerly loads all external weights and clears their external references, so it is not suitable for repeatable load/unload cycles.
- There is no model-level, name-based weight loading/unloading API.

## Proposed behavior

During metadata-only parsing, retain a deferred source reference for each skipped inline `raw_data` payload. Treat the original `.onnx` file as a backing data file: record its location, the absolute byte offset of the payload (excluding protobuf tag/length bytes), and its byte length. Reuse the external-data reading machinery where appropriate without rewriting the original file.

Expose equivalent Python and C++ APIs that can:

1. Load model metadata without reading/materializing weight payloads.
2. Load one weight by name without materializing other weights or reparsing the entire model.
3. Unload one weight by name while retaining its source reference.
4. Reload an unloaded weight repeatedly on the same model object.
5. Optionally load/unload all weights through explicit bulk operations; individual loading must not depend on bulk loading.

Exact API names remain to be designed. Preserve existing eager-loading behavior and existing `skip_raw_data` semantics unless an explicit new option requests deferred loading.

## Requirements and edge cases

- Support both single-file inline raw payload

issues.body:
## Objective

Implement a native incremental layout engine that assigns visual positions to ONNX nodes. It must support streaming construction and graph edits, be usable immediately during model loading, persist its state in `metadata_props`, and handle nested subgraphs.

This issue concerns layout computation and persistence, not a new graphical viewer.

## Required behavior

### Truly incremental placement

- Use a directed, layered layout, initially oriented left to right, with stable positions as the primary objective.
- Support adding nodes and connections progressively, including resolving connections whose producers were not yet available.
- Handle insertion, deletion, replacement and rewiring without routinely recomputing the complete graph. Update the affected dependency region, local collision neighborhood and affected edge routes only.
- Preserve unaffected node positions and relative ordering where possible. Do not renumber or globally compact the layout after every edit.
- Allow negative coordinates. Do not translate the complete graph to force nonnegative positions after loading or a mutation.
- Account for node dimensions and input/output port ordering when placing nodes and avoiding overlap.
- Derive layer constraints from dependencies; use predecessor/port alignment or a barycenter heuristic for vertical placement, followed by local collision resolution.
- A mutation can legitimately affect a large dependency region. Do not claim constant-time updates; distinguish affected-region propagation from an unconditional full-graph pass.

### Available during loading

- Expose a loading-time option/hook so placement can run as nodes and nested graphs are loaded, without waiting for a viewer or a separate post-load layout pass.
- Reuse valid persisted positions when present; place missing nodes and repair affected constraints incrementally.
- State the behavior when loading without layout enabled and preserve existing loading semantics for callers that do no

issues.body:
## Objective

Implement a graph-rewriting pattern that discovers repeated computational layers in an LLM and encapsulates each occurrence as a `Layer` node with an explicit subgraph body.

The pattern must be **disabled by default** and enabled explicitly. Detection must work from graph structure, not rely on exporter-specific node names or a fixed transformer architecture.

## Detection and expansion

1. Select an anchor: a `MatMul`, `Attention`, GQA operator, or a composite/function operator containing one of these operations. Define supported domain/operator identities explicitly; do not infer semantics from a name substring alone.
2. Build a small structural seed using a bounded neighborhood of predecessors and/or successors around the anchor.
3. Find repeated occurrences of that seed in the model. Match topology, input/output port roles and relevant operator semantics while allowing per-layer tensor names, parameter values and compatible shape differences to vary. Specify which attributes/types/shapes constrain matching.
4. Expand the corresponding occurrences together through matching predecessors and successors for as long as the repeated structure permits, up to junctions or other valid boundaries. Do not let one occurrence absorb another layer or shared external computation.
5. Resolve overlapping candidates and multiple anchors in the same layer deterministically. MatMul and attention anchors must not produce duplicate or nested wrappers for the same detected occurrence.

The result must be a set of non-overlapping repeated regions with explicit boundaries. Do not silently treat a partially matching or semantically different region as another occurrence.

## Choosing cut points

Look for boundary cuts that:

- Cut as few dataflow edges as possible.
- Favor the smallest tensors crossing those cuts, using inferred shapes and element types when available.
- Preserve meaningful repeated-layer structure and valid acyclic dataflow.

Define a deterministic compar

issues.body:
## Observed behavior

While adding a searchable native backend-test selector to xadupre/onnx-light-viewer, the published 0.1.35 C++ library returned 2,404 cases from `core::backend_test::CollectTestCases()`, but only 2,400 distinct names.

Each of these names occurs twice:

- `test_cc_greater_or_equal_float16`
- `test_cc_less_or_equal_bfloat16`
- `test_cc_less_or_equal_float16`

For each duplicated pair, the exported metadata also has the same model_name, kind (`node`) and empty tag. No case materialization is needed to reproduce this: collect the default TEST registry and count names.

## Expected behavior

Case names should identify individual backend tests uniquely, or distinct variants should carry distinguishing metadata. Name-only consumers otherwise cannot distinguish the entries or reliably select the intended case.

## Scope

The viewer selector uses unique catalog IDs instead of treating names as identities, so both entries remain selectable. Deduplicating or renaming upstream cases is deliberately deferred to this separate issue; no upstream implementation changes are included in the viewer feature.

## Context
Follow-up to #5473 and #5465, deferred at the maintainer’s request. The canonical graph can now be reconstructed using private in-memory undo history, but rewriting export still retains redundant graph representations and can duplicate initializer payloads.

## Current behavior and updated direction
- Python `GraphBuilder.to_onnx` first exports `canonical`, imports it into an independent `working` builder, and retains `canonical` to preserve compatible existing named plans.
- In fd4b62a05 on #5473, the optimized-graph validation snapshot and runtime whole-graph roundtrip self-checks are removed at the maintainer’s request. Complete correctness comparisons belong in unit tests. This follow-up must not replace the removed snapshot with another runtime self-check.
- Compatibility decisions for existing named plans use native field equality rather than serialized graph/function strings, and are skipped when no existing plans need preservation.
- Import follows `ImportGraph → MakeInitializer → RepeatedProtoField::push_back → TensorProto::CopyFrom`. Ordinary owned tensor payloads are copied; borrowed raw-data buffers with a shared owner have a sharing fast path. The initial graph export can also copy payloads through the same mechanism.
- Consequently, reconstructible graph structure and unchanged weights can still occupy multiple allocations during capture, export and undo.

Relevant implementation: `onnx_light/onnx_core/graph_builder.py`, `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_graph.cc`, `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc`, and `onnx_proto/src/onnx.cc`.

## Requested follow-up
- Remove the need to retain the full Python canonical model once undo can reconstruct the cleaned reference. Retain only the information needed to preserve compatible existing named plans and metadata.
- Avoid copying unchanged initializer payloads when exporting, importing, capturing and undoing graphs. Establish explicit safe ownership/sharing semantics for ordinary owned buf

issues.body:
## Objectif clarifié

Ne pas recréer les nœuds Identity lors du rejeu inverse. Les nettoyages qui renomment les résultats doivent être effectués **avant la capture des rewritings réversibles**, et non enregistrés parmi les modifications à inverser.

Le point de départ est donc le graphe canonique déjà nettoyé. Le rejeu inverse doit revenir à ce graphe, pas au graphe antérieur à la suppression des identités.

```text
Graphe initial
  -> nettoyages avec renommages, dont suppression des Identity
  -> graphe canonique nettoyé
  -> capture et application des rewritings réversibles
  -> graphe optimisé
  -> rejeu inverse des rewritings
  -> graphe canonique nettoyé, sans réintroduire les Identity supprimés
```

## Pourquoi séparer ces deux phases

La suppression de `b = Identity(a)` redirige les consommateurs de `b` vers `a`. Le couple `b -> a` ne mémorise pas quels consommateurs utilisaient déjà `a`. Mais il ne faut pas ajouter un journal pour inverser ce nettoyage : **son inversion est explicitement hors objectif**. En plaçant le nettoyage avant la capture, les plans commencent après ces substitutions et ne doivent jamais les annuler.

## Travail attendu

- Recenser les transformations qui produisent `LocalRewritingProto.value_renames`, notamment la suppression des identités et les déduplications qui redirigent des usages.
- Séparer ces nettoyages de la capture des plans réversibles ; les appliquer avant de fixer leur graphe canonique de référence.
- Préserver les noms aux frontières des remplacements enregistrés. Ne pas introduire de renommage dans les plans réversibles ; adapter ou exclure une transformation qui ne respecte pas cette contrainte.
- Ajouter le rejeu inverse des modifications enregistrées, dans leur ordre inverse, avec validation des positions, dépendances et sous-graphes.
- Conserver les informations nécessaires pour restaurer les éléments supprimés par ces seules modifications réversibles. Le format actuel conserve leurs positions, mais pas leurs défin
issues.title: Exclure les renommages des plans de rewriting réversibles

issues.body:
## Problème

La conversion des initializers en nœuds `Constant` lors de l’export en `FunctionProto` peut produire une fonction invalide pour l’opset sélectionné.

Exemple : un graphe en opset 8 peut utiliser un initializer `INT64` comme entrée de forme de `Reshape`. Son export en fonction introduit un `Constant` de type `INT64`, alors que le schéma applicable, `Constant-1`, n’accepte que `FLOAT16`, `FLOAT` et `DOUBLE`. Le graphe initial est valide, mais pas la fonction exportée. La prise en charge de `INT64` par `Constant` commence à l’opset 9.

Signalé dans la revue de #5464 : https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5464#discussion_r4338746686

## Correction attendue

- Résoudre le schéma de `Constant` applicable à l’opset ONNX de la fonction.
- Vérifier chaque type d’initializer avant de le convertir, en réutilisant les contraintes de types du schéma plutôt qu’une liste parallèle codée en dur.
- Lever une `BuilderError` explicite pour une conversion non représentable, en indiquant le nom de l’initializer, son type et l’opset sélectionné.
- Ne pas augmenter implicitement l’opset : cela pourrait changer la sémantique des autres opérateurs.
- Couvrir les exports de fonctions directs et après optimisation, ainsi que les définitions de fonctions locales utilisant cette conversion.

## Critères d’acceptation

- Un export de fonction en opset 8 contenant un initializer de forme `INT64` pour `Reshape` échoue avec un diagnostic clair, sans modifier le builder source.
- Le même cas en opset 9 réussit et préserve les valeurs.
- Une constante flottante compatible reste exportable en opset 8.
- Les imports d’opsets restent inchangés, y compris en cas d’erreur.

## Références locales

- `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc` : `PrependInitializerConstants`.
- `onnx_light/onnx_op/operator_sets_generator.cc` : `ConstantTypes`.
- `onnx_light/onnx_lib/defs/generator/old.cc` : schéma historique de `Constant-1`.

agent_prs.title: Fix CopyFrom replacement semantics for rewriting variants

issues.body:
## Problem

The latest review of #5452 reports that `ModelProto::CopyFrom` does not replace existing `rewritings` correctly. `CopyProtoThroughWire` parses directly into the existing destination, and the new map reader rejects a key already present in that destination as though it were duplicated within the incoming message.

Reported consequences:
- Copying from a source with a variant name already present in the destination throws instead of replacing the destination.
- Copying from a source without variants leaves stale destination variants attached.
- Self-copy can throw when variants are present.

Stale variants are particularly concerning because they can leave rewriting plans associated with a different canonical model after a copy.

## Relevant code

- `onnx_proto/include/onnx_proto/stream_class_read.hpp`, around line 485 in the reviewed revision.
- `CopyProtoThroughWire` in `onnx_proto/include/onnx_proto/stream_class.hpp`, around lines 224–249.
- Reported against #5452 at commit `f0a84c8dd6753cf57b285b150ac458dbc9a823bc`.

## Expected behavior

`destination.CopyFrom(source)` replaces destination state, including its rewriting variants. Self-copy preserves the model. Duplicate keys within an incoming serialized message must still be rejected.

Consider copying through a fresh temporary model and replacing the destination only after the copy succeeds, rather than weakening duplicate-key validation.

## Regression coverage

- A populated destination and a source sharing a variant name.
- Disjoint source and destination variant names: old destination-only names disappear.
- A source with no variants copied into a populated destination.
- Self-copy of a model containing variants.
- Duplicate wire keys remain rejected.

This issue records the finding from the general review; it has not been independently reproduced as part of issue creation.
issues.title: Fix ModelProto::CopyFrom replacement semantics for rewriting variants

issues.body:
Follow-up to #5430 and review discussion: https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5430#discussion_r4334484036.

## Problem

ApplyRewritings reconstructs a GraphBuilder from BuildGraphImpl before applying the supplied rewrites. Reconstruction can infer tags that differ from tags already stored in the source builder. This occurs before the rewrite-preservation guard starts, so the discrepancy is not prevented by that guard.

This is not specific to an empty plan. Any subsequent call can encounter the same discrepancy while reconstructing its starting graph. For example, an earlier rewrite may preserve weight tags for Y and Z after swapping mixed-tag Add inputs, while reconstruction infers shape tags from the new input order.

## Required behavior

As clarified by the maintainer, verify that reconstructed value tags are consistent with existing value tags wherever the source builder already has a tag. If reconstruction produces an inconsistent tag, throw an explicit exception rather than silently accepting it or overwriting either assignment to hide the mismatch.

Perform this consistency check during reconstruction, before applying the supplied rewrites. An empty plan must take the same validation path as a non-empty plan; an empty-plan-only shortcut does not fix the underlying problem.

## Acceptance criteria

- Compare existing source value-tag assignments with the reconstructed assignments for the corresponding values, including scoped values in nested builders where reconstruction occurs.
- Reject missing or different reconstructed assignments for values with an existing tag, reporting the value and the existing versus reconstructed tags (including an absent reconstructed tag).
- When no existing tag is present, allow normal inference; absence of a source tag is not itself an inconsistency.
- Validate before executing the supplied rewrites and leave the source builder unchanged on failure.
- Cover the same reconstruction mismatch with both an empty plan and a d

issues.body:
Follow-up to #5425 and review discussion: https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5425#discussion_r4334540166

## Problem

GraphBuilder::InsertNodesInDependencyOrder can miss a cycle when the furthest prerequisite lies outside that cycle. For the tentative order:

```text
Add(b, a) -> c    [added]
Neg(c) -> b       [added]
Abs(X) -> a       [retained]
```

the current algorithm can return:

```text
Abs(X) -> a
Add(b, a) -> c
Neg(c) -> b
```

The dependency cycle between b and c remains. The current moving[order[last]] check only examines the endpoint of the insertion interval; an external prerequisite can extend that interval and mask an internal cycle. RefreshAfterRewriting can consequently install an invalid node order before refreshing metadata.

## Required approach

The insertion algorithm itself must either produce a dependency-consistent order or reject a cyclic rewrite before installing the new order. Fix cycle detection within its targeted dependency traversal rather than adding a separate whole-graph validation pass, topological sort, or metadata rebuild after every mutation.

Distinguish nodes currently being visited from nodes already processed during the relevant local dependency traversal (or use an equivalent sound local algorithm). Revisiting an active node detects a cycle; reaching an already processed shared prerequisite must not reject an acyclic diamond. The traversal and bookkeeping should remain bounded by the affected dependency region, without repeated scans of unrelated graph nodes.

- Reject the example above before installing the rewritten node order or refreshing its metadata.
- Cover self-cycles, multi-node cycles, and a cycle masked by a prerequisite outside the cycle.

agent_prs.body:
Fixes #5420.

GraphBuilder must remain dependency-consistent after every mutation and rewrite, not merely after export. This PR does not support retaining non-topological recorded orders.

- Insert new producers before existing consumers whenever their inputs permit it; otherwise move only blocked consumers and their affected consumers.
- Do not topologically sort during mutations or coordinate normalization. Leave valid node sequences unchanged; export retains sorting only as a fallback after detecting a real dependency-order violation.
- Normalize batches using indexed live ranks, restricting edits to affected intervals and materializing the final sequence once. Explicitly record displaced retained nodes so replay preserves positional follow-up coordinates.

agent_prs.title: Add const prepared-artifact lookup to ValueStore

issues.body:
## Context

Declarative preparation callbacks estimate source, temporary and additional prepared bytes before `RuntimeSession::ExecutePreparations` admits work under a memory budget. The runtime also charges the existing `ValueStore::prepared_bytes()` total.

An estimator must therefore distinguish an artifact that needs allocation from one already published in the shared store. Otherwise it can count the same prepared buffer twice and defer work that actually fits the budget.

## API gap

The estimator receives `const RuntimeContext&`, exposing a const `ValueStore`. The currently published API provides `Bind(key)` (non-const, creates missing slots), `IsReady(slot)` and `Get(slot)`, but no const lookup from a cache key to an existing slot/value. A second kernel with shared immutable sources cannot use these APIs to discover the first kernel’s published artifact during estimation.

## Concrete example

Two MatMulNBits nodes share INT4 B/scales with K=64, N=16:

1. Sources occupy 640 bytes; one packed artifact needs 768 bytes.
2. With a 1,408-byte budget, the first preparation is admitted and publishes the artifact.
3. The second estimator still reports 768 additional prepared bytes.
4. Admission computes 768 existing + 640 source + 768 additional = 2,176 bytes and defers the second preparation.
5. Inference later drains preparations without the bounded limit; execution discovers and reuses the artifact, allocating no second buffer.

This is an overestimate/admission problem, not duplicate packed storage or incorrect inference results.

## Expected outcome

Provide a supported, non-mutating way for an estimator to find an existing artifact by its execution cache key and check publication. Define missing versus bound-but-unpublished behavior and preserve store isolation and const access. An optional-slot lookup is one possible API, not an implemented prerequisite.

Add focused coverage for unknown, unpublished and published artifacts, no lookup-induced slot allocation,

issues.body:
## Problem

When an output already has an inferred shape, `GraphBuilder::MakeOutput(const ValueInfoProto&)` stores the supplied declaration in outputs_ but does not seed or validate its tensor shape against the existing ShapesContext entry.

This can leave different public views describing different shapes. Outputs()/BuildGraph retain the declaration, whereas GetShape() retains the inferred shape and final export writes the inferred description back over the declaration.

## Source

Baseline reviewed: `03c242aeb`.

- `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc:1124-1157`: shape seeding guarded by `!Shapes().Has(name)` followed by storage of value_info.

The caller supplied a contradictory declaration; the issue is accepting it and exposing inconsistent views, not a requirement to overwrite valid inference with an incompatible shape.

Check the declared tensor dtype/shape against an existing inferred descriptor and reject incompatible declarations with BuilderError before storing them. Preserve supported unknown/symbolic dimension compatibility. issues.body:
## Goal

Support both preparation timings through the actual RuntimeSession execution path:

1. Explicitly prepare immutable kernel inputs before the first inference.
2. Preserve lazy preparation on the first Run when explicit preparation was not requested.

Also allow preparation to start during model loading: once an eligible weight is available and its kernel representation is known, prepack it while other weights are still loading. Do not wait for the complete model payload to be loaded before beginning every preparation.

## Current behavior

RuntimeSession initializes kernels and calls their Prepare hooks synchronously during its first Run. Prepared values are owned by the session hierarchy through ValueStore and reused on subsequent runs. There is no public model/session preparation phase separate from inference.

- Declaration records the source inputs, the compatible target representation, required dependencies, output slots, and executable packing operation. Registering the declaration must not run that operation or publish an output as ready.

agent_prs.title: Preserve AllocationHandle ownership when IOArena export rejects a foreign buffer

issues.body:
## Problem

`IOArena::ExportHandle(AllocationHandle&&)` evaluates `Export(handle.Release())`. `Release()` clears the owner and buffer before `Export()` validates that the buffer is live in this arena.

If the handle belongs to another arena, Export throws as documented, but the supplied handle is already empty. Its allocation is no longer returned through the normal RAII ownership path. In the originating arena the slot can remain live and unavailable for reuse until arena teardown.

## Source

Baseline reviewed: `03c242aeb`.

- `onnx_light/onnx_core/compute/raw_buffer_allocator.cc:343-368`: membership validation and ownership-transfer order.
- `onnx_light/onnx_core/compute/raw_buffer_allocator.h:392-394`: documented rejection.
- `onnx_light/onnx_core/runtime/memory/simple_tensor.cc:60-69`: AllocationHandle::Release clears ownership.

## Illustrative scenario

Obtain a handle from arena A, then pass it to arena B's `ExportHandle(std::move(handle))`. The call rejects the foreign allocation, but the caller's handle has already been consumed.

This is an invalid argument path, not a successful cross-arena transfer. The concern is exception-safe ownership, not a claim that process memory is permanently leaked after arena destruction.

## Expected outcome

Validate membership and lease restrictions before consuming the handle, preserving ownership if validation fails. Document the failure guarantee and add a focused cross-arena failure test proving that the original owner/handle remains usable and can return its allocation normally.

## Evidence

Review-team finding F2, confirmed by static ownership tracing and downgraded to minor because it requires a rejected argument. No tests or builds were run.

agent_prs.title: Keep nested subgraph builders coherent after parent opset changes

issues.body:
## Problem

A subgraph builder copies its parent's opset map when created. A later `SetOpsetVersion()` on the parent updates only the parent's map and ShapesContext. The refresh path recursively revisits subgraphs using each child's own map, so existing children keep the old opset during inference.

## Source

Baseline reviewed: `03c242aeb`.

- `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc:492-504`: parent opset update.
- `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc:815-889`: refresh uses each builder's own opsets.
- `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc:3062-3064`: initial parent-to-subgraph opset copy.

## Illustrative scenario

Create a parent at default-domain opset 18, create its subgraph and add nodes, then change the parent to opset 17. Parent model metadata uses 17 while the existing subgraph builder still reports and infers with its copied 18. Bare subgraphs do not carry independent function-style opset imports.

## Expected outcome

Ensure a supported parent opset change leaves nested graph builders' effective opsets and dependent metadata consistent, with targeted propagation to affected descendants and consumers. Avoid redundant whole-graph rebuilds or delayed repair at export. Add a focused nested-builder regression test.

issues.body:
## Context

PR #5396 extracts the threading infrastructure into a standalone library. Its shared proto library now depends on the shared threading library.

A standalone shared proto consumer should run from a non-system installation prefix without requiring `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` when both libraries are installed together.

Add an appropriate origin-relative install RPATH (`$ORIGIN` on Linux) to the shared proto library and an installed-consumer test that references only out-of-line proto symbols. Confirm that the test exercises an indirect threading dependency rather than retaining it as a direct executable dependency.

`PropagateValueAsShapeArithmetic` right-aligns `ValueAsShape` vectors and fills missing leading entries with the integer 1. These vectors contain tensor values, not tensor dimensions: a length-one operand must repeat its actual element for Add/Sub broadcasting.

For operands with values `(N, M)` and `(5)`, Add currently derives `(N+1, M+5)` instead of `(N+5, M+5)`. Sub and the mirrored operand order are affected too. This is a valid length-one tensor broadcasting scenario, not a malformed model.

agent_prs.title: Remove unused OpenMP dependency from standalone proto package

issues.body:
## Problem

The standalone proto project detects OpenMP, publicly links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` when found, and exports a corresponding `find_dependency(OpenMP COMPONENTS CXX)` requirement.

No current C/C++ source or header in `onnx_proto/` uses OpenMP directives or APIs. The resulting installed-package dependency therefore appears unnecessary for this extracted component.

A package built where GCC OpenMP is available can become unusable by a Clang consumer without a Clang-compatible OpenMP setup, even though the proto headers themselves compile with Clang.

References:
- `onnx_proto/CMakeLists.txt:16,69`.
- `onnx_proto/cmake/onnx_protoConfig.cmake.in:5`.

## Reproduction

After installing the standalone package built with GCC and detected OpenMP:

```bash
cmake -S onnx_proto/tests/consumer -B /tmp/proto-clang-consumer \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
    -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/proto-install
```

On the reviewed Linux environment, configuration fails inside the package dependency lookup:

```text
Could NOT find OpenMP_CXX (missing: OpenMP_CXX_FLAGS OpenMP_CXX_LIB_NAMES)
```

This is a package-consumption failure, not an installed-header syntax failure. The current Clang syntax-only consumer check does not exercise this boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove the proto-only OpenMP dependency if it is not needed, or identify and document a real requirement.
- Do not remove OpenMP from higher-level runtime/kernel components that actually use it.
- A Clang consumer can configure, link, and run against the installed GCC-built proto package without requiring an unused Clang OpenMP toolchain.
- Cover installed-package consumption through CMake, rather than relying exclusively on syntax-only header checks.
- Preserve static/shared exports and optional OpenSSL behavior.

Related: #5348.

## Origin

Reported during review of #5305: https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5305#discussion_r4303072699

Related to #5302. This is a static path-validation issue, not the directory-replacement races tracked in #5304.

## Reproduced problem

The mbext fast test `tests/fast/test_builder_dtypes.py::TestReuseDownloadedWeights::test_reuses_safetensors_checkpoint` exports weights under a relative subdirectory:

```text
export/
  model.onnx
  .weights/
    model.safetensors
```

An initializer has `external_data.location=".weights/model.safetensors"`, with offset and length referring to its raw tensor bytes in that file. Loading the exported model through onnx-light fails with:

```text
External data location must be a filename with no folder, name='model.embed_tokens.weight.source', location='.weights/model.safetensors'
```

The mbext audit observed this with local onnx-light revision `67d07cdd9`. The blanket restriction is still present on the current default branch in both writing and reading paths: [onnx.cc at bfe901550ad1dfd6679b80da3ba5a8c620e437e5](https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/blob/bfe901550ad1dfd6679b80da3ba5a8c620e437e5/onnx_light/onnx_proto/onnx.cc#L619-L638), and the corresponding read-side checks around lines 772-804.

## ONNX contract

The [ONNX external-data specification](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/ExternalData.md#external_data-field) defines `location` as:

> file path relative to the filesystem directory where the ONNX protobuf model was stored. Up-directory path components such as .. are disallowed and should be stripped when parsing.

A relative child directory such as `.weights/` or `weights/shard_0.bin` is therefore permitted. Rejecting every nonempty parent path is stricter than this contract. This is about path resolution, not interpreting the safetensors container: the existing external-data offset/length identify the raw tensor bytes.

## Requested change

Accept safe relative subdirectories in external-data locations across the relevant load/save APIs. Preserve the location when reusing source weight files instead of requiring users to copy or flatten them next to the model.

issues.body:
## Motivation

The native generation loop currently treats `position_ids` as an INT64 matrix with the same `[batch, sequence]` shape as `input_ids`. Multimodal rotary position embeddings use multiple coordinate channels instead. For example, Qwen3.5 consumes `[3, batch, sequence]` position IDs representing temporal, vertical, and horizontal coordinates.

This prevents `ReferenceEvaluator.generate()` from running otherwise executable M-RoPE decoder graphs.

## Proposed behavior

Extend generation position handling with a configurable position layout/update strategy that can:

agent_prs.title: Keep global runtime registries read-only and resolve explicit local scopes first

issues.body:
## Design requirement

No session or runtime context may modify a process-wide registry to satisfy its own model or execution requirements. Runtime resolution must consult all applicable local registries first, then fall back to global registries only when the entry is absent locally.

Global registration must remain an explicit application-level setup operation. Constructing, preparing, executing, resetting, or destroying a session/context must not insert, remove, replace, temporarily override, or save-and-restore global registrations. A global registry must not act as a hidden parameter carrying session-specific configuration.

## Context

Follow-up to the registry restoration discussion in #5270.

The particular save/swap/restore mechanism currently discussed there operates on `RuntimeContext::functions()`, a **context-local** map of borrowed `FunctionProto` pointers, not a process-wide registry. However, temporarily repurposing the caller context registry as the current model registry still introduces implicit execution state and requires restoration on success and failure. Model definitions can otherwise leak into another invocation or outlive their source model.

The existing custom-kernel dispatcher already consults context-local registrations before global custom kernels and the built-in table. Preserve that local-first approach and make model/session scope explicit rather than installing temporary definitions into a shared registry.

## Open design decision

For conflicting model-local identities, choose either deterministic rejection before execution or explicit model/session scoping that supports common names. A function identity includes normalized domain, name and overload. Neither choice may leak borrowed pointers or mutate global registries. The same-name acceptance criterion below permits either explicit rejection or correct scoped resolution.

## Required behavior

- Model-local functions and session/context-local kernel registrations remain local t

agent_prs.body:
Supports token generation with an optional embedding model and one shared CPU executor.

- **Two native entry points:** `Generate(ModelProto, context, ...)` and `Generate(GenerationPipeline, context, ...)`. The pipeline contains only `prefill` (the principal language model) and optional `embedding` model pointers, never a context or model owner.
- **Prompt and token phases:** The same language model handles the prompt and subsequent tokens. When present, embedding runs before the language model in both phases. Graphs connect through their declared input/output names.
- **Shared execution and diagnostics:** Split-model generation uses one call-local context configured from the language-model evaluator, with its custom kernels and CPU executor. Events remain visible on that evaluator, including after failures. Stages share call-local arenas, not the evaluator allocator configuration.
- **Call-local state:** Each generation call owns its sessions and persistent feedback state. Native runtimes borrow models; Python export boundaries retain the necessary source references. Persistent state is session-owned, with reset but no separate binding or close lifecycle.

```python
tokens = language_model.generate(
    {"input_ids": input_ids, "vision": prepared_features},
    embedding=embedding,
    max_new_tokens=20,
)
```

The updated scope deliberately excludes per-stage name mappings and a preprocessing graph list. Image/audio preprocessing runs before generation, and its results are supplied as ordinary feeds. Pipeline-wide custom kernels are registered on the language-model evaluator.

Fixes #5264
agent_prs.title: Support multi-graph generation with a shared CPU executor

issues.body:
## Motivation

`ReferenceEvaluator.generate()` currently drives one `ModelProto`. Multimodal and split-embedding exports commonly use separate `embedding.onnx`, `vision_encoder.onnx`, and `decoder.onnx` graphs. A generated token ID must pass through the embedding graph before the decoder can consume the resulting `inputs_embeds`.

Creating an independent executor or thread pool for every graph is wasteful because these stages execute sequentially. Compatible evaluators should retain one shared `CpuExecutor` and one execution policy for the complete generation pipeline.

## Proposed behavior

Add a multi-graph generation API or pipeline abstraction that can:

- connect generated token IDs to an embedding graph and then to the decoder;
- describe component input/output mappings explicitly;
- execute optional vision or audio preprocessing graphs during prefill;
- keep decoder persistent bindings and cache state local to the generation call;
- lease the same compatible `CpuExecutor` for every component instead of creating per-graph worker pools;
- expose executor identity and counters so tests can verify that all stages share the executor.

## Acceptance criteria

- A split embedding + decoder fixture generates the same tokens as an equivalent fused graph.
- Both evaluators report the same `cpu_executor_instance_id`.
- Execution counters show dispatches from both graphs on that shared executor.
- Repeated and concurrent generation calls do not leak persistent state between calls.
- Thread-count, affinity, spin, and nesting options are resolved once for the pipeline.

agent_prs.title: Propagate immutable initializer provenance into nested sessions

issues.body:
## Problem

Kernel preparation currently identifies preparable inputs only from initializers seeded by the current `RuntimeSession`. A model-local `FunctionProto` has no initializer list, so when an immutable root initializer is bound to a function formal parameter, the child session loses the information that the value is immutable. Captured immutable initializers in nested subgraphs have the same gap.

The nested sessions share the hierarchy-wide `ValueStore`, but that alone does not make inner kernels receive the corresponding names in `preparable_inputs`. Consequently, kernels such as `Gemm` do not publish or reuse prepared weights for these nested constant inputs. Execution remains correct, but the preparation path is inactive.

ONNX Runtime handles the equivalent cases through default AOT function inlining and explicit parent-scope constant propagation for subgraphs. onnx-light should preserve the provenance without requiring function inlining.

## Expected behavior

- Map immutable root initializer provenance through model-local function bindings, including transitive nested-function calls.
- Propagate captured immutable initializer provenance into nested graph sessions.
- Do not mark overridable initializers that are also graph inputs as immutable.
- Add tests showing that an inner preparation-capable kernel receives the mapped formal/body name and publishes into the shared `ValueStore`.

Deferred from #5219 to avoid expanding that runtime ownership PR further.

`RuntimeSession` could construct kernels using an opset supplied separately through `RuntimeContext`, even when it disagreed with the model’s `opset_import`.

- **Model sessions:** Select each kernel’s opset from the session-owned import for its node domain. Reject missing or duplicate imports, unsupported standard-domain versions, and conflicting context opsets.

agent_prs.title: Use model opset imports for runtime kernel selection

issues.body:
## Problem

`RuntimeSession` receives a `ModelProto` containing `opset_import`, but kernel construction uses the separate `KernelContext::opset` supplied through `RuntimeContext`. Callers must manually duplicate the model opset, and the runtime does not reject mismatches. This allowed an opset-23 benchmark model to execute with kernels configured for opset 18.

## Proposed direction

- Store the model opset imports in `RuntimeSession` when it is constructed from a `ModelProto`.
- Derive each kernel construction context from the node domain and the session-owned opset imports.
- Remove the requirement for callers to provide an opset through `RuntimeContext`, or deprecate that API before removing it.
- Define behavior for sessions built directly from a `GraphProto` or `ExecutionPlan`, which currently lack model opset metadata.
- Validate missing domains, duplicate imports, and unsupported opset versions explicitly.
- Propagate the same source of truth into nested graph and function sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- A model cannot silently execute kernels under a different opset than its `opset_import`.
- Runtime callers do not manually copy model opset versions into `RuntimeContext`.
- Tests cover default and custom domains, nested sessions, missing imports, and the legacy graph/plan constructors.
- Existing backend tests and Python bindings migrate to the simplified API.
issues.title: Make model opsets the single source of truth for runtime kernels

agent_prs.body:
Encrypted model I/O offered authenticated ChaCha20-Poly1305 and legacy, unauthenticated AES-256-CBC, but no authenticated AES option. This change adds AES-256-GCM while preserving read compatibility with both existing formats.

- **Format:** Introduces `ONNXCRY3` with a random PBKDF2 salt, 12-byte nonce, authentication tag, and ciphertext. The magic, salt, and nonce are authenticated as additional data.
- **API:** Accepts `encryption="AES-256-GCM"` in C++ and Python save APIs; existing load APIs detect the format automatically.
- **Documentation and coverage:** Describes the new format and recommends authenticated formats for new files. Adds file and in-memory round-trip, wrong-key, tampering, and truncation cases.

```python
onnxl.save_encrypted(model, "model.onnxc", key="passphrase", encryption="AES-256-GCM")
model = onnxl.load_encrypted("model.onnxc", key="passphrase")
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #5209
agent_prs.title: Add AES-256-GCM encrypted model support

issues.body:
## Motivation

Encrypted model I/O currently supports legacy unauthenticated AES-256-CBC (`ONNXCRY1`) and authenticated ChaCha20-Poly1305 (`ONNXCRY2`). Add AES-256-GCM through the existing OpenSSL EVP integration so users can choose an authenticated AES format.

## Proposed format

Introduce `ONNXCRY3` with the following layout:

| Offset | Size | Field |
|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 8 | Magic: `ONNXCRY3` |
| 8 | 16 | Random PBKDF2 salt |
| 24 | 12 | Random GCM nonce |
| 36 | 16 | Authentication tag |
| 52 | N | AES-256-GCM ciphertext |

Use `EVP_aes_256_gcm()` and the existing 32-byte PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key derivation. Authenticate the format header, salt, and nonce as additional authenticated data so metadata tampering is detected.

## API

- Accept `encryption="AES-256-GCM"` in C++ and in Python `save_encrypted` / `save_encrypted_string`.
- Detect `ONNXCRY3` automatically in the existing load APIs.
- Preserve read compatibility with `ONNXCRY1` and `ONNXCRY2`.
- Document AES-256-CBC as a legacy format without authentication and recommend AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for new files.

## Acceptance criteria

- File and in-memory round trips succeed with AES-256-GCM.
- Wrong keys and modifications to the header, salt, nonce, tag, or ciphertext fail authentication before protobuf parsing.
- Truncated and empty payloads fail with explicit errors.
- Existing AES-256-CBC and ChaCha20-Poly1305 tests remain unchanged and pass.
- C++ headers, Python docstrings, API documentation, and encrypted-format documentation describe `ONNXCRY3`.
- The implementation is conditionally available with the existing OpenSSL build support and uses the OpenSSL EVP API.
issues.title: Support AES-256-GCM encrypted models through OpenSSL

agent_prs.body:
Native normalization kernels used separate mean and variance passes, limiting stable, parallel reduction. This change gives variance computations shared accumulator semantics while preserving dtype and stash-precision behavior.

- **Accumulation:** Add a typed `(count, mean, M2)` Welford accumulator with fixed-size partials and index-ordered Chan merges. Chunk boundaries and merge order do not depend on worker scheduling.
- **Kernels:** Migrate training BatchNormalization, InstanceNormalization, GroupNormalization, LayerNormalization, and MeanVarianceNormalization. Keep centered subtraction during normalization to avoid large-offset cancellation.
- **Scope and coverage:** Add C++ cases for serial/parallel equivalence, edge cases, and poorly conditioned inputs, plus small, crossover, and large reduction benchmarks. Document why inference-only statistics and uncentered sums of squares do not use Welford. Portable thresholds remain unchanged.

agent_prs.title: Use deterministic Welford/Chan accumulation for native variance kernels

issues.body:
## Objective

Audit native kernels that compute means, variances, or related streaming statistics and use Welford accumulation with deterministic Chan merging wherever it improves numerical stability and enables safe parallel reduction.

## Initial scope

Review at least:

- `BatchNormalization` (inference/training statistics where applicable)
- `InstanceNormalization`
- `GroupNormalization`
- `LayerNormalization`
- `MeanVarianceNormalization`
- any other kernel or runtime utility computing variance from accumulated samples

`RMSNormalization` and pure sums/sums-of-squares should only be changed if Welford/Chan is mathematically appropriate; otherwise document the exclusion or use the suitable stable summation algorithm.

## Requirements

- Introduce a reusable typed accumulator for `(count, mean, M2)` rather than duplicating operator-specific implementations.
- Support deterministic Chan merges of partial accumulators for parallel kernels.
- Keep each worker's traversal order deterministic and define a fixed merge order so results do not depend on scheduling.
- Preserve current dtype and stash-precision contracts, including FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 promotion behavior.
- Handle empty, scalar, zero-variance, large-magnitude, and poorly conditioned inputs explicitly.
- Do not regress allocator discipline: temporary storage must remain bounded and use repository runtime allocation conventions.
- Add focused C++ tests comparing serial and parallel policies, adversarial numerical cases, and existing reference outputs.
- Add benchmark coverage for small, crossover, and large reduction groups on x86-64 and ARM64 before changing portable thresholds.
- Record reviewed exclusions for sites where Welford/Chan does not apply or cannot outperform the existing algorithm.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every native variance computation has either migrated to the shared Welford/Chan implementation or has a documented reason to retain another algorithm.
- Parallel and serial paths use the same
issues.title: Use Welford/Chan accumulation for variance computations where appropriate

agent_prs.title: Avoid copying unchanged nodes during local-function inlining

issues.body:
## Context

PR #5166 currently copies unchanged nodes into the rebuilt node list in `GraphBuilder::InlineFunctionCalls` (`kept.push_back(node)` in `onnx_light/onnx_core/builder/graph_builder.cc`). The remaining review comment identifies a potential allocation/copy overhead for large graphs:
https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-light/pull/5166#discussion_r4205953216

The copy is intentional: if a later function call fails during expansion, moving earlier nodes would leave the original `nodes_` list partially moved-from. Simply replacing the copy with `std::move(node)` breaks the existing failure-preservation regression.

## Scope

Avoid unnecessary copies of unchanged nodes during local-function inlining, while preserving the current graph and builder state on the failure paths already covered by tests. Investigate a staging/commit approach or equivalent that delays destructive moves until the relevant expansion has succeeded. Do not change proto serialization or cache APIs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve the behavior covered by `GraphBuilder.InlineLocalFunctionsRejectsMissingAttributeReferences`, including the preceding root node, unchanged serialized graph, absence of leaked initializers/subgraphs/names, and repeated failure.
- Preserve existing successful inlining behavior and unrelated/shared subgraph builders.
- Add coverage for the chosen failure-safe optimization and demonstrate reduced unchanged-node copying on a representative large graph, including no-call and mixed call/non-call cases.
- Do not claim whole-operation transactional guarantees beyond what is implemented and tested.

This issue tracks a potential performance cost, not a measured performance regression. It is separate from the Windows serialization failure.
issues.title: Optimize unchanged NodeProto handling during function inlining without breaking failure safety

issues.body:
With onnx-light 0.1.30, optimizing the graph emitted by the skl2onnx MLPClassifier converter removes the `Reshape(-1)` between `ai.onnx.ml::ArrayFeatureExtractor` and `Cast`. The optimized model declares a label output of shape `[batch]`, but ONNX Runtime produces `[1, batch]` and warns that the actual output shape does not match the model.

Before optimization the converter emits:

```
ArgMax -> ArrayFeatureExtractor -> Reshape(-1) -> Cast

After optimization it becomes:

The Reshape is required by ArrayFeatureExtractor output semantics and must not be removed.

issues.body:
## Problem

The GenAI compatibility benchmark fails while generating TinyLLM with the `onnx-light-cpu` backend:

```text
ValueError: kernel::ReduceSum: data must be a FLOAT or DOUBLE tensor.
```

The scenario itself uses `fp32`, but the generated graph contains integer tensors such as `attention_mask`. A `ReduceSum` node receives an `INT64` tensor, which is valid for the ONNX operator schema.

The failure is in the generic onnx-light kernel:

```text
onnx_light/onnx_extensions/kernels/kernels/reduction/kernel_reducesum.cc
```

The implementation currently validates and dispatches only `FLOAT` and `DOUBLE`.

## Expected behavior

`ReduceSum` should support `INT64` inputs and preserve the input tensor type in its output, consistently with the ONNX schema. Add a C++ backend regression test covering `ReduceSum(INT64)`.

## Reproduction

The failure is visible in the `main-branches-abi3` and `main-branches-native` jobs of this workflow run:

https://github.com/xadupre/onnx-asv-benchmark/actions/runs/37203414292

The ABI-domain issue is no longer involved: kernel registration succeeds and execution reaches this `ReduceSum` validation error.

agent_prs.title: Handle partial release metadata in ExecutionPlan

issues.body:
## Problem

`ExecutionPlan::BuildActions()` treats release metadata as all-or-nothing across a graph. If any node has `onnx_light.release_after`, `annotated` becomes true and topology-derived releases are disabled for every other node. If any node also has `onnx_light.not_used_after`, strict validation then requires every consumed intermediate to have an explicit release entry.

A partially annotated model therefore fails during session execution with:

```text
RuntimeError: `released.count(out) != 0` failed. [onnx-light] ExecutionPlan: result `B` is never released or unlocked (missing release metadata).
```

This is the same failure observed on the mbext Tiny-LLM prefill graph, where `/model/attn_mask_reformat/attn_mask_subgraph/Sub/Cast/output_0` is consumed by `GroupQueryAttention` but has no `release_after` entry. This is not a missing kernel.

## Reproducer

Commit `3835fa5d2` on branch `test/partial-release-metadata-model` adds the backend model `test_cc_release_partial_metadata` under `cases_for_shapes/release`. Its graph is:

```text
Add(X, W) -> A -> Relu -> B -> Identity -> Y
```

The model carries `not_used_after = X;W` on Add and `release_after = A` on Relu, while B intentionally has no release annotation. Construction of the strict, metadata-driven execution plan rejects B instead of deriving its last-use release from graph topology.

## Expected behavior

ExecutionPlan should either:

1. derive topology releases for intermediates missing from otherwise partial `release_after` metadata, or
2. ensure the annotation pass always writes a complete release schedule before strict validation is enabled.

Partial annotations should not make an otherwise executable ONNX model fail before kernel execution.

## Verified environment

- onnx-light main at `1a9dd3c39` (0.1.29) with reproducer commit `3835fa5d2`
- `_onnxpybackend` rebuilt successfully
- backend model materializes as a 3-node MODEL/RELEASE case
- `ReferenceEvaluator.run()` reproduces the exact missing-
issues.title: ExecutionPlan rejects partially annotated release metadata
