## What happened

On a Cloud Agent, `npx @kodycodes/cli@1.13.0 status` printed `API token expires: 2026-10-12T01:41:07.994Z` for a cli-bootstrap token, but at 02:57 UTC the same stored token still authenticated `execute --local` (ship-pr ticks, reply-review, merge) and minted a narrower token through `auth bootstrap --scopes`.

## What you wanted

`kody status` should show the effective expiry (idle refresh or max lifetime), or label the stored value as the last-known idle deadline, so agents do not re-bootstrap or misread an expired-looking token.

## How to reproduce

Bootstrap a short token with `auth bootstrap --code …`, use it past the printed `expires` time, then run `kody status` and compare against a successful `kody whoami`.

## Cost

Small: it misled me into checking credential health before each step and complicates reasoning about which token a demo used.

## Preliminary investigation

Seen while shipping kentcdodds/kody#3447 with @kodycodes/cli 1.13.0. I did not inspect whether the server extends the idle TTL without the CLI rewriting the stored expires_at.
issues.title: Friction: kody status shows a stale API token expiry after the token keeps working

issues.body:
## What happened

`npx @kodycodes/cli login --device --mcp-url https://kody-pr-4476.kody-a99.workers.dev/mcp` printed the device code, the preview /device page showed "Device approved", and then the CLI exited with "Kody rejected the API token (expired, revoked, or malformed) ... Server said: Invalid API token." and saved no credentials. It failed the same way twice, including after the stale preview credentials file was moved away. Adding `--api-url https://kody-pr-4476-api.kody-a99.workers.dev` made the same flow succeed at once. An earlier login against the same preview, about 40 minutes before, had worked without --api-url.

## What you wanted

Device login should derive the preview Open API host from --mcp-url, the way execute's own error suggests it knows the pairing ("credentials for <preview> are only sent to <preview>-api"), or say that --api-url is needed. It should not fail after the human approved.

## How to reproduce

With HOME pointing at a fresh dir, run `npx @kodycodes/cli login --device --mcp-url https://kody-pr-<N>.kody-a99.workers.dev/mcp`, approve on the preview /device page, and watch the CLI fail with Invalid API token. Repeat with `--api-url https://kody-pr-<N>-api.kody-a99.workers.dev`: it succeeds.

## Cost

About 10 minutes and three device approvals while re-verifying a production-regression fix on its preview.

## Preliminary investigation

No KODY_* env vars were set. The preview API /health was ok on the same commit. I suspect the CLI verifies the new token against the default api.kody.codes (or some cached API URL) instead of the preview API host, but I did not read the CLI login code.
issues.title: Friction: CLI device login to a PR preview fails after approval unless --api-url is passed

## What happened

While verifying #4496, wrapping-key storage is now rollback-protected, but saveContext still runs after that try/catch. If the local key write fails (unwritable state dir, keyring write error after wrappingFor succeeded), the server context remains with no usable local key.

The same DELETE then POST delete rollback that wrappingFor already uses, wrapped around saveContext.

Same orphan as #4496: revoke plus a new name to recover.

## Preliminary investigation

packages/cli/src/execution-context/commands.ts: wrappingFor is in try/catch with DELETE+POST delete; saveContext is the next statement with no rollback. No test covers a saveContext throw after register.

## What happened

Running the ship-pr tick via `kody execute --local` with a CLI login minted by cliCredentialBootstrap failed with insufficient_scope for org:execute. After re-bootstrapping with that scope it failed for package:execute, then again for integration:read. Each round needed a new cliCredentialBootstrap call plus `kody auth bootstrap`.

The errors come back one scope at a time, which suggests the check stops at the first missing scope. I did not look at the CLI or the scope-check code.

## What happened

Ran `npx @kodycodes/cli execute --local /home/ubuntu/tick.ts` (a valid ESM module). The CLI bundled the path string itself as the module and workerd failed with "service main: Uncaught SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression flags at main.js:1".

Running adminPackageCodemodDryRun / adminPackageCodemodApply for one large package (kentcdodds `discord`, `kody-discord`) through `npx @kodycodes/cli execute --local` exited non-zero after ~7 minutes. stderr only had the 'Fetching local-execute package graph' line, and stdout was empty. The server kept running: a retry of the same cursor reported the package `clean` because the first apply had already published.

## What you wanted

A configurable capability timeout (flag or env), and a clear stderr message naming the timeout, so a long admin step is not mistaken for a failure and retried blind.

## How to reproduce

Call a capability that runs longer than 7 minutes through `kody execute --local` (for example adminPackageCodemodApply with limit 1 on a large package).

## Cost

About 1 hour during the codemod 0012 rollout: failed retries, then patching the cached CLI (capabilityProxyHttpTimeoutMs) locally to 25 minutes.

## Preliminary investigation

`dist/capability-proxy.js` hardcodes `capabilityProxyHttpTimeoutMs = 7 * 60_000` as the undici headers/body timeout; createCapabilityProxyAgent() is called with no argument and no env override.

Relevant files:
- `packages/cli/src/capability-proxy.ts`

agent_prs.body:
## Intent

Close the safely actionable credentials leftovers: fail closed where the stamp scan could not see a module, make placement repair atomic with the value write, show owners their invalid slots, and give admins a count of package-scoped secrets that the 0010 scan cannot see.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

- The publish stamp gate skipped server modules Babel could not parse, so a module using `credential` or `kody` in unsupported syntax published without a check.
- `secretSet` wrote the value in one D1 batch and repaired the manifest placement in a second write, so a failed repair left a new value with a stale placement.

## What happened

The migration can report zero 0010 findings while package-scoped buckets remain, so the plan section 7 done criterion overstates progress.

docs/contributing/package-codemods.md now documents the limit (kentcdodds/kody#3374). The data lives in the secrets table (scope, binding_key); tools/credential-pattern-report.ts only reads scan step JSON.

## What happened

parseAuthoredPackageJson still records kody.invalidCredentialSlots for a kody.credentials slot that fails validation, for example `raw: true` in published mode (packages/worker/src/package-registry/manifest.ts). ## What you wanted

A decision on the field. Either something surfaces a bad slot to the package owner (package_get, publish, or repo checks), or the field and its tests are removed so the manifest carries no dead state.

## How to reproduce

Run `git grep -n invalidCredentialSlots -- packages ':!*.test.ts'` on main after 936dd8dbf. The only hits are the writer in manifest.ts and the type in types.ts.

## Cost

Low today. It is dead state, and a future reader could assume it is enforced. A package with a broken slot gets no signal about it.

## Preliminary investigation

#3357 added the field so one bad slot fails on its own instead of dropping every slot. In #3408 the gateway stopped reading slots for placement, which removed the only consumer. @kody/bluesky 1.1.0 publishes a `raw: true` slot that lands in invalidCredentialSlots. It works in production now because nothing gates on slots.

- `packages/worker/src/package-registry/manifest.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/package-registry/types.ts`

## What happened

On package-scope secretSet that repairs an untouched default placement, upsertSecretEntriesAtomically commits the new value first, then updateSecretEntryPlacement runs as a separate statement. A SQLITE_BUSY on the repair leaves value written with unrepaired headers-only placement until a later retry.

## What you wanted

Resolve repairs before the batch, append prepareUpdateSecretEntryPlacementStatement to the same D1 batch, and auditPlacementDeclarationRepaired only after the batch succeeds so value and placement cannot diverge mid-write.

## How to reproduce

Trigger package secretSet with an untouched default_unread/default_undeclared row while D1 is under load so the post-upsert placement UPDATE fails; observe placement_origin still default_* after the value write.

## Cost

Temporary wrong placement metadata (and wrong credential-page note) until reconnect/retry; becomes user-visible breakage once placement enforcement ships.

## Preliminary investigation

CodeRabbit on #4120 (discussion_r4331557301). Decided wontfix there with observe-only impact. Related paths: packages/worker/src/mcp/secrets/service.ts saveSecretsAtomically repair loop, update-secret-placement.ts, upsertSecretEntriesAtomically.

issues.body:
## What happened

When parseModule (credentials/module-placeholder-scan.ts) returns null, the credential stamp scanners fall back to narrow text patterns (e.g. the kody.mcp and server-eval regex fallbacks in credentials/credential-stamp.ts) or skip the module. A module that fails to parse can alias or pass `credential` around without a non_literal failure. #4650 added parser retries (TypeScript without JSX, decorators-legacy), which covers `<T>x` assertions and decorators, but any other syntax the parser rejects still fails open.

## What you wanted

A server-runtime module the stamp scanner cannot parse should fail closed with a clear diagnostic (or at least whenever it mentions credential/credentials/kody), rather than passing silently.

## How to reproduce

Call scanCredentialStamp with a server module that imports credential from kody:runtime, contains syntax `@babel/parser` rejects under every plugin set in parseModuleSourceAllowingTypeAssertions, and has `const open = credential`. No non_literal failure is reported.

## Cost

Found while fixing the type-position bug. A gap in the publish gate, not seen in the wild.

## Preliminary investigation

parseModule in module-placeholder-scan.ts swallows parse errors and returns null. forEachScannableModule passes null to visitors, and the stamp visitors only run text fallbacks for kody.mcp and eval. Suggested fix: emit a parse-failure diagnostic for unparseable server-runtime modules that reference credential/credentials/kody, gated by a test.

Relevant files:
- `packages/worker/src/credentials/credential-stamp.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/credentials/module-placeholder-scan.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/module-source.ts`

agent_prs.body:
## Intent

Make hosted execute runs that outlive the MCP transport budget end with a known, recorded outcome instead of `platform_interrupted`, make keyed retries and `runGet` report finished runs right away, and stop a rejected first `packageSave` from leaving a half-created package.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

Hosted execute on the stateless MCP lane and the Open API route runs in a plain Worker request. Once the follow response goes out at the 45s transport budget, only `waitUntil` keeps the sandbox alive, and that is about 30s. A run past roughly 75s was cut off mid-flight with no terminal write, so its run row stayed `running` until stale reconciliation marked it `platform_interrupted` about 3 minutes later. That one mechanism explains the reports in this batch: two `packageSave` calls in one module, a long admin publish repair, a ship-pr tick whose idempotent retries said "still running" for minutes, and a fleet rebuild that hit the limit on every attempt.

## Summary

- **Detached run deadline** (`execute.ts`, `execute-transport-budget.ts`): on lanes where only `waitUntil` keeps work alive (`detachedWorkLimitMs`, set by the stateless MCP lane and `/v1/execute`), a run still going 20s after its follow response is aborted with the normal sandbox timeout (`Execution timed out after Ns: ...`). The run record gets that outcome while the isolate can still write it, so `runGet` and keyed retries see it right away. The follow response text says how long the run has left. The Durable Object MCP lane is unchanged.
- **Open API execute waits out the sandbox** (`openApiExecuteTransportBudgetMs` = 105s): the CLI's cloud execute is not an MCP client with a 60s deadline, so `/v1/execute` now returns the finished result instead of a follow handle for runs that fit the 90s sandbox budget.
- **`runGet` returns `result`**: the retained return value (the same 4 KiB snapshot as `run.metadata.result`) is a top-level field on finished runs. The follow respons
agent_prs.title: fix(execute): known outcomes for long hosted execute, runGet result, packageSave rollback, chunked admin rebuilds

issues.body:
## What happened

Running the #4129 fleet rebuild in production through hosted execute, the immediate post-rebuild verification reported 43 packages as still stale or failed; targeted dry runs minutes later showed all of them current. Separately, one package with about 29 stale targets hit the hosted execute time limit on every apply attempt (limit 1, repeated retries), so it could not be rebuilt and is only covered by the quiet-allow window.

## What you wanted

Apply results that reflect the stored artifacts once the write settles (or a clear pending/verify-later outcome), and a way to rebuild a package with many targets without one run exceeding the execute limit (for example per-target batching or a background job).

## How to reproduce

Call kody.adminPreBindingArtifactRebuild({ dryRun: false, limit: 5 }) from hosted execute in production on packages that need rebuild; compare its stale_after counts with kody.adminPreBindingArtifactRebuild({ dryRun: true, packageIds }) a few minutes later. For the time limit, target a package with ~29 stale targets with limit 1.

## Cost

Hours of retries and manual delayed re-verification during the #4129 rollout; one package left unrebuilt.

## Preliminary investigation

Delayed targeted dry runs showed every apparent failure current, which points to a read-after-write lag on artifact reads rather than build failures; not confirmed which store lags. The time-limit package fails at the same point regardless of batch size because all its targets are rebuilt in one force rebuild call (rebuildPublishedPackageArtifactsViaRepoSession with all targets).

Relevant files:
- `packages/worker/src/package-runtime/pre-binding-artifact-rebuild.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/mcp/capabilities/admin/admin-pre-binding-artifact-rebuild.ts`
issues.title: Friction: adminPreBindingArtifactRebuild: post-rebuild check reads old artifacts, and large packages exceed the execute time limit

## What happened

## What happened

A first packageSave for a new package whose job used a 1m interval on a pro-plan account threw "Your "pro" plan cannot run jobs more often than every 15 minutes". The package was still created: packageList showed it, and retrying packageSave with the same name (schedule fixed) failed with "would overwrite existing package source" until confirm_destructive_overwrite.

On a pro-plan account, packageSave a brand-new package whose package.json kody.jobs entry has schedule { type: "interval", every: "1m" }. Observe the plan error, then packageList (the package exists), then packageSave again with every: "15m" (overwrite refusal).

## Cost

A leftover package plus a confusing overwrite refusal; I had to save under a second name and delete both afterward.

## Preliminary investigation

Observed once in production on 2026-10-30. Did not trace whether the package row is written before job schedule validation; no root cause claimed.

issues.body:
## What happened

A hosted MCP execute that paged a read-only admin scan several pages in one module ran past the transport budget and returned inProgress with a runId and a server-assigned idempotencyKey. Retrying execute with that same key a few minutes later returned inProgress again, but with a different runId, and never surfaced the first run's result. This happened twice in one session. runGet with the first runId reported the run as not found.

## What you wanted

Retrying with the same idempotencyKey reads the original run (in progress or retained result), as the execute description promises, and runGet finds the runId execute handed back.

## How to reproduce

From hosted MCP execute, run a module that loops several pages of `adminPackageCodemodScan` (limit 50) so it exceeds the transport budget. Note the runId and idempotencyKey. Wait two to three minutes and retry execute with the same code, params, and idempotencyKey. Compare the runId; then call runGet with the first runId.

## Cost

Each retry silently re-ran the whole scan, so the long-running multi-page approach never returned. Worked around by issuing one page per execute with an explicit idempotencyKey per page, which took many more calls.

## Preliminary investigation

## Intent

Make hosted execute runs that outlive the MCP transport budget end with a known, recorded outcome instead of `platform_interrupted`, make keyed retries and `runGet` report finished runs right away, and stop a rejected first `packageSave` from leaving a half-created package.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

Hosted execute on the stateless MCP lane and the Open API route runs in a plain Worker request. Once the follow response goes out at the 45s transport budget, only `waitUntil` keeps the sandbox alive, and that is about 30s. A run past roughly 75s was cut off mid-flight with no terminal write, so its run row stayed `running` until stale reconciliation marked it `platform_interrupted` about 3 minutes later. That one mechanism explains the reports in this batch: two `packageSave` calls in one module, a long admin publish repair, a ship-pr tick whose idempotent retries said "still running" for minutes, and a fleet rebuild that hit the limit on every attempt.

## Summary

- **Detached run deadline** (`execute.ts`, `execute-transport-budget.ts`): on lanes where only `waitUntil` keeps work alive (`detachedWorkLimitMs`, set by the stateless MCP lane and `/v1/execute`), a run still going 20s after its follow response is aborted with the normal sandbox timeout (`Execution timed out after Ns: ...`). The run record gets that outcome while the isolate can still write it, so `runGet` and keyed retries see it right away. The follow response text says how long the run has left. The Durable Object MCP lane is unchanged.
- **Open API execute waits out the sandbox** (`openApiExecuteTransportBudgetMs` = 105s): the CLI's cloud execute is not an MCP client with a 60s deadline, so `/v1/execute` now returns the finished result instead of a follow handle for runs that fit the 90s sandbox budget.
- **`runGet` returns `result`**: the retained return value (the same 4 KiB snapshot as `run.metadata.result`) is a top-level field on finished runs. The follow respons
agent_prs.title: fix(execute): known outcomes for long hosted execute, runGet result, packageSave rollback, chunked admin rebuilds

## What happened

A hosted (context cloud) execute module that awaited kody.packageSave for two small new packages back to back (4 text files each) ran about 3 minutes and ended with error_name platform_interrupted, outcome unknown. Only the first package was created. Happened twice in a row. The same packageSave done one package per execute finished in about 30 to 45 seconds each.

## What you wanted

Two small packageSave calls in one execute should finish, or fail with a clear limit error, instead of an unknown-outcome interruption that leaves partial state.

## How to reproduce

From MCP execute with context cloud, run a module that does `await kody.packageSave({ files: b })` then `await kody.packageSave({ files: a })` for two new 4-file packages (package.json, README.md with ## Intent, AGENTS.md, one src file). Poll runGet: status error, platform_interrupted after ~180 s, and only the first package exists.

## Cost

About 10 minutes plus guesswork about which package was saved; partial state had to be found by trying static imports.

## Preliminary investigation

Confirmed with runGet (no logs, log_count 0). Splitting into one packageSave per execute worked every time. Did not look at the packageSave implementation or the hosted execute wall-clock budget.
issues.title: Friction: Hosted execute that calls packageSave twice ends platform_interrupted

## Intent

Tighten the publish and package-source path: one key shape for published snapshot files, no tip promotion that a deferred rebuild is sure to reject, repo ids in admin repo flag tools, a smaller artifact module, and room to grow the package authoring guide.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

Each issue below names a papercut in the publish and package-source lane that is still present on main.

## Summary

- #3569: `writePublishedSourceSnapshot` and external publish re-key source-root-relative check files from the repo root through the new `repoRelativeSourceFiles` helper (`repo/published-source-files.ts`). `PublishedSourceSnapshot.files` documents one repo-root key shape. Snapshots already written in the old shape still read, because `packageSourceFiles` accepts both.
- #4145: when `deferBundleCheckToRebuild` skips esbuild, the bundle check now walks static relative imports from the bundle targets (`repo/unresolved-relative-imports.ts`). If any import resolves to no file, the check fails before `finalizePublishedEntitySource` moves the tip. Type-only imports and unparseable files are skipped.
- #3814: `admin_feature_flag_repo_*` accepts an `entity_sources.id` or a `user_repos.id` and returns both `sourceId` and `repoId`.
- #4304: persistence and build-target code moves from `published-bundle-artifacts.ts` (1302 lines, now 821) to `published-bundle-artifact-persist.ts`. The old module re-exports the persist APIs, so callers do not change.
- #4299: shorter `package_authoring` summary, and the duplicate Remix route sample is now a sentence that links to the Package apps Remix recipe. Full-body headroom goes from 16 to 400 characters. `guide.node.test.ts` now requires at least 256 characters of headroom, so the next small edit still fits while `bodyMode` stays `full`.

Fixes #3569
Fixes #4145
Fixes #3814
Fixes #4304

- New or updated tests: `published-source-files.node.

issues.body:
## Leftover

External package publish (`packagePublishExternalPush` / `publishFromExternalRef`) sets `deferBundleCheckToRebuild: true` so pre-promotion checks only verify declared entrypoints exist in the snapshot (`cheapBundleCheckResult` in `packages/worker/src/repo/checks.ts`). Full esbuild runs later during artifact rebuild.

### Gap

A commit whose export/app entry files exist but whose **relative imports** resolve to missing snapshot paths can:
1. Pass the deferred cheap bundle check
2. Advance `published_commit` via `finalizePublishedEntitySource`
3. Fail only afterward as `checks_failed` when rebuild cannot bundle

So the tip can move to a commit that never produced callable artifacts. (`packageCheck` / non-deferred publish paths still run full esbuild and refuse earlier.)

### Why not fix in the CLI snapshot PR

`kody dev check` now fails when local bundle inputs are outside the publish snapshot path set. That closes the local false-pass. A pre-promotion relative-import walk on the hot external-publish path is a separate product/risk decision (must stay cheap and not reintroduce full check-time esbuild before tip move).

### Suggested follow-up

- Add a cheap relative-import resolution pass (or equivalent) when `deferBundleCheckToRebuild` is set, **before** tip promotion; missing declared entrypoints already fail today.
- Or refuse tip move / roll back when rebuild returns bundle `checks_failed` (product decision).
- Keep full esbuild deferred to rebuild unless product chooses otherwise (hosted build steps remain a pending decision).

### Pointers

- `packages/worker/src/repo/checks.ts` (`deferBundleCheckToRebuild`, `cheapBundleCheckResult`)
- `packages/worker/src/mcp/capabilities/packages/publish-external-push.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/repo/external-publish.ts`
- Tests: `checks-defer-bundle.node.test.ts` (missing **export path** fails; transitive relative misses are not covered under defer)
issues.title: Cleanup: refuse external publish tip promotion when deferred rebuild will fail unresolved relative imports

agent_prs.body:
## Intent

Close the Sentry and GitHub package friction batch: worker RPC errors reach Sentry, the Sentry REST escape hatch honors method and body, PR merges work on merge queue branches, and a failed merge always says why.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

- Bare `WorkerEntrypoint` classes run RPC methods with no Sentry client, so throws and `captureException` there were dropped (same gap that hid the backup lag on `JobsHost`).
- The Sentry `request` export only read `path`, `query`, and `init`, so a top-level `method: 'PUT'` with `body` silently ran a GET.
- `pr/merge` only used the REST merge PUT, which GitHub refuses on merge queue branches.
- `ship-pr/merge` returned a bare `merged: false` when the delegated merge did not land.

## Summary

This repo (#4546):
- New `getWorkerEntrypointSentryOptions` (disabled without a DSN). `KodyApi`, `DynamicWorkerUsageTail`, and `RuntimeWorkerService` are now exported through `Sentry.withSentry`, like `JobsHost`. `RuntimeWorkerService` drops its hand-rolled per-request wrap in favor of the class wrap.
- `worker-entrypoint-sentry.node.test.ts` fails on any top-level `WorkerEntrypoint` class in `packages/worker/src` that is exported bare or not wrapped. `KodyFetchGateway` and `PackageAppRuntimeBridge` stay bare by an explicit allowlist: their throws are caller-facing results for sandboxed user code (host denials, missing credentials, undeclared capabilities), so wrapping would page on user mistakes.

Kody packages (already pushed and published; not part of this diff):
- Sentry package `2.1.0` (`2358b6d`), #4633: `request` accepts top-level `method`, `headers`, and `body` (objects sent as JSON); unknown keys and a body without a method throw. Verified live: an unknown key now throws instead of a GET.
- GitHub package `0.2.0` (`4060707`), #4241: `pr/merge` enqueues through GraphQL `enqueuePullRequest` (pinned to the head SHA) when the PR is blocked and the base branch has a merge queue, or when the PUT is refuse

issues.body:
## What happened

On a high-risk PR (mergeAuthority true, squash) whose tick said ready_to_merge (MERGEABLE/CLEAN), the first ship-pr/merge call returned { merged: false, dryRun: false, headSha } with no result, error or refusal reason. The PR stayed open. An identical second call a minute later merged it.

## What you wanted

merge either merges, or returns a reason (refusal gate, GitHub error, timeout) so the agent knows whether to retry, fix something, or stop.

## How to reproduce

Tick a high-risk PR to ready_to_merge, then run `kody:@kentcdodds/ship-pr/merge` with { prUrl, risk: 'high', mergeAuthority: true, mergeMethod: 'squash' } via npx `@kodycodes/cli` execute --local --file. Observe the returned object when merge does not happen.

## Cost

One wasted round trip plus guessing whether a retry was safe.

## Preliminary investigation

GitHub showed the PR open, mergeable true, mergeable_state clean right after the failed call; no new review threads had appeared. The retry returned result.status merged within 9 s (timeoutMs 25000). I did not see what the first call's result field held, because my wrapper only printed selected keys and result was absent.
issues.title: Friction: ship-pr/merge can return merged:false with no reason while the PR is clean and mergeable

## Intent

Close the Sentry and GitHub package friction batch: worker RPC errors reach Sentry, the Sentry REST escape hatch honors method and body, PR merges work on merge queue branches, and a failed merge always says why.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

- Bare `WorkerEntrypoint` classes run RPC methods with no Sentry client, so throws and `captureException` there were dropped (same gap that hid the backup lag on `JobsHost`).
- The Sentry `request` export only read `path`, `query`, and `init`, so a top-level `method: 'PUT'` with `body` silently ran a GET.
- `pr/merge` only used the REST merge PUT, which GitHub refuses on merge queue branches.
- `ship-pr/merge` returned a bare `merged: false` when the delegated merge did not land.

## Summary

This repo (#4546):
- New `getWorkerEntrypointSentryOptions` (disabled without a DSN). `KodyApi`, `DynamicWorkerUsageTail`, and `RuntimeWorkerService` are now exported through `Sentry.withSentry`, like `JobsHost`. `RuntimeWorkerService` drops its hand-rolled per-request wrap in favor of the class wrap.
- `worker-entrypoint-sentry.node.test.ts` fails on any top-level `WorkerEntrypoint` class in `packages/worker/src` that is exported bare or not wrapped. `KodyFetchGateway` and `PackageAppRuntimeBridge` stay bare by an explicit allowlist: their throws are caller-facing results for sandboxed user code (host denials, missing credentials, undeclared capabilities), so wrapping would page on user mistakes.

Kody packages (already pushed and published; not part of this diff):
- Sentry package `2.1.0` (`2358b6d`), #4633: `request` accepts top-level `method`, `headers`, and `body` (objects sent as JSON); unknown keys and a body without a method throw. Verified live: an unknown key now throws instead of a GET.
- GitHub package `0.2.0` (`4060707`), #4241: `pr/merge` enqueues through GraphQL `enqueuePullRequest` (pinned to the head SHA) when the PR is blocked and the base branch has a merge queue, or when the PUT is refuse

issues.body:
## What happened

The DR staging watchdog threw its 2+ UTC day lag error on three mornings, but no Sentry issue opened. JobsHost was a bare WorkerEntrypoint, so its RPC methods ran without a Sentry client and Sentry.captureException was a no-op. Only RPC-level failures, such as Worker OOM, reached Sentry through the calling jobs worker. #4541 wrapped JobsHost with Sentry.withSentry. Other bare WorkerEntrypoint classes in packages/worker likely have the same gap.

## What you wanted

Every main-worker RPC entrypoint that can throw or call captureException reports to Sentry. A guard test should fail when a new bare WorkerEntrypoint export is added without the wrapper.

## How to reproduce

Run `grep -rln "extends WorkerEntrypoint" packages/worker/src` and compare the exported classes with the ones wrapped by Sentry.withSentry in packages/worker/src/jobs/jobs-host.ts. Then throw from an RPC method of an unwrapped one (e.g. packages/worker/src/open-api/kody-api.ts) while SENTRY_DSN is set: no event is sent.

## Cost

A multi-day DR backup stall went unpaged for about 3 days.

## Preliminary investigation

Confirmed with Workers logs that `scheduled_lane_failed lane=dr_export_watchdog` fired on 2026-10-27, 10-28 and 10-29 while Sentry had no matching issue. The other entrypoints have not been audited individually yet.

Relevant files:
- `packages/worker/src/jobs/jobs-host.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/open-api/kody-api.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/mcp/executor.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/mcp/fetch-gateway.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/package-runtime/package-app.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/runtime-worker.ts`
issues.title: Friction: Main-worker WorkerEntrypoint RPC classes have no Sentry client, so captureException there is dropped

## What happened

Deploy runs whose display SHA matches what they deploy, or the deployed SHA in the run title/summary, so ship-pr and agents can tell 'my merge deployed' from 'a deploy ran while my merge was on main'.

The workflow_run-triggered deploy resolves DEPLOY_SHA from WORKFLOW_RUN_SHA (the Validate run's SHA), while the run's headSha shown by the API is main HEAD at trigger time.

- `tools/ci/deploy-sha-guard.ts`

## What happened

On the Collaborators tab, invite create/revoke handoff UI is guarded by generation + startedPathname so a late success/error after switching packages cannot paint the wrong package. Mid-ship CodeRabbit asked for per-package handoff persistence; we wontfix-ed that expansion to avoid restarting CI on an already-approved ship.

## What you wanted

If the user starts an invite on package A, navigates to package B while the request is in flight, then returns to A (or stays on B), the correct package should still show the handoff outcome without relying only on Pending invites.

Observe late write is dropped (correct safety). 5. Return to A — handoff UI for that invite is gone even though Pending invites lists it.

## Cost

Agents re-debate generation vs per-package store on every invite UI change; users can miss the in-tab handoff after a quick package switch.

## Preliminary investigation

packages/worker/client/routes/package-collaborators-invites.tsx uses postChange startedPathname + generation guards (158173c00). Thread 4286124682 decided wontfix mid-ship on #3813. Expanding to a per-package handoff map would be a focused follow-up with e2e coverage for mid-flight navigation.

- `packages/worker/client/routes/package-collaborators-invites.tsx`

issues.body:
## What happened

Promote-time listing auto-follow correctly forwards actorUserId and rejects a community-banned org member. If that sync fails, scheduled community_listing_behind_backfill later advances the listing as the package owner without re-checking the original publish actor.

## What you wanted

Backfill (or a gate before it) should not silently advance a public listing that was blocked only because the promoting actor is community-banned — either persist the publish actor on the published commit and re-assert, or require an eligible non-banned actor/approval before catalog catch-up.

## How to reproduce

1. Org member who is community-banned but still has package:write promotes a package that already has an active listing.
2. Inline syncActiveCommunityListingToPublishedCommit fails the actor ban check; published_commit still advances.
3. Wait for community_listing_behind_backfill (or run it).
4. Listing pin moves to the new published_commit without checking the banned actor.

## Cost

Moderate auth gap on auto-follow recovery path; needs schema or approval policy design, not a one-line fix.

## Preliminary investigation

publishCommunityListing asserts owner ban always and actor ban when actorUserId !== owner. finalizePublishedEntitySource now passes actorUserId on the inline path (PR #3729). Backfill calls sync without actorUserId. Persisting last-publish actor on entity_sources was declined as heavy lift for that UX PR; CodeRabbit outside-diff finding cr-comment:v1:a15855090ebbe7c5f75df8aa.

## What happened

softDeleteOrg stamps orgs.deleted_at before softDeleteOrgOwnedAppRows tombstones org_memberships. If a later step throws (OAuth revoke, jobs, billing), the org is deleted while Owner memberships stay live. Observe orgs.deleted_at set and org_memberships.deleted_at still NULL for Owners. 4. Without the PR #3950 listing fix, /account/organizations omits the org from Recently deleted.

## Cost

Support/restore dead-ends and confusing Owner access (live membership on a deleted org). Every soft-delete failure after the stamp hits this shape.

## Preliminary investigation

packages/worker/src/orgs/soft-delete.ts claimSoftDeleteGeneration then softDeleteOrgOwnedAppRows; restoreOwnerMembershipJoinSql added in #3950 as a listing/auth workaround. Covered by soft-delete.node.test interrupted soft-delete case.

Make pre-push and validate faster without dropping checks, and make pre-push catch the same syntax errors CI does.

**Door:** `two-way`

Pre-push reran related tests for every path merged in from main (losing push races), Start typechecks ran uncached on every validate, CI installs ran a duplicate npm audit, and a syntax error passed pre-push but failed CI lint.

issues.body:
## What happened

Two agents shipping the same PR branch both ran pre-push test:push (~11 minutes). By the time the first finished, the remote tip had moved, so git push was rejected (cannot lock ref / non-fast-forward). This repeated several times while merging main and renumbering migrations for #3854.

## What you wanted

A push that already validated the tree (or a short ship-path hook) should land without losing a multi-agent race, or the hook should skip when the tree hash was already green for that tip plus parents.

## How to reproduce

1. Open one PR branch with two Cloud Agents both merging main and pushing. 2. Each push runs full npm run test:push (~10+ min). 3. Observe remote tip advances under the slower agent and push is rejected.

## Cost

Each failed race burns ~11 minutes of CI-equivalent local test time and stalls squash-merge; #3854 needed multiple reset/merge/push cycles before landing.

## Preliminary investigation

Observed on cursor/fix-memory-personalize-purge-grants-730b while shipping #3854. pre-push already skips when tree <hash> already green, but that only helps identical trees; concurrent merge commits of main create new tips that each re-run the full suite.

Relevant files:
- `tools/git-hook-checks.ts`
- `package.json`
issues.title: Friction: Ship concurrent agents: long pre-push test:push loses the push race

## Intent

Make four flaky checks deterministic without changing product behavior beyond one dev-server watcher guard.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

These tests fail intermittently on CI from shared state, races, or mid-transition scans, not from real regressions.

## Summary

- `packages/cli/test/auth-bootstrap.test.ts`: the three `runCli` tests now set `APPDATA` to the temp home and clear the per-user keyring entry for `apiUrl` before and after. The earlier `auth bootstrap` test stored a real token in the OS keyring for the same `apiUrl`, and Windows Credential Manager ignores `HOME`, so `whoami` could read that token instead of its own (#4723).
- `packages/cli/src/package-app-dev.ts`: after a failed `kody.dev.prebuild`, a watcher event for one of that build's trigger files whose mtime predates the failed prebuild start is treated as an echo and ignored, even after the 1.5s absorb window. Real saves (newer mtime) still rebuild. The prebuild test now covers both: a stale `utimes` echo does not rebuild (fails without the fix), and a real save after the failure recovers (#4720).
- `packages/worker/src/execution-contexts/session-do.workers.test.ts`: fixture `acceptBy` now uses the same 30s `frameWaitMs` as `next()`, so a slow runner accept under load is not dispatched as expired. Production accept window is unchanged (#4610).
- `e2e/a11y.spec.ts`: `/login` and `/signup` wait for the submit button to be enabled and at `opacity: 1` before the Axe scan. The reported `#0a1d10` on `#2c923c` (4.41) matches the dark tokens blended at the disabled `0.7` opacity, so the scan ran mid fade. No brand token change (#4507).

issues.body:
## What happened

PR 4609 raised the session-do workers next() helper to 30s so a late run.request frame is not a 5s flake. runRequest() still sets acceptBy to Date.now() plus 3s (ecpDefaultAcceptWindowMs). Post-merge review (CodeRabbit and Bugbot) pointed out that a frame arriving after 3s still makes dispatch timeout or abort, so the success-path tests can fail on committed instead of no run.request frame.

## What you wanted

Success-path fixtures should keep acceptBy open at least as long as next() waits, so a late first frame can still be accepted.

## How to reproduce

In session-do.workers.test.ts, runRequest() sets acceptBy to now+3s. connect().next() waits up to 30s. Under validate or CI load, if run.request arrives after 3s the test gets the frame then dispatch returns timeout or aborted.

## Cost

The 4609 flake fix can still fail under the same load, only with a different assertion.

## Preliminary investigation

Read session-do.ts dispatch: accept waiter is Math.max(0, request.acceptBy - now) from the fixture timestamp, then a second Date.now() > acceptBy check before commit. Production routing uses ecpDefaultAcceptWindowMs (3s). This leftover is test-fixture only; do not change the production accept window.

Relevant files:
- `packages/worker/src/execution-contexts/session-do.workers.test.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/execution-contexts/session-do.ts`
issues.title: Friction: session-do tests still use a 3s acceptBy while next() waits 30s

## Intent

Admin tooling for the #4129 rollout. It rebuilds every stored package bundle built before per-package `fetch`/`kody` binding, and sizes and (later) applies an allowed-packages grandfather backfill. Without both, turning on enforcement in #4235 could break uses that work today.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `needed`

**What to delete:** Delete `adminCredentialAllowedPackagesGrandfather` and `adminPreBindingArtifactRebuild` once #4235's 30-day strict date has passed and the fleet rebuild has reported 0 stale targets.

## Why

- Load sites repair single-package pre-binding bundles in memory on every load, and never persist the repair. They rebuild bundles that inline other packages only when the source needs no npm install. Mixed bundles that need npm keep serving pre-binding code, which attributes a wrapper package's credential use to its caller. `adminPublishedImportableArtifactBackfill` only rebuilds missing importable-module targets, so it cannot close this gap.
- #4235 refuses self-authored/adopted packages that are not on a credential's non-empty allowed list. Before that ships, every package using such a credential today needs to be found and grandfathered.

## Summary

- `adminPreBindingArtifactRebuild` (dryRun default true, paged with `cursor`, `contextRuns: 'deny'`):
  - Scans the stored isolate bundles of every published package (module, importable, job, app; browser app-client is skipped) for pre-binding code, including bundles that inline other packages.
  - Apply force-rebuilds only those targets at the current published commit, re-checks that the commit did not move, and re-reads each target afterwards (`stillStaleAfterRebuild`).
  - Rebuilds artifacts only. No change to source, versions, visibility, enablements, jobs or hostnames.
- `adminCredentialAllowedPackagesGrandfather` (dryRun default true, paged):
  - Static join: the literal user credential names a package's own published source reads, using the same `scanPackageCredentials` + `

agent_prs.body:
## Intent

Tighten several auth, isolation, and input-handling paths so runtime behavior matches the documented security model in `docs/contributing/security.md`. No intended user-facing behavior change for legitimate use.

**Door:** `two-way`

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

A review pass across the Worker, package runtime, email, and CLI surfaces found places where a check ran against stale state, trusted a weaker signal than intended, or had no bound. Each change here aligns the code with an existing invariant or with a sibling path that already does the stricter thing.

## Summary

- **Sessions:** OAuth authorize, provider linking, and social start resolve the live session (`readLiveAuthSession`) instead of only verifying the cookie signature. Expired or password-revoked cookies count as signed out. A password change clears a pending email change, and verifying an email change no longer re-mints a revoked session.
- **OIDC logout:** `post_logout_redirect_uri` needs a valid `id_token_hint`. A bare `client_id` is no longer enough. Logout with no redirect is unchanged.
- **Tokens:** `cliCredentialBootstrap` called with an org-bound parent token now mints an org-bound child for the parent's org, matching `tokenCreate`. MCP-session bootstraps are unchanged. The `tokenCreate` error text is updated to match.
- **Invite links:** a membership link keeps working only while its creator still has `member:write` (or is an Owner). Team and package links already used this rule, and it matches the "loses access" wording in the organizations guide.
- **Request bodies:** new `readRequestBodyUpTo` streams with a byte cap, used for Open API JSON, webhook, and connect-ticket bodies, so chunked bodies without `Content-Length` can't buffer without limit.
- **Highlight worker:** accepts `/highlight` only on the service-binding origin (shared `highlightServiceOrigin`) and caps snippet count and total characters.
- **Package apps:** cross-origin realtime WebSocket upgrades must send a match

issues.body:
Follow-up from the #4506 audit.

`/connect/webhook-apply` approval (`approveConnectWebhookApply` → `approveWebhookApplyDestination` in `packages/worker/src/webhooks/apply-destination-approval.ts`) writes a `webhook_apply_destination_grants` row for the signed-in org with no permission check. Any org member who opens the approval link can Allow a package webhook's apply destination.

It does not widen a credential's reach: at apply time a `secretName` destination still needs the host in the credential's approved hosts, and an `integration` destination still needs the host in the integration's allowed hosts, and both resolve through `resolveCredential` (Use). So this is not the #4506 credential-Write gap, but it is an unauthenticated-by-permission approval of a package-level grant.

**Decision needed:** which permission gates this approval: `package:write` on the webhook's package, Write on the destination's credential when it has one, or both.

**How to reproduce:** as a team-org member with no package grants, open `/connect/webhook-apply?handle=…&fingerprint=…` for a pending destination of an org package and click Allow; the grant row is written.

issues.body:
Not required now — the logic already exists inside `RLM_DecisionTableManagerController`. This is about making it usable outside a Lightning page: two SOQL queries plus describe walking, ~100 lines.

Output per table: source object, objects its parameters read across, objects its criteria traverse, last sync, freshness verdict.

Build it when one of these bites, not before:
1. **CI / post-build gate** — fail or warn when a table is stale after `prepare_rlm_org` instead of relying on someone opening the Home page. Strongest case.
2. **Debugging without a browser** — makes "was this table stale?" greppable.
3. **Cross-org / cross-release diff** — which tables gained or lost a dependency across a release.
4. **Feeding refresh automation.**

Implementation traps already established, so they need not be rediscovered:
- `DecisionTableParameter.DomainObject` holds the literal four-character **string `'null'`** for a same-object column — `String.isBlank` does NOT catch it. This shipped as a live bug once.
- Criteria field paths are **field names, not relationship names**; resolve each hop through the describe, never by trimming `Id`.
- Every table declares exactly one `DecisionTableDatasetLink` even when `MultipleSobjects` — that is not where the extra objects live.
- Polymorphic lookups resolve to several objects; refuse rather than guess.
- `DecisionTableDataset`/`DecisionTableRecordset` reject aggregates and partial filters, so a table's own row count is unreachable. Only source counts exist.

Open question: whether it shares logic with the Apex or reimplements. Divergence would be its own defect.

issues.body:
**No LWC in this repo is unit-tested.** `jest.config.js` and the `sfdx-lwc-jest` scripts exist; there are zero `*.test.js` files.

That gap became concrete during #317. The `rlmDecisionTableManager` dialog's focus behaviour now has **four interacting rules, three of which were review findings** — and all four are verified only by reading tab order against the template. A regression in any of them is invisible to every gate the repo has.

## The rules a first suite should pin

- initial focus lands on `section[role="dialog"]` (`tabindex="-1"`) so the dialog is announced
- the **leading sentinel sits outside the section** — moved there because, as its first child, it caught forward Tab and bounced to the footer, looping dialog → footer → dialog and skipping all 8 helptexts
- the trailing sentinel (last child, inside) wraps Tab-off-the-end back to the section
- `handleDetailKeydown` handles Shift+Tab from the section as a backstop, plus Escape

## Also worth covering in the same suite

- `detailRow` is a **getter** deriving from `rows`, not a tracked field — a refresh must update the open dialog rather than freezing it
- the `_connected` guards after each of the three awaits (`queueRefresh`, `poll`, `loadTables`), so an async continuation cannot resume against a destroyed component
- `readError` returns a recovery message and must not surface raw serialized error objects

## Scope

Start with this one component; the goal is a working Jest setup plus a suite that would fail on the round-15 sentinel bug, not repo-wide coverage.

Manual in-org keyboard verification is tracked separately in the private context pack — this issue is the automated half, and the two are complementary: the walkthrough proves it once, the suite keeps it proven.

## Summary

Fixes #587. Follows #603 (merged).

In Release 264 the platform chooses between a full and an incremental refresh unless an incremental one is requested (org preference `AutoSelectRefreshDT`, on by default). An incremental refresh moves only `LastIncrementalSyncDate`. The Decision Table Manager and `check_decision_table_freshness` compared the source's newest change against `LastSyncDate` alone, so a table the platform refreshed incrementally kept reading **Stale** right after the refresh. That's what #587 reported for the price book tables.

The behavior was read from Core source (`DecisionTableMediumVolumeBuilderJob`, 264 patch branch) and confirmed live:

- `isDecisionTableIncremental=true` is honored.
- `false` or omitted lets the platform choose: full if the last full refresh is more than 24h old, otherwise incremental below a 20% changed-row threshold.
- `IsIncrementalSyncEnabled` isn't consulted.

These come from the implementation, not a documented contract. The decision-tables skill records them, with GUS references.

- **Freshness verdict:** judged against the later of `LastSyncDate` and `LastIncrementalSyncDate`, the rule the Decision Table app page uses. The reason text says which sync it rests on. The template-spin check deliberately stays on `LastSyncDate`. An incremental applies changes on top of rows that may have been built in another org, so only a full refresh clears it, and the reason now says so.
- **Manager component:** the grid's sync column and the detail-pane stat show the latest sync (new `latestSyncDate` / `latestSyncKind` on the wrapper), with both raw stamps in the helptext. The refresh toggle's off state reads "Platform chooses". The toast no longer claims "Full refresh queued".
- **Refusals removed:** the Manager and `scripts/decision_tables/refresh_decision_table.py` no longer refuse an incremental request on `IsIncrementalSyncEnabled=false`. `--allow-disabled-incremental` stays as a no-op so existing invocations still par

issues.body:
DTs for price book entries show stale, despite being refreshed in 264.

Findings so far
- The platform picks the refresh type. 264 added “smart” auto-selection. It chooses full or incremental based on how many source records changed, and the first refresh after 24 hours is full. The isDecisionTableIncremental flag doesn’t force the type. That matches what we saw: false and omitting it both stamped only LastIncrementalSyncDate.
- The stamps are split. A full refresh updates LastSyncDate and an incremental one updates LastIncrementalSyncDate. The app UI shows the later of the two, and Setup in 264 shows only the full date. The fix to Setup’s display is promised for the release after 264.
- IsIncrementalSyncEnabled is irrelevant. A engineer said it is “not consequential” for this.
- The recommended freshness rule is the later of the two stamps. Our Manager uses only LastSyncDate, which is why it disagrees with the app UI.


Toggling the setting for refresh type override in setup → Decision Tables → Settings, seems to fix the issue

issues.body:
## Symptom

`python scripts/ai/pr_gate.py` fails `skill_manifest` (and `pr_gate_suite`, which runs the gate end to end) when run from a **git worktree** of this repo, if `origin` uses an **SSH host alias** from `~/.ssh/config` (e.g. `git@github.com-<alias>:bgaldino/rlm-base-dev.git`, a common setup for juggling several GitHub accounts):

```
[WARN]  foundations: REJECTED candidate <main checkout> — its git remote (git@github.com-<alias>:bgaldino/rlm-base-dev.git) names a different repo than the declared repo_url. ...
[ERROR] foundations (rlm-base-dev): required clone not found
```

The same command passes in the main checkout. Setting `FOUNDATIONS_REPO_ROOT=<worktree>` works around it. CI is unaffected (HTTPS remote).

## Cause

Two conditions together, both in `scripts/ai/skill_manifest.py`:

1. **The worktree isn't recognized as self.** The `foundations` hint `../rlm-base-dev` resolves to the manifest's own repo only when the checkout has that directory name. That case is accepted as `verified-self` (`_identity_of`, ~L389) with no remote comparison. From a worktree, `manifest_root` is the worktree, so the same hint points at the *main checkout* and falls through to the remote comparison.
2. **An SSH host alias compares as a provable mismatch.** `_normalize_repo_url` (~L297) takes the scp-style host literally (`github.com-<alias>`). `_urls_equivalent` then returns `False` against `https://github.com/bgaldino/rlm-base-dev`, so the clone is **rejected** rather than treated as unverifiable (`None`), even though `owner/repo` is identical and `ssh -G <alias>` resolves the host to `github.com`.

## Possible fix (decide in the PR)

- When it has a `.cursor/skills` surface, accept the manifest's own repo root as the foundations clone even when no hint names it. This covers worktrees and clones with other directory names.

## Context
`.github/workflows/prepare-rlm-org.yml` pins the runner to **`node-version: "24.16.0"`** (added in #257, squash `d819b721`).

This is a hold-the-line workaround for a **Node 24 minor regression**, not a permanent choice:
- `node-version: "24"` floats to "latest 24.x". The runner moved **24.16.0 → 24.17.0**.
- On **24.17.0**, the npm-installed sf CLI exits 13 on `sf org login` (`Detected unsettled top-level await … await cli.run()` in the CLI entrypoint). `sf --version` still works, so setup steps pass and it only fails at Authenticate Dev Hub.

## Bug

On the Billing Settings page (`/lightning/setup/BillingSettings/home`), enabling the **Configure Email Delivery Settings** toggle does not automatically populate the **Select Default Email Template** field. The field only populates when the toggle is cycled — turned off and then back on again.

## Current behaviour

`prepare_billing` step 10 (`deploy_billing_template_settings`) re-enables the Invoice Email/PDF toggles to trigger default template auto-creation. However it does not cycle the **Configure Email Delivery Settings** toggle, so the default email template (`Default Invoice Email Template`) is never set in the UI after a fresh org build.

`deploy_billing_template_id_settings` is marked *NOT USED IN FLOW* and explicitly sets `defaultEmailTemplate` by ID — but it is not wired into the flow, so this gap is currently unaddressed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `prepare_billing` on a fresh org with `billing=true`
2. Navigate to `/lightning/setup/BillingSettings/home`
3. Observe **Configure Email Delivery Settings** is enabled but **Select Default Email Template** is empty
4. Manually toggle **Configure Email Delivery Settings** off, then back on
5. Observe **Select Default Email Template** now populates with `Default Invoice Email Template`

## Expected behaviour

After `prepare_billing`, the **Select Default Email Template** field should be pre-populated — no manual toggle cycle should be required.

## Proposed fix

A robot task (following the pattern in `configure_core_pricing_setup.robot` and `configure_product_discovery_settings.robot`) that:
1. Enables **Configure Email Delivery Settings** if off
2. Waits for the page to settle
3. Cycles the toggle (off → on) to trigger default template auto-population
4. Verifies **Select Default Email Template** is populated after the cycle

Wire the new task into `prepare_billing` between steps 10 and 11 (after `deploy_billing_template_settings`, before `deploy_post_billing_ui`), gated on `billing=true`.

### Product Description
no change

### Technical Description
Adds a CI check that fails a PR until every PR listed in its new "Prerequisite PRs" section is in a `v*` release tag. Authors list merged PRs whose manual steps (for example a data migration command) must run on a deployment before this PR can ship.

- `scripts/check_prerequisite_releases.py` reads the section from the PR description, fetched through the API so a re-run sees edits. For each listed PR it gets the merge commit and runs `git tag --list 'v*' --contains <sha>`. Pre-release tags count; `w_v*` widget tags don't. A line it cannot read (anything other than one `#1234` per line, or "None") fails the check, so a typo cannot let a PR through.
- `.github/workflows/pr_prerequisites.yml` runs on PR opened, reopened, pushed and **edited**, the last so that changing the list re-runs the check. Like `pr_risk_label.yml`, it takes the script from the default branch, with a sparse checkout and full history.
- On a `v*` tag push, a second job re-runs the check on every open PR whose latest run finished without passing, so PRs waiting on that release turn green without a new push.

Decisions and known limits for the reviewer:
- GitHub cannot re-run a workflow run older than 30 days. With a roughly monthly release cadence, a PR that failed early in a cycle and was not touched since may stay red after the release, and needs a push or an edit. Fixing this would mean having the tag-push job post the check result itself.
- The workflow YAML still runs from the PR (as with `pr_risk_label.yml`), so a PR could edit it to skip the check. Real protection needs a CODEOWNERS rule on `.github/workflows/` or `pull_request_target`.
- This PR's own run of the check will fail, because the script is not on the default branch yet. That is expected; it is not a required check yet.
- Not tested on GitHub yet: re-running a fork PR's run from the tag-push job.

After merge: add **`Prerequisite PRs released`** as a required status chec

issues.body:
Add a check that blocks a PR from merging until every PR it depends on has shipped in a tagged release.

## What needs to be done

### PR template
Add a "Prerequisite PRs" section to `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Authors list the merged PRs whose manual steps (for example, a data migration command) must run on a deployment before this PR can ship, one per line as `- #1234`. If there are none, the author can delete the section, leave it empty, or write "None".

### Check script
Add `scripts/check_prerequisite_releases.py`, with tests in `scripts/test_check_prerequisite_releases.py`. The script:
- reads the "Prerequisite PRs" section from the PR body; a missing section, an empty one, or one that says "None" means there are no prerequisites
- for each PR listed, gets its merge commit and checks whether any `v*` release tag contains it, pre-release tags such as `v1.0.0-rc1` included (widget `w_v*` tags are ignored)
- fails and names each prerequisite that is not merged or not yet in a release

### Workflow
Add `.github/workflows/pr_prerequisites.yml`. It runs when a PR is opened, reopened or pushed to. Like `pr_risk_label.yml`, it takes the script from the default branch, so a PR cannot change the check it is judged by.

When a `v*` release tag is pushed, the check is re-run on every open PR, so PRs waiting on that release turn green without anyone touching them.

### Repo settings
Mark the new check as a required status check in branch protection for `main`.

### Product Description
After `sync_team`, the target team now has the source team's moderation providers, its selected provider, the moderation and auto-block switches, and its creator. Before, the target team always arrived with moderation off and `created_by` empty. Changes to these settings on the source reach the target when the sync runs again or with `--follow`.

### Technical Description
The team row is imported first, before any other row, so its foreign keys to rows imported later (`created_by`, `moderation_provider`) could not be translated and were left out.

- **Partial manifest entries.** `ManifestEntry` gets an optional `fields` tuple. A partial entry serves only `id`, `updated_at` and those fields, and the importer applies each row as an update to a row that was already imported. It never creates rows. A source on older code serves no `fields` key, and the client treats a missing key as a full entry.
- **`team_settings` entry.** `TEAM_SETTINGS_FIELDS` are excluded from the `team/` endpoint and served by `ManifestEntry("teams.team", "team_settings", "updated_at_id", fields=...)`, placed after `users` and `moderation_providers`. The `updated_at_id` cursor lets later passes pick up changes to the team.
- **Checkpoint.** A partial row's `updated_at` is stored under its own key (`teams.team[<fields>]`). The full team row is stored with the same timestamp, so without a separate key the partial row would be skipped. If a foreign key can't be translated yet, it is set to null and no timestamp is stored, so a later read applies the row again.
- **`ModerationProvider`** is synced as a secret entry with `config` sealed, like the other provider types.
- **Separate fix:** deleting a moderation provider changed the team through `QuerySet.update()` and `SET_NULL`, and neither moves `team.updated_at`. The pre-delete signal now sets `updated_at` on every team using the provider, so the sync sees the change.

- The sync still stores cursors an

**Depends on:** #4702 (task 5), #4703 (task 6)

**Problem**

The `sync_team` command does not copy a team's moderation setup to the target server:
- `ModerationProvider` is in `IGNORED_MODELS`, so no providers are synced.
- `moderation_enabled`, `moderation_provider` and `auto_block_enabled` are in `EXCLUDE_REGISTRY["teams.team"]`, so after a migration the target team has moderation turned off.

They are excluded because the sync imports the team row first, before any other row, since every other row is assigned to it (`load_team`). `moderation_provider` points at a `ModerationProvider` row that hasn't been imported yet at that point, so the importer can't translate it.

`Team.created_by` has the same problem. It points at a user, and users are imported after the team, so the importer sets `created_by` to null on every synced team today.

A second gap: `load_team` reads the team from the source only on the first run. With `--follow`, or on a later run, changes to the team's own fields never reach the target.

**Proposed solution**

Support partial manifest entries, then add one that serves the team fields which point at rows imported later.

- `ManifestEntry` gets an optional `fields` tuple. A partial entry serves only those fields plus `id` and `updated_at`. The importer then updates rows that an earlier step already imported; it never creates rows.
- A new `TEAM_SETTINGS_FIELDS` list: `created_by`, `moderation_provider`, `moderation_enabled`, `auto_block_enabled`. These fields are left out of the `team/` endpoint and served by a new `team_settings` resource, `ManifestEntry("teams.team", "team_settings", "updated_at_id", fields=TEAM_SETTINGS_FIELDS)`. That entry goes after `users` and `moderation_providers`, so both foreign keys can be translated. Because it uses an `updated_at_id` cursor, later passes pick

### Product Description

The bug - For Anthropic LLM Nodes, citation markers in the reply were always removed, so **no citation references were shown.**

Chatbots that use an **Anthropic model with citations enabled** now show footnote references and a reference list for the collection files they cite, **as GPT-backed bots already do.** 

### Technical Description

#### Root cause of bug
- [Anthropic's web search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#citations) returns its sources as `citations` on the response's text blocks. The Anthropic parser adds them to the text as `[title](url)` links. They are links, not files, so they never appear in `cited_files`

#### The Fix
Resolves: #4821 
- `parse_output_for_anthropic` is now a wrapper around the existing recursive logic (renamed `_parse_content`). It resolves markers once on the fully assembled text, so a marker split across content blocks still resolves, and it runs a single query per reply.

- The lookup respects `include_citations` and is scoped to the team, as in `_default_parser`.

#### The Tests
- Tests in `test_output_parsing.py` cover the marker-to-footnote result, string/single/multiple/split-block content, repeated and multiple markers, parity with `_default_parser`, and guards (other team's file, unknown id, `include_citations=False`).
- `citations.md` gains a "Collecting Cite

issues.body:
## Summary

On a pipeline bot whose LLM provider is Anthropic, `generate_citations: true` can never produce a reference. Every citation is deleted as a hallucination, so `cited_files` is always empty.

## Mechanism

`apps/service_providers/llm_service/main.py`, `AnthropicLlmService.get_output_parser` returns `parse_output_for_anthropic` (`apps/service_providers/llm_service/parsers.py`).

That parser handles Anthropic's native URL citations and returns `LlmChatResponse(text=...)` on every path. It never calls `extract_file_ids_from_ocs_citations`; only `LlmService._default_parser` does. So `LlmChatResponse.cited_files` stays at its default, an empty set.

`populate_reference_section_from_citations` then builds `files` from `cited_files` and removes any `<CIT n />` whose id is not in it:

```python
if file_id not in files:
    # LLM hallucinated a file id. We don't want to show this to users, so remove the citation.
    return ""
```

So on an Anthropic bot even a perfectly formatted `<CIT 63004 />` is removed and no reference section is ever built.

## Repro

- A pipeline bot with LLM `type: anthropic`, model `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `generate_citations: true`, and a collection attached.
- On a 64-prompt suite, `metadata.cited_files` was `[]` on all 64 responses. The same suite showed the model emitting citation markers.

## Suggested fix

Call `extract_file_ids_from_ocs_citations` on the assembled text in `parse_output_for_anthropic`, as `_default_parser` does, and merge the result into `cited_files`.

Related: a separate issue covers off-spec citation spellings leaking file ids.

Re-verified against `main` on 2026-10-16: `parsers.py` still has no extraction call. Reported from Dimagi's ACE agent (internal tracker dimagi-internal/ace#2018).

### Product Description
With auto-block on, each flagged message gives the participant a strike. On the third strike the participant is blocked from all of the team's chatbots, and the team is notified. Team members chatting in the app never get strikes. The participant page shows the strike count, and unblocking resets it to 0.

### Technical Description
- `Participant.strikes` is a `PositiveIntegerField(default=0, db_default=0)`.
- `add_strike` is in `apps/moderation/services.py`:
  - It runs in one `transaction.atomic()`: an `F("strikes") + 1` update, a read-back under the row lock, and at `STRIKE_LIMIT` (3) a `get_or_create` of the `DeniedParticipant`. A failed block therefore rolls back the strike.
  - The notification is sent `on_commit`, and only when the denylist row was created. Its identity includes the denylist row id, so a participant blocked a second time triggers a new notification.
  - It does nothing when auto-block is off or the participant is exempt. `is_exempt` makes one membership query on `participant.user_id`.
- The stage gives the strike straight after recording the flagged result, in its own `try`, so a failure while replacing the reply can't lose the strike.
- `unblock_participant` (in `apps/moderation/enforcement.py`) deletes the denylist row with one audited queryset delete and resets strikes even when no row existed.
- `strikes` is left out of the team data export, because the denylist isn't exported either.
- A test increments strikes from two threads at once and checks both count. It is a transactional test. Under `-n 8` it sometimes errors during database setup with a content-type duplicate key; `test_chatbot_archive` already hits the same race on main. It passes when run on its own or with 2 workers.

### Product Description
Notices that originate outside a chatbot's own activity no longer involve archived chatbots: a custom action health-check failure only alerts when a chatbot that is not archived still uses the action, and the deprecated and removed model notices no longer list an archived chatbot's pipeline. Notifications raised by a bot's own activity (trace errors, delivery failures, custom action calls) are unchanged.

### Technical Description
The issue's audit was mostly right about what is already excluded. Two gaps remained:

* `apps/custom_actions/tasks.py`: the periodic scheduler now only checks actions a non-archived chatbot can call (`CustomAction.in_use_filter()`: a non-archived node on a non-archived chatbot, and for a working node only an operation the action still allows). The single-action task still runs when called from the create view or the check-health button, records the status, and alerts the team only on a DOWN transition for an action in use. A DOWN recorded by such a direct check on an unused action does not re-alert when a chatbot later adopts the action; the user saw that status when they ran the check.
* `apps/data_migrations/management/commands/base.py`: `Experiment.archive()` leaves the working pipeline unarchived, so `get_affected_teams_data` reported that pipeline as a standalone pipeline. A pipeline any chatbot owns, archived or not, is now never reported on its own.

The widget version notices and HTTP sunset notices were verified to read only live channels or working versions, so they need no change. Notifications already stored about a bot that is archived later are left as they are.

issues.body:
## Problem

Notifications can name, link to and be triggered by **archived chatbots**. Most notification paths take a bot (or a team-level object) and never check `is_archived`, so an archived bot, or the traffic still reaching one of its versions, can still produce alerts to the team. The notifications should be suppressed for archived bots, or at least not be raised on their behalf.

**I could not tell which notification prompted this.** I audited the code instead (read from `main` on 2026-11-03; nothing was run). If you remember the notification (type, text, bot), add it here so the repro can be confirmed; the audit below is where an archived bot could and could not get through.

## What archiving does today (context)

`Experiment.archive()` on a working version archives all its versions, soft-deletes its channels (`channel.soft_delete()`), hard-deletes its scheduled messages, and archives its triggers. It does not stop in-flight work, and it leaves sessions, traces and custom actions in place. `Experiment.objects` hides archived rows; `get_all()` reaches them.

## Audit

**Already excluded (verified in code):**
- `notify_deprecated_widget_versions`, `notify_widget_version_release`, and `ratchet_widget_auth_levels` only look at channels with `deleted=False`, and archiving soft-deletes the channels.
- HTTP sunset notices (`apps/experiments/sunsets.py`) select from `Experiment.objects.working_versions_queryset()`, which hides archived bots.
- Deprecated and removed model notices (`get_affected_teams_data`): archived chatbots and nodes are hidden by their managers, and #4850 (merged) stopped it listing non-working or archived pipelines.

**No archived-bot check (the gap):**
| Notification | Raised from | Check present |
|---|---|---|
| `trace_error_notification` | `OCSTracer._fire_error_notification_if_needed` | only `not self.experiment.is_working_version` |
| `audio_synthesis_failure_notification`, `audio_transcription_failure_notification` | `apps/channels/stages

issues.body:
## Goal

Remove low-value tests from the rest of the suite, a few files per PR. These are mostly tests written by agents to verify their own changes rather than to protect behaviour: they restate the implementation, assert nothing that could fail for a real reason, or duplicate a test that already exists.

PR #4587 did the first batch (51 tests, 663 lines) and is the worked example — read its description for the reasoning before starting a task.

Each task names 1-3 test files. That is deliberately small: the removals are judgement calls, and a PR touching a few files can be checked line by line.

## Context

### The test that a test has to fail

**Remove a test if deleting it cannot make a real bug pass.** That is the whole criterion. The categories below are what it looks like in this codebase:

**Mock-delegation change detectors.** Everything is mocked, and the only assertion restates the body of the method under test. The clearest case was `apps/ocs_notifications/tests/test_notifications.py`, where nine tests each mocked `create_notification` and asserted the exact kwargs dict the thin wrapper passes it. Same shape wherever a sender or client method forwards its arguments to a service:

```python
def test_send_text(self):
    service = MagicMock()
    sender = FacebookMessengerSender(service=service, page_id=PAGE_ID)
    sender.bind(_bound_context())
    sender.send_text("hi", recipient=RECIPIENT)
    service.send_text_message.assert_called_once_with(message="hi", from_=PAGE_ID, ...)
```

**Tautological.** Asserting a no-op does nothing; `isinstance` checks on a one-line factory that constructs exactly that class; pydantic or dataclass tests asserting the constructor stores what you passed it; asserting a class attribute equals its declared value.

**Duplicates and strict subsets.** Two tests with identical bodies and different names, or one test whose setup and assertions are wholly contained in another. `test_task_legacy_payload_falls_back_to_routing` was byte

agent_prs.body:
### Product Description
With the flag on and moderation turned on in Team settings, every participant message is checked by the team's OpenAI moderation provider while the bot writes its reply:
- **Strike category flagged** (`sexual/minors`, `illicit`, `illicit/violent`, `harassment/threatening`, `hate/threatening`): the bot's reply is replaced with a short message, in the conversation's language, saying the message was flagged. The flagged message is left out of the LLM history on later turns.
- **Other categories**: recorded, and the reply is sent as normal.
- **No result** (rate limit, error, or nothing within 30 s): the reply is sent, the message is recorded as not moderated, and the team is notified.

Team members are moderated too.

### Technical Description
- `moderate_message(chat_message_id, moderation_provider_id)` runs on `Queues.BACKGROUND`, so in production it does not compete for the chat worker's threads with the chat tasks that wait for it (see Follow-up):
  - It retries on connection and 5xx errors (2 retries, 1 s and 2 s backoff, 2 s request timeout), so it finishes within the 30 s wait.
  - It returns `skipped` straight away on a 429. The SDK's own retries are turned off.
  - It writes nothing to the database. It takes the message id rather than the text, so participant text doesn't appear in Celery error reports.
- `AbuseRulesStage` starts the task. `ModerationResultStage`, the first terminal stage, waits with `AsyncResult.get(timeout=30, disable_sync_subtasks=False)`.
  - It still runs after an early exit in a core stage.
  - Any exception inside it is logged and the normal reply is sent.
- `record_moderation_result` is the only writer of `moderation_status` and `moderation_detail`, and keeps rule hits.
- Replacing the reply:
  - The stored AI message is overwritten with the fallback text first, so the EventBot that writes the replacement never sees the discarded answer.
  - The replacement goes out on the normal response path. Web and API calle

### Product Description
With the abuse detection flag on, Team settings has a new **Moderation** section:
- Team admins pick a moderation provider, turn moderation on, and turn auto-block on. They can add or edit a provider in a dialog without leaving the page.
- If the selected provider was deleted, a banner explains that moderation was turned off.

- The section lives in `apps/moderation` (form, views, URLs, templates). It registers itself with team settings through a new `register_settings_section` hook in `apps/teams/settings_sections.py`. That keeps `apps/teams` (foundation tier) from importing `apps/moderation`.

issues.body:
## Problem

When the bot sends a file, the chat widget shows only the file name and a paperclip icon. The name is not a link, so the user cannot download the file.

## Cause

- The widget renders the attachment name as plain text (`components/chat_widget/src/components/ocs-chat/ocs-chat.tsx`, ~line 2432).
- The API's `content_url` for attachments points to `/api/files/<pk>/content`. That endpoint requires an API key or a team member's login, so an anonymous widget user can't use it.

## Expected

The file name is a link that downloads the file. The link only works for files in the user's own session.
