issues.body:
## Anlass

Miete und Leasing beweglicher Wirtschaftsgüter werden der Gewerbesteuer zu einem Fünftel hinzugerechnet. Für bestimmte Fahrzeuge gilt nur die Hälfte davon (§ 8 Nr. 1 Buchst. d Satz 2 GewStG):

- reine Elektrofahrzeuge,
- extern aufladbare Hybride mit höchstens 50 g CO₂/km oder mindestens 80 km elektrischer Reichweite,
- Fahrräder, die keine Kraftfahrzeuge sind.

Das gilt für Verträge, die nach dem 31.12.2019 geschlossen wurden, und letztmals für den Erhebungszeitraum 2030. Bei Verträgen vor 2025 reichen 60 km Reichweite (§ 36 Abs. 4 GewStG). DATEV hat dafür eigene Konten: SKR03 4575 und SKR04 6565, „Mietleasingaufwendungen für Elektrofahrzeuge und Fahrräder, die gewerbesteuerlich hinzuzurechnen sind“ (DATEV-Kontenrahmen 2026). Haben kennt diese Konten, rechnet sie aber wie normales Leasing zu 20 %.

Beispiel mit erfundenen Beträgen: Eine GmbH least seit 2024 ein Elektroauto für 9.600 € im Jahr und bucht die Raten auf 4575. Haben setzt 1.920 € als Finanzierungsanteil an statt 960 €. Die Steuer ändert sich erst, wenn alle Finanzierungsanteile zusammen den Freibetrag von 200.000 € übersteigen. Das ist bei kleinen GmbH selten, die Erklärung soll aber trotzdem stimmen.

## Stand in Haben

Geprüft auf `main` @ [`fc76efc6`](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/commit/fc76efc609f86e44e490dad181765e15873a2782):

- [`HINZURECHNUNG`](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/fc76efc609f86e44e490dad181765e15873a2782/packages/core/src/koerperschaft.ts#L68-L87) zählt 4575 und 6565 zusammen mit den übrigen Konten der Gruppe „beweglich“ zu 20 %, in jedem Jahr.
- Keine Ausgabenkategorie bucht auf 4575 oder 6565; „Kfz: Leasing“ bucht auf 4570 und 6560 ([`posting.ts#L183`](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/fc76efc609f86e44e490dad181765e15873a2782/packages/core/src/posting.ts#L183)). Auf diese Konten kommen Beträge heute nur über manuelle Buchungen und Importe.
- Die Gewerbesteuererklärung übermittelt die Summe der Gruppe „beweglich“ in voller Höhe als ein Feld `E4003502`

agent_prs.title: Doku: ELSTER auf arm64 lohnt sich erst mit Hersteller-ID (#1320)

issues.body:
## Anlass

[„ELSTER auf arm64“](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/cb5d9241/docs/installation-anbindungen.md#L35-L63) beschreibt, wie Haben den ERiC-Worker auf arm64 unter QEMU startet: QEMU besorgen, rund 730 MB Laufzeit anlegen, Mount und Variable eintragen, nach jedem Update wiederholen. Dass das erst etwas bringt, wenn eine eigene Hersteller-ID da ist, steht dort nicht, nur auf einer anderen Seite. Wer ohne ID einrichtet, hat danach dieselbe simulierte Prüfung wie vorher.

## Stand in Haben

Geprüft auf `main` (cb5d9241).

- ERiC verlangt die Hersteller-ID seit Version 43 schon fürs Prüfen; ohne sie laufen Prüfen und Senden simuliert ([Einrichtung ELSTER](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/cb5d9241/docs/einrichtung-elster.md#L16-L19)). Die ID gibt es nach Registrierung im ELSTER-Entwicklerbereich, „Tage bis Wochen“.
- Zum Senden braucht es zusätzlich die Zertifikatsdatei, die jede Übermittlung unterschreibt ([ebenda](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/cb5d9241/docs/einrichtung-elster.md#L17)).
- Der Abschnitt zu arm64 verweist darauf nicht; er beginnt mit der Begründung, warum emuliert wird ([L37](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/cb5d9241/docs/installation-anbindungen.md#L37)).

## Vorschlag

Am Anfang von „ELSTER auf arm64“ ein Satz: Die Laufzeit lohnt sich erst mit eigener Hersteller-ID (Link auf [Einrichtung ELSTER](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/cb5d9241/docs/einrichtung-elster.md)), zum Senden braucht es dazu die Zertifikatsdatei; bis dahin prüft und sendet Haben simuliert, auch ohne QEMU.

## Akzeptanzkriterien

- Der Abschnitt nennt die Voraussetzung vor Schritt 1, mit Link auf die Einrichtung.
- Doku-Build mit `--strict` grün.

---

## Was sich ändert

- **„Kfz: Leasing“** (SKR03 4570, SKR04 6560) wechselt von „Aufwendungen für den Fuhrpark“ (`otherCost.vehicles`) zu „Leasing für bewegliche Wirtschaftsgüter, übrige“ (`otherCost.leasingAll.moveable.other`). agent_prs.title: E-Bilanz: Kfz-Leasing beim Leasing, Konten der Hinzurechnung auf ihren Positionen (#1327)

issues.body:
## Anlass

In der Maintainer-Prüfung von #1311 kam heraus: In der E-Bilanz stehen SKR03 4575 und SKR04 6565 („Mietleasingaufwendungen für Elektrofahrzeuge und Fahrräder, die gewerbesteuerlich hinzuzurechnen sind“) in der Auffangposition „nicht zuordenbar“. 4570 und 6560 (Kategorie „Kfz: Leasing“) stehen bei „Aufwendungen für den Fuhrpark“. Laut HGB-Taxonomie ist beides falsch, und weitere Konten der Gewerbesteuer-Hinzurechnung landen ebenso in Auffangpositionen.

Beispiel mit erfundenen Beträgen: Eine GmbH least einen Verbrenner für 3.600 € im Jahr über „Kfz: Leasing“ (6560) und ein E-Auto für 4.800 € auf 6565. Haben übermittelt 3.600 € unter „Aufwendungen für den Fuhrpark“ und 4.800 € unter „sonstige betriebliche Aufwendungen, nicht zuordenbar“. Das Mussfeld „Leasing für bewegliche Wirtschaftsgüter“ bleibt leer. Die Übermittlung klappt trotzdem.

Die Taxonomie sagt es in ihren Erläuterungen (label-guidance-de, gleich in 6.9 und 6.10) ausdrücklich:
- „Aufwendungen für den Fuhrpark“ (`otherCost.vehicles`): „ohne Abschreibungen, Zinsen und Leasingkosten“.
- „Leasing für bewegliche Wirtschaftsgüter“ (`otherCost.leasingAll.moveable`): „Inkl. Aufwendungen für Kfz-Leasing“.

Auffangpositionen sind nur dafür da, dass sich eine Unterscheidung „nicht aus der Buchführung ableiten“ lässt (BMF-Schreiben vom 28.09.2011, Rz. 19); Mussfelder sind sonst zu befüllen (Rz. 16). Ein eigenes Konto für Leasing ist so eine Unterscheidung.

## Stand in Haben

Geprüft auf `main` @ [`6066c773`](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/commit/6066c773c60694a3cfa6209030107322d68b0fc0), also mit #1311. Feste Positionen hat nur, was in [`EBILANZ_KONTEN`](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/6066c773c60694a3cfa6209030107322d68b0fc0/packages/core/src/ebilanz.ts#L336-L339) steht; alle anderen Aufwandskonten gehen nach [`ebilanzPosition`](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/6066c773c60694a3cfa6209030107322d68b0fc0/packages/core/src/ebilanz.ts#L364-L369) in [`otherCost.misc`](https://github.com/firs

agent_prs.body:
Stufe 2 aus #504: das Firmenportal über den Instanzen der eigenen Firmen. Wer sich dort per SSO anmeldet, sieht die Firmen, in deren Inhaber-Gruppe er beim Anmeldedienst ist, und wechselt mit einem Klick dorthin. In Haben steht mit `HABEN_FIRMENPORTAL_URL` statt „Firma wechseln“ die Zeile „Zum Firmenportal“. Eine neue Firma steht damit nur noch im Firmenportal, nicht in der `.env` jeder Instanz, und ob jemand sie sieht, entscheiden die Gruppen.

## Was sich ändert

- **`apps/firmenportal`** (neu, Image `tristanteu/haben-firmenportal`): Bun-Server ohne Datenbank, der HTML auf dem Server rendert, ohne Skript.
  - **Anmeldung mit `openid-client`** 6.8.8 (von der OpenID Foundation zertifiziert, vom Autor von `jose`, MIT): Authorization Code mit PKCE (S256), `state`, `nonce`, `client_secret_basic`, ID-Token nach OpenID Connect Core 1.0, 3.1.3.7 samt Signatur gegen die JWKS (`enableNonRepudiationChecks`; ohne prüft die Bibliothek die Signatur nach 3.1.3.7, Schritt 6 nicht), UserInfo mit demselben Subject (5.3.2).
  - **Darüber hinaus wie in Haben (`apps/web/src/server/oidc.ts`):** exakter Issuer, mindestens eine Signatur aus RS256, PS256, ES256 oder EdDSA, Endpunkte nur über HTTPS (http nur für localhost außerhalb von `NODE_ENV=production`), Gruppen wörtlich aus genau einem Claim, zuerst aus UserInfo, sonst aus dem ID-Token.
  - **Sitzung:** zustandslos in Cookies (`__Host-`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`), mit `PORTAL_SECRET` per HMAC signiert. Der Ablauf gilt 10 Minuten, die Sitzung 15 Minuten wie eine Berechtigung in Haben. Die Sitzung trägt das Subject, die Anzeige für „Angemeldet als“, die Stellen der Firmen in der Liste und deren Fingerabdruck; ändert sich `PORTAL_FIRMEN`, gilt sie nicht mehr.
  - **Ablauf ohne Zwischenklicks:**
    - Ohne Sitzung leitet `/` gleich zum Anmeldedienst, ohne eigene Seite davor.
    - Die Firmen verlinken auf `/login?anmelden=sso` ihrer Instanz; Haben startet dort die SSO-Anmeldung selbst (siehe unten).

## Anlass

Eine Person führt drei kleine Firmen und betreibt dafür drei Instanzen von Haben nebeneinander. Für jede Firma legt sie von Hand ein Verzeichnis, eine `.env` mit eigenen Schlüsseln und den Eintrag im Proxy an. Bei jedem Update wiederholt sie das dreimal, und ob die Sicherung der zweiten Firma letzte Nacht gelaufen ist, sieht sie erst nach der Anmeldung dort.

Der ursprüngliche Wunsch war Mandantenfähigkeit: mehrere Firmen in einer Instanz. Warum der Vorschlag davon abweicht, steht unter „Vorschlag“.

## Was sich ändert

Refs #955

Neue Doku-Seite [Compose-Generator](https://haben.app/compose-generator.html) unter *Betrieb*: Sie erzeugt im Browser die `.env` für [Docker Compose](https://haben.app/installation.html#docker-compose), bei Bedarf `compose.override.yml` und die Befehle für den ersten Start. Passwörter und Schlüssel entstehen per `crypto.getRandomValues` in derselben Stärke wie `openssl rand -hex 24` und `-base64 32`; nichts verlässt den Browser.

- **Keine `compose.yml`:** Sie kommt unverändert aus `deploy/compose.yml` (der `curl`-Befehl steht in den Startbefehlen) und lässt sich bei jedem Update neu laden. Was vom Standard abweicht, steht im Override wie in `deploy/compose.override.example.yml`: eigener Reverse Proxy im Docker-Netz oder auf dem Host, Registry (Docker Hub oder GHCR) und Tag für `db`, `app`, `backup` und `restore`, der Mount für ELSTER auf arm64 und `extra_hosts` für Ollama auf dem Server.
- **Keine fremden Geheimnisse:** Schlüssel von Anthropic, eines OpenAI-kompatiblen Dienstes, S3 und das OIDC-Clientsecret fragt die Seite nicht ab; in der `.env` steht dafür `hier-eintragen`. agent_prs.body:
Refs #750.

Fachlicher Entwurf (ADR mit Status „Vorschlag“) für die erfolgsneutrale Behandlung erhaltener Anzahlungen bei GmbH und UG. Er unterscheidet Leistungsrealisierung und Umsatzsteuerzeitpunkt, enthält Dezember-/Januar- und Teilzahlungsfälle sowie eine Testmatrix für unbezahlte Anforderungen, erbrachte Teilleistungen, vollständige Vorauszahlung, Schlussrechnung und Korrekturen.

Der Entwurf hält die noch zu treffenden Entscheidungen fest: OPOS-/Journalbehandlung unbezahlter Anforderungen, Konten und Ausweis sowie Realisierung und Übergang bei unverändert gesperrtem Altbestand. Für den Ausweis nennt er das Wahlrecht nach § 268 Abs. 5 Satz 2 HGB (Verbindlichkeiten oder offen von den Vorräten abgesetzt) und die infrage kommenden Konten aus den DATEV-Kontenrahmen 2026 mit Fundstelle (SKR03 1710, 1711, 1718, 1722; SKR04 3250, 3260, 3272, 1190). Die Klassifikation und Steuerlogik aus #745 sollen wiederverwendet werden; dieser noch offene PR ist als Voraussetzung gekennzeichnet. Die Architekturseite verweist unter „Entwurfsentscheidungen“ auf den Entwurf.

Nur Dokumentation: Der PR stellt keine Buchungslogik um und erledigt #750 deshalb nicht.

Bei der Selbstprüfung von PR #745 zu #622 fiel ein eigener Bilanzierungsbedarf auf: Eine Anzahlung vor Leistung wird im Journal bereits beim Festschreiben der Abschlagsrechnung auf Erlöse gebucht. Der Umsatzsteuerfix ändert diesen bestehenden Netto-Buchungsweg nicht.

Die Umsatzsteuer aus der Zahlung entsteht bereits im Dezember. Die Trennung folgt aus § 252 Abs. 1 Nr. 4/5 HGB, § 266 Abs. 3 C.3 HGB und § 13 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 a UStG.

Eigenständiger Folgeschritt für die von Haben unterstützten GmbH-/UG-Abschlüsse. Die Klassifikation aus #745 wiederverwenden; keine zweite Anzahlungskennzeichnung und kein zweiter Umsatzsteuerrechenw

issues.body:
**Symptom**

`e2e-teil (4)` wird an Wochenenden rot, unabhängig vom Branch:

```
✘ 111 [rechnungen] › e2e/rechnungen.spec.ts:2041:1 › Lastschriftdatei: fällige Rechnung wählen, pain.008 herunterladen, danach nicht mehr angeboten (#445)
Error: expect(locator).toContainText(expected) failed
Expected substring: "AB-2026-01"
Received string: "Fällige Rechnungen … Betrag 30.11.2026 Alpenblick Media AG Rechnung 2026-007 Erst ab 16.11.2026 einzureichen, 14 Tage vor Fälligkeit 297,50 € …"
> 2056 |   await expect(form).toContainText("AB-2026-01");
```

Lauf `43526673044` auf `7891776ce2` (14.11.2026, 00:23 CET): 1 failed, 111 passed.

**Ursache**

Der Test davor legt seine Rechnung ohne Rechnungsdatum an (`e2e/rechnungen.spec.ts:2014`, Standard = heute) mit dem Standard-Zahlungsziel von 14 Tagen. `invoiceDueDate` (`packages/core/src/holidays.ts`) schiebt die Fälligkeit auf den nächsten Werktag, und die Lastschriftliste gibt eine Zeile erst ab Fälligkeit − 14 Tage frei.

Damit hängt der Test an einer Annahme über den Wochentag: Fällt der 14. Tag nach dem Rechnungsdatum auf einen Samstag, Sonntag oder Feiertag, wandert die Fälligkeit nach vorn, das Freigabefenster liegt in der Zukunft, die Zeile ist gesperrt und die Zusicherung auf den Mandatstext schlägt fehl.

| Rechnungsdatum | Fälligkeit | frei ab | Ergebnis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fr 13.11.2026 | Fr 27.11.2026 | 13.11. | grün |
| Sa 14.11.2026 | Mo 30.11.2026 | 16.11. | **rot** |
| So 15.11.2026 | Mo 30.11.2026 | 16.11. | **rot** |
| Mo 16.11.2026 | Mo 30.11.2026 | 16.11. | grün |

Betroffen ist jeder Lauf an Samstagen und Sonntagen (und an jedem Tag, an dem der 14. Tag ein Feiertag ist) — auch `main`, nicht nur ein einzelner Beitrag. Auf `main` (`f7fea04e`) waren die Läufe am 13.11. grün, weil sie auf einen Freitag fielen.

**Vorschlag**

In `e2e/rechnungen.spec.ts:2014` ein festes Rechnungsdatum setzen, wie es die Datei an anderen Stellen schon tut:

```ts
await page.getByLabel("Rechnungsdatum").fill(day(-3));
```

Unter **Beträge je Steuersatz** am Beleg hat jede Zeile ein Feld **Brutto**. Steht auf einer Kleinbetragsrechnung nur der Endbetrag, rechnet Haben daraus Netto und Vorsteuer vor.

- Brutto eingeben: Aufteilung in Entgelt und Steuer nach § 35 Abs. 1 i. V. m. § 33 UStDV (Kleinbetragsrechnung bis 250 €), mit `taxIncluded` aus `@haben/core`, kaufmännisch gerundet; Netto plus Vorsteuer ergeben immer das Brutto (119,00 € zu 19 % → 100,00 € + 19,00 €). Über 250 € bleibt die ausgewiesene Steuer maßgeblich (§ 15 Abs. 1 Nr. 1, § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 UStG), das sagt auch die Doku.
- Ein unlesbares Brutto sperrt Speichern und Buchen wie ein unlesbares Netto (`bruttoLesbar`).
- Anderer Satz: Grundlage ist der zuletzt eingegebene Betrag. Nach einem Brutto bleibt das Brutto und Netto und Vorsteuer ändern sich (119,00 € zu 7 % → 111,21 € + 7,79 €); nach einem Netto bleibt es wie bisher.
- Netto oder Vorsteuer von Hand: das Brutto folgt. Eine von Hand geänderte Vorsteuer bleibt wie bisher stehen, ein neues Brutto gilt wieder als Vorschlag.
- § 13b und innergemeinschaftlicher Erwerb: kein Brutto, gezahlt wird das Netto; Verhalten unverändert.
- Dauerbelege bleiben unverändert.

Die Rechenlogik liegt in `apps/web/src/lib/betragszeile.ts` (die Belegseite ist schon über 1.100 Zeilen lang), mit Unit-Tests in `betragszeile.test.ts`. Neuer E2E-Test „Beleg mit Bruttobetrag“ in `apps/web/e2e/belege-steuern.spec.ts`. CSS: `.amount-row.with-gross` mit fünf Spalten, am Handy wie bisher zwei. Doku in `docs/belege.md` (Schritt 4 und Abschnitt „Beträge“).

- `bun --bun vitest run apps/web/src/lib/betragszeile.test.ts`: 12 bestanden.

agent_prs.body:
Unter **Beträge** in `docs/belege.md` steht jetzt, dass das Brutto auch für Fahrausweise gilt, unabhängig vom Betrag: Nach [§ 35 Abs. 2 UStDV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustdv_1980/__35.html) teilt man Fahrausweise im Sinne von § 34 UStDV wie Kleinbetragsrechnungen in Entgelt und Steuer auf, ohne die Grenze von 250 €. Steht auf dem Fahrschein kein Steuersatz, gilt der ermäßigte Satz (Satz 3, § 12 Abs. 2 UStG); bei Flugscheinen gibt es Vorsteuer nur mit angegebenem Regelsatz (Satz 4). Ein grenzüberschreitender Fahrausweis gilt nur mit einer Bescheinigung des Beförderers über den Inlandsanteil als Rechnung ([§ 34 Abs. 2 UStDV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustdv_1980/__34.html)). Vorschlag aus dem Review von #925.

## Geprüft

- Wortlaut von § 34 Abs. 1 und 2 und § 35 Abs. 2 UStDV auf gesetze-im-internet.de nachgelesen.
- Selbstprüfung (`beitrag-pruefen`) und unabhängiges Review (`doku-pruefen`) als Kommentare im Pull Request.

agent_prs.title: Betrieb: Instanzen-Werkzeug pflegt die Liste für „Firma wechseln“ (#909)

issues.body:
## Anlass

Wer mehrere Firmen mit dem Instanzen-Werkzeug betreibt, bekommt „Firma wechseln“ in der Navigation nur, wenn in der `.env` jeder Instanz dieselbe Liste `HABEN_FIRMEN` steht. Heute trägt man sie von Hand in jede Datei ein und startet jede App neu, bei jeder neuen Firma wieder. Das Werkzeug kennt alle Instanzen und ihre Domains schon.

Der Teil stammt aus #549 (Befehl `firmen`, Option `--firmenname`, damals im Bash-Werkzeug) und ist beim Ersatz durch #905 herausgenommen worden, weil das Werkzeug inzwischen in TypeScript vorliegt.

## Stand in Haben

Geprüft auf `main`, Commit `01a3d903`.

- Die App liest `HABEN_FIRMEN` (`Name|https://adresse`, getrennt durch `;`), prüft sie beim Start und zeigt dem Inhaber die anderen Firmen ([firmen.ts](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/01a3d903/apps/web/src/lib/firmen.ts), [installation.md, „Firma wechseln“](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/01a3d903/docs/installation.md#L529)). Eine fehlerhafte Liste verhindert den Start.
- Das Werkzeug kennt die Befehle `neu`, `update`, `status`, `liste` ([haben-instanzen.ts](https://github.com/firsttris/haben/blob/01a3d903/deploy/instanzen/haben-instanzen.ts#L154)) und setzt `HABEN_FIRMEN` nicht; in `deploy/instanzen` kommt die Variable nicht vor.
- Die `.env` einer Instanz schreibt es mit `envSetzen` und liest sie wie Compose (`env-datei.ts`); laufende Apps bringt `update` mit `up -d` auf einen neuen Stand.

## Vorschlag

- **`firmen`** baut aus den Instanzen der Basis die Liste (Name und `https://<DOMAIN>`), schreibt sie als `HABEN_FIRMEN` in jede `.env` und bringt laufende Apps auf den Stand ihrer `.env`. Gestoppte Instanzen bekommen nur die Datei.
- **Name je Instanz:** `neu --firmenname NAME` legt ihn als `HABEN_FIRMENNAME` in der `.env` ab; ohne Angabe gilt der Name der Instanz. Unter „Haben“ steht weiter der Name aus den Firmendaten; der hier ist nur der Eintrag in der Liste der anderen.

`GET /api/health` prüft ohne Anmeldung die PostgreSQL-Verbindung und den Stand der Migrationen. Bei Bereitschaft liefert der Endpunkt `200` mit `{"status":"pass"}`, sonst `503` mit `{"status":"fail","reason":"database"}` oder `"reason":"migrations"`. `status` folgt dem IETF-Entwurf `draft-inadarei-api-health-check`, `reason` mit festen Werten ergänzt Haben; Feldnamen und Werte sind englisch, weil der Endpunkt für fremde Programme gedacht ist. `warn` mit `200` bleibt für spätere Hinweise frei. Der Content-Type bleibt `application/json`. Die Antwort ist nicht cachebar und enthält keine Versions- oder Firmendaten. Bei einer blockierten Abfrage antwortet der Endpunkt nach zwei Sekunden und bricht die Abfrage ab.

Die App-Rolle erhält Leserecht auf den Zeitstempel im Migrationsjournal; bestehende Installationen bekommen es beim nächsten Start. Der Image-Healthcheck nutzt den Endpunkt. Die Installationsanleitung beschreibt die Antwort im Abschnitt „Image“ und verweist für Version, ERiC und Sicherung auf `haben status`.

Der Test der öffentlichen API-Routen erfasst den Health-Endpunkt ausdrücklich. Das Produktionsimage wird per Compose mit getrennter App-Rolle und bisheriger Einrollen-Anmeldung als `healthy` geprüft. agent_prs.body:
Das Instanzen-Werkzeug hat den Befehl `portal`: Er richtet das Firmenportal hinter dem gemeinsamen Caddy ein und gleicht es danach bei jedem Aufruf mit den Instanzen ab, mit Farbe und Logo jeder Firma. Er schreibt nur, was sich ändert, und startet nur neu, was eine geänderte Datei hat; so lässt er sich stündlich aus cron oder einem systemd-Timer aufrufen.

Umgesetzt #1036, zusammen mit #1044
Refs #504

Baut auf #1044 (Farbe und Logo im Firmenportal) auf und enthält dessen Commits, bis es gemergt ist.

## Einrichten

- `portal <domain> --oidc-issuer … --oidc-client-id … (--oidc-client-secret-file … | --oidc-client-secret-stdin) [--oidc-name …]` legt `<basis>/firmenportal/` an: `compose.yml` aus `deploy/firmenportal/` ohne den Port auf `127.0.0.1` (der Weg führt nur über den Caddy), `.env` mit eigenem `PORTAL_SECRET` (Rechte 600) und `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=firmenportal` (ohne `haben-`, damit die übrigen Befehle es nicht für eine Instanz halten), Override im eigenen Netz `haben-proxy-firmenportal` als `haben-firmenportal`, dazu `logos/`. Die Domain kommt in den gemeinsamen Caddy, die Ausgabe nennt Redirect-URI und Rückweg nach dem Abmelden für den Anmeldedienst.
- Danach `portal` ohne Angaben; eine andere Domain oder neue `--oidc-…` lehnt es ab.
- Ohne gemeinsamen Caddy (Instanzen mit `--eigener-proxy`) bricht es ab, statt einen zweiten zu starten. Ein vorhandenes Compose-Projekt `firmenportal` (etwa von Hand eingerichtet) übernimmt es nicht, ein Verzeichnis `firmenportal/` einer älteren Instanz fasst es nicht an. Der Name `firmenportal` ist für Instanzen reserviert.

## Abgleich

- `PORTAL_FIRMEN` aus allen Instanzen mit `OIDC_ONLY=true`: `HABEN_FIRMENNAME` (sonst der Name), `https://<DOMAIN>`, `OIDC_GROUP_INHABER`. Farbe und Logo aus `haben status --json` jeder laufenden Instanz; ein Logo holt `haben kennzeichen` nur, wenn sich die Prüfsumme geändert hat, und nur wenn Bytes, Format und Prüfsumme zur Meldung passen. Gestoppte Instanzen behalten Farbe und Logo von bishe

## Was
Umzug aus sevDesk analog zum Lexoffice-Umzug. Auf **Archiv › Umzug** wählt man jetzt „Umzug aus Lexware Office“ oder „Umzug aus sevDesk“. Die Schritte 1 (Verbindung) und 2 (Abruf) hängen von der Quelle ab, die Schritte 3–5 (offene Posten, Exporte, Abgleich) teilen sich beide.

- **`packages/import/src/sevdesk/`**: `SevdeskClient` (gedrosselt, mit Retries, Paging über `limit`/`offset`, PDFs über `getPdf?preventSendBy=true`, damit nichts als versendet markiert wird; XML; Belegdatei über `/Document/{id}/download`), Zod-Schemas und reine Mappings auf `LegacyVoucher`.
  - RE/TR/ER → Rechnung, AR → Abschlagsrechnung, SR/Gutschrift → negative Gutschrift. Belege C/D → Einnahme/Ausgabe, negative Summen → Gutschrift.
  - Entwürfe, Vorlagen (WKR, RV) und Mahnungen bleiben draußen.
  - Steuersätze kommen aus den Positionen. Rundungsdifferenzen zum Kopf landen beim größten Satz, die Steuerdifferenz beim größten Satz mit Steuer.
  - Zahlungen: `paidAmount` und `payDate` werden als eine Zahlung geführt.
- **DB** (0080/0081): `sevdesk_connection` (verschlüsselter Token, Audit), `contacts.sevdesk_id`, `source` an `lexoffice_imports` und `lexoffice_vouchers`. sevDesk-Belege landen in denselben Tabellen, die nur ergänzt werden dürfen, mit IDs wie `invoice/123`. So funktionieren Abgleich, offene Posten, Altbelege und Jahresexport für beide Quellen ohne Sonderfälle. Es läuft weiterhin höchstens ein Abruf gleichzeitig.

agent_prs.body:
Der DATEV-Export ließ den Punkt im Belegfeld 1 stehen. DATEV erlaubt dort nur Ziffern, Buchstaben und `$ & % * + - /`, höchstens 36 Zeichen; Punkt, Leerzeichen und Umlaute sind ausdrücklich unzulässig (DATEV, [ASCII-Import: Feldbeschreibungen für Standardformate](https://apps.datev.de/help-center/documents/1003221), Dok.-Nr. 1003221, Stand 13.08.2026, Abschnitt 3, Feld 11). Das Nummernformat von Haben erlaubt Punkte, `RE.{JJJJ}.{NNN}` landete also als `RE.2026.001` im Stapel.

Umgesetzt #675

## Was sich ändert

- **Belegfeld 1** (`packages/import/src/datev-export.ts`): Der Punkt wird zu `-` (`RE.2026.001` → `RE-2026-001`, Entscheidung im Issue), alle anderen Zeichen außerhalb der Liste fallen wie bisher weg, danach höchstens 36 Zeichen. Rechnung bzw. Beleg und ihre Zahlungen, Ausbuchungen und Kassenbuchungen bekommen ihre Nummer aus derselben Quelle (`datev-vorgaenge.ts`) und laufen durch dieselbe Bereinigung; sie tragen also dieselbe Belegfeld-1-Nummer, und der OP-Ausgleich in DATEV greift.
- **Warnung bei Zusammenstößen:** Ergeben verschiedene Nummern nach dem Bereinigen dasselbe Belegfeld 1 (etwa `RE.1` und `RE-1`, Umlaute oder das Kürzen auf 36 Zeichen), liefert `buildDatevBuchungsstapel` je Belegfeld eine Warnung mit allen Nummern. `/api/datev/$jahr` gibt sie URI-kodiert im Header `X-Haben-Hinweis` mit, höchstens 2000 Bytes (`hinweisHeader` in `lib/download.ts`): nginx legt alle Antwort-Header in einen Puffer von einer Speicherseite und antwortet sonst mit 502 statt der Datei. Was nicht passt, zählt die letzte Zeile („Und 12 weitere.“), eine einzelne zu lange Zeile wird nach Codepoints gekürzt, damit kein Surrogatpaar zerfällt; die DATEV-Karte in den Einstellungen und die Exporte auf der Seite Steuerberatung zeigen sie nach dem Herunterladen als Hinweis. Die Datei kommt trotzdem.
- `DatevCard` lädt über `downloadFrom` wie die Seite Steuerberatung, statt einen eigenen fetch zu führen; `downloadFrom` liefert den Hinweis zurück.
- **Doku:** `docs/auswertungen.md`

Zahlungsdienstleister wie Etsy nennen im Umsatz die Bestellnummer statt der Rechnungsnummer („Payment for Order #…“). Haben vergleicht dann nur den Betrag und schlägt bei mehreren Rechnungen gleichen Betrags die ältere vor.

- Neuer Grund „Bestellnummer im Verwendungszweck (…)“ mit 60 Punkten, für Rechnungen, Korrekturen und Stornos (`externalId`, `buyerOrderReference`, `sellerOrderReference`).
- **Nur bei exaktem Betrag:** Gebühren, Gebühren-Gutschriften und der Karteneinzug bei einer Erstattung nennen dieselbe Bestellnummer, gehören aber nicht zur Rechnung.
- Nummern unter fünf Zeichen und Nummern, die nur der Anfang einer anderen sind, zählen nicht. Bei Bestellnummern gilt das auch für angrenzende Buchstaben: `AU2026042` passt nicht auf `AU2026042A`. Die Suche nach Rechnungsnummern behält ihre Zifferngrenzen („RE2026-0042“ findet weiter „2026-0042“).
- Korrektur und Storno einer Rechnung, deren Bestellnummer nur als externe Referenz (`externalId`, etwa aus der API) am Original steht, finden die Erstattung über diese Nummer; die Referenz wird beim Lesen über `correctsId` aufgelöst, gespeichert wird nichts Neues.
- Tests in `matching.test.ts`, `matching.order-reference.review.test.ts`, `bank.test.ts` und `bank-order-reference.review.test.ts` (Postgres), Doku in `docs/bank.md`.

### Worum geht es?

Ich verkaufe über Etsy und importiere die Monatsabrechnung (Etsy-CSV) in ein Konto vom Typ Zahlungsdienstleister. Zu jeder Bestellung gibt es in Haben eine eigene Rechnung, die per REST-API mit `externalSource=etsy`, `externalId=<Bestellnummer>` und `buyerOrderReference=<Bestellnummer>` angelegt wird.

Im Bankabgleich steht beim Verkauf aber nicht die Rechnungsnummer im Verwendungszweck, sondern die Bestellnummer der Plattform: `Sale · Payment for Order #1234567890`. Haben vergleicht dann nur den Betrag. Haben zwei offene Rechnungen denselben Betrag (bei einem Shop mit festen Preisen der Normalfall), schlägt Haben die ältere vor, oft die falsche.

Beispiel mit erfundenen Werten:

| Umsatz | offene Rechnungen | Vorschlag heute | richtig |
|---|---|---|---|
| 28.06. · +22,00 € · `Payment for Order #1234567890` | 2023-004 (22,00 €, Bestellung 1111111111), 2023-006 (22,00 €, Bestellung 1234567890) | 2023-004 | 2023-006 |

Jeden Verkauf von Hand prüfen und über „Andere Rechnung“ die richtige wählen. Das kostet bei gleichen Beträgen jedes Mal einen Blick in die Bestellung.

Part of #1456 (slice 2b-0). The minimum first PR of the Phase-2 plan: no schema
change, no migration, no boundary file, no dependency on the rest of Phase 2.

## The six relations

Six `Person` relations were never repointed by the participant merge. The rows
stay pinned to a record the rest of the app treats as nonexistent — and two of
them are why the tombstone can't simply be deleted later.

| Relation | FK | Why the repoint matters |
|---|---|---|
| `RawBadgeLog.personId` | **RESTRICT** | This is the one that gates future deletion. A scan left on the tombstone makes `DELETE FROM "Person"` fail, on essentially every real tombstone. Plain `updateMany` — no unique constraint. |
| `OrgMembershipProcess.noteAckById` | SET NULL | Who read a family's intake note. Left behind, it becomes "nobody read it" the moment the row goes. |
| `Event.attendanceConfirmedById` | SET NULL | Who confirmed attendance. Same erasure. |
| `TrustedAdultReview.decidedById` | SET NULL | Which board member decided a trusted-adult review. Same erasure. |
| `PersonRole.personId` | **CASCADE** | A role left on a tombstone is a security grant that a later delete destroys **silently, with no audit row**. Repointed with dedupe (Decision 4's default). |
| `PersonRole.grantedById` | SET NULL | Who granted the role. |
| `BackgroundCheckAttestation.subjectPersonId` | SET NULL | The adult an attestation names — and the second half of the collision problem below. |

All of it lands inside the existing transaction, with tallies in the audit
`moved` object alongside the existing ones.

composite PK, no surrogate id and no separate unique. So the holder repoint uses
the same loop-or-skip idiom already established for `bgAttestations`, keyed on

Part of #1456 (phase 2b).

Phase 1 stopped new merges creating residue; 2b-0 (#1697) repointed the six relations the merge never touched. This adds the `PersonMerge` archive and moves the two readers that would otherwise die with the tombstone `Person` row onto it.

**Archive-first, delete-later.** Nothing is deleted here. The merge still writes the tombstone and still sets `mergedIntoId`; it now also records the merge in `PersonMerge` in the same transaction. Both records exist and agree, the archive backfills forward from today, and every reader added here prefers the archive with a tombstone fallback. Deleting the tombstone row is 2b-3, after the 2a census.

## The model

`fromId` / `toId` / `mergedAt` / `snapshot`, `@sensitivity` on every field, `classifications.ts` regenerated. The diff there is **purely additive**, which is the documented boundary-isolation exemption — `registry.ts` and `scopeBindings.ts` are untouched, and there is **no `SCOPE_BINDINGS` entry** (Decision 5, matching the `IdCounter` precedent).

`fromId` is `@unique` with **no foreign key** — the row exists to outlive the `Person` it names. That is what makes the scan lookup a `findUnique` and a double-archive impossible.

**Snapshot tier is `pii`**, carrying `name`, `email`, `lastBackgroundCheck` and the four role mirrors. **No `dateOfBirth`** (Decision 1, ruled): a Json blob is classified as one field, so DOB would re-tier the whole column from `pii` to `personal` for no reader. That is pinned by an exhaustive `toEqual` rather than `toMatchObject` — a subset assertion would not catch DOB being added back, which is the entire point of the ruling. The role mirrors ride along because the `AuditLog` pre-image that would otherwise hold them is written **only for a session actor**, so a token-auth merge would have no record of the authority the merged-away record held.

A household lead has no way to say "we're leaving." Only the Board ends a membership, by revoking it. Until the Board acts, a family that has left keeps getting the renewal emails every year and stays on the member lists.

1. Keep as today: the family asks, the Board revokes.

issues.body:
## Problem

`settledThisCycleWhere` (lifecycle.ts) determines which membership year a family bought by checking `stageEnteredAt` — the timestamp of the last stage transition (BG clearance / activation), not `paidAt`. For renewals this is benign: they only open in-window, so activation is necessarily in-window too.

For INITIALs it creates an ambiguity: a family can pay pre-window and have their BG review clear in-window. `activate()` stamps `stageEnteredAt` at review clearance time, so the system reads the family as "bought the coming year" — decided by board review latency, not by when the money moved.

Documented as `KNOWN LIMIT` in the `settledThisCycleWhere` docblock (added in #1654).

## Concrete risk window

Families paying for summer programs (FRC, drone) in June / early July. Those payment dates overlap with the renewal window opening (2 months before the boundary). If a family joins June 28, pays that day, and BG clears July 3 — the system says they bought the *following* year, the sweep never opens a renewal, and they get ~13 months of coverage. An identical family whose review finished June 29 gets the boundary as their horizon.

## Options to consider

1. **Use `paidAt` instead of `stageEnteredAt`** — directly answers "when did the money move?" but changes the semantics for every other consumer of the fragment, and `paidAt` can be null for granted/comped settlements.

2. **Year-specific membership product** — make the membership itself carry the year it covers, so the system doesn't need to infer it from timing. Eliminates the ambiguity at the product level rather than patching the query. Bigger lift.

3. **Accept as-is** — the pre-#1654 code had the same `stageEnteredAt` timing on `membershipValidThrough`'s inline probe (for renewals), and #1654 only newly exposes it to INITIALs. The practical exposure is narrow: it requires a family to both (a) pay pre-window and (b) have their review clear post-window-open, within a few days of the boundary. The known

issues.body:
Three receipts for one purchase can end up with two of them finalized and pushed to expense. At no point does finance see those two side by side. The tests in #2515 drive each case through the service API.

## Cause

`checkDuplicate` (`packages/receipt/src/lib/receipt-flow.ts:94`) and `insertReceipt` (`packages/receipt/src/lib/insert.ts:66`) each record **one** suspect per receipt:

- **The suspect's state is ignored.** A discarded or rejected receipt is still chosen as the suspect.
- **The field match has no `orderBy`.** It runs `findFirst` on retailer + date + total, then order number, then receipt number. Among several earlier copies, the one returned is whichever row Postgres reads first, and that order changes when a row is updated. The file-hash match is deterministic: it takes the earliest upload.
- **Nothing is re-checked.** Once a flag is cleared, that receipt is never checked again. Clearing or discarding a suspect does not re-check the receipts flagged against it.

## Scenarios (A uploaded first, then B, then C, all the same purchase)

1. **Each copy is cleared against A.** B and C are both flagged against A. Finance clears B, then clears C. All three are finalized. C's compare only ever shows A, never B, which is already finalized.
2. **The original is discarded.** A is discarded, either to keep B (the two-step flow) or before B and C arrive. A rejected A behaves the same way. B and C are flagged against the dead A, finance clears both, and both are finalized.
3. **A copy of a copy.** B is a second file with the same fields as A, and C is a re-upload of B's file, so C's hash suspect is **B**. Finance correctly discards B as a copy of A. C is now flagged only against the discarded B, so its compare never shows the live A. Clearing C finalizes it beside A.

Scenarios 2 and 3 are the confusing ones. Each decision looks right on its own screen, yet the result is two live copies.

issues.body:
Finance works from two queues for one job: receipt finance review (`/receipts/review`) and the expense FINANCE flags (`/expense/flags`). QuickBooks failures and account holds add more screens (`/expense/holds`, the expense detail page). The flags table shows a raw kind code and an expense id. Checking a flag off asks for no note, happens away from the expense, and is a separate act from the fix it asks for: a QuickBooks retry doesn't close `QB_POST_FAILED`, and recording the Board's authorization doesn't close `THRESHOLD_CROSSED`.

Decision (@thpr): fold the expense flags into the receipt review queue, so finance has one queue. Each row opens the record, which says in plain words why it is waiting, marks the field, and has the action on the same page. After the decision the page returns to the queue. Board items follow the same pattern in a Board view.

This is theme 1 of the receipt-flow conversion audit. Audit items: 1.4, 1.7, 2.9, 2.15, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.9, 3.10, 3.12, 3.16, 3.20, 3.21, 3.22, 3.27.

It builds on #2466 (state tabs and `GET /api/receipts/queue-counts`), #2468, #2462 (conflict-aware counts), #2464 and #2479 (finance review carried to expense), and #2465.

The design doc comes first, in its own PR. Implementation follows after review.

`docs/in-design/2662_PURCHASE_OUTCOME_EMAIL.md` proposes emailing the uploader, and the person reimbursed when that is someone else, when:

- finance rejects a receipt;
- an expense closes with a rejected line;
- a reimbursement is signed off and sent to the books.

Each email names the purchase and links to the receipt. It carries only what the recipient's own receipt pages already show.

**Questions for @thpr** (each in the doc with options and a recommendation):

- **Q1:** who gets each email
- **Q2:** whether an approver's exception emails anyone
- **Q3:** whether "complete" emails everyone or only reimbursements
- **Q4:** opt-out
- **Q5:** whether finance's reason goes in the email

Two points follow from existing rules and need no answer. Neither email names the other person. A reimbursee with no verified sign-in email gets nothing.

issues.body:
Decided by @thpr on 2026-10-28. This covers the email part of findings 1.18 and 3.30 from the receipt-flow conversion audit. The in-app part (a My receipts pill for rejected receipts, and the purchase's outcome shown past "Receipt finalized") is separate work under #2467.

## The gap

Nothing emails the person whose purchase it is when it reaches an outcome. They see what happened only if they open the app and look:

- **Receipt rejected by finance.** Finance must give a reason (#2592), but the uploader is not told.
- **Expense outcome.** After a receipt is finalized, its expense can have a line rejected (finance rejects an exception, with a required note), or be completed: signed off and posted to QuickBooks, or skipped. The submitter, and the reimbursee if that's someone else, is not told.

## Wanted

An email to the person whose purchase it is when it reaches an outcome:

- the receipt is rejected, with finance's reason
- an expense line is rejected, with the note
- the expense is complete (posted to QuickBooks, or skipped as a backfill)

Use the app's existing email plumbing (`checkin-app/src/lib/notifications.ts`, `email.ts`). The receipt and expense packages don't call it today.

## To decide in the design

- Who gets each email: the uploader, the reimbursee, or both when they differ.
- Whether an exception raised by an approver (not final) emails anyone, or only shows in the app.
- Whether "complete" emails at all, or only reimbursements do (the person is waiting for money).
- Opt-out, and what the email may say, given the data tiers in `docs/security/SECURITY-POLICY.md`. A reason can contain personal detail.

Low priority. Not started.

issues.body:
## Description

When a user who administrates an organization is deleted, its id stays in the organization's `authorized_authorities` field. The organization then keeps an administrator that no longer exists: it cannot be deleted, and the stale administrator cannot be removed with `organizationAdminRemove`.

## Environment

1. OS: macOS (dev platform)
2. Version: master (7.261117.0)
3. Other environment details: reproduced through the GraphQL API

## Reproducible steps

1. Create an organization, and a user member of it (`userAdd` with `objectOrganization`).
2. Make the user an administrator of the organization: `organizationAdminAdd(id, memberId)`.
3. Delete the user: `userEdit(id) { delete }`.
4. Delete the organization: `organizationDelete(id)`.
5. Remove the administrator instead: `organizationAdminRemove(id, memberId)`.

## Expected output

Deleting the user removes it from the administrators of its organizations. The organization can then be deleted (step 4).

## Actual output

- Step 4 fails with `Cannot delete an organization that has an administrator.`
- Step 5 fails with `User is not part of the organization`, because the deleted user is no longer a member.
- The only workaround is to clear the field by hand: `organizationFieldPatch` with `authorized_authorities: []`.

## Additional information

- `userDelete` (`opencti-graphql/src/modules/user/user-domain.ts`) cleans triggers, notifications, workspaces, public sharing and deduplication rules, but not `authorized_authorities`.
- The user merge already rewrites this field with a query scoped to organizations (`src/modules/userMerge/userMerge-rightsHandler.ts`). A fix should be scoped the same way: on feeds, collections and background tasks, `authorized_authorities` holds capability names, not user ids.
- An organization administrator can delete a user of its organization but is not allowed to change `authorized_authorities`, so the clean-up cannot run with the caller's rights.

issues.body:
## Description

`subscribeToInstanceEvents` calls the `preFn` and `cleanFn` options without awaiting or catching them. These are async functions: `userEditContext`/`userCleanContext` and the edit context helpers of about fifteen other resolvers. When one of them rejects, the rejection is unhandled and is logged as `[OPENCTI] Engine unhandled rejection`.

In production it shows up as `User cannot be found.`, a `FunctionalError` thrown by `loadUserToUpdateWithAccessCheck` (`opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/src/modules/user/user-domain.ts:655`). It is reached through `userEditContext` and `userCleanContext` (`user-domain.ts:2652-2662`), which run from the `user(id)` subscription (`opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/src/modules/user/user-resolver.ts:239-242`). This happens when a user is deleted while someone has their page open, or when a client subscribes with an id that no longer exists.

Root cause, in `opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/src/graphql/subscriptionWrapper.ts`:

- `:68` `if (preFn) preFn();` runs without `await`. If it rejects, the subscription goes on, and the rejection is reported to `process.on('unhandledRejection')` (`opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/src/boot.ts:113`).
- `:89-91` `withCancel(filtering, () => { cleanFn(); })` also ignores the returned promise. When the subscription closes, a failing clean is unhandled too.
- The option types `preFn?: () => void` and `cleanFn?: () => void` (`:61-62`) hide the fact that these functions return promises.

Proposed fix:

- Type both options as `() => Promise<unknown> | void`.
- `await preFn()` before `internalLoadById`, so a failure becomes a normal subscription error returned to the client.
- In `withCancel`, call `Promise.resolve(cleanFn()).catch((err) => logApp.warn('[SUBSCRIPTION] Error cleaning edit context', { cause: err }))`. A failed clean on close is not worth an error, because the edit context key expires on its own after 5 minutes.

## Environment

1. OS: any
2. Version: 7.261026.0 to 7.261103.0 (c

issues.body:
## Description

When more than 500 enrichments run in an investigation, the enrichment panel shows only some of them. The rest never appear in the To review, Ongoing or Done tabs, even when you select their entities on their own. Two limits cause this:

1. **Back end:** `findInvestigationEnrichmentWorks` (`modules/workspace/investigation-enrichment.ts`, step 01) first reads all of the investigation's works to find their source entities. It calls `fullEntitiesList` with no `orderBy`, so paging sorts on `standard_id.keyword` by default. Work documents have no `standard_id`, so `search_after` stops after the first page of 500 works. Only the sources found in those 500 works are kept. Every other place that lists works passes `orderBy: 'timestamp'` (`domain/work.js`, `domain/file.js`).
2. **Front end:** `InvestigationEnrichmentTool.tsx` queries `enrichmentWorks(entityIds: $entityIds)` without `first`, so the back end's default page size of 500 also caps the list and the badge.

## Environment

1. OS: any
2. Version: master (7.261109.0)
3. Other environment details: two enrichment connectors handling Domain-Name (one manual, one automatic)

## Reproducible steps

1. Create an investigation with 1001 Domain-Name entities.
2. Select all of them and launch an enrichment with a connector that handles Domain-Name.
3. Wait for the background task to complete and the connector queue to empty.
4. Open the enrichment panel.

## Expected output

The panel shows one enrichment per entity and connector, here about 2000, all in To review.

## Actual output

- The To review badge shows 500.
- The API holds 2012 enrichments for the investigation, all `TO_REVIEW` and all pointing at entities in the investigation.
- `enrichmentWorks` without `first` returns 500. With `first: 5000` it returns 592, which covers only 291 of the 1001 entities.
- Passing `entityIds` for one of the 710 missing entities returns 0 enrichments.

## Additional information

Suggested fix: pass `orderBy: 'timestamp'

## Description

The `xtm_hub_token` field of the GraphQL `Settings` type returns the XTM Hub platform token to every authenticated user, whatever their capabilities. The settings loaded by every user at startup (`RootPrivateQuery`) ask for it, so the token reaches every browser.

Only the users who manage the XTM Hub registration (`SETTINGS_SETMANAGEXTMHUB`) need to read it.

## Environment

1. OS: any
2. Version: master (7.261116.0)
3. Other environment details: a platform registered to XTM Hub

1. Log in as a user without the `SETTINGS_SETMANAGEXTMHUB` capability.
2. Run `query { settings { xtm_hub_token } }`.
3. The XTM Hub platform token is returned.

## Expected output

`xtm_hub_token` is `null` for users without `SETTINGS_SETMANAGEXTMHUB`. It stays `null` rather than raising an error, because the settings query every user runs asks for the field.

## Actual output

The platform token is returned to any authenticated user.

## Additional information

- Writing the token through `settingsEdit` is already redacted from the activity and audit logs: `xtm_hub_token` is in the baseline list of redacted keys (#19676).
- After the fix, a document download from XTM Hub by a user without the capability carries only the XTM Hub user token. XTM Hub accepts such a download; whether downloads should require a platform credential is handled separately, together with the move to per-instance key pairs.

### Proposed changes

* The Redis entry of the Composer managed token (`composer:<catalog_id>:token:<user_id>`, unchanged) now holds a record: the encrypted token, its token id, and a fingerprint of the connector manager `public_key` it was encrypted with.
* The record is served only when its fingerprint matches the current manager key **and** the user still holds its token. Otherwise the token of the record is revoked, a new one is generated, encrypted with the current key, and the record is overwritten. One record, overwritten on every rotation, also covers a key coming back (A → B → A).
* Only the token of the record is revoked, never the first `Composer managed token` of the user, which another connector sharing the user may serve. A token revoked by an administrator is regenerated instead of being served forever.
* The lock moves from the connector to the user (`composer-token-<user_id>`): connectors sharing a user share its tokens, and the record too when they share the catalog. Composer resolves all managed connectors in parallel, so concurrent reads no longer revoke the same token twice (`Token not found`) or race on the record.
* The user cache can lag behind a token just created: a miss is decided on the stored user, so the hit path stays on the cache.

## Description

Renovate runs on Mend-hosted Renovate, on the Community (Free) plan.

- A Mend job has a memory limit of 3 GB.
- The weekly lock file maintenance job runs out of memory (`kernel-out-of-memory`). It failed on 2026-11-08 and on 2026-11-22.
- Ordinary jobs that run `yarn install` already peak at about 3 GB.
- The memory is used by Yarn when it converts the downloaded packages to zip archives. Yarn starts one worker per CPU, and each worker keeps about 0.5 GB.
- `yarn.lock` was refreshed by hand in #20302. The next lock file maintenance job will fail again.

## Goal

Run Renovate in a GitHub Actions workflow of this repository, instead of the Mend-hosted app.

- The standard GitHub runners have more memory than the Mend jobs.
- The repository configuration stays in `renovate.json5`.
- Commits are made through the GitHub API with a GitHub App token. GitHub signs them, as the `master` ruleset requires.
- The workflow runs every hour. It also runs when a person checks a box in the Dependency Dashboard or in a Renovate pull request.
- The job logs are in the Actions tab.

## Prerequisites

- A GitHub App installed on this repository.
- The repository variables `RENOVATE_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RENOVATE_APP_SLUG` and `RENOVATE_APP_USER_ID`.
- The repository secret `RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- The Mend Renovate app is removed from this repository when the workflow is merged.
issues.title: chore(ci): run Renovate as a self-hosted GitHub Actions workflow

## Use case

The `/auth/:provider` and `/auth/:provider/callback` routes (`opencti-graphql/src/http/httpPlatform.js`) serve the redirect-based authentication providers (OpenID Connect, SAML...). They resolve any registered passport strategy by its name, including strategies that are not meant to be used through these routes.

## Proposed solution

- Only serve, on these routes, the providers that use them.
- Tests: the routes keep working for the redirect-based providers and refuse the others.

## Additional information

Part of #18212 (secure by design).

agent_prs.title: feat(platform): remove the inline script of the platform page and 'unsafe-inline' from the CSP script-src (#20303)

issues.body:
## Description

The Content-Security-Policy of the platform always allows inline scripts: `script-src` is `'self' 'unsafe-inline'`.

Security audits and DAST scans flag `'unsafe-inline'` in `script-src`. It weakens the protection against cross-site scripting.

The platform page has one inline script of its own, in `index.html`:

```html
<script>window.BASE_PATH = "%BASE_PATH%"</script>
```

It only gives the base path (`app:base_path`) to the frontend. The backend fills `%BASE_PATH%` when it serves the page.

The page can also hold the HTML of `app:script_snippet`. This snippet is empty by default.

## Goal

- The frontend reads the base path without an inline script, for example from a `<meta>` element that the backend fills.
- `index.html` has no inline script.
- `script-src` has no `'unsafe-inline'` by default. This covers the default policy and the public dashboard policy.
- When `app:script_snippet` is set, `script-src` keeps `'unsafe-inline'`, so that existing snippets keep working.
issues.title: feat(platform): remove the inline script of the platform page and 'unsafe-inline' from the CSP script-src

### Proposed changes

* Regenerate `yarn.lock` from scratch, as Renovate lock file maintenance does.
* The Renovate lock file maintenance job runs out of memory on Mend-hosted Renovate. Renovate has not opened a lock file maintenance pull request since #19582.
* This is a one-time refresh. The Renovate configuration does not change.

Commands:

```bash
rm yarn.lock
yarn install --mode=update-lockfile
yarn dedupe --strategy highest --mode=update-lockfile
```

Result:

* 192 packages change version.
* 1 package is added: `bare-buffer`.
* 2 packages are removed: `cssesc` and `resolve-protobuf-schema`.
* No package goes down in version.
* `package.json` files do not change. The 27 `patch:` entries are still in the lock file.
* `npmMinimalAgeGate` in `.yarnrc.yml` applies. Yarn resolves no version younger than 3 days, except the preapproved `@filigran/*` packages.

### Related issues

* Closes #20300

### How to test this PR

```bash
yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build
```

The CI runs the builds and the tests on the new lock file.

issues.body:
## Description

Renovate has not opened a lock file maintenance pull request since #19582 (2026-11-04).

The weekly lock file maintenance job runs out of memory on Mend-hosted Renovate:

- Renovate deletes `yarn.lock` and runs `yarn install --mode=update-lockfile`.
- Yarn resolves the whole workspace from scratch.
- The job hits the 3 GB memory limit of the Mend job and the kernel kills it (`kernel-out-of-memory`).
- This happened on 2026-11-08 and on 2026-11-22.

Transitive dependencies in `yarn.lock` have not been refreshed since 2026-11-04.

## Goal

Refresh `yarn.lock` once, by hand, the way Renovate's lock file maintenance does it:

- Delete `yarn.lock`.
- Run `yarn install --mode=update-lockfile`.
- Run `yarn dedupe --strategy highest`, as `postUpdateOptions: ['yarnDedupeHighest']` does.

The Renovate configuration does not change in this issue.
issues.title: chore(deps): refresh yarn.lock by hand, as Renovate lock file maintenance runs out of memory

issues.body:
## Description

The repository ships a VS Code dev container in `.devcontainer/`. Nobody seems to use it, and it is out of date:

- The `Dockerfile` installs Node.js 16. The repository runs on Node.js 22.
- The `Dockerfile` installs docker-compose 2.5.1.
- `devcontainer.json` never runs `install.dependencies.sh`. The dependencies are not installed when the container starts.
- `devcontainer.json` declares `extensions` and `settings` at the top level. This is the old format. VS Code now reads them under `customizations.vscode`.

It still costs upkeep. Every change to the platform configuration or to the tooling must also update these files. Since 2022, every commit on `.devcontainer/` was such a follow-up change.

## Goal

Remove the dev container.

- Delete `.devcontainer/` (`Dockerfile`, `devcontainer.json`, `config.json`, `install.dependencies.sh`).
- Remove the two `.devcontainer/(.*)` excludes from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

Nothing else in the repository refers to the dev container. The long-term support branches keep it.

issues.body:
## Use case

Nothing in the backend or its dependencies needs to add properties to `Object.prototype` at runtime. Locking it at startup makes the platform more predictable: an object's missing field always reads as missing.

## Proposed solution

- Seal `Object.prototype` as the very first step of the backend entry point (`src/back.ts`), before any dependency loads.
- Use `Object.seal` rather than `Object.freeze`. Its existing members (`toString`, `valueOf`, `constructor`...) stay writable, because several dependencies (moment, ipaddr.js, bluebird...) assign them on their own prototypes. Under `Object.freeze` those assignments throw in strict mode.
- Add a unit test asserting the prototype is sealed once the entry module is loaded.
issues.title: chore(core): seal Object.prototype at backend startup

agent_prs.title: fix(graphql): accept __type queries from authenticated users while secure_by_default is off (#20298)

issues.body:
## Description

PR #19370 blocks `__type` queries like `__schema` queries when the introspection is disabled. This check does not depend on `app:graphql:secure_by_default`.

The introspection is disabled by default: `app:graphql:playground:force_disabled_introspection` is `true`. So the platform refuses every `__type` query by default, even from an authenticated user.

Before #19370, the check only looked for `__schema` in the query string. The platform accepted `__type` queries.

Other products of the suite send `__type` queries:

- OpenAEV sends `__type(name: "Connector")` before each register and each ping of its coverage connector. The connector no longer registers (OpenAEV-Platform/openaev#9647).
- XTM One sends `__type(name: "System")` to read the system taxonomy.

#19370 puts the new protections behind `app:graphql:secure_by_default`. The `__type` check should follow the same switch.

## Environment

1. OS: any
2. Version: 7.261106.0 and later. It is the first release with c812cc4376584a67ed487494e3c5a35e5b5372ba.
3. Other environment details: default GraphQL configuration

## Reproducible steps

1. Start the platform with the default GraphQL configuration.
2. Send `{ __type(name: "Connector") { fields { name } } }` with a valid token.

## Expected output

The query returns the fields of the `Connector` type.

## Actual output

The query fails with `GraphQL introspection not authorized!`.

## Additional information

Proposed fix:

- When `app:graphql:secure_by_default` is `false`, accept `__type` queries from authenticated users. Refuse them from anonymous users.
- When `app:graphql:secure_by_default` is `true`, refuse `__type` queries like `__schema` queries.
- `__schema` queries keep their current behavior.

When a live stream client disconnects during the recovery phase, the platform logs `[STREAM] Processing error` at error level.

The pending Elasticsearch or OpenSearch call is then aborted (`Request has been aborted by the user`). `elPaginate` converts it, through `wrapEngineError`, into a `ClientAbortError` (code `CLIENT_ABORT_ERROR`). The call stack is `loadElementMetaDependencies` → `elList` → `elPaginate`, reached from the recovery `queryCallback`.

The catch in `liveStreamHandler` doesn't tell this case apart from a real failure:

- `opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/src/graphql/sseMiddleware.js:1058-1059`: `logApp.error('[STREAM] Processing error', { cause: err, id, type: 'live' })`.
- `sseMiddleware.js:1064-1065`: `[STREAM] Initialization error` has the same catch-all.

The GraphQL path already handles this. #17389 introduced `CLIENT_ABORT_ERROR` and `isClientAbortError` (`src/database/engine.ts:643`), #19214 extended it to aggregations, and `loggerPlugin` logs `CLIENT_ABORT_ERROR` at warn through `FUNCTIONAL_ERRORS`. The stream middleware doesn't use any of it.

## Environment

1. OS: any
2. Version: 7.261103.0 (still present on master)
3. Other environment details: seen in production error logs

## Reproducible steps

1. Create a live stream with many matching elements.
2. Connect to `/stream/<id>` with a `recover` date far in the past, so the recovery has to page through Elasticsearch.
3. Close the connection while the recovery is running.

## Expected output

The disconnection is logged at info, or at most at warn, and the handler stops quietly. The client is gone, so nothing needs to be sent to it.

## Actual output

`[STREAM] Processing error` is logged at error, with cause `CLIENT_ABORT_ERROR` wrapping `RequestAbortedError: Request has been aborted by the user`.

### Proposed changes

Fixes how observables are extracted from a STIX indicator pattern (`createObservables: true`, promote to observables, playbooks, `x_opencti_observable_values`). The listener now reads each value by its token type instead of guessing from the text:

* **String values** are decoded per the STIX grammar (`StringLiteral : QUOTE ( ~['\\] | '\\\'' | '\\\\' )* QUOTE`): the quotes are removed and the two allowed escapes are decoded (`\'` → `'`, `\\` → `\`). Before, every `'` was stripped, so `message=\'hello\'` became `message=\hello\`, and `\\` stayed doubled.
* **Quoted path keys** are decoded the same way. `[file:'name' = 'x.exe']` used to be dropped, and `hashes.'a\'b'` gave `a\b`.
* **Hex, binary and timestamp literals** lose their prefix and quotes. `h'd41d…'` used to give `hd41d…`, which failed the MD5 check and was dropped.
* **Only equalities create observables.** `!=` and `NOT =` exclude a value, so `[domain-name:value != 'google.com']` no longer creates a `google.com` observable linked by `based-on` (`NOT !=` still counts as an equality).
* **The current comparison is reset after each equality**, so the literals of a following `IN (...)` set are no longer taken as observables. `[ipv4-addr:value = '9.9.9.9' OR ipv4-addr:value IN ('1.1.1.1','2.2.2.2')]` now gives one observable instead of three.

* closes #14752

    "createObservables": true

}

issues.body:
## Description

When creating an indicator via the `indicatorAdd` GraphQL mutation with `createObservables: true`, 
the STIX pattern is stored correctly on the **indicator** — including escaped single quotes (`\'`). 
However, the **URL observable** that is automatically generated loses the single quotes entirely, 
retaining only the backslashes.

This causes a data integrity mismatch between the indicator pattern and the observable value it is "based on".


## Environment

- OpenCTI version: 6.9.20
- Deployment type: SaaS


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the GraphQL Playground on your OpenCTI instance (`/graphql`)
2. Run the following mutation:

### Mutation
​
```
mutation IndicatorAdd($input: IndicatorAddInput!) {
  indicatorAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    standard_id
    entity_type
    parent_types
    observables {
      edges {
        node {
          id
          standard_id
          entity_type
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
​

### Variables
​
```
{
  "input": {
    "pattern_type": "stix",
    "pattern": "[url:value = 'https://example.com/params?&message=\\'hello\\'']",
    "name": "Test",
    "x_opencti_main_observable_type": "Url",
    "createObservables": true
  }
}
​
```

3. Take the observable `id` from the response
4. Run the following query with that ID:

```
query {
  stixCyberObservable(id: "<observable-id-from-above>") {
    ... on Url {
      value
    }
  }
}
​
```


## Expected Result

The observable `value` should preserve the escaped single quotes from the STIX pattern:
​
https://example.com/params?&message=\'hello\'

## Actual Result
The observable value strips the single quotes, leaving only backslashes:

​https://example.com/params?&message=\\hello\\ ​

issues.body:
## Use case

Before #19476 and #19473, XTM Composer received a single token per user for managed connectors. It was named `Composer managed token` and was never set to expire. Since #19473, each managed connector gets its own token, tagged with the platform-only `managed_by_type`/`managed_by_id` fields. The platform only issues and revokes tagged tokens.

On an upgraded platform:

- Every managed connector gets its own token the first time XTM Composer polls after the upgrade (the Redis key changed). Its contract hash then changes and XTM Composer redeploys it with the new token.
- The old `Composer managed token` token has no `managed_by_*` fields, so nothing revokes it anymore. It stays valid forever on the connector's user, although no connector uses it.

## Current workaround

An admin revokes the `Composer managed token` tokens by hand from each connector user's token list.

## Proposed solution

When the platform issues a connector token for a user, it also revokes that user's tokens named exactly `Composer managed token` that have no `managed_by_*` fields. This runs under the existing per-user token lock. Before #19476 the platform already found and revoked this token by this exact name.

- Serving a cached token revokes nothing.
- Tokens with any other name are never touched.

The check is temporary. It can be removed once no supported upgrade path starts before #19476.

## Additional information

Not covered:

- Old tokens on users whose managed connectors were deleted before the upgrade. Deletion never revoked them.
- Old tokens on users whose connectors are no longer polled by any XTM Composer.

An admin can revoke these by hand. A migration could cover the users with no managed connector left.

issues.body:
## Use case

The "Backend / Integration tests" job is the longest job of the OpenCTI CI: 23 min median on master (6 green runs on 2026-11-04), about 5 min longer than the slowest e2e shard, so it sets the duration of every PR's CI.

A good part of that time is spent waiting, not testing:

| Where | What | Cost per run |
|---|---|---|
| `ci-test-backend.yml`, step "Wait for OpenCTI sync instances to start" | Blocks until the 4 sync instances are healthy, while only `tests/11-sync` uses them, ~11 min later | 133 s |
| `tests/11-sync/02-Direct/sync-direct-test.js` | `wait(120000)` after starting the synchronizer. The remote instance's logs show it caught up with the stream about 20 s after starting | ~90 s |
| `tests/utils/testStream.js` | `fetchStreamEvents` closes the stream only after 30 s without a new event (the comment says 5 s), paid by both stream tests | ~50 s |
| `tests/10-streams/00-Raw/raw-test.js` | blind `waitInSec(10)` before reading the stream | replaced by an active wait |
| `tests/03-integration/01-database/runFunctionAsLongRunning-test.ts` | waits 20 s + 10 s because the 10 s timeout of `runFunctionAsLongRunning` is hardcoded | ~25 s |
| `tests/11-sync/*` | the 4 syncs (raw, live, direct, restore) each target their own remote instance but run one after the other | ~370 s in a row |

## Current workaround

None: every PR pays these waits.

## Proposed solution

Only how long the tests wait changes. Every assertion stays as it is.

1. **Sync instances**: the job waits only for the search engine, like the "Rules and Taxii tests" job does. The sync tests wait for their remote instances in a `beforeAll` (health endpoint, 5 min timeout).
2. **Direct sync**: polls the remote `debugStats` until they match the local ones, and until the uploaded file is present on the remote report, twice in a row, 5 s apart, with a 5 min timeout. On timeout it falls through to the unchanged `checkPostSyncContent`, which reports the differences.

issues.body:
## Use case

Follow-up of the PO review of the workflow engine (epic #17012). The review found 5 points: 3 bugs, 1 functional gap and 1 UX issue. This issue tracks all of them.

## Items

### 1. [bug - high] Entity workflow transitions run while the entity is in a draft

When you open an entity inside a draft, its workflow is still active. The Processing status panel shows the transition buttons, and every transition can be executed, including approval steps. An entity can be approved from inside a draft.

Expected: workflows on an entity are disabled while that entity is in a draft. The draft's own workflow (DraftWorkspace) is a separate case and must keep working.

Code:
- Front: the overview renders `WorkflowTransitionsForEntity` with no draft check (`opencti-front/src/private/components/common/stix_domain_objects/StixDomainObjectOverview.jsx`).
- Back: `triggerWorkflowEvent` has no draft-context guard (`opencti-graphql/src/modules/workflow/domain/workflow-domain.ts`), although workflow initialization is already skipped in a draft. The fix needs a server-side refusal, not only hidden buttons.

### 2. [bug - medium] Playbook "Manipulate knowledge" > Replace status lists statuses not in the workflow

### Proposed changes

* A live stream connection resolved its user once, when it opened, and kept filtering events with those rights for up to a day. When a service account consuming a restricted stream was turned into a regular user (outside the platform organization), the stream kept sending everything: the context still had `user_inside_platform_organization = true`, which is always true for service accounts.

issues.body:
## Description

In a Form Intake, when a lookup field (main entity or additional entity) selects an EXISTING Observed-Data, the form submission is accepted, but the worker fails to process the Observed-Data of the bundle: the work logs `Missing required elements for Observed-Data creation (objects)`.

The backend puts the existing entity in the bundle as a full STIX object to (re)create, built from an entity loaded without its relations. For an Observed-Data the `objects` relation is missing, so the STIX object has an empty `object_refs`, which an Observed-Data cannot have (its standard id is built from `objects`).

## Environment

1. OS: any
2. Version: master 59d8539442 (also reproduced by code reading on c6a503300a~1, the commit before #19019, so it predates the deferred creation work)

3. Open the form, focus the Entity field, select the existing Observed-Data, click Submit.

Selecting an existing entity in a lookup only references it. The submission is processed without error (nothing to create for an entity that already exists), like a Report lookup.

issues.body:
## Context

The user merge (#17258) only rewrites what its register (`USER_MERGE_REGISTER`) knows about. A user reference added later without a register row stays on the source account, which the merge disables and then deletes. Nothing fails, but the target silently loses what the reference gave.

An audit of the register against the current schema found it up to date for typed attributes, with one gap and two weak spots.

## Gap: default values naming users

`EntitySetting.attributes_configuration[].default_values` and the CSV / JSON mapper `representations[].attributes[].default_values` (including the inline `csv_mapper` of a CSV feed) can hold user ids:
- default assignees and participants;
- default authorized members, stored as serialized `{id, access_right}`.

No register row or handler covers them, so after a merge:
- every new entity is still assigned to the disabled source, or grants it access;
- those new references block the deletion gate until the merge is re-run;
- once the source is deleted, the defaults silently drop.

## Weak spots in the guardrails

- No test checks the **registered** handlers against the register. `userMerge-coverage-test` only uses mocks. A `transfer` / `conditional` row added without a handler would block the deletion of every merged source.

### Proposed changes

* `getEntitiesMapFromCache` rebuilt a new `Map` of every cached entity of the type (keyed by `internal_id`, `standard_id`, stix ids, `uri_key`) on **each** call, even when the cache had not changed. That's O(number of entities) of CPU and allocation per call, about 1.6 ms for 10k users and 9 ms for 50k, on hot paths: per subscription, per request in the IP allowlist middleware, per notification, and soon per live stream batch (#19625).
* The map is now built on first use and kept in the cache entry, next to the values (`entitiesMap`). Later calls return the same map, so a lookup is O(1) while nothing changes.
* Every change of the values goes through a new `setCacheValues`, which drops the map: initial load, reset, and add/refresh/remove events. The map is dropped even when an update function changes the list in place and returns the same array (the users `add` does `values.push`).
* If the values change while a call is waiting for them, that call builds a map for itself only and does not store it, so a map built from old values is never kept.
* Because the map is now shared, `getEntitiesMapFromCache` returns a `ReadonlyMap`, and the functions it is passed to take a `ReadonlyMap`. The type check proves that no TypeScript caller modifies it. The JavaScript callers (`httpServer.js`, `ipWhitelistMiddleware.js`, `group.js`, `file.js`, `stixCoreObject.js`, `markingDefinition-utils.js`) were checked by hand: they only call `get`/`has`.
* Resolved filters, which are already stored as a map, are unchanged.

### Related issues

* closes #19634

### How to test this PR

Unit tests in `tests/01-unit/database/cache-test.ts`:
- the same map is returned while the values do not change;
- the map is built again after an in-place add, after a refresh, after a remove and after a reset;
- a map built from values replaced during the call is not kept.

There is no functional change: every existing lookup (users, markings, groups, settings...) must behave as before.
agent_prs.title: perf(cache): keep the entities map in the cache instead of rebuilding it on each call (#19634)

issues.body:
## Use case

`getEntitiesMapFromCache` (`opencti-platform/opencti-graphql/src/database/cache.ts`) is the way to look up a cached platform entity by id (users, markings, groups, organizations, settings...). It has about 90 call sites, some of them on hot paths:

- per GraphQL subscription, to resolve the session user (`httpServer.js`);
- per request in the IP allowlist middleware (`ipWhitelistMiddleware.js`);
- on each batch of every open live stream, to keep the stream user up to date (#19599);
- when rendering data changes, resolving markings, etc.

The cache keeps an **array** of entities per type. On **every** call, `getEntitiesMapFromCache` iterates this array and builds a brand new `Map` keyed by every id of every entity (`internal_id`, `standard_id`, `x_opencti_stix_ids`, `uri_key` for public dashboards), then the caller usually reads a single entry and throws the map away.

The cost is O(number of cached entities) of CPU on the event loop plus a full map allocation for the garbage collector, paid at each call even if the cache did not change. Measured with Node 22 on a laptop, building the map for users with an `internal_id` and a `standard_id`:

| Cached users | Map rebuild per call |
|---|---|
| 1,000 | ~0.07 ms |
| 10,000 | ~1.6 ms |
| 50,000 | ~9 ms |

For example, 20 busy live streams on a platform with 10k users, each getting a batch for nearly every event at 50 events/s, spend about 1.6 s of CPU per second only rebuilding the users map.

## Current workaround

None. Callers that need a single entity can scan `getEntitiesListFromCache` instead, but that's still O(n) per call and every existing caller would have to change.

## Proposed solution

Build the map once and keep it in the cache next to the list:

- `getEntitiesMapFromCache` returns the stored map if there is one, otherwise builds it from the current values and stores it.
- The stored map is dropped whenever the values of the type change: loaded, reset, or updated by an add/refresh/remove event

### Proposed changes

The `workflowMigrationPreview` and `workflowMigrate` endpoints, for both GLOBAL and REQUEST_ACCESS, are now on master through #19709. This PR serializes workflow definition writes and fixes the rollback of `workflowMigrate(..., publish: true)` when the publish step fails.

* **Serialize workflow definition writes.** `workflowDefinitionSet`, `workflowDefinitionPublish`, `workflowDefinitionRestorePublished` and `workflowDefinitionDelete` now all take the `workflow-status-lifecycle:<type>` lock that the status cleanup manager already uses. A publish reads its draft under that lock, so a save, restore or delete can no longer change the workflow between the read and the publication.
* **Run the migration under the same lock.** `workflowMigrate` holds the lock from its existence check through the save, the publish and the rollback. No user save or publish can land in between.
* **Restore an overwritten draft.** With `overwrite: true`, if the publish fails, the existing workflow gets its previous draft (or none), version history and name back. Without an existing workflow (or with a link to a missing one), the created workflow is unlinked and deleted, so a retry needs no `overwrite`. The fix applies to both scopes.
* **Never roll back a live workflow.** The rollback acts only while the stored draft is still the one the migration wrote. A publish that failed after writing has already made the workflow live, and it stays as it is. A rollback error is logged and the original publish error is rethrown.
* **Editor autosave under lock contention.** A save can now wait on the lock and time out, and the lock serves its waiters in no particular order. The workflow editor now sends one save at a time: a change made while one is in flight waits, and only the latest is sent. ### Proposed changes

* Create the worker telemetry instruments (`opencti_bundles_global_counter`, `opencti_bundles_processing_time_gauge`) from the worker `MeterProvider` once it is configured, instead of at module import time. When telemetry is disabled, a `NoOpMeter` is used. The instruments are now `Worker` attributes passed to `PushHandler`.
* Record bundle processing time with `timedelta.total_seconds()` instead of `timedelta.seconds`. `.seconds` is the integer seconds component, so any bundle processed in under a second was recorded as `0`, which explains the zero-valued metrics in the issue.
* Expose `opencti_max_ingestion_units` and `opencti_running_ingestion_units` as observable gauges, read at each Prometheus scrape instead of once per 60s main loop iteration:

issues.body:
## Description

A significant logical issue exists in the telemetry setup, which could result in metrics not being collected or exported as intended. This manifests as missing or zero-valued metrics in Prometheus, even when telemetry is enabled. Workers not reporting correctly.

## Environment

1. OS Ubuntu 24.04
2. OpenCTI version: 6.8.16
3. OpenCTI client: PYTHON
4. Other environment details:

## Reproducible Steps

Steps to create the smallest reproducible scenario:
N/A

## Expected Output

<!-- Please describe what you expected to happen. -->

## Actual Output

<!-- Please describe what actually happened. -->

## Additional information

<!-- Any additional information, including logs or screenshots if you have any. -->

Identified Issue - Incorrect Order of Telemetry Initialization

The telemetry instruments (counters and gauges such as bundles_global_counter and running_ingestion_units_gauge) are defined at the module level using meter = metrics.get_meter(__name__). This occurs before any instance of Worker is created and before the MeterProvider is set in the __post_init__ method (which only happens if telemetry_enabled is True).

Root Cause:

The get_meter function retrieves a meter from the current global MeterProvider. At module import time, no custom provider has been set, so it defaults to a no-op provider (which discards all metrics). The instruments created on this no-op meter will not function, even after metrics.set_meter_provider(provider) is called later. Changing the provider does not retroactively affect existing meters or instruments.

Impact:

If telemetry is enabled via configuration, the metrics (bundle processing counts and gauges) will not be recorded or exposed via Prometheus, leading to ineffective monitoring.

Recommended Fix:

Relocate the meter and instrument definitions inside the if self.telemetry_enabled block in __post_init__, immediately after setting the MeterProvider. This ensures the instruments are created on the active provide
