### What happens

On a box whose netavark uses the iptables backend (Ubuntu 24.04: netavark 1.4.0, podman 4.9.3), slot containers can lose their host-port DNAT rules while staying healthy. `/health` answers 200 inside the container, but the published port on the host black-holes: connections pile up in the accept queue of the conmon port-holder socket (Recv-Q ~480) and time out. hal0 neither detects nor repairs this:

- `hal0 doctor ports` prints `netavark DNAT audit skipped: nft failed (1): Error: No such file or directory ... list table inet netavark`. The audit reads only the nftables `inet netavark` table, and since #3237 it skips silently when that table is absent, so on iptables-backend boxes there is no detection at all.
- The slot list shows the affected slots stuck in `warming`, with no reason given.

### Observed (2026-11-16, test box)

- `iptables -t nat -S NETAVARK-HOSTPORT-DNAT` held rules only for the two containers recreated most recently: OpenWebUI (recreated 04:07:52Z) and the FLM slot (recreated 04:15:32Z). Rules for the agent, brain and memory slot containers (running for days) and for the langfuse containers were gone. The rules most likely went when the OpenWebUI container was torn down and recreated; that is the earliest recreate, but the mechanism is not proven.
- Linger is on for root (`loginctl show-user root -p Linger` = yes), so this is not the #1814 stranded-netns variant.
- `podman network reload --all` restored every rule without restarting any container, and all slots answered 200 again.

### What happens if nobody fixes it

Every GPU slot on the box goes dark after an unrelated container recreate (an OpenWebUI component converge is enough). Chat, agents and memory extraction stop. The UI shows `warming` forever and doctor reports nothing.

### Where

- `src/hal0/system/netavark.py`: the audit is nft-only.
- `hal0 doctor ports` (the `Port DNAT rules` row), and `hal0 doctor ports --fix`.
- The watchdog demotion path described in #1820.

## What happens

The memory engine runs `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_MAX_SLOTS` tasks at once. hal0 renders this in `src/hal0/memory/extraction_env.py:262`; the live box runs 6. Consolidation reserves 2 of them by default (engine `config.py`, `WORKER_SLOT_TYPE_DEFAULTS`: `consolidation: 2`, `retain: 0`), and the rest are one shared pool.

`refresh_mental_model` tasks take shared slots and then sit waiting for an LLM permit (`LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT=2`, usually held by consolidation) until their 1800 s wall timeout. When one fails, the next queued refresh takes the slot. With a few dozen refreshes queued, retains get no worker slot at all.

Seen on a live box on 2026-11-15:
- The engine's `WORKER_STATS` showed `reserved: [consolidation=2/2] | shared=4/4`, and all 4 shared slots were refreshes.
- A retain due for retry at 14:29Z had not started by 14:41Z.
- Health reported `retain_operations_stalled`.

The refresh flood on that box came from an hourly operator script refreshing every stale page. That script is now report-only. Refreshes queued after consolidation can fill the pool the same way, though.

## If nobody fixes it

Coding-agent, Hermes and Open WebUI retains can wait for hours while refreshes time out one after another.

## Fix (S)

Render `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_RETAIN_RESERVED_SLOTS=1` in the extraction drop-in, and add it to the doctor's expected env.

Care is needed at the floor. `WORKER_SLOTS_FLOOR` is 3 (`extraction_env.py:206`), and 2 reserved for consolidation plus 1 for retain leaves no shared slot, so refreshes would never run. Either reserve the retain slot only when `worker_slots >= 4`, or raise the floor to 4. The floor exists because of the OOM history in #3534, so check the memory cost before raising it.

The box has the drop-in `operator-retain-slot.conf` with this value as a stopgap. Remove it once hal0 renders the setting.

Closes #3698.

## Why

The coding-agents plugin re-sends its commit log (the last 300 commit messages, newest first, as one document) whenever a session starts on a HEAD it has not sent, and every worktree and branch has its own HEAD. The memory engine matches stored chunks by position (`_classify_chunk_diff` in the engine's `retain/orchestrator.py`), so one new commit on top shifts every chunk and the whole document is extracted again: about 220 chunks.

On a live box on 2026-11-15 one of these took more than four hours on the local memory slot. It held up every other retain, and health reported `retain_operations_stalled`.

## What changes

- `/api/memory/compat` lets one retain with strategy `gitlog` through per stored document per `[memory.compat] gitlog_min_interval_s`. The default is one day, and `0` turns it off. `gitlog:` is a shared prefix, so this is one document per project across all clients.

The Hindsight coding-agents plugin re-sends its commit log (the last 300 commit messages, newest first, as one document `gitlog:<repo>`) whenever a session starts on a HEAD that no stored document is tagged with (`deepen.js` `ingestGitLog`, gated on the `gitlog-head:<sha>` tag). One new commit on top shifts every chunk, so the diff is `0 unchanged` and the engine falls back to a full retain: about 220 chunks of 3000 characters, one extraction call each.

issues.body:
### What happens

`GET /api/memory/health` sums the queue (`waiting`, `failed`, `oldest_waiting_s`, `consolidation_pending`, `consolidation_failed`) and the knowledge counts over every bank the engine lists. After the fold-in cuts a box over to the two_bank layout (ADR-0058), the retired pre-fold-in banks (for example `Hal0::Agents`, `pi-coder`, `coding-agent::*`) stay in the engine. Nothing writes to them, auto-consolidation is off for them, and their content already lives in the platform bank, so their counts never drain and are counted twice.

Observed on a folded-in box on 2026-11-15: `consolidation_pending` was 19,054, of which 8,995 sat in retired `Hal0::Agents`. All 63 "failed" operations were in retired banks, so the verdict was `attention / queue_operations_failed` from banks nobody uses.

- Repro in a test: provider with `two_bank=True`, engine with `hal0:shared`, `hal0:private` and a third bank holding failed operations; the verdict is `attention`.

### If nobody fixes it

Operator confusion: Health shows a permanent `attention` verdict and an inflated queue on every folded-in box, and the "oldest waiting" figure points at ingest lag that is not there.

agent_prs.title: docs(xdna): record per-op NPU exclusion with confirm-and-unload (ADR-0059)

issues.body:
## What happens

A per-op `xdna` slot and the FLM slot cannot run at the same time. Whichever one starts second fails to get an NPU hardware context, in either order. A fused `xdna` slot does coexist with FLM, which is what ADR-0057 decision 5 ("NPU coexistence with `flm` is warn-and-time-slice, not exclusion") and the "Coexistence with FLM" section of `docs/guides/run-xdna-npu.mdx` describe. That premise does not hold for per-op models.

Observed on an XDNA2 box (Strix Halo, amdxdna, firmware via the in-tree driver), nightly 1.8.0-nightly.20261114164931, xdna image `72f6dfa-rf1a3931`, FLM 1.0.12 with chat + STT + embed enabled:

1. **Per-op slot up first, then FLM.** `POST /api/slots/flm/load` returns 200, then the FLM container exits 1 and systemd restarts it in a loop:
   ```
   [ERROR]  Failed to load embedding model: DRM_IOCTL_AMDXDNA_CREATE_HWCTX IOCTL failed (err=-22): Invalid argument
   ```
   The slot ends in `error`.
2. **FLM up first, then the per-op slot** (`qwen3.5-0.8b`, UD-Q4_K_XL, `xdna_path: per-op`). `POST /api/slots/<name>/load` returns 500 and the slot ends in `error`. Every per-op kernel fails to load, then the first decode fails:
   ```
   E xdna-runtime: failed to load kernel /opt/xdna/kernels/gemm_int8_int32_M256_K1024_N2048_c8.xclbin: DRM_IOCTL_AMDXDNA_CREATE_HWCTX IOCTL failed (err=-22): Invalid argument
   ... (same for the other gemm_*_c8 kernels and pgemm_c8.xclbin)
   E srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Compute error.
   ```
3. **FLM up first, then the fused slot** (`Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M-so5`, `xdna_path: fused`). It starts, logs no HWCTX errors, answers a chat request, and `/api/npu/occupancy` reports `single_tenant: false` with the shared warning. That case works.

The per-op slot runs fine on its own: it answers, and decode runs at about 8 tok/s.

The cause is not confirmed. The per-op path opens one hardware context for each of several full-array (`_c8`) kernels at load time. The NPU's context or column budget is probably exhauste

issues.body:
## What happens

The NPU tab's status line always shows `—` for power mode and fabric clock, and the GGML lane's power-mode banner can never fire on a real box.

`HardwareStats.snapshot()` produces `npu_pmode` and `npu_fclk` (`src/hal0/hardware/stats.py:327-328`), but `GET /api/stats/hardware` builds its response from a fixed key list (`src/hal0/api/routes/hardware.py:541-578`) that does not forward either key. The UI reads both from that endpoint (`ui/src/api/hooks/useStatsHardware.ts:116-117`, `ui/src/dash/npu/npu-pure.ts:76-77`, `ui/src/dash/npu/ArrayBand.jsx:39`).

There is also a type mismatch: `npu_fclk()` returns the raw token such as `"2000Mhz"` (`stats.py:267-289`), while the UI types it as `number | null` and only shows it when `typeof === 'number'` (`npu-pure.ts:77`). Forwarding the key alone would still show `—`.

## If nobody fixes it

Operators running a GGML slot on a non-turbo power mode never see the warning, so they lose the roughly 15% prefill and 20% decode that turbo gives (see `docs/guides/run-xdna-npu.mdx`). The status line keeps showing `—` even on a box that can report the value.

## Reproduce

On an XDNA2 box on nightly 20261114124338 (main 365eb9884): `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/stats/hardware` returns no `npu_pmode` or `npu_fclk` key. Found during the #3648 live check.

## Fix

Forward both keys from `stats_hardware`, and either parse fclk to MHz as a number on the server or relax the UI check. Note that `xrt-smi` may not be installed (then pmode stays `null`, which the UI already handles as unknown). Add a route test asserting both keys reach the response.

agent_prs.body:
## What
After a runner-image pull (or tag delete) the NPU tab's `npu_engines.xdna.pulled` stayed stale for up to ~60 s.

## Root cause
Two stacked 30 s caches in `api/routes/npu.py` (the facts cache and the image-store cache under it). Invalidating only the outer cache is not enough: the facts refresh would re-read the still-fresh (stale) inner cache and re-cache the old answer for another 30 s. Also, a refresh already in flight when the pull finishes could write its pre-pull read back.

## Changes
- `invalidate_engine_caches()` marks both caches stale, keeping the last value so the facts never flicker to `None`, and bumps a generation counter. Refreshes that started under an older generation discard their result.
- After an invalidation `_local_image_refs()` reads the store inline (its only caller is the facts worker thread, never the request path).
- Called from the runner-pull job's terminal path (`registry/runner_pull_jobs.py`) and from the tag-delete route.

## Verification
- New tests in `tests/api/test_npu_occupancy.py`: stale-then-fresh across both caches (fails on main), in-flight image-store and facts refreshes discarded.
- Call sites covered in `tests/api/test_runner_images_routes.py`: the pull-lifecycle test asserts one invalidation once the job is terminal; the delete-tag test asserts one after a `removed` delete. Each fails with its call site deleted.
- `uv run pytest tests/api/test_npu_occupancy.py tests/api/test_runner_images_routes.py`: 147 passed; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

## Out of scope
CHANGELOG (consolidated PR). UI is unchanged. Not invalidated: the pull a slot load triggers (`slots/image_pull.py`) and the CLI `run_runner_pull` (separate process); a pull started there can still show a stale "not pulled" for up to ~60 s. Follow-up.

Closes #3645

issues.body:
### What happens

`/api/npu/occupancy` reports `npu_engines.xdna.pulled`. That value passes through two 30-second caches in a row (`src/hal0/api/routes/npu.py`): the engine/host facts cache calls `_engine_facts_sync`, which reads the image store through its own 30 s `_local_image_refs` cache. Nothing clears either cache when a runner-image pull finishes. ## Summary

`hal0 memory migrate fold-in` (#3621) carried a coding bank's knowledge pages into `hal0:shared` at the root, under ids the engine chose, with the plugin's own trigger. `/api/memory/compat` (#3634) serves the plugin one `project:<slug>` folder and shows only pages with hal0's project scope and private guard. So after a cutover none of the folded pages showed, and every `metadata.relatedPageId` and `[[page:<id>]]` link pointed at nothing.

With this change, each page a coding bank carries lands in its project's folder, stamped as compat stamps a page. It keeps its name and source query, and the id it had in the old bank still works through compat. ## What happens

`hal0 memory migrate fold-in` (#3621) carries each coding bank's mental models and knowledge pages into `hal0:shared`, but the engine gives the pages fresh ids and the fold-in leaves them at the bank root. Their trigger keeps its old scope, without the private-memory guard. #3634 serves the coding-agents plugin's knowledge base through `/api/memory/compat` from one `project:<slug>` folder per project, and shows only pages that carry the project scope plus that guard. So once a box is folded, compat shows none of the old pages. The plugin's five standard pages rebuild from the folded facts on its next run, but per-initiative pages are lost to the plugin, along with every `[[page:<id>]]` link and the marker memories' `metadata.relatedPageId`. On the reference box that is about 25 initiative pages in `coding-agent::hal0-mono` alone.

## If nobody fixes it

Running the fold-in on a box whose coding agents use knowledge pages throws away their curated initiative history. The data stays on the old bank, unread, and on the target, hidden.

## Proposal

In the fold-in, for each coding bank:
- move its pages into that project's `project:<slug>` folder in `hal0:shared`, creating the folder as compat does;
- re-stamp each page with the owner the fold-in already resolves, plus compat's scope and private guard;
- record a map from old page id to new page id;
- have compat resolve an old id through that map, for links and `relatedPageId`.

The pre-check and the ledger have to cover pages the same way they cover models.

## Fix size

M. It depends on #3634, which defines the folder and the scope.

## Summary

`/api/memory/compat` answered 404 on every knowledge-base route. The Hindsight coding-agents plugin reads that as "this server has no pages", so a plugin pointed at compat lost its knowledge pages at session start, its `hindsight_*_knowledge_page*` tools and `hindsight_capture_initiative`. This PR serves the six knowledge-base routes the plugin calls, with the same bank-to-project mapping, auth, write envelope and read scope as the existing compat routes. ADR-0058 decision 4b anticipated this ("until they are mapped to per-project folders"), and this PR is that mapping.

**Design.** Every bank name is the platform bank, which also holds hal0's own pages and every other project's. Each project therefore gets one folder at the root of the platform bank's tree, named `project:<slug>`. It is created on the first page or folder write, under a per-project lock. If the engine answers that create with 409 (the folder was made concurrently elsewhere), the tree is read again and that folder is used. The plugin is shown that folder's contents as its whole tree. ADR-0058 decision 4b moves coding-agent harnesses off the engine's own port onto hal0's engine-compatible endpoint `/api/memory/compat` (`hal0 memory agents install <harness> --bridge-key-file`, #3613/#3618). ## What was wrong

The engine queues `refresh_mental_model` and `consolidation` operations by itself: after a restore, and when its start-up recovery requeues `processing` rows. The embedder switch's quiet checks gave up after `quiet_s` (120 s) and then read the still-running refresh as a change to the bank. On a box with slow local extraction, a run rolled back with "bank changed while the engine was isolated", which blames a client that isn't there.

## What changes

### Waiting for the engine's own work

- `engine_maintenance` tells the engine's own work apart. When a bank's stats show pending or processing operations, it lists them (`GET /v1/default/banks/{bank}/operations?status=pending|processing`, key `operations`). If every live operation is one of `ENGINE_OPERATION_TYPES` (`refresh_mental_model`, `consolidation`, read from `operation_type` and falling back to `task_type`), and they account for the whole stats count, that work is waited for.
- The wait is bounded by a new `Timeouts.engine_ops_s` (900 s). It applies in `_quiet_state` (after each restore, and in every comparison before a delete or a restore-in-place), in `_wait_quiet` (before a rebuilt copy is deleted), in `_settle` (after the pause), and in the preflight of a real run. If the work doesn't end in time, the error names each operation by type, bank, id and status, and `details["engine_operations"]` carries the same.
- The preflight of a real run waits for that work and then goes on. The 900 s is one budget shared by all banks, not 900 s per bank. If the work doesn't end, the preflight refuses with the new code `engine_operations`, naming the work and stating how long it really waited and the budget. A dry run lists the work as a warning and doesn't wait.
- Any other queued work (a retain, or anything the listing doesn't show) is refused exactly as before. So is engine work queued alongside it.

## What happens

The embedder switch preflight refuses while operations are pending, but the engine can queue a `refresh_mental_model` LLM operation on its own (after a bank restore or after a restart, since startup recovery requeues processing rows). In a CT-class test-rig run of PR #3602, such a refresh on `shared` was still processing during the next switch. The switch's existing "bank changed while isolated" guard fired as designed and the run rolled back, recording the store as mixed. A later run succeeded and cleared the mixed record.

## If nobody fixes it

On a box with slow local extraction, a switch can roll back repeatedly because of refreshes the engine starts itself, and the operator sees a mixed-embedder store until a run finally gets through. No data is lost (the guard and rollback work), but the switch is unreliable and the cause is not obvious from the refusal.

## Reproduce

1. Run `hal0 memory embedder switch <model> --apply` on a bank with auto-refreshing mental models.
2. Immediately run the switch back. The engine has queued a mental-model refresh after the restore; the preflight does not see it as blocking, and the run rolls back mid-way.

## Fix size

S. Have the preflight (and the isolation window) treat engine-originated `refresh_mental_model` and consolidation ops as blocking, or wait for them to settle, and say which op blocked in the message.

Found during the #3602 follow-up live test (#3597).

## What happens

At install time `installer/install.sh` seeds two banks by posting to hal0's `/api/memory/banks/<id>/import` with the ids `shared` and `private:hermes` (around lines 4160-4170). That route forwards the path segment to the engine verbatim (`src/hal0/api/routes/memory_admin.py`, the bank import forward), so the engine gets banks named literally `shared` and `private:hermes`.

Two consequences:

1. **A stray bank on every install.** The provider spells the private namespace `private__hermes` (`src/hal0/memory/hindsight_provider.py`, the namespace-to-bank mapping), and with the default `[memory] unified_bank = true` it uses no private bank at all. The engine bank `private:hermes` is never read or written by hal0 under any setting. A fresh install on a test container shows exactly two banks, `shared` and `private:hermes`.
2. **The configured platform bank is ignored.** `[memory] bank` (ADR-0052) can name a different engine bank behind the `shared` namespace. The installer still seeds `shared`, so on such a box the mission and disposition land on a bank the provider does not use.

## If nobody fixes it

Every box carries a dead bank that shows up in the dashboard's bank list and in counts, and a box with a renamed platform bank starts with an unseeded real bank and a seeded phantom one.

## Reproduce

Fresh install, then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9177/v1/default/banks`.

## Fix size

S. Seed through the provider's own mapping (the Python seeding hook added in #3546 already does this: `provider.platform_bank`, and a private bank only when `unified_bank` is off), and have the installer call that instead of posting literal ids. ADR-0058 decision 7 replaces both ids with `hal0:shared` and `hal0:private`, so this may be best folded into that change.

## What was wrong

`hal0 memory embedder switch --apply` restored each bank into `<bank>.switch-<run>` while the original still existed, then renamed that copy into place. In hindsight-api 1.2.0 (`engine/transfer/importer.py`):

- `_restore_knowledge_pages` gives a node a fresh UUID when its id is still held by another bank. Knowledge-node ids are unique across the whole schema, so every `kf-`/`kp-` id in the copy became a bare UUID.
- `_restore_bank` drops every directive id (`_drop_ids`) when the target id is not the archive's own.
- Neither id can be set from outside: `create_knowledge_page` and `create_directive` mint their own.

The plugin's seeding and `spec_apply` find pages by name, so those were never affected.

A side effect: a copy restored under the temporary id takes that id as its display name when the name was the default, and the rename kept it. Every bank came out named `<bank>.switch-<run>`. A restore into the bank's own id keeps the original name.

The rebuilt copy is now only the check, made before any original is touched. #3572 added an owner rule for directives, but only on the two-bank `hal0:private` bank. Every existing box is legacy unified. A rehearsal on main 315f54cbb found two problems there:

- another agent's `memory_directive_update` rewrote hermes's directive;
- an anonymous MCP caller, or any agent, could create a bank-wide directive. Every agent's reflect loads bank-wide directives, Hermes's included.

## What changes

`src/hal0/memory/hindsight_provider.py`, the directive section. Both MCP mounts (`hal0-memory` and `hal0-admin`'s memory delegates) go through this code. The rule now holds on every bank and in every layout:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| create | stamped `agent:<caller>` + `visibility:private`. The caller's own `agent:`/`visibility:` tags are dropped. |
| update with `tags` | re-stamped the same way, so the directive cannot be made bank-wide or another agent's |
| create / update / delete by an unidentified caller (none, `anonymous`, `unknown`) | 403 `memory.directive_owner_required` (the code #3572 uses) |
| get / update / delete of another agent's private directive | 404 `memory.directive_not_found`, the same answer as a missing directive |
| update / delete of a bank-wide directive (untagged, or tagged without `visibility:private`) | 403 `memory.directive_operator_managed` |
| list | unchanged: the caller's own directives plus the bank-wide ones |

There are two ownership edge cases where the bank, not the `visibility:` tag, decides:

- On `hal0:private`, a directive tagged `agent:<id>` alone belongs to that agent. A reflect there is held to the `agent:` tag only.
- Under the split layout, a directive in the caller's own `private__<id>` bank that carries the caller's `agent:` tag belongs to the caller. No other agent reflects on that bank. An untagged row there (for example one seeded from `spec/templates/private.json`) is hal0-managed, so it is operator-managed like on every other layout.

## Problem
Hindsight 1.2.0 defaults `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_MAX_SLOTS` to 10 (`DEFAULT_WORKER_MAX_SLOTS = 10`, read from the pinned engine's `config.py`). hal0 capped LLM concurrency but never the worker pool, so ten queued tasks ran at once and the engine was OOM-killed 10 times in 17 hours on an 11 GiB box.

- New `[memory.graph].extraction_worker_slots`, default **4**, range 3-32, carried by `ExtractionLimits.worker_slots`.
- Rendered as `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_MAX_SLOTS` in the managed `extraction-model.conf` drop-in, and as the baseline in `installer/systemd/hindsight-api.service`.
- `installer/wrappers/hal0-systemctl` allow-lists the new env name (integer only), as the root-side writer would otherwise refuse the drop-in.
- Settings apply class, dashboard limits panel and TS types updated.
- `hal0 doctor` row `memory_engine_env` now shows the worker slots and LLM concurrency in force. The new key is a managed key, so a unit still on a different value is reported as drift with both numbers, and a key missing from a drop-in that predates it reads "unset (engine default 10; hal0 renders 4)" with `hal0 update` or a memory settings save as the remedy (not daemon-reload plus restart).

The incident peaked at 6.3 GB RSS with 10 slots, so 4 slots roughly keeps the peak to about 40% of that. It is a fixed default, not derived from MemTotal; operators with RAM to spare can raise it.

## What happens

`HindsightProvider.list_mental_models` (src/hal0/memory/hindsight_provider.py:2959) forwards the caller's `detail`, which defaults to none, so the engine lists at its default `metadata` detail. At that detail Hindsight 1.2.0 returns every model with `trigger: null` (checked on a 1.2.0 engine on the test rig: the same model listed at `detail=metadata` has `trigger: null`, at `content` and `full` and on a single GET it has the stored trigger with `exclude_mental_models: true`).

`_readable_models` then judges each row with `read_scope.model_scope_confined_to`, which needs `trigger.exclude_mental_models is True`. With a null trigger no model is ever confined, so while the bank holds another agent's private memory the listing drops every model, the caller's own correctly flagged ones included. A get of the same model works, because a single GET carries the trigger. The knowledge-base tree is not affected: its page nodes carry the effective trigger.

In a bank holding alice's private document (`visibility:private`, `agent:alice`), create a model as bob through hal0 (tags `[agent:bob]`; hal0 sets `exclude_mental_models`). `memory_mental_model_list` as bob without `detail` does not list it; `memory_mental_model_get` as bob returns it.

XS. For listing rows whose `trigger` is not a dict, read the model on its own (as `hal0.memory.model_owner_repair._with_trigger` does), or list at `content` detail and strip the content fields when the caller asked for metadata.

## What

`hal0 doctor perms` expected `0755` for `state/agents/hermes` but a fresh install has `2755`. This PR declares `2755` for the two rows that target that directory (`provision.json`, `venv.pin`) instead of clearing the bit.

## Why 2755 and not "clear setgid"

- `installer/install.sh` makes `/var/lib/hal0` and `state/` setgid `2775` so the hal0 group is inherited by everything beneath. A `mkdir` under it births `state/agents/hermes` setgid, and umask 022 drops group write, which gives `2755`. That is the skeleton working as designed.
- Setgid on a directory only makes new entries inherit the group. It widens nothing, which is the property the old comment ("never widens it") cared about. Every sibling shared dir in the table already declares a setgid mode.
- Clearing it would make the installer's inheritance and the audit fight on every new install.

## About the issue's diagnosis

The issue suspects a numeric `chmod 0755` keeps setgid on directories. That is true of coreutils `chmod`, but `hal0 doctor perms --fix` goes through `nofollow.chmod`, which is `fchmod(2)`, and the kernel sets the mode exactly (checked: `fchmod(fd, 0o755)` on a `2755` directory yields `0755`, and `perms.commit` converges a `2755` dir to `0755` in a temp tree). So I could not reproduce "--fix cannot clear it" from the code; I could not see why it persisted on the reporting box. Declaring `2755` removes the failure without relying on that, and a bare `0755` directory (older installs) is repaired to `2755` by `--fix`.

## Problem
hindsight-api 1.2.0 (`query_analyzer.py`) unpacks each dateparser `search_dates` hit as `(text, date)`. dateparser 1.5.0 returns three-tuples for absolute-date text, so temporal query analysis raised `ValueError`, Hindsight dropped the constraint, and date-bounded recall silently stopped filtering. hal0 pinned only the engine, not its dependencies.

## Evidence
Scratch venv, `hindsight-api==1.2.0`, `DateparserQueryAnalyzer().analyze("README.md updated on November 9, 2026 at 5:10 PM")`:

| dateparser | result |
| --- | --- |
| 1.2.2, 1.3.0, 1.4.0 | ok, constraint 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-09 |
| 1.5.0 | `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` |

- `ENGINE_DEP_CONSTRAINTS = ("dateparser<1.5",)` in `hal0.memory.engine_upgrade`, installed beside the engine pin on a venv rebuild.
- `install.sh` fresh install installs the same constraint (`HINDSIGHT_DEP_CONSTRAINTS`); a lockstep test keeps the two in sync.
- `hal0 update` repairs an engine already at the pin: probe the venv, `pip install` the constrained requirement in place, re-probe, then restart the engine. A failed install never restarts it. Boot-time diagnose mode only logs.

On the live hal0 1.8.0 box, Hindsight 1.2.0's temporal query analyzer crashes on absolute-date text when it is paired with the installed `dateparser` 1.5.0. Hindsight catches the exception and silently drops the temporal constraint, so date-bounded recall returns unfiltered results while logging a warning for every affected query.

The live journal contains **1,924** such warnings in the last 24 hours:

```text
hindsight_api.engine.search.temporal_extraction - Temporal query analysis raised ValueError
(treating as no temporal constraint): too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

## How to reproduce

The installed engine reproduces the failure without any private data or live request:

```sh
cd /var/lib/hal0/memory/hindsight
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from hindsight_api.engine.query_analyzer import DateparserQueryAnalyzer

a = DateparserQueryAnalyzer()
print(a.analyze("README.md updated on November 9, 2026 at 5:10 PM"))
PY
```

```text

  ...
  File ".../hindsight_api/engine/query_analyzer.py", line 455, in analyze

dateparser 1.5.0

`render_showcase_env` rendered the engine's embedder from `[memory.models]`, whose model defaults to `hindsight-ai/hs-embed-1`. agent_prs.body:
## What and why

ADR-0058 decision 2: `hal0 memory embedder switch <model>` is the one way a memory store's embedder changes.

hindsight-api's embedder is instance-wide and a stored vector does not say which model made it, so the only honest way to change the model is to re-embed every bank. The engine does that itself on a bank restore: an export archive never carries embeddings, and `transfer/import` in `restore` mode writes the whole bank into a new id with the engine's current embedder and no LLM call. This PR wraps that in a command that either finishes or leaves the store exactly as it was.

```
hal0 memory embedder switch MODEL [--provider local] [--apply|--dry-run] [--allow-pending] [--json]
hal0 memory embedder switch --resume | --status | --clear-gate [--json]
```

A dry run by default. It is not a client of hal0-api: it runs on the box, as root, and talks to the engine directly. It never asks a question.

Part of #3518

Head `1dde04ba0` was run for real on a test container and every scripted step passed. The isolation was then run live against a real engine; this push (rebased onto #3546 and #3558) adds the proofs and refusals from the last review and has not been run live yet. The command list for it is at the end.

## Isolation: the structural change

hal0's write gate stops every write that goes through hal0. It cannot stop a client that talks to the engine's own port, and almost every remaining defect needed exactly such a client. So for the whole of an `--apply` or `--resume` the engine is taken away from them. All code references below are to `src/hal0/memory/embedder_switch.py` unless a file is named.

**Mechanism.** One drop-in in the engine unit's `.d` directory, `zzzz-hal0-embedder-switch.conf` (`ISOLATION_DROP_IN_NAME`, `:209`):

```ini
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=<the command the unit runs now, with --host 127.0.0.1 --port <private>>
Environment=HINDSIGHT_API_ENABLE_AUTO_CONSOLIDATION=false
```

- The unit sets host and port as `ExecStart`

The showcase drop-in from #3486/#3507 renders `HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_LOCAL_MODEL` from `[memory.models].embeddings_model`, which defaults to `hindsight-ai/hs-embed-1` (`src/hal0/config/schema.py`, `MemoryModelsConfig`). ## What

A bridge key whose client name hal0 reserves (`unknown`, `anonymous`, `unresolved`, `shared`, `admin`, `hermes`, `pi`, any `hal0*`, any `hermes__*`) is now refused wherever a bridge key is accepted, not only when it is minted. A key minted before its name joined the list gets `403 bridge.client_name_reserved` on every non-OPEN path: every `/mcp/*` mount, `/api/memory/compat`, `/api/bridge/me`, and WebSocket upgrades.

## Why

On the `/mcp/memory` mount a bridge principal's client name is its memory identity. `unknown` is the identity stamped on every write whose caller had none (`hal0.memory.envelope.UNKNOWN_AGENT`). ## What happens

Memory writes from a caller with no resolvable identity are stamped `agent:unknown` (`src/hal0/memory/envelope.py`, `UNKNOWN_AGENT`). Private notes are readable by the agent whose `agent:` tag they carry. The bridge key store does not reserve the client name `unknown` on main (`src/hal0/bridge/keys.py`, the reserved-names list), so an operator, or anyone able to mint a key, can create a bridge client called `unknown`. On the `/mcp/memory` mount a bridge principal's client name is the agent identity (`src/hal0/mcp/mcp_mount.py`), so that client reads and can modify every private fact tagged `agent:unknown`.

One live box has 321 facts tagged `agent:unknown`.

PR #3558 reserves `unknown` and `unresolved` for new keys and refuses an existing key with such a name on its own endpoint, but an existing key would still work on the MCP mount.

## If nobody fixes it

A naming accident (or a deliberate choice by someone with key-minting rights but no intent to read others' notes) exposes private memory written by unidentified callers.

## Reproduce

Mint a bridge client named `unknown` with the `memory` scope on a build without #3558; call `memory_recall` through `/mcp/memory`; private facts tagged `agent:unknown` come back.

## Fix size

XS. Refuse reserved names where the bridge principal is resolved (so an existing key with a reserved name is rejected on every mount), not only at mint time. Add `anonymous` and the platform's own agent names to the check if they are not covered.

Resolves H0-192 (memory-slot design §5.6, step 1). Fixes #3393.

## Problem

`hal0_llm_slot_views` translates each NPU slot's `-FLM` id with `flm_id_to_tag_async` on every `hal0/<role>` request (`src/hal0/api/__init__.py:567-577`). That reads the FLM catalog, which expires after 5 minutes (`src/hal0/providers/flm.py:1184`). With the FLM slot stopped, an expired catalog re-probes through `_probe_flm_catalog` (`flm.py:1289`), which launches a one-shot rootful `hal0-flmctl run-list` container.

## Change

- `_FLM_ID_TAG_MEMO` (`src/hal0/providers/flm.py:1208`): `flm_id_to_tag` stores each id it resolves and answers from the memo first; misses are never stored, so an id FLM lists later still resolves.
- `flm_id_to_tag_async` skips the catalog refresh for a memoized id.
- `reset_flm_catalog_cache()` clears the memo (`flm.py:1487`); its caller after an FLM pull is `src/hal0/registry/pull.py:2580`.
- The memo sits in `flm_id_to_tag`, so every caller gets it, including the slot manager stamp (`src/hal0/slots/manager.py:4226-4236`) and `src/hal0/api/routes/v1.py:421,813,1750`.
- Tests: `tests/conftest.py` gets an autouse fixture that empties the memo around each test.
- CHANGELOG `### Fixed` entry.

On "prefer the stamped tag": `flm_tag` exists only in the `model_info` dict built by `_resolve_model_info` (`manager.py:4236`) and handed to the provider (`providers/container.py:2393`). It is not stored on the slot config that `hal0_llm_slot_views` iterates, so reading it there would need new plumbing. The stamp itself calls `flm_id_to_tag_async` (`manager.py:4233`), so the memo covers it with no second copy.

## Verification

- New failing-first test `tests/api/test_llm_slot_views.py::test_llm_slot_views_flm_probe_runs_once_with_expired_cache_and_stopped_slot`: catalog expired three times and later probes return nothing; the probe ran once and the tag still resolved.
- New `tests/providers/test_flm.py::test_flm_id_to_tag_memoizes_hits_and_never_misses`.
- `ruff check src tests`

issues.body:
## Impact

`hermes acp` can't start on a box provisioned by hal0. Anything that drives Hermes over the Agent Client Protocol fails as soon as it launches. For example, the Multica runtime fails every task with `hermes initialize failed: hermes process exited`. Hermes's own gateway, dashboard and MCP still work.

## Cause

The pin in `installer/agents/hermes/requirements.txt:35` is `hermes-agent[web,mcp] @ git+…@4d04303818b6`. Upstream declares the ACP server dependency as its own optional extra, `acp = ["agent-client-protocol==0.9.0"]` in the pinned checkout's `pyproject.toml`. `release_extras()` in `src/hal0/agents/hermes_release.py:403` builds the release from the pin's extras plus the configured gateway platform extras. Nothing in that path adds `acp`, so every immutable release ships without the `acp` module.

## Repro

On a hal0 box:

```
/var/lib/hal0/venvs/hermes/bin/python -c "import acp"
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'acp'

hermes acp
# The ACP server can't start: its protocol packages are missing from this install.
# From the Hermes environment, run: hermes pm install --extra acp
```

`release.json` for the current release lists extras `web, mcp, anthropic, discord, slack, sms, telegram, wecom`, with no `acp`.

## Fix options

1. Add `acp` to the pin's extras (`hermes-agent[web,mcp,acp]`) and update the pin-format assertion in `tests/agents/hermes/test_contract_compatibility.py:550`. The upstream lock already resolves the extra, so the hash-checked `uv export --extra acp` path covers it.
2. Treat `acp` as an opt-in extra, like the platform extras, if hal0 doesn't want the dependency on every box.

Patching the venv in place with `hermes pm install --extra acp` is not a fix. Releases are immutable, and the next rebuild drops the package again.

Size: XS. Because this changes the bundled Hermes install, it should get a release-test pass before merge.

issues.body:
## Impact

Operators who reach the dashboard through a reverse proxy, but haven't set `HAL0_OPENWEBUI_PUBLIC_URL` / `HAL0_COMFYUI_PUBLIC_URL`, get Open WebUI and ComfyUI links that 404 or fail. A user without Traefik or Caddy who later adds any proxy hits this too, and there is no hint about which env var fixes it.

## Where

- `src/hal0/api/routes/config.py:282` (`get_urls`, `_behind_proxy` branch): with no public URL declared, the Open WebUI link becomes `http://<forwarded host>:3001`. The forwarded host is the proxy, and port 3001 on the proxy is not Open WebUI.
- `src/hal0/api/routes/config.py:203` (`_comfyui_link`): same pattern with `:8188`.

## Expected

### What happens

If a client calls `POST /v1/embeddings` (or `/v1/rerank`) naming a model that resolves to a loaded chat slot, hal0 forwards the request to that chat llama-server and passes its error through unchanged:

```
HTTP 501 {"error":{"code":501,"message":"This server does not support embeddings. Start it with `--embeddings`","type":"not_supported_error"}}
```

(for rerank: "Start it with `--reranking`"). This happens even when the embed slot is loaded and could serve the request, and although `/v1/models` labels that model `['chat']` only. The reverse direction (chat to an embed slot) returns a typed 409 `dispatch.capability_mismatch`.

A typed `dispatch.capability_mismatch` naming the slot and the embed/rerank capability, instead of an upstream hint (`--embeddings`) a hal0 user cannot act on. ## Impact

`GET /api/benchmarks/plan` returns `500 Internal Server Error` when any suite under `/etc/hal0/bench/suites/` uses the cell kind `batch`. One bad suite file breaks the plan view for every suite, and the error is logged as `hal0.unhandled` with a full traceback.

## Evidence

Seen on a 1.7.1 nightly box (`hal0-1.7.1-nightly.20261102071057`) at 2026-11-03 06:36 local:

```
[error] hal0.unhandled error="suite 'concurrency': unknown cell kind(s) ['batch'] (known: ['chat', 'embed', 'http_pp', 'http_tg', 'pp', 'rerank', 'reuse', 'tg'])"
"GET /api/benchmarks/plan HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

The traceback runs from `get_plan` into `src/hal0/bench/planner.py:694`, which raises a bare `ValueError`.

The suite is an operator-placed `concurrency.toml` (Tier C `server_ab --mode batch` sweep, `kinds = ["batch"]`, `np = [1, 2, 4, 8]`).

## Inconsistency in the source (origin/main a041dc33)

- `src/hal0/bench/planner.py:80`: `KNOWN_KINDS` does not include `batch`.
- `src/hal0/bench/planner.py:818`: `kind_cost` still has a `"batch": 3` entry.
- `src/hal0/bench/runner.py:132`: `_EXPECTED_S` still has `"batch": 600`.

So `batch` is half removed: the planner rejects it, while the cost and timeout tables still carry it.

## Expected

- An invalid suite should be reported as a per-suite validation error (a 4xx, or a skipped suite with a reason in the plan response), not an unhandled 500 that hides every other suite.
- Decide whether `batch` is a supported kind. If it is, add it to `KNOWN_KINDS` with an adapter. If not, delete the dead `kind_cost` and `_EXPECTED_S` entries.

agent_prs.body:
Fixes #3364

## Cause

The flake is a real bug in the launcher, not in the test harness. `box_firewall_open` in `installer/box/box.sh` (previously lines 748 and 752) decided whether ufw was active with:

```bash
ufw status 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -q '^Status: active'
ufw status 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1, $2}' | grep -qxF "${p}/tcp ALLOW"
```

The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. `head -1` and `grep -q` both exit before `ufw` has finished writing. When `ufw` writes after that point it dies with SIGPIPE (141) and `pipefail` makes the whole pipeline false. An active ufw is then treated as inactive, no ports are opened, and `firewall_allowed()` returns `set()`. That matches the assertion in CI. It only happens when the reader exits first, which is why it shows up on loaded runners and moves between commits. A real `ufw status` with a long rule table hits the same race on an operator's host.

## Fix

Capture `ufw status` into a variable and match on the variable, so no pipe is closed early. The second check uses an `awk` that reads all of its input. The `sort -V | head -1` at `box.sh:537` is left alone: `sort` reads all input before it writes, so it can't SIGPIPE.

I added `test_active_ufw_is_detected_when_its_table_is_written_late`. A `ufw_slow` knob makes the stub write its table after a delay, which turns the race into a deterministic failure. No xfail, skip or retry.

## Reproduction

Local venv, Python 3.12, 20-core box:

- Serial, 30 runs of the single test: 0 failures. The flake does not show without load.
- `pytest tests/installer/test_box_launcher.py -k firewall -n 24 --count 300` (pytest-xdist, pytest-repeat) on unfixed `origin/main`: **16 failed, 884 passed**, with the CI assertion.
- Same command with this change: **900 passed**.
- The new test on the unfixed launcher: fails. With the fix: passes.

## Checks run

- `pytest tests/installer -n 8`: 2275 passed, 1 skipped (needs a hal0 service account).
- `make lint`: clean. `shellcheck -S warning i

issues.body:
Split from #2261 (item 2, hardening). The test-isolation half of #2261 is fixed in #3358.

## Problem

`refresh_path_links()` (`src/hal0/updater/updater.py:3755`) links `Path(sys.prefix) / "bin" / {hal0,hal0-agent}` into `HAL0_PATH_LINK_DST` (`updater.py:3752`, `:3790-3794`) and is guarded only by `os.geteuid() == 0`. It trusts `sys.prefix` without checking that it is the installed venv.

## Impact if nobody fixes it

Any root process that runs `activate_release()` or `hal0 doctor wrappers --fix` from a venv other than the installed one (a dev checkout via `uv run`, an ephemeral uv build env) repoints the system `/usr/local/bin/hal0` and `hal0-agent` at that venv. When that venv is ephemeral the links dangle and `hal0` disappears from `PATH`. That is the failure observed in #2261.

## Proposed fix

Require `sys.prefix` to resolve under `_usr_lib_root()` (or the FHS venv). Otherwise log a warning and return `"skipped"` for each link. Add a test that drives it with a `sys.prefix` outside the installed venv.

Recovery today: `sudo /usr/lib/hal0/venv/bin/hal0 doctor wrappers --fix`.

Size: XS-S.

issues.body:
## Summary

Running the backend test suite as **root** on an installed box rewrites the host's real `/usr/local/bin/hal0` and `/usr/local/bin/hal0-agent` symlinks to point into the test runner's virtualenv. When that virtualenv is ephemeral (a uv build/run env under `/root/.cache/uv/...`), the links dangle once the run exits and `hal0` disappears from `PATH`.

Observed on the fleet test box during the v1.3.0 gate run (suite run as root from a checkout at `49d91293`):

```
/usr/local/bin/hal0       -> /root/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpPajMcC/bin/hal0        (target gone)
/usr/local/bin/hal0-agent -> /root/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpPajMcC/bin/hal0-agent  (target gone)
```

Both link mtimes match the test run to the second. Over ssh, `hal0: command not found`. Sudoers, `/usr/lib/hal0/bin` wrappers and `hal0-gpu-perms.service` were **not** modified.

## Cause

`activate_release()` unconditionally calls `refresh_path_links()` (`src/hal0/updater/updater.py:4244`). `refresh_path_links()` is guarded only by `os.geteuid() == 0` and links from `Path(sys.prefix) / "bin"` into `HAL0_PATH_LINK_DST` (`updater.py:4122`, `:4125-4170`).

Tests that drive `activate_release()` redirect `_usr_lib_root()` but not `HAL0_PATH_LINK_DST`, and assume the suite is non-root:

- `tests/updater/test_wrapper_refresh.py:233` — `test_activate_release_includes_wrappers_refreshed_key` (its docstring: "Under test (non-root) it must be an empty list")
- `tests/updater/test_privileged_seam.py:404` — `test_activate_release_swaps_the_symlink_and_reports_previous`

`tests/updater/test_path_link_refresh.py` does redirect `HAL0_PATH_LINK_DST` and fakes `geteuid`, so the dedicated tests are safe; the integration tests are not.

## Proposed fix

1. Test isolation: an autouse fixture (updater conftest, or top-level) that points `HAL0_PATH_LINK_DST` at `tmp_path` and forces the privileged `refresh_*` helpers' destinations into temp dirs, so no test can write host system paths regardless of euid.
2. Hardening (product)

## What happens

After #2778 (fixes #2747), `HindsightProvider.delete()` refuses an observation id that maps to more than one source document with `memory.delete.observation_multi_source`. In unified mode the resolution and the refusal run before any delete (`src/hal0/memory/hindsight_provider.py`, the `_deletable_ids` then `_refuse_multi_source` calls at the top of `delete()`). In legacy multi-bank mode the loop deletes the call's plain document ids first and resolves observation ids afterwards, so in a multi-id call the refusal can fire after earlier documents in the same call are already gone, and the response then carries no deleted count for them.

Blast radius is nil: those document ids were named explicitly by the caller, and a call with more than one id already goes through the approval gate (`src/hal0/mcp/admin.py` `is_gated`). A single-id legacy call cannot partially delete.

## If nobody fixes it

A legacy-mode bulk delete that mixes document ids and a multi-source observation id deletes the documents, then reports a refusal with no count, so the caller has to re-list to learn what happened.

## Fix

Resolve every id first (documents and observations), refuse if any observation is multi-source, then delete, in legacy mode as unified mode already does. One test: legacy, `["doc-a", OBS_multi]`, assert nothing deleted and the typed refusal.

Fix size: XS. Found during the review of PR #2778. Legacy multi-bank mode is not the default.
issues.title: memory: legacy multi-bank delete removes plain document ids before resolving observation ids, so a multi-source refusal can land after part of the call was deleted

## Summary

`scripts/harness.sh` recorded each tier's exit code (`INSTALLER_RC` ... `CLEANUP_RC`) but never read it. A tier script that crashed left its rows `missing` and the run could still end in `harness OK` (exit 0). This is a contributor-only harness (no CI job runs it).

issues.body:
**What happens if nobody fixes it**

`scripts/harness.sh:79-84` records each tier script's exit code in `INSTALLER_RC`, `CLI_RC`, `RUNTIME_RC`, `AGENTS_RC` and `CLEANUP_RC`, but never reads them (shellcheck SC2034). The comment just above those lines says a crash aborts the run; it does not.

A tier script that crashes mid-run, for example under `set -e` or with a syntax error, leaves its remaining rows as `status: "missing"` in the report, and the exit decision counts only `fail` rows. So a run where a whole tier crashed can still end in `harness OK` and exit 0.

**Reproduce**

Make `tests/harness/cli-test.sh` `exit 3` on its first line, then run `make harness`. The exit status is still 0.

**Fix**

Fail the run (and name the tier) when any `*_RC` is non-zero. With #2349's gate, that can be passed to `scripts/harness-gate.py` or checked just before it.

**Fix size:** XS

_Found while fixing #2349._

issues.body:
## Impact

`store.path_escape_warn` is logged on every resolve for a running slot whose model file lives outside the model store root. On a 1.7.1 nightly box with four such slots it fired 1,668 times in 64 minutes (about 26 per minute), which accounts for a large share of hal0-api's journal volume (162 MB in 24 hours across hal0-api and the agent unit).

## Evidence

```
WARNING  store.path_escape_warn  store.py:126
         path=<external-mount>/hy-memory-30b-a3b/... store_root=/var/lib/hal0/models
```

Counts by model path between 06:03 and 07:07 on 2026-11-03: hy-memory 1,001, gemma4 479, lfm2.5 115, qwopus 73.

Source (origin/main a041dc33): `src/hal0/providers/container.py:738` calls `assert_under_store(str(path), severity="warn")` for an already-running slot. `src/hal0/config/store.py:126` then logs a warning on every call. Status polling resolves these paths constantly, so the warning repeats without limit for a configuration that is stable and intentional (registered models on a separate mount).

## Expected

Warn once per (slot, path), for example on adoption or start, or move the repeated case to debug level. Alternatively, if external model paths are supported, recognise registered external paths and skip the warning. The warning should still fire the first time a path escapes the store.

Size: XS–S.

`hermes reprovision --repair` keeps a model the operator picked in Hermes (#3309) and says so once, as a terminal print (#3315). A root-run converge or install wrote `hermes.pin-override`, `openwebui.pin-override`, the Hermes `provision.json` and `venv.pin` for the first time as root-owned files, so the unprivileged `hal0` service could not rewrite them. - New `doctor perms` rows: `state/*.pin-override` (0644), and `state/agents/hermes` `provision.json` / `venv.pin` (0644, directory 0755 as install-time mkdir births it). No mode is widened and no new privilege is granted; the owner copied is the one that already controls the directory.

issues.body:
## What happens

The Memory page follows the `shared` bank. `GET /api/memory/graph/status` sums `failed_operations` over every bank into one `errors` number (`_augment_build_counters`, `src/hal0/api/routes/memory.py`), so a bank other than `shared` that fails every retain only moves that total. The page never names the bank. In #3215 a coding-agent bank had 7,227 failed operations for nine days and the page showed no bank-level signal.

## What happens if nobody fixes it

An operator sees "N errors" and "Retry N failed" but cannot tell which bank is failing or whether it is the one they care about, so a misconfigured bank is found by reading the Hindsight operation log by hand.

## Reproduce

Retain into any non-`shared` bank until operations fail, then open Settings > Data > Memory: only the summed `errors` count changes.

## Fix

Return per-bank failed counts from the status endpoint (the stats walk already reads them) and render the non-zero ones as a `warnings` Banner using the pattern in `ui/src/dash/settings/pages/data/extractionThroughput.js`. The cap-vs-chunk warning itself shipped with the #3215 fix (PR for fix/3215-retain-completion-cap); this is only the per-bank counts. Size: S-M.

Related: #3215, #2798.

## What was wrong

`commit_scan_rows` (the `POST /api/models/scan` commit path) never checked for halogen companion files. A row pointing at an ngram table, vision sidecar, mtp head or overlay `.hgn` file was registered as a model, which a slot cannot load. #3277 closed this for add-from-path only.

## Fix

The companion check and its message moved out of `add_from_path` into `halogen_companion_refusal()` in `src/hal0/services/models_service.py`. Add-from-path raises it, unchanged (same `models.halogen_companion` code, message and details). `commit_scan_rows` calls the same helper before detection and before the row is built.

**Per-row skip, not a 409 for the whole request.** `commit_scan_rows` already reports every per-row refusal (`image_asset`, `invalid_provider`, `invalid_model`, facts screening via `Hal0Error`, `already_registered`) as an entry in `skipped` and keeps committing the rest of the batch. The companion refusal follows that convention: `{"path", "reason": "models.halogen_companion", "message": <same hint as add-from-path>}`, matching the existing `Hal0Error` skip shape. Failing the whole request would discard the valid checkpoint rows next to it.

- New `tests/registry/test_discover_comfyui_skip.py::test_scan_commit_skips_halogen_companion_keeps_checkpoint`: a companion row is skipped with the code and checkpoint hint, and the checkpoint row beside it registers. Fails without the fix (verified by stashing the src change).

agent_prs.body:
## What was wrong

`SlotManager._halogen_sentinel` treated only `probe_timeout` as ambiguous. A single `probe_transport_error` or `probe_http_5xx` on the first real chat turn after `/health` went ok raised `SlotOutputSanityFailed`, stopping the unit and discarding a load that can take minutes. The generic output-sanity gate follows "no corroboration, no conviction"; the halogen path did not.

## Summary

`test_board_socket_survives_rotation_that_keeps_sessions` failed at random with `concurrent.futures.CancelledError`. The test was right; the defect is in the proxy's teardown.

`proxy_board_events` cancelled its two pumps and waited with `asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)`. If the caller is cancelled during that wait and a pump is still unwinding, gather raises the pump's `CancelledError` instead of the caller's, and `return_exceptions` does not change that. The pump's error does not carry anyio's "Cancelled via cancel scope" message, so the scope around the route (`CancelScope.__exit__`, `is_anyio_cancellation`) does not recognise it and lets it escape. `BlockingPortal._call_func` then cancels the future, and `fut.result` raises in `WebSocketTestSession.__exit__`. The window is about one event loop iteration: `TestClient`'s `cs.cancel` has to land right after the proxy starts its teardown, which is why it needs a loaded machine.

**Production impact is small.** Reading Starlette's and FastAPI's websocket path and hal0's middleware, I found no anyio scope around this route under uvicorn, so the escaping exception itself looks like a `TestClient` symptom. The same interrupted wait did have one real effect: it skipped the `cm.__aexit__` and browser close below it, so a task cancel in that window left the upstream socket unclosed. The likely source of such a cancel in production is process shutdown; I did not exercise that against a live server, only with the regression test.

- `asyncio.wait` replaces `gather`. It does not forward cancellation to the children, which are already cancelled, and the caller keeps its own `CancelledError`.
- The closes move into a `finally`, so a cancel during the wait cannot skip them.

Stopping `hal0-agent@hermes` overran `TimeoutStopSec=15` because the shim (the unit's main process) outlived its child, not because the dashboard ignored SIGTERM.

## What happens

Stopping `hal0-agent@hermes.service` regularly runs past the unit's 15 s stop timeout (`TimeoutStopUSec=15s`), and systemd SIGKILLs the agent:

```
hal0-agent@hermes.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.
hal0-agent@hermes.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
hal0-agent@hermes.service: Failed with result 'timeout'.
```

On a test box this happened on 2026-10-14, 10-19, 10-20 and twice on 10-21. It is not new with the Hermes release layout (#2851): the first three predate it. Since #2851, every Hermes release activation stops the agent, and so does the flip-back after a failed re-verify. Each one now takes 15 s longer than it needs to, and each one SIGKILLs the dashboard process instead of letting it shut down cleanly. It also happened when stopping an agent that had been running for only 17 s.

## If nobody fixes it

Every `hal0 update` that changes the Hermes release, and every flip-back, takes 15 s longer and ends with a SIGKILL. The unit is recorded as `Failed with result 'timeout'`, which looks like a fault in the journal and in `systemctl status`. Anything the dashboard or agent does on SIGTERM (flushing state, closing sessions) is cut off.

## Reproduce

On an install with the agent running: `systemctl stop hal0-agent@hermes`, then `journalctl -u hal0-agent@hermes -n 10`. The stop takes about 16 s and ends with the SIGKILL lines above. The unit runs `ExecStop=/usr/local/bin/hal0-agent hermes stop` with `KillMode=control-group`.

## Fix size

S. Find which child process ignores or outlives SIGTERM (the dashboard process or `hal0-agent hermes stop` itself), then make it exit promptly or forward the signal.

On netavark 1.4 with the iptables-nft backend there is no `inet netavark` nft table to list. Netavark's rules live in the iptables-nft `nat` table instead: `iptables -t nat -S` on the same box shows `NETAVARK-HOSTPORT-DNAT` and `NETAVARK-HOSTPORT-MASQ` chains, with container ports published and working.

So the row is a false positive (the box is healthy), and it also means the stale-DNAT detector from #1814 cannot run on this netavark. A leaked rule would not be seen on such a box.

### How to reproduce

1. Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 (podman 4.9.3, netavark 1.4.0), install hal0 1.7.1, and run at least one slot so a published slot port exists.
2. `hal0 doctor all` shows the `Port DNAT rules` WARN above.
3. `sudo nft list table inet netavark` fails with `No such file or directory`; `sudo iptables -t nat -S | grep NETAVARK-HOSTPORT` lists the chains.

Every `hal0 doctor` run on stock Ubuntu 24.04 shows a WARN that sends the operator looking for a firewall problem that does not exist, and a real stale-DNAT port black hole on such a box (the failure #1814 describes) goes unreported.

While the img slot is held back by the crash-loop breaker, every image request still unloads the LLM set before it gets refused. Chat drops, the LLMs reload, and the image request fails anyway.

Closes #3307.

## Problem

`_has_retired_tuning` reads the schema, then queries the tables and columns it saw, in separate autocommit reads. A second connection committing migration 015 in between makes the query raise `no such table: legacy_model_tuning` or `no such column: preferred_runner`. This turned `test_concurrent_adds_do_not_lose_rows` red on `python (3.12)` in #3306, whose diff doesn't touch this code. On a real box it would be a failed first request after updating to a release carrying 015.

## Change

The reads now run in one read transaction, so they share a WAL snapshot. The peer's commit still goes through, because a WAL reader doesn't block a writer. The transaction ends before the backup's `VACUUM INTO`, and a caller's own open transaction is left alone (the `check_migration_015` doctor row from #3302 is the second caller, on a read-only connection).

## Tests

A connection subclass applies the peer's drop at the exact point between the reads, for both errors. Both fail on the old code with those errors. A third test covers the caller's open transaction.

`tests/db` and `tests/registry`: 811 passed. Not run: the full suite locally, or a live box.

This touches the migration runner, so it needs an operator merge. Rebased on main with #3302; the new read error test covers an automatic rollback mid-check.

## What happens

When two connections run `migrate()` on a database that still needs migration 015, the one inspecting the database for the pre-015 backup can crash with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: legacy_model_tuning` or `no such column: preferred_runner`.

`_has_retired_tuning` (`src/hal0/db/migrate.py:132`) reads the schema, then queries the tables and columns it saw. These are separate reads in autocommit, so another connection can commit 015 between them. Its docstring says it handles this by reading the live schema, but the gap between that read and the query remains.

Seen in CI on `python (3.12)`, PR #3306, whose diff does not touch this code: `tests/registry/test_sqlite_store.py::TestConcurrency::test_concurrent_adds_do_not_lose_rows` failed with `assert 40 == (12 * 4)`. Two writer threads died with those two errors, from `_ensure_migrated` to `_backup_before_tuning_drop` to `_has_retired_tuning`. The test is timing-dependent; `python (3.14)` passed on the same commit.

Expected: the inspection sees one consistent view of the database and never raises because a peer finished 015.

## How to reproduce

Run that test repeatedly on a loaded machine, or use the deterministic form: apply 015's drops from a second connection between the first connection's `sqlite_master` read and its next query.

The first requests after updating to a release carrying 015 can fail with an unhandled 500 on any path that migrates on first use (registry store, slot identity table, port authority). The database is not damaged, and a retry succeeds. CI also goes red at random on unrelated PRs.

## Fix

Run the inspection inside a read transaction, so its reads share one WAL snapshot. Add the deterministic test above for both errors.

agent_prs.title: fix(installer): skip the hal0 subuid range inside a nested user namespace

issues.body:
### What happens

The installer gives the `hal0` service user a subordinate uid/gid range of `100000:65536` without checking whether that range exists in the machine's own uid map. Inside an unprivileged LXC or Incus container it does not: the container's own map is `0 100000 65536`, so it owns ids 0 to 65535 only, and ids 100000 to 165535 are not mapped for it. Rootless podman as `hal0` then cannot build a user namespace.

On an unprivileged Ubuntu 24.04 LXC (Proxmox VE 9.2, kernel 7.0.6-pve) the install ends with:

```
OK  allocated rootless uid/gid range 100000:65536 for hal0
...
!!  podman system migrate (as hal0) failed — run it once as the hal0 user before the first dashboard image pull
```

Running it by hand, as `hal0`, with `/var/lib/hal0` already `hal0:hal0 2775` so the earlier "VAR_DIR still root-owned" reason does not apply:

```
level=error msg="running `/usr/bin/newuidmap 25607 0 999 1 1 100000 65536`: newuidmap: write to uid_map failed: Operation not permitted"
Error: cannot set up namespace using "/usr/bin/newuidmap": exit status 1
```

`podman info` and `podman unshare cat /proc/self/uid_map` as `hal0` fail the same way (exit 125). `newuidmap` is setuid root and `max_user_namespaces` is 2147483647, so it is not a missing setuid bit or a userns limit. A single-uid namespace works (`sudo -u hal0 unshare --user --map-root-user cat /proc/self/uid_map` prints `0 999 1`); only the multi-id map via subuid fails.

The code: `installer/install.sh:994-995` hardcodes `SUB_START=100000` / `SUB_COUNT=65536` (then moves the start past any range already claimed in `/etc/subuid` / `/etc/subgid`), writes the entries at `:1000-1013`, sets `HAL0_SUBUID_JUST_ALLOCATED=1` at `:1015`, and the migrate runs at `:3562-3563`. The start value assumes the full 32-bit host uid space. `hal0_lxc_kind` (`installer/lib/preflight.sh:162`) already classifies the box as `lxc-unprivileged` from `/proc/self/uid_map`, but the subuid block does not consult it. This is the failure #2119 fi

issues.body:
### What happens

`hal0 update` never rewrites `hal0-api.service`. The unit is generated only by `installer/install.sh` (heredoc at `installer/install.sh:1918-1970`), so a box installed on an older release keeps that release's unit forever, whatever later releases change in it.

A box upgraded in place to 1.7.1 shows it:

```
$ systemctl show hal0-api -p TimeoutStopUSec
TimeoutStopUSec=1min 30s
```

The current installer writes `TimeoutStopSec=30` (`installer/install.sh:1967`, added for #2727), and `systemctl cat hal0-api` on that box has no `TimeoutStopSec` line at all. The same gap is why the box lacked the `systemd-journal` group added in #2435 and needed a hand-written drop-in (the product fix for the symptom was #2911).

The updater already has the right shape for this. `refresh_gpu_perms_unit` (#1953, `src/hal0/updater/updater.py:3160`) and `refresh_privileged_wrappers` (#1689, `:3321`) re-install units and wrappers from the activated release on the privileged side. Slot units are re-rendered by `rerender_slot_units` (`:2907`). `hal0-api.service` is the one hal0-owned unit with no refresh path.

### How to reproduce

1. Install an older release (for example 1.5.0) with `install.sh`.
2. `hal0 update` to current main or 1.7.1.
3. `systemctl show hal0-api -p TimeoutStopUSec` reports the 90 s default; `systemctl cat hal0-api` differs from what `install.sh` writes today.

Every fix that lands in the API unit (stop budget, supplementary groups, environment files, hardening) reaches fresh installs only. Upgraded boxes drift further each release, and each drift turns into a one-off field repair like the journal-group drop-in. A hung stop step waits 90 s for SIGKILL instead of 30 s, which stretches the API outage during updates.

M. Move the unit body out of the `install.sh` heredoc into a template shipped in the release tree, render it from both `install.sh` and a new privileged-side `refresh_api_unit` that follow

### What you want

`POST /api/agent/approvals/{id}/approve` and `POST /api/agent/approvals/{id}/deny` should accept only a browser admin session (the operator's dashboard cookie) or the CLI acting as root. A bare `Authorization: Bearer` key of any tier — admin, client, or the new bridge tier — should be refused on these two routes.

This is item 2 of ADR-0024 (`docs/adr/0024-agent-credential-tier.md`), which is still PROPOSED. ADR-0043 (agent bridge) lands items 1 and 3 for bridge principals and leaves this one open.

### Why, and what it unlocks

The owner-approval queue is the control that stops an agent taking a destructive action on its own. Today the two decision routes are ordinary ADMIN routes (`src/hal0/api/routes/approvals.py:111` and `:140`): they check the tier, not who is deciding. The bundled Hermes agent authenticates to hal0 with a literal copy of the box admin key (`HAL0_MCP_TOKEN`, written by `hermes_provision.py`), so with the terminal toolset enabled a prompt-injected agent can approve its own queued call with one `curl`. The admin MCP server already hides `approval_approve`/`approval_deny` from agents (`src/hal0/mcp/admin.py`, `EXCLUDED_TOOLS`), but the REST route behind them does not know the difference.

Closing this makes the inbox a real gate rather than an advisory one, which is what ADR-0004 promises.

The approval gate stays bypassable by any key holder. The bridge (ADR-0043) does not widen the hole — bridge keys are refused on `/api/*` — but every box where Hermes has the terminal tool keeps the self-approval path ADR-0002 documents as an accepted risk.

agent_prs.title: fix(slots): end the readiness wait when the slot unit is already parked

issues.body:
## What happens

An explicit `POST /api/slots/<slot>/load` of a model that llama-server cannot load blocks for the full `HEALTH_TIMEOUT_S` (180 s, `src/hal0/slot_lifecycle_budget.py:31`) before it returns the correct `500 slot.spawn_failed`. This happens even though the runner exits 64 about 0.3-1.3 s after start and `RestartPreventExitStatus=64` makes systemd park the unit terminally (`ActiveState=failed, NRestarts=0, ExecMainStatus=64`) at once.

Cause: `ContainerProvider.wait_ready` (`providers/container.py` ~2023-2037) polls only `/health`, and `SlotManager.load` checks `unit_failure_reason` (`slots/manager.py` ~1893-1908) only after the timeout returns WARMING. During the window the API shows `state=warming, container_status=crashed`, empty `metadata.message`.

A load sent while the unit is already parked `failed` behaves the same: load calls `reset_failed` and restarts the unit (the retry is intended, #1424), the unit dies again in ~1 s, and the request still waits ~182 s.

This conflicts with the #2037/#2039 CHANGELOG line (CHANGELOG.md:3718-3720): "A doomed model load ran to its full timeout — the runner entrypoint now exits 64 so the load fails fast instead of burning the budget". The rationale in known-issue `crash-loop-warming-180s-window` (protect a slow load from a racing watchdog) predates #2037 and does not apply to a unit systemd already holds terminal with exit 64.

## What should happen

`wait_ready` should notice a terminal unit (ExecMainStatus in {64, 132}, or ActiveState=failed with NRestarts=0) and return early, so the load fails in seconds with the same `slot.spawn_failed` envelope.

## How to reproduce

agent_prs.body:
## What

hal0 never set `HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_WALL_TIMEOUT`, so Hindsight's 3600 s default applied. With `llm_timeout_s` also 3600 the limit could fire inside a single LLM call. hal0 now derives the limit and writes it from the same drop-in as the other extraction limits.


## Formula

```
per_call = llm_timeout_s x (extraction_llm_retries + 1)
wall     = max(min(max(3600, 3 x per_call), 14400), per_call + llm_timeout_s)
```

- Always strictly above one call's whole retry budget, so a call is never cut mid-flight.
- Never below Hindsight's own 3600 s, so no document that fits today starts failing. Defaults (300 s, 1 retry) give 3600 s.
- Capped at 4 h: a limit too high lets one document hold the single extraction lane (`extraction_max_concurrent = 1`). Only an operator-chosen per-call budget already past the cap raises it (3600 s x 6 attempts -> 25200 s), because the limit must stay above one call. The box in #3214 (3600 s, 1 retry) gets 14400 s.
- No new config field: it is a function of two existing ones, documented on `llm_timeout_s` and `extraction_llm_retries`. The root-side drop-in validator (`hal0-systemctl`) accepts the new name; `hal0 update` already refreshes the wrapper (#1689). A drop-in that predates this change reads as drift and is rewritten on the next graph save.

## Engine behaviour (hindsight-api 1.1.0, read from the wheel)

`worker/poller.py`: the retain ceiling is an absolute `asyncio.timeout`; on expiry the task is `_mark_all_failed` with the "exceeded the Ns wall-clock limit" message. That is terminal, so a wall-limit cancellation is neither retried nor counted toward `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_MAX_RETRIES`; `retry_count` stays untouched. Only `RetryTaskAt` (worker-retryable errors) and startup recovery of a stuck `processing` row increment it. So the re-run described in #3214 is not the wall limit itself; the lasting fix is that the limit now sits above a call and is bounded.

## Not in this PR

Flagging long-running operations and cancel on the M

### What happens

On a fresh install, a root process writes the component-state file first. The installer runs `run_post_activation_migrations()` as root in a heredoc (`installer/install.sh:2995-2997`). That calls `converge_components` and then `record_component_result` (`updater.py:1994` -> `state.py:42`), which creates `/var/lib/hal0/state/` as `root:root 0755` and `components.json` as root `0600` (mkstemp mode). hal0-api (`User=hal0`) starts about one second later; its boot-time converge diagnose then fails for all four components with `components.state_persist_failed` EACCES on mkstemp in the directory.

Add a `PermRow` for `var_lib/state` (`hal0:hal0 2775`, covering `components.json`) so `doctor perms` reports and fixes it, or chown `state/` in the installer right after the migration step.

issues.body:
## What happens

A fresh `install.sh` run inside an **unprivileged** Ubuntu 24.04 LXC with `features: nesting=1,keyctl=1,fuse=1,mknod=1` already set fails the required container-runtime gate:

```
OK  podman: 4.9.3
XX  podman info/version succeeded but 'podman run' failed — the runtime can't actually launch a container
!!    inside an unprivileged Proxmox/LXC container this needs 'features: nesting=1' (and often keyctl=1)
!!    set it in /etc/pve/lxc/<CTID>.conf on the PROXMOX HOST, then: pct stop <CTID> && pct start <CTID>
XX  no container runtime — install podman (see above), then re-run install.sh
```

The remedy is wrong: nesting and keyctl were on. The real failure, from the smoke test itself:

```
Error: initializing source docker://quay.io/podman/hello:latest: pinging container registry quay.io:
  Get "https://quay.io/v2/": dial tcp: lookup quay.io on 9.9.9.9:53: dial udp 9.9.9.9:53: socket: permission denied
```

`curl`, `apt` and a Python `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM)` all work in the same shell. Only podman cannot create a socket.

## Root cause

Ubuntu 24.04 (apparmor 4.0.0-beta3) ships `/etc/apparmor.d/podman`, `crun`, `buildah`, `runc`, `rootlesskit` and `slirp4netns` as `flags=(unconfined)` profiles whose only purpose is to grant `userns` on a host with `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`:

```
abi <abi/4.0>,
profile podman /usr/bin/podman flags=(unconfined) {
  userns,
}
```

With `lxc.apparmor.allow_nesting = 1` (what the `nesting=1` feature turns on) the guest loads those profiles into its nested policy namespace. On a current host kernel with fine-grained network mediation the nested "unconfined" profile is enforced for the network class and has no inet rule, so every `socket()` from `/usr/bin/podman` is denied. The host kernel log says exactly that:

```
audit: type=1400 apparmor="DENIED" operation="create" class="net" info="failed af match" error=-13
  namespace="root//lxc-<id>_<-var-lib-lxc>" profile="podman" comm="podman" family="inet" soc
issues.title: installer: unprivileged Ubuntu 24.04 LXC fails the podman smoke with 'socket: permission denied' (guest unconfined-flag AppArmor profiles); preflight blames nesting=1

issues.body:
### What happens

On a fresh install the installer runs as root and binds the brain model ("brain model ready: lfm2.5-2.6b bound to the 'brain' slot", install log line 754). That registration calls `tombstones.clear()`, which takes `_locked()` unconditionally, and `_locked()` does `os.open(lock, O_RDWR|O_CREAT, 0o664)` (`registry/tombstones.py:59`) with no fchmod. Under umask 022 the sidecar is born `/var/lib/hal0/registry/ignored-paths.json.lock` root:hal0 0644. hal0-api runs as `User=hal0`, opens it O_RDWR, gets EACCES, and every later tombstone read-modify-write (model add, add-from-path, scan commit/auto-register, pull completion, delete) logs `tombstones.lock_failed ... [Errno 13] Permission denied` and holds only the in-process threading lock. The cross-process flock — which the `_locked()` docstring and ADR-0026 say exists to serialise "a root-run CLI next to the API" — is permanently disabled.

Permanent, not self-healing like #2670: `os.open` never replaces the file, and `install/perms.py` has `*.lock` rows only for `/etc/hal0` and the `/var/lib/hal0` top level (`perms.py:440-451`), none for `registry/*.lock`, so `hal0 doctor perms` prints "ownership clean" rc 0 and `--fix` would not repair it.

### What should happen

The lock sidecar should be 0664 hal0-writable however it is created: fchmod 0o664 after O_CREAT in `_locked()` (as `_write()` already does for the JSON at line 123), and/or a PermRow for `registry/` with `glob="*.lock"` and `child_mode=0o664`; or fall back to an O_RDONLY open for the flock.

### What you want

Move the vendored `@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` dependency from 0.8.1 to 0.8.3 in `src/hal0/agents/pi_coder/plugins/hindsight/package.json` (and the matching `HINDSIGHT_PIN="0.8.1"` check in `scripts/smoke-pi.sh`), and set the package's `autoUpdate` option to false wherever hal0 writes its config, so the version hal0 ships is the version that runs. ### Why, and what it unlocks

A pin that is silently overridden by a daily self-update is not a pin: the Pi agent's memory behaviour can change under an operator between hal0 releases, and the release notes cannot describe what the box runs. Bumping restores the one-owner rule for this version and takes the two behavioural fixes.

issues.body:
### What happens

`hal0 agent reprovision hermes` adds a `model_aliases.<slot>` entry to `/var/lib/hal0/.hermes/config.yaml` for each llm slot with a model, but never removes the entry for a slot that has since been deleted. Aliases are written only through additive `hermes config set` pairs (`src/hal0/agents/hermes_provision.py:2040-2045`), and `_merge_config_yaml_layers` (`:2490`) only deep-merges ("merge, never clobber"). The only removal path in the file is `_prune_mcp_servers_yaml` (`:2297`, #2332), which covers `mcp_servers` only.

What a user sees: the dead alias is NOT in the `/model` picker (that lists the gateway's live `/v1/models`), but `/model <dead-alias>` still resolves to the stored `model:` value (`model_switch.py:737-739`) — if another slot still serves that model the request quietly goes there; otherwise the gateway returns 404 `dispatch.no_route`. Hermes's status bar picks the shortest alias for the current model (`_reverse_alias_for_display`), so a dead alias with a shorter name can mislabel the live model.

### What should happen

Track which aliases hal0 wrote and prune the ones whose slots no longer exist, the way #2332 does for `mcp_servers`. Do not wipe the whole `model_aliases` table (hermes documents it as user config).

### How to reproduce

```sh
hal0 slot create skal --type llm --hardware vulkan --model lfm2.5-2.6b --port 8197
hal0 agent reprovision hermes </dev/null; grep -n '^  skal:' /var/lib/hal0/.hermes/config.yaml   # present
echo y | hal0 slot delete skal; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' :8080/api/slots/skal     # 404
hal0 agent reprovision hermes </dev/null; grep -n '^  skal:' /var/lib/hal0/.hermes/config.yaml   # still present
