agent_prs.body:
Closes #2944

## Problem
A `/v1` request for an unloaded model drove `SlotManager.load` and waited for it. If the client left, the request kept waiting out the ready timeout, and the dispatcher's own load, entered next, recovered the stale `WARMING` state and started a second cold load.

## Change
- `hal0.slots.abandon`: a contextvar carrying a client-gone probe, plus `ClientGoneProbe` and `wait_for_load`.
- The probe listens for the next ASGI message (`http.disconnect`) rather than calling `Request.is_disconnected()`, which reads under an already-cancelled scope and can miss a disconnect (see `live_sockets.guard_http_stream`, and `_client_has_gone` in `v1.py`). It is sticky and serialised, so the handler's polling and the load task never read `receive` at once.
- `_dispatch_and_forward` (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank, audio, speech) publishes the probe. It returns 499 before dispatch if the client left during a load that took 0.5 s or more, so the dispatcher never enters its own load. Fast requests pay no probe.
- `SlotManager.load` with a probe: the caller stops waiting once the client is gone and gets the slot's current status. After taking the slot lock, a load for a gone client starts nothing (no cold load, no stale-state recovery) unless the slot is already loaded. Stale-state recovery is unchanged for the next live request.
- No probe (reaper, reconciler, CLI, bridge, image route) means today's behaviour.

## Does the first load continue?
Yes. The first load runs to completion; only the wait and the second load stop. It holds the slot lock, other requests may be queued on it, and cancelling a start mid-flight is unsafe (see the shield in `hal0/providers/flm.py`). The abandoned load runs as a detached task that keeps a reference until it finishes. A waiter leaving cancels nothing, so the lock is never left held by a cancelled wait and other waiters are not disturbed.

## Tests
New: `tests/slots/test_load_client_gone.py` (disconnected client leaves stal

issues.body:
## What happens

A `/v1/chat/completions` request for a model whose slot is not loaded makes hal0-api load the slot and wait for it. If the client gives up (its own timeout, a closed connection), hal0-api keeps going: it waits out the slot's ready timeout and, when that load does not converge, re-enters the load from the stale `WARMING` state (`slot.load_from_stale_inflight_state`, `src/hal0/slots/manager.py` ~:1800-1823) and starts a second cold load for a request nobody is waiting for.

Seen on a fleet box during a Hermes repair: the provisioner's smoke test asked for `hal0/agent` (a 27B, 17.6 GB model) with a 60 s client timeout. hal0-api started the load at 02:36:50, its ready wait timed out at 02:40:44, the unit was torn down (the OOM killer fired in `system-hal0-slot.slice` at 02:42:13), and a second load of the same model ran from 02:42:14 to 02:44:21. Both loads stalled the box (hindsight-api's own loop watchdog reported its event loop blocked for 30 s; the Hermes agent was killed by its systemd watchdog during each load).

## If nobody fixes it

One abandoned request can cost two back-to-back multi-minute cold loads of a large model, on a box (or a shared host) that is already under memory pressure from the first one.

## Fix size

M. Tie the lazy load to the request: when the client disconnects, stop waiting and do not re-enter the load from a stale state for that request (Starlette exposes `request.is_disconnected()`; the dispatcher's wait can race it). Keep the stale-state recovery for the next live request. Tests: a disconnected client during the ready wait leads to no second load.

Found while investigating the watchdog kill fixed by `fix/repair-smoke-cold-load` (the smoke test no longer issues that request).

agent_prs.body:
## What

Banks created by the Hindsight coding-agent plugin carry `retain_chunk_size = 12000` on their strategies. Hindsight refuses every retain whose chunk size is not strictly below `retain_max_completion_tokens`, and hal0 pinned that to 4096, so every write into those banks failed (7,227 failed operations on one box).

- Default `[memory.graph] extraction_max_tokens` is now `16384` (schema, `ExtractionLimits`, the base `hindsight-api.service`, docs). The field description no longer claims the floor stays above a chunk size of 3000.
- New `hal0.memory.retain_chunk_guard` reads each bank's resolved config (`GET /v1/default/banks/{id}/config`, including `retain_strategies.*.retain_chunk_size`) and reports banks whose largest chunk is not below the cap.
- `PUT /api/memory/graph` adds a `warnings` entry (plus `chunk_check`) when a bank is not cleared; the existing save-warnings banner on the Memory page renders it. New read-only `GET /api/memory/graph/chunk-check` backs a `hal0 doctor all` row, `memory_retain_chunk`.
- Warn only, never refuse. If the engine is unreachable the check is skipped (`chunk_check: null`, doctor `warn`), not reported clean.

## Upgraded boxes

`save_hal0_config` dumps the whole model, so any box whose `hal0.toml` hal0 has written already holds `extraction_max_tokens = 4096` explicitly and keeps it; only a config without the key resolves to 16384. Those boxes get the warning (PUT and doctor) instead of a silent change. The base unit value is only a fallback under the drop-in.

## Trade-off

A larger cap lengthens the throughput projection (`~3500 / prompt tok/s + max_tokens / decode tok/s`): at 16384 a slot decoding under ~55 tok/s now projects past the default 300 s `llm_timeout_s` and gets the existing too-slow warning. The warning is advisory. The retain wall limit that bounds how long a document can hold the extraction lane is #3214, a follow-up PR.

## Not in this PR

Per-bank failed counts on the Memory page: split out as #3241.

- Renderer stamps every slot unit with `Label=io.hal0.unit-sha=<sha256>`, hashed over the rest of the unit text (so it never covers itself). Same config renders the same hash; nothing clock- or host-volatile is in the text.

issues.body:
## What happens

After updating a box from a pre-#3066 build to `1.7.1-nightly.20261027155413`, the updater rewrote the `img` slot's Quadlet unit (`User=996:989`, the `/opt/hal0-models` mount, `/home/hal0`, `HOME`/`USER`/`LOGNAME`, `--temp-directory /tmp`) but reported **"no slot drift seen yet"**, and `hal0 update --restart-slots` answered **"no slots need restart."** The container kept running as root (`podman top hal0-slot-img` → `root root`, `Config.User` empty) until I restarted the slot by hand. After the restart: `hal0 hal0`, `user=996:989`, render as hal0 OK.

## Why

`hal0.slots.drift.compute_config_drift` compares only `_CONFIG_DRIFT_KEYS` (`--ctx-size`, `--model`, `--alias`, `--port`, `-b`, `-ub`) plus the image reference (`src/hal0/slots/drift.py`). A change to the unit's **identity** (`User=`), **mounts** (`Volume=`), **environment**, `--group-add`, or any non-llama flag in `Exec=` (ComfyUI's `--temp-directory`) is invisible, so the post-update banner and `--restart-slots` both stay silent.

## What happens if nobody fixes it

Every box updated to 1.7.1 keeps its `img` container running ComfyUI **as root** until something restarts the slot, which defeats the security fix in #3066 for the window between update and the next reboot or manual restart. The update guide and CHANGELOG tell operators to run `hal0 slot restart img` once, but the tool that exists to catch exactly this (`--restart-slots`) says nothing. The same blind spot hides any future change to `User=`, mounts or env on the llama/FLM/TTS slots (#3126).

## Reproduce

1. Box on `1.7.0-nightly.20261027004630` with `img` loaded (container started as root).
2. `hal0 update --target 1.7.1-nightly.20261027155413 -y` → "no slot drift seen yet".
3. `hal0 update --restart-slots -y` → "no slots need restart."
4. `podman inspect -f '{{.Config.User}}' hal0-slot-img` → empty; unit on disk says `User=996:989`.

## Fix sketch

Make the drift comparator also compare the rendered unit's identity/mount/env surf

## What happens

The extraction throughput preflight added in #2793 (`src/hal0/memory/extraction_env.py`, `measure_extraction_throughput` / `_probe_body`) posts to the slot's `/v1/chat/completions` without a `model` field. hal0's own FLM health probe always sends one (`src/hal0/providers/flm.py:1074`). The NPU serialises requests, so a probe queued behind a running extraction can time out, and with `llm_timeout_s` below about 205 s that gets cached as `too_slow`.

## If nobody fixes it

Operators with an FLM extraction slot see a wrong or misleading memory warning from `hal0 memory graph check`, `doctor all`, the installer, and the memory graph PUT. It is a warning only; nothing is refused.

## Fix sketch

Send the slot's model id in the probe body, and either skip the probe on FLM slots or treat a timeout on a slot with no busy signal as `unknown`, not `too_slow`. Needs NPU hardware to verify. Size guess: XS–S.

A rare lost update on the brain profile: either its MCP entries vanish until the next hal0-api start, or a sweep's header or memory change is undone. The window is milliseconds, and it only opens when the brain wiring and a profile sweep coincide, which is why nobody has seen it yet.

`_gated_run` in `tests/bridge/test_service_runs.py` returned as soon as the ledger said `waiting_for_approval`. tests/bridge/test_service_runs.py:785
```

## Cause

`_gated_run` (`tests/bridge/test_service_runs.py:766`) returns as soon as the ledger says `status == "waiting_for_approval"`. The other two `_gated_run` callers (`:817`, `:1050`) are exposed the same way.

## What happens if nobody fixes it

Unrelated PRs go red on python 3.12 or 3.14 at random and get re-run, which hides real failures. Third timing flake this week after #3201, #3202 and #3209.

Test only: make `_gated_run` wait for the mirrored row, not the status, for example until `pending_of(row).get("approval_id")` is set on the ledger (the field `_store_approval_id` writes), or until `queue.list_pending()` has the row. Keep the product ordering; it is ADR-0043 decision 9. Size XS.

issues.body:
### What happens

`tests/api/test_redact.py::TestRedactionTimeIsLinear`'s guards (and the sibling parametrised `test_a_long_glued_run_is_fast` at line 1373, assertion at line 1380) measure wall-clock time with `time.perf_counter()` and fail when one 80 KB redaction takes longer than `_BOUND_S = 1.0` (line 1020). On the devops box with four test suites sharing 12 cores (load above 5) a lane's full unit tier stopped on `test_a_long_glued_run_is_fast` at 1.17 s; the module passes alone (1474 passed). The docstring says each line takes "well under 0.1 s with the fix" and that the 1 s bound "only leaves room for a slow CI box", so a loaded box is enough to trip it. The tests are marked `@pytest.mark.timing` but the default unit tier still runs them.

These guards exist for a real regression (the `--flag` rule was cubic on v1.4.0-rc: 80 KB of `api_token_` took 21 s), so they must stay.

### If nobody fixes it

Full-tier runs and CI python jobs go red at random under load and get re-run, which CONTRIBUTING forbids; a real quadratic regression would hide behind "it is just the flaky timing test".

### Reproduce

Run `tests/api/test_redact.py -k Linear` while two other full suites run on the box; or `taskset`-pin the run to one busy core.

### Fix-size guess

XS: measure CPU time (`time.process_time()`) instead of wall clock, which ignores scheduling delay, and keep the 1 s bound; or assert the ratio against a short baseline line measured in the same process. Either keeps the regression guard's intent. Same family as #3201 and #3202.

## What happens

`hal0 config validate` has help text "Validate all config files against the current schema." It only loads hal0.toml, upstreams.toml and providers.toml (`src/hal0/cli/config_commands.py:382-408`, same on the box and on main). It never runs the typed `SlotConfig` load over `/etc/hal0/slots/*.toml`. A slot TOML with an unknown key therefore gets "All configs pass schema validation." rc=0, while the daemon's typed load of the same file refuses it on every boot (the refusal is by design, ADR-0029 §5):

The key does not break the slot (the launch path reads the raw dict; rerank is ready and serving on 8086 with this exact file). ## Summary

The Overview Hardware card captioned the GPU row with `useHardware().data.gpu`, the raw `gpu_name` from `/api/hardware`. On a Strix Halo box whose pci.ids predates the part that is `Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. [AMD/ATI] Device 1586 (rev c1)`: truncated, and it names nothing. Closes #3156.

**No shared display-name owner existed.** I looked for the mapping the dock, the Engine tab and `hal0 doctor` use and found none: the only PCI-string-to-label code was a private helper, `_friendly_gpu`, in `src/hal0/bench/runner.py`. So this adds the owner server-side and makes both consumers read it (anti-scar rule 1):

- New `hal0.hardware.gpu_name.gpu_display_name(name, *, cpu_model)`, a pure function. An unresolved AMD lspci line (`Device 1586`) takes the iGPU marketing name from the CPU string (`AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S` gives `Radeon 8060S`), else `AMD Device 1586`. A resolved line takes its bracketed Radeon name (`Navi 31 [Radeon RX 7900 XTX]` gives `Radeon RX 7900 XTX`); a multi-SKU bracket (`Radeon Graphics / Radeon 8050S / Radeon 8060S`, as newer pci.ids list Strix Halo) defers to the CPU string. Anything that is not an lspci AMD line (NVIDIA product name, a VM's virtio GPU, `AMD GPU`) passes through unchanged.
- `/api/hardware` (`_flatten_for_ui`) publishes `gpu_display_name` beside the raw `gpu_name`. `gpu_name` is unchanged, so diagnostics (`useDiagnoses`) and the bench path that read it keep working.
- `bench/runner.py::_friendly_gpu` now calls the owner instead of keeping its own regex. It still appends `(gfx1151)` on `platform == "strix-halo"`, as before; that is the bench label's existing behaviour and is not changed here.
- UI: `normalizeHardware` exposes `gpuDisplayName` (the server's `gpu_display_name`, else the raw `gpu`, so a new UI against an older API shows what it showed before). `ui/src/dash/overview/hardware.jsx` reads it.

Not changed: the Slots telemetry header (`telemetry-header.jsx`) and the Settings Hardware & Runtimes page

## Summary

`test_terminate_stops_descendants_of_the_child` failed intermittently with `assert not _running(grandchild)` (`assert not True`). The cause is in the test's liveness check, not in `_terminate` or `_signal_group`.

- `_running` treated any `/proc/<pid>/stat` state other than `Z` as alive. When the killed `sleep` is reaped by init, `wait4` marks it `EXIT_DEAD` (state `X`) a few microseconds before `/proc` drops the entry. The poll loop and the final `assert not _running(...)` read the file separately, so under load the second read can land in that window, see `X`, and fail right after `_terminate` did its job. That also fits the failure the issue's reporter saw: `1 failed in 0.18s`, far short of the 5 s poll budget.
- The pid-reuse theory in the issue is a real but second-order risk (`pid_max` is 4194304 here, so a reused pid inside the window needs a wrap). The fix covers it too: the grandchild's start time (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22) is captured before terminating, and a pid with a different start time counts as gone.
- `Z`, `X` and `x` all count as not running now. The assertion is not weakened, and there is no retry, skip or xfail: a grandchild still alive after the group is killed still fails the test.
- `_terminate` and `_signal_group` (`src/hal0/api/agents/repair.py`) are unchanged. The SIGKILL to the group always reached the grandchild; the traces below show it in `Z` or `X` on every failing run.

Closes #3201.

`tests/api/test_agent_repair_job.py::test_terminate_stops_descendants_of_the_child` fails intermittently with `assert not _running(grandchild)` (`assert not True`), most recently on the `python (3.12)` job of PR #3197 (run 41279861531, 2026-11-01 06:21Z) while `python (3.14)` passed on the same commit; the PR touches only the slot tune write guard. agent_prs.body:
## Summary

Closes #3183.

A slot file that already carried an invalid `[tune]` key (hand-edited, or written by an older build) made `guard_and_normalize_tune` (`src/hal0/slots/config_write.py`) refuse every later tune write with `validation.tune_invalid`, including a write that set a different, valid key. The error named the stored row. The drawer never shows that row, because the read path (`slot_tune_table_valid` in `src/hal0/slots/tune.py`) already ignores an invalid stored key and falls back to the profile. The operator had no field to fix.

**Fix.** The write path now validates only the keys the write carries. For the keys already stored and not touched by the write, it reuses `slot_tune_table_valid`: valid ones are kept, invalid or unknown ones are dropped and logged once per write as `slot.tune_stored_key_dropped`. A bad key in the payload is still refused with `validation.tune_invalid` and its own `loc`. `tune: null` (`hal0 slot edit --tune-reset`) still clears the whole table.

**Why this option and not "validate only touched keys, leave the rest".** Both options keep every valid key the operator wrote. The deciding points:

- One owner of "which stored keys count". The read path already drops invalid stored keys per key. Reusing that function means the write and read sides cannot disagree about a stored key. Leaving the key in place would keep it forever, since the drawer cannot show it.
- A slot file with an invalid `[tune]` key fails the typed load elsewhere (`discover.ref_slot_load_failed`, then `models.auto_scan_prune_skipped`). Rewriting the table without it heals the file; keeping it verbatim would persist a file the schema rejects.
- Nothing observable is lost. The dropped key was already inert, so the effective tune and the drawer read the same before and after.

### What happens

When a slot file on disk already carries an invalid `[tune]` key (hand-edited, or written by an older build), `reconcile_and_guard_slot_config` refuses every later write to that slot with `validation.tune_invalid`, including writes that do not touch `tune` (`src/hal0/slots/config_write.py:508-524`). ## Summary

`hal0 slot create --model <id>` and `hal0 slot edit --model <id>` (and the REST routes and `slot_create` / `slot_edit` MCP tools that end in them) accepted a model id the registry does not know and wrote it into the slot TOML. - **The check.** `check_model_registered` in `hal0.slots.config_write`, next to `check_model_fits_slot`. An unknown id is refused with `validation.model_not_registered` (HTTP 400). The message names the id and says how to register one (`hal0 model add <path>` / `scan` / `pull`, `hal0 model list`); `details` carries `slot`, `model_id`, `hint`; the slot file is not touched.
- **Where it runs.** `POST /api/slots` and `PUT /api/slots/{name}/config`, through one new route helper (`_guard_model_registered`). The CLI (`slot create`, `slot edit --model`), the dashboard, and the `slot_create` / `slot_edit` MCP tools all reach the slot store through those two handlers, so one gate covers every surface. It is not in `reconcile_and_guard_slot_config`: that pipeline has no registry handle, and its in-process callers (stacks apply) are deliberately left alone, see Merge Danger.
- **What still passes.** A registered id or an installed FLM id (`model_meta.is_resolvable`, the same predicate `swap`/`load` use); a curated catalogue id (`load` pulls it on demand, the regression note for this issue asks for exactly this); any id on an NPU or ComfyUI slot (FLM tags and image catalogue ids are never registry rows, and `resolve_servable_model` leaves them alone too); any id on a self-managed speech engine slot (Kokoro, Qwen3-TTS, Moonshine, VibeVoice: `SELF_MANAGED_PROVIDERS`, `provider_requires_model` is False, weights are baked in or operator-staged; added in the second commit after Codex and Greptile flag

issues.body:
### What happens

On a box where at least one model of the slot's capability is registered and on disk, `hal0 slot create <n> --type embedding --model <id>` succeeds (exit 0) even though `<id>` is not in the registry and is not a curated catalog id. `hal0 slot edit <n> --model <id>` also succeeds. The slot TOML keeps `[model] default = "<id>"`. On `hal0 slot load <n>`, `registry.fallback.resolve_servable_model` substitutes a registered same-capability model and the load reports success: `Loaded <n> -> state=ready model=<other id>`. The slot state message stays empty; the only flag is a `slot.model_default_fallback` WARNING in the hal0-api journal.

`hal0 slot swap <n> --model <id>` and `POST /api/slots/<n>/load` with a `model_id` refuse the same kind of id with HTTP 404 "not resolvable — not in the registry ... (slot not touched)". So create and edit skip the `is_resolvable` gate that swap and load-with-model apply.

The substitute is not "the default model of that type": the per-type marker was on lfm2.5-2.6b, and the fallback picked qwen3-embedding through the name-similarity then largest-size heuristic because it was the only embedding candidate.

### What should happen

Create and edit should apply the same `is_resolvable` gate as swap and load-with-model, while still accepting curated "will pull" catalog ids (create_slot's own comment names that as intended). At minimum the slot's `metadata.message` should name the substitution.

### How to reproduce

```sh
hal0 slot create zz-emb --type embedding --hardware vulkan --model not-a-registered-id
# Created slot zz-emb on port 8084 (model=not-a-registered-id)   rc=0
hal0 slot load zz-emb
# Loaded zz-emb -> state=ready model=qwen3-embedding-0-6b-q8-0
hal0 slot show zz-emb         # metadata.message "", config_drift.drifted false
journalctl -u hal0-api | grep model_default_fallback      # the only signal
hal0 slot swap zz-emb --model also-not-registered         # HTTP 404 not resolvable (slot not touched)
hal0 slot ed

The gateway unit hal0 renders carried a fixed `TimeoutStopSec=70`, the value Hermes derives for its default drain timeouts. A box that raises `agent.restart_drain_timeout` (the report in #2895 sets 180, which needs 210 s) had systemd SIGKILL the gateway mid-drain on every restart, including each `hal0 update`, cutting off agent turns still in flight.

- **Owner of the setting.** The drain timeouts are Hermes config, not hal0's: `agent.restart_drain_timeout` / `agent.cron_drain_timeout` (env `HERMES_RESTART_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` / `HERMES_CRON_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`), read upstream at `hermes_cli/gateway.py:3510-3537` with defaults at `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:111,117`. hal0 never reads or writes them (no hit in `src/`). Every hal0-api boot with healthy memory adds one new copy of the Hermes identity card and one new copy of the hal0-brain identity card to the shared bank, and never deletes the earlier copies. agent_prs.title: fix(logging): never print traceback frame locals to the journal

issues.body:
### What happens

`hal0 serve` configures structlog with its default exception renderer, which keeps `show_locals=True` (`src/hal0/cli/main.py:172`). Every `log.exception(...)` / `log.error(..., exc_info=True)` in hal0-api therefore prints the local variables of each frame in the traceback. A frame that holds a credential in a local — an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` request header, a provider API key, a bridge key — prints it to the journal.

Found while reviewing the agent bridge's Hermes client (ADR-0043, PR 2): an `httpx.InvalidURL` raised from a mistyped `API_SERVER_HOST` escaped the `httpx.HTTPError` catch, reached a `log.error(exc_info=True)`, and the Hermes profile key appeared three times in the rendered traceback. The bridge client now maps every exception from the HTTP call to its own error type, but the renderer setting is process-wide and predates the bridge: any other caught exception with a secret in a local has the same exposure.

### If nobody fixes it

Credentials land in `journalctl -u hal0-api`, which is readable by `systemd-journal` group members and ends up in doctor bundles and Sentry breadcrumbs. CLAUDE.md classifies a privacy or security exposure as P0.

### Reproduce

Run `hal0 serve` with stderr not a TTY, trigger any handler that catches an exception while a header dict with a bearer is in scope (the bridge probe at the reviewer's scratchpad did this with `API_SERVER_HOST=[::1`), and read the journal: the key is printed as a local, wrapped onto its own line at 80 columns, so line-based redaction does not catch it.

### Fix-size guess

XS: configure the structlog `ConsoleRenderer`/`ExceptionRenderer` with `show_locals=False` (and the same for the JSON renderer path if it formats tracebacks), plus one test that renders an exception with a `Bearer` local and asserts the key is absent. Related: #3136 (memory tag trust), ADR-0043.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

agent_prs.title: fix(memory): shared memory by default with provider-owned provenance tags

issues.body:
### What happens

With the shipped default `[memory] unified_bank = true` (`src/hal0/config/schema.py:2530`), a memory write's private owner is derived from the first `agent:<id>` tag plus `visibility:private`. The Hindsight provider appends its own `agent:<client>` tag only when the caller sent none (`src/hal0/memory/hindsight_provider.py:1287-1291`), and the read path trusts that tag (`:1137-1141`). So any caller that can reach `memory_add` — through `/mcp/memory` with the client or admin key, or through the REST shim — can plant a note in another agent's private memory by sending `tags=["agent:brain", "visibility:private"]`, and the owning agent then reads it back as its own.

Found while reviewing the agent bridge's teach tools (ADR-0043, PR 3): a bridge client with only the `agents` scope could do the same through `agent_memory_add`; that surface now strips caller-supplied `agent:`, `visibility:` and `project:` tags. The `/mcp/memory` front door and the REST memory routes still accept them.

### If nobody fixes it

Any memory-capable client (Hermes profiles, Pi, Open WebUI tools, a remote bridge client with the `memory` scope) can write into any other agent's private namespace — including the brain steward's — which is exactly what `private:<id>` namespaces exist to prevent, and a prompt-injected agent can seed another agent's context.

### Reproduce

`POST /api/memory/add` (or `memory_add` on `/mcp/memory`) with `X-hal0-Agent: cc`, `X-hal0-Private: 1`, body `{"text": "x", "tags": ["agent:brain", "visibility:private"]}`; then search as `brain` in private mode — the note is returned.

### Fix-size guess

S: the provider should own the `agent:` and `visibility:` tags (overwrite, never trust the caller's), and `project:` should follow the existing ACL; one test per front door (MCP memory server, REST shim, admin dispatcher). Related: ADR-0043 teach tools, #3133, #3134.

issues.body:
### What happens

The img slot's ComfyUI container runs as root under rootful podman, with `seccomp=unconfined`, `apparmor=unconfined` and `label=disable`, and the GPU devices passed through (`src/hal0/providers/comfyui.py`, `container_spec`). Its bind-mount sources are read-write directories that the `hal0` service account owns: the ComfyUI data root's `models`, `output`, `input`, `user` and `custom_nodes` (`hal0.comfyui.paths`). Podman resolves each bind-mount source path as root when the container starts, following symlinks.

So the `hal0` account can get root in two ways:
- **Plant code.** Anything it writes into `custom_nodes/` runs as root inside the container at the next img start. ComfyUI imports every custom node.
- **Swap a source for a symlink.** It can replace a mount source with a symlink to a root-only host directory. The container then mounts that directory read-write.

A compromise of the `hal0` account, for example through a hal0-api bug, becomes root on the box. The security review of #3058 raised this. It is not caused by #3058: that change adds a read-only mount under `/var/lib/hal0`, which the same symlink swap applies to.

### How to reproduce

As `hal0` (the owner of `<model store>/comfyui/custom_nodes`), write a file there that runs code at import, then run `hal0 slot restart img`. Its code runs as uid 0 in a container with the host's GPU devices and no seccomp. Alternatively, as `hal0`, replace `<model store>/comfyui/output` with a symlink to a root-only directory, then restart img. The container now mounts that directory read-write at `/opt/ComfyUI/output`.

### If nobody fixes it

The `hal0` account is effectively root, so every hal0-api RCE or file-write bug becomes full box compromise. That undoes the privilege drop the service-user flip was meant to provide.

### Fix size, your best guess

M to L. Options:
- run ComfyUI as a non-root uid in the container (`--user`, or `UserNS=keep-id`/`auto` in the quadlet) so a planted node cannot act

On small boxes, first-run setup recommends and downloads about 7 GB of a model that the box then refuses to render.

## Where

- `src/hal0/comfyui/picker.py`: `recommended_for` and `image_pool_gb`.
- `src/hal0/comfyui/catalog.py`: `recommended_model_id` thresholds.
- `src/hal0/comfyui/fit.py`: `assess`.

## Fix

Make the recommendation honour the fit check. Recommend the largest renderable model whose native-size fit is not `wont_fit` against the live memory budget, and fall back to the RAM rule only when the budget is unknown. Add a test for a 17 GB box. The dashboard already leads with an alternative when the recommended model is `wont_fit`.

## What happens

The installer scripts start Python from a heredoc without `-I`:

- `installer/bootstrap.sh:393`
- `installer/install.sh:1148`
- `installer/lib/preflight.sh:1936`

Each runs `python3 - <<...`. When the script comes from stdin, Python puts the current working directory first on `sys.path`, so any module the snippet imports that is not already loaded is looked up there first. The operator runs these scripts as root from whatever directory they are in.

#3007 fixed the same pattern in the sudo wrappers (`hal0-agentenv`, `hal0-benchctl`), where it crossed the hal0 → root grant.

## If nobody fixes it

If an operator runs the installer or `hal0 update` from a directory the `hal0` account can write, for example `/var/lib/hal0` or a model directory, a compromised `hal0` account that planted a module there gets code execution as root. This needs the operator to be in such a directory, so it is less likely than #3007. The result is the same.

## Reproduce

```
mkdir /tmp/x && echo 'print("HIJACKED")' > /tmp/x/json.py
cd /tmp/x && python3 - <<'PY'
import json
PY
```

This prints `HIJACKED`. Substitute whichever modules the three snippets import.

## Fix size

XS. Use `python3 -I -` in all three places, and extend `tests/installer/test_wrapper_python_isolated.py` to scan `installer/*.sh` and `installer/lib/*.sh` as well.

## Summary

`hal0-agentenv secret-keys <agent>` runs as root through the hal0 sudo grant and read `/var/lib/hal0/secrets/agents/<agent>.env` by pathname (`[[ -f ]]`, then `open(sys.argv[1])`). `/var/lib/hal0` is owned by the hal0 account, so that account could swap `secrets/` or `secrets/agents` for a symlink (or a tree of its own) and have root print the key names of any root-readable file.

The verb now runs the same embedded descriptor walker #3003 added for the write verbs, as a fourth, read-only verb `keys`. It walks from `/` by descriptor (`O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` inside any directory that is not root-only), requires `secrets/` and `secrets/agents` to be root-only directories, opens the vault `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` and checks it is a regular file. A symlink or foreign directory is refused with exit 3; `hermes_platforms.read_vault` already treats a non-zero exit as "no keys". The read verb creates, chowns and chmods nothing; a missing directory or vault still prints nothing and exits 0. The leaf open is now shared with the merge writer, which keeps strict UTF-8 decoding.

The output is unchanged: key names only, never values, skipping empty and false-flag values.

Closes #3014

issues.body:
## What happens

When ComfyUI sends back text that cannot be encoded as JSON, an image render fails with a bare `500` and an empty body. The normal answer is the `502 dispatch.upstream_failed` error envelope.

The trigger is a lone surrogate escape such as `"\ud800"`, which Python decodes but cannot encode again as UTF-8. It can arrive in either of two places:

- the `prompt_id` that `/prompt` returns (or the whole `/prompt` response), or
- the `/history` outputs.

The provider copies that text unchanged into `ComfyUIInferError.details`, under `prompt_id` and `response`. When hal0's error handler serialises `details`, it fails.

## If nobody fixes it

The render was failing anyway, so nothing is lost: the progress tracker and the listener are still cleaned up, and the image job closes. A client just gets a 500 with no body instead of the error envelope, and the log shows an encoding traceback instead of the upstream failure.

This is only reachable if the ComfyUI side of the img container is broken or malicious. Stock ComfyUI uses `uuid4` prompt ids.

## Where

- `src/hal0/providers/comfyui.py`: the `ComfyUIInferError(... details={"prompt_id": ..., "response": ...})` sites in `infer` and `_await_history`. They predate the image readiness work; on main at c76c35cb they are around lines 746, 782 and 822-853.
- The pattern to reuse is `hal0.comfyui.gate_reason.clean_reason(text, limit=...)`. It already cleans websocket node names and the `prompt_id` on `/status` (PR for the image readiness API).

## Fix

Run each string from ComfyUI through `clean_reason` before it goes into `details`. Keep the raw id for polling `/history`.

The test: a fake ComfyUI returns `{"prompt_id": "\ud800"}` and then a non-200 from `/history`. `/v1/images/generations` must answer 502 with the envelope, not 500.

Size: XS.
issues.title: Image render error answers a bare 500 when ComfyUI returns text JSON cannot encode

The render progress listener connects to ComfyUI's websocket on loopback through `websockets.connect` (`src/hal0/providers/comfyui.py:~210-217`) and passes no `proxy` argument. websockets 15 defaults to `proxy=True`, which reads the system proxy environment. Pass `proxy=None` when the installed websockets accepts it. `pyproject.toml` allows `websockets>=13`, and 13.x has no `proxy` keyword, so probe the signature once rather than passing the keyword unconditionally. The parked editor-proxy branch (`feat/comfyui-editor-proxy`, `_WS_NO_PROXY`) has such a probe. Add a test that the connect call carries `proxy=None` when the keyword is available.

agent_prs.title: ci: use uv sync --locked so lock drift fails CI

issues.body:
## What happens

CI installs with `uv sync --frozen` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:68`, also `hindsight-pin-gate.yml:121` and `sync-docs-discourse.yml:107`). The comment above it (`ci.yml:62`) says `--frozen` fails if `uv.lock` drifts from `pyproject.toml`. It does not: `--frozen` uses the lockfile as-is and never checks it against `pyproject.toml`. `--locked` (or a separate `uv lock --check` step) is the flag that fails on drift.

This let a stale `uv.lock` sit on main during the v1.6.5 cycle: a `pyproject.toml` range change merged without the matching lock update, and it only surfaced when the dependabot PRs #3027/#3028 regenerated the lock and appeared to "revert" the range.

## If nobody fixes it

A `pyproject.toml` dependency change can merge with a lock that no longer matches it. CI stays green and tests the old pinned versions, while anyone running `uv lock` gets a different resolution. Release builds and CI can quietly diverge from what `pyproject.toml` declares.

## Fix

Add a `uv lock --check` step to the python job in `ci.yml` (cheap, no install), or switch the install to `uv sync --locked`. Correct the comment at `ci.yml:62`.

Size: XS. CI/CD change, so it needs a human merge.
issues.title: ci: uv sync --frozen does not catch a stale uv.lock

agent_prs.title: fix(registry): re-hash the resume prefix off the event loop

issues.body:
### What happens

When a model pull resumes from a partial download, `_download_one` in `src/hal0/registry/pull.py` (around line 1013) calls `_rehash_prefix(part, hasher)` directly on the event loop. That re-reads and SHA-256-hashes every byte already on disk before streaming continues. On a large partial this blocks hal0-api's whole event loop for the length of the hash: the dashboard, `/v1` dispatch, health probes and SSE all stall. A 20–40 GB partial takes tens of seconds at typical disk and hash speeds.

The expected behaviour is that the hash runs off the loop, for example with `await asyncio.to_thread(_rehash_prefix, part, hasher)`, the same way other blocking file work in the pull path is handled.

### How to reproduce

1. Start pulling a large model (several GB) and interrupt it partway, for example by restarting hal0-api, which keeps the `.part` file and its resume sidecar.
2. Start the same pull again.
3. While it resumes, request any API endpoint. It does not answer until the prefix has been hashed.

Code: `src/hal0/registry/pull.py`, `_download_one`, at the `hashed = _rehash_prefix(part, hasher)` call on the 206 path.

### If nobody fixes it

Every resumed large pull freezes the API for as long as the prefix takes to hash. The ComfyUI image-model installer (in progress) reuses `_download_one`, and image components are 15–41 GB each, so resumes there will freeze the dashboard for a minute or more.

### Fix size

XS. Run `_rehash_prefix` with `asyncio.to_thread`. The hasher object is not shared across threads at the same time, so handing it to the worker is safe. Add a test that the resume path awaits the hash off the loop.

### hal0 version

main at caa2e4cb (v1.6.x). Found in review of the image-catalog branch.

## Summary

`hal0 update` printed "no slots need restart." and then slots restarted. The commit job is marked `applied` before hal0-api bounces (`src/hal0/api/routes/updater.py` ~L362-380), so the CLI's drift probe (`update_commands.py`, post-apply `_fetch_slot_drift`) hits the old API, which renders the old config and sees no drift. issues.body:
## What happens

`hal0 update` printed "no slots need restart." (`src/hal0/cli/update_commands.py:515`), yet the utility and brain slots went down for about 12 s right after. Seen on a fleet box updating to `1.6.0-nightly.20261024063955`.

The update rewrote the slot unit files. The drift check that feeds the message ran before the API restarted onto the new code, so it reported zero drift. Once `hal0-api` came back, the next load of each slot saw the drifted config and restarted it (`slot.load_converging_drifted_config`, `src/hal0/slots/manager.py:1774`). Both slots came back healthy.

## If nobody fixes it

The operator is told no slot will restart, then sees serving slots drop. Anyone updating mid-request gets an unexplained interruption and has no warning to wait for idle.

## Reproduce

1. On a box with at least one loaded slot, update to a build whose slot unit render differs from the installed one.
2. Read the "no slots need restart." line in the update output.
3. Watch `journalctl -u 'hal0-slot@*'` or the API log: the slots restart via `load_converging_drifted_config` after `hal0-api` restarts.

## Fix

Compute drift against the new code's render (after the API restart), or reword the message to cover the converge-on-load path, e.g. list slots whose unit changed and say they will restart on next load.

Size: S.

## Summary

An LLM slot that is still loading when image mode starts no longer finishes loading beside ComfyUI (#3056). The switch into image mode unloaded only the llm-group slots ready for dispatch. A slot in a cold start or a wake-on-request (`pulling`, `starting`, `warming`) was in neither the unload set nor the saved set. Its load finished onto the GPU while ComfyUI rendered, and nothing unloaded it.

```diff
 _llm_slots_to_unload
-  llm-group and is_ready_for_dispatch
+  llm-group and (is_ready_for_dispatch or state in {pulling, starting, warming})

 _ensure_img_locked
   persist mode=img, saved set (now includes the loading slot)
   drain
+  _await_loads(slots)                    # phase "unloading"
+    wait while a slot is in a loading state AND SlotManager.is_busy(slot)
+    past 120 s: roll back to LLM mode, raise 503 gpu.slot_still_loading
   _unload_for_img(slots)                 # #3059's rollback-on-failure
   cold-start img if down

+SlotManager.is_busy(name)               # a load/unload/restart holds the slot lock
```

- **Why waiting works.** `SlotManager.load` holds the slot's lock for its whole run, `_await_ready` included, so `unload()` can't run mid-load. The switch waits for the load and then unloads the slot like any other. The slot stays in the saved set, so the restore brings it back.
- **A slot parked in `warming`** by a load whose health wait timed out is not busy. There is no load in progress, but its container is up, so it is unloaded straight away. `is_busy` is what tells the two apart (#1791).
- **A load that outlasts the 120 s wait** rolls the switch back to LLM mode and raises 503 `gpu.slot_still_loading`, with `details.slots`. The load carries on in LLM mode.
- **The #3059 restart reconcile** treats loading states the same way.
- **`unload_set`** on `GET /api/comfyui/arbiter` lists a loading slot in LLM mode, which is what a switch would now unload.
- **#3079's bare-metal RAM credit:** this PR also resolves the Codex review note t
agent_prs.title: fix(arbiter): take LLM slots still loading into the switch into image mode

issues.body:
### What happens

When the GPU arbiter switches into image mode, it unloads only the GPU LLM slots that are ready for dispatch at that moment (`src/hal0/slots/arbiter.py` `ensure_img`, ~:498-503: `gpu_exclusive_group(c) == "llm" and self._manager.is_ready_for_dispatch(...)`). An LLM slot that is still loading (a cold start or wake-on-request already in progress) is neither in the unload set nor in `saved_llm_slots`. Its load keeps going, the llama-server comes up on the GPU while ComfyUI renders, and nothing unloads it.

Expected: a slot that is mid-load when the switch starts is either waited for and then unloaded with the rest, or its load is cancelled, and it ends up in the saved set so the restore brings it back.

### How to reproduce

`src/hal0/slots/arbiter.py` `ensure_img` snapshot (~:498). Start a cold load of a large GPU LLM slot (`hal0 slot load <slot>`, or a chat request that wakes it), then trigger an image render (`/v1/images/generations`) while the slot is still `loading`/`warming`. After the switch, `hal0 slot list` shows the slot coming up ready while the mode is image.

### If nobody fixes it

ComfyUI renders beside an LLM the arbiter believes is unloaded. On the shared-memory GPU (Strix Halo GTT) that is the co-residency the arbiter exists to prevent: an image render plus a large LLM can exhaust memory and get the render or the slot OOM-killed. The image-gen overhaul makes switches far more frequent (image mode now ends after each render and comes back for the next), so the window is hit more often.

### Fix size, your best guess

S. In the switch, also take slots in a loading/warming state: wait for them (bounded) and add them to the unload and saved sets, or cancel their load first. Add an arbiter test with a fake slot that is mid-load when `ensure_img` runs.

### hal0 version

1.6.5 + main at ac29ff8b (pre-existing; found while reviewing the image-mode rework on `fix/owui-images-via-v1`)

## Summary

A failed unload during the switch into image mode now rolls the switch back to LLM mode. Before, it left image mode recorded with the LLM slot still on the GPU (#3059). The arbiter persists `mode=img` before the unloads, for crash recovery. A slot whose unload raised, such as a stop that outlived its budget (#2738), stayed loaded while the mode said image. The ComfyUI gate then let prompts through and ComfyUI rendered beside the LLM until the grace period ended.

```diff
 _ensure_img_locked
   if already image mode
+    _finish_unloads(st)        # saved-set slots still loaded (api restart mid-switch)
     _revive_img(st)
     return
   persist mode=img, saved set
   drain
-  for slot in llm_slots: unload(slot)          # first exception escapes, mode stays img
+  _unload_for_img(llm_slots, saved, img)
+    on the first failure:
+      reload saved-set slots that are no longer loaded (not the failed one)
+      persist mode=llm, saved=[], pinned=false
+      re-raise
   cold-start img if down
```

- **The failed slot is left to the slot layer.** Its stop may still be running, and its state is ERROR or a provisional `slow_stop` ERROR.
- **Slots not yet reached are not touched.** They are still loaded.
- **The next render retries the switch.**
- **After an api restart mid-switch,** the next `ensure_img` unloads any saved-set slot still loaded before it revives the engine, with the same rollback.
- **The status fallback stays** for the window before anything reconciles: `phase` reads `unloading` from #3070.
- **The rollback log is `gpu_arbiter.unload_failed_rolled_back`,** not `img_load_failed_rolled_back`.

- **Before:** `ensure_img()` with `agent`'s unload raising left `mode == img` and agent loaded. The old #3070 test asserted that state and only checked that `phase` said `unloading`.
- **After, a failed unload during a switch** gives `mode == llm`. The state file holds `{"mode": "llm", "pinned": false, "saved_llm_slots": []}`. The calls are
agent_prs.title: fix(arbiter): roll a switch back to LLM mode when an LLM slot's unload fails

issues.body:
### What happens

When the GPU arbiter switches into image mode, it saves `mode=img` and the LLM slot list before unloading those slots (crash-recovery ordering, `src/hal0/slots/arbiter.py` `ensure_img`). If an unload then fails, for example a `SlotTerminateTimeout` (#2738), the slot stays loaded on the GPU while the saved mode says image. Status reports generation, the ComfyUI gate's prompt hand-off answers "held", and ComfyUI renders beside the still-loaded LLM. The next `ensure_img` only revives the img slot; it does not retry the unload. Reproduced on the image-mode rework branch with a fake manager whose unload raises.

A related, shorter window: a hal0-api restart in the middle of a switch reports generation for about 12 s, until the restore loop reconciles.

Expected: a failed unload aborts the switch. Roll back to LLM mode, or retry or force the unload, so image mode is never reported while an LLM slot from the saved set is still loaded.

### How to reproduce

`src/hal0/slots/arbiter.py` `ensure_img`: `mode=img` is persisted before the unload loop. In a test, make one LLM slot's unload raise `SlotTerminateTimeout`, then read `/api/comfyui/arbiter` and call `ensure_img` again. The mode stays image and the slot stays loaded.

### If nobody fixes it

On the shared-memory GPU, ComfyUI renders next to an LLM the arbiter believes is gone. That is the co-residency the arbiter exists to prevent, and a memory-exhaustion path that can OOM-kill the render, the slot or more. Switches now happen after every render, so a flaky unload is hit more often. Same class as #3056.

### Fix size, your best guess

S. On any unload failure inside the switch, restore LLM mode (or retry with force), and never leave image mode reported with a saved-set slot loaded. Add an arbiter test with a failing unload, and one for an API restart mid-switch.

### hal0 version

main after the image-gen overhaul (eff16cff); worse with Plan 2b's per-render image mode (PR pending)

## Summary

The image fit check refused large models on bare-metal unified-memory hosts while LLM slots were loaded, even though switching to image mode frees that memory (#3072). On such a host the GTT the LLM slots hold comes out of system RAM, so `MemAvailable` drops by everything they hold. The `/v1` preflight judged the RAM need before the switch unloads them. A 128 GB box with about 85 GB of slots loaded therefore refused `qwen-image-lightning` with 422 `image.wont_fit`.

```diff
 build_memory_budget(sample, per_slot, ..., ram)
   render_free_gb     = total - other guests - starting - 2 GB
+  credit             = min(resident slots' pool figures, pool used - image engine)
+                       only when the pool is shared AND ram.source == "system"
+  render_ram_free_gb = min(ram.limit_gb, ram.free_gb + credit)

 assess(need, budget)
-  ram verdict  = judge(need.ram_gb, ram.free_gb)
+  ram verdict  = judge(need.ram_gb, render_ram_free_gb)
+  reason, when the credit is in it: "... GB free with the chat slots paused (... GB system)"

 read_ram()
+  source = "container" also when something (lxcfs) is mounted over /proc/meminfo
```

- **Containers get no credit, LXC guests included.**
  - A guest's RAM is not charged for GTT.
  - A slot's cgroup `memory.current` includes page cache that `MemAvailable` already counts as available. Crediting it would overstate free RAM and bring back the capped-guest OOM this check exists to stop.
  - The lxcfs mount check means a guest without `/run/systemd/container` can't pass for a bare-metal host.
- **What is credited.**
  - The credit is capped at the pool used outside the engine, because per-slot figures can be estimates.
  - A `starting` slot is not credited: the switch doesn't unload it.
  - The result never exceeds the RAM limit.
- **Contract changes.**
  - `MemoryBudget` gains `render_ram_free_gb`; it is additive on `/api/stats/hardware` `memory`.
  - `fit.ram_free_gb` now carries the credited figure.

agent_prs.title: fix(images): credit the RAM image mode frees on bare-metal unified memory in the fit check

issues.body:
## What happens

The image fit check (`hal0.comfyui.fit.assess`) judges a model's RAM need to load against this box's RAM free now (`read_ram()`). The `/v1/images/generations` preflight runs it before `ensure_img()` unloads the GPU LLM slots, so RAM those slots hold is not credited.

Whether that matters depends on where GPU memory is charged:

- **Strix Halo LXC guest:** GTT is not charged to the guest. On one such guest the device GTT counter read 43 GiB while the guest's RAM used read 16 GB. The slots hold only their process RSS in the guest's RAM, a few GB each. The refusal is close to right.
- **Bare-metal unified-memory host:** GTT pages come out of system RAM, so `MemAvailable` drops by everything the LLM slots hold. A 128 GB box with about 85 GB of LLM slots loaded refuses `qwen-image-lightning` (47.9 GB) with 422 `image.wont_fit`, although the switch would free that memory and the render would fit.

## If nobody fixes it

On bare-metal unified-memory hosts with large LLM slots loaded, large image models are refused until the operator unloads slots by hand, or the client sends `extra_body.hal0_skip_fit_check`. LXC guests, including capped ones like the 48 GB guest this check was built for, are not affected.

## Why it was not fixed in #3070

The credit is only right where GPU memory is charged to the RAM reading.

- Crediting a slot's GPU footprint on an LXC guest would overstate free RAM by the model's size. That brings back the OOM the check exists to stop: Qwen on a capped guest.
- The per-slot `mem_mb` is `max(cgroup memory.current, file size + KV estimate)`, which says nothing about which side was charged.

## Where

- `src/hal0/comfyui/fit.py`, `assess`: the RAM side.
- `src/hal0/hardware/memory_budget.py`, `read_ram`.
- Slot attribution is in `src/hal0/slots/capacity.py`, `build_per_slot`.

## Fix

- Credit RAM that unloading would actually free, only where it is charged to the RAM reading.

## Summary

```diff
 img slot load (providers/comfyui.py container_spec)
+  gate_credential.ensure_token()        # <var_lib>/comfyui-gate/token, 0600 in 0700, service user, no-follow writes
+  Volume=<var_lib>/comfyui-gate:/opt/hal0-gate:ro
+  Environment=HAL0_COMFYUI_GATE_TOKEN_FILE=/opt/hal0-gate/token   # the path, never the value
 hal0_gpu_gate (in the container), each of its 3 requests
-  urllib.request.urlopen(url)            # no credential, default proxy + redirect handling
+  _hal0_request(): reads the token file, unredirected "Authorization: Bearer", to an IP/localhost URL only
+  _OPENER: no proxy, no redirects
 AuthEnforcementMiddleware
   _decide(class, principal) refuses
+  and (method, exact path) in _GATE_REQUESTS and bearer == gate token
+      and HTTP only and peer is loopback or hal0-api's bind address
+    scope["hal0.comfyui_gate"] = True; pass

+  gate-admitted and (mode != generation or force or pin)  →  403 auth.forbidden

agent_prs.title: fix(comfyui): the GPU gate authenticates with a token of its own (#3058)

issues.body:
### What happens

The ComfyUI GPU gate (the `hal0_gpu_gate` custom node inside the img container) asks hal0-api for the arbiter state (`GET /api/comfyui/arbiter`), to hold the GPU (`POST /api/comfyui/prompt-handoff`) and to switch into image mode (`POST /api/comfyui/switchover`) before ComfyUI runs a prompt. It sends no credential. With `hal0 auth require on`, hal0-api answers 401 on every bind, loopback included, and the gate fails closed. So on a box with auth enforcement on, every image is refused: the ComfyUI editor, `/v1/images/generations`, Open WebUI's image button and omni.

The image-mode rework (Plan 2b, branch `fix/owui-images-via-v1`) ships this as a documented limitation. The gate refuses a 401/403 at once with its own message, and `HAL0_COMFYUI_GATE_FAIL_OPEN=1` restores the v1.6.5 behaviour, where the prompt goes through unguarded.

Expected: the gate authenticates with a narrow credential of its own, never the admin key, so auth-on boxes generate images with the GPU guard in place.

### How to reproduce

On a box with the image-mode rework: `hal0 auth require on`, then render an image through `/v1/images/generations` or the ComfyUI editor. The gate's arbiter read gets 401 and the prompt is refused.

### If nobody fixes it

Operators who follow the documented auth hardening lose image generation, or must turn on the fail-open opt-out and accept the LLM + diffusion co-residency risk the gate exists to prevent.

### Fix size, your best guess

M. hal0 mints a gate token into a 0600 file the img container reads (written next to the slot's env, rotated with the container). The auth layer admits that token only for `GET /api/comfyui/arbiter`, `POST /api/comfyui/prompt-handoff` and a generation-only `POST /api/comfyui/switchover`. The gate sends it as a bearer token. This is auth code and needs a security review. **The operator has ruled that the 1.7 tag waits for this fix.**

### hal0 version

main after the image-gen overhaul Plans 1-3 (eff16cff) plus Plan

agent_prs.title: feat(openwebui)!: Open WebUI images through /v1, and image mode only while an image renders (image-gen overhaul 2b)

issues.body:
## What happens

When the operator works in the ComfyUI editor directly, hal0's idle reaper can unload the img slot in the middle of the session. The reaper decides a slot is idle from requests that passed through hal0: `sweep_candidates` (`src/hal0/slots/reaper.py:338-366`) reads `_last_used`, which only hal0-dispatched requests bump, falling back to the state record's `updated_at`. Jobs queued from the ComfyUI editor go straight to ComfyUI and never touch it, so after the global `idle_timeout_s` (300 s by default) the reaper hard-evicts img (`reaper.py:400`; img is not in `_PINNED_BY_DEFAULT`, `reaper.py:86`), even while the editor has jobs running or queued.

This comes from reading the code; it has not been reproduced on a box yet. A live check did see the reaper evict img after 300 s of no hal0 traffic (`slot.idle_evicted`).

Expected: ComfyUI activity that hal0 did not dispatch (a running or pending prompt, recent history) counts as activity for the img slot.

## How to reproduce

1. Load the img slot and open the ComfyUI editor (through an SSH tunnel today).
2. Queue a long job, or keep working in the editor, for more than 5 minutes without sending any `/v1/images/generations` request through hal0.
3. Watch the API log for `slot.idle_evicted` on img, and the editor losing its backend.

## If nobody fixes it

Editor users lose running jobs and their session every five minutes unless they know to pin the slot with `idle_timeout_s = 0` (`reaper.py:76`), which then keeps the GPU in image mode forever.

## Fix

Before evicting img, ask ComfyUI whether it is busy (its `/queue` running and pending lists, or the newest `/history` timestamp) and treat that as activity, the same way the reaper already honours its serving-count guard. A cheap alternative is to bump img's last-used timestamp from the arbiter or from a ComfyUI queue poll. Add a test where the reaper's sweep keeps img while a stubbed ComfyUI reports a running prompt.

Size: S.

issues.body:
## What happens

After the idle reaper unloads the img slot, the next `POST /v1/images/generations` returns 404 `dispatch.no_route` ("capability routing selected slot 'img' but no matching slot upstream is registered") instead of cold-starting the slot. It keeps failing until something loads img by hand (`POST /api/slots/img/load`).

The reaper hard-evicts img after the global `idle_timeout_s` (img is not in `_PINNED_BY_DEFAULT`, `src/hal0/slots/reaper.py:86`; the unload is at `reaper.py:400`). The unload deregisters the img upstream, but nothing tells the GPU arbiter, so `/var/lib/hal0/gpu_arbiter.json` keeps `"mode": "img"`. The next request calls `arbiter.ensure_img()` (`src/hal0/api/routes/v1.py:1893`), which returns early because the persisted mode is already img (`src/hal0/slots/arbiter.py:483`). That skips the `_cold_start_img` path that would reload the slot, and dispatch finds no upstream. The comment at `v1.py:1902` ("ensure_img() above guarantees the img upstream is registered") no longer holds.

Each failed request also re-stamps `last_img_activity` (`touch_img_activity()` runs before dispatch), so the arbiter's idle restore never fires while a client keeps retrying.

This is a different cause from #725 (dispatch ran before the arbiter loaded the slot), which is fixed.

## How to reproduce

1. With the global `idle_timeout_s` at its default (300 s), render once: `POST /v1/images/generations {"model":"<an installed image model>","prompt":"x"}` → 200.
2. Wait more than 300 s. The API log shows `slot.idle_evicted` for img; `gpu_arbiter.json` still says `"mode": "img"`.
3. Render again: 404 `dispatch.no_route`.

Seen on `origin/main` d6bd52ec (v1.6.5). `arbiter.py` and `reaper.py` are unchanged by the image-catalog PRs #3032/#3037.

## If nobody fixes it

Image generation through `/v1` (and Open WebUI, once its own bugs are fixed) stops working five minutes after each use on every box and stays broken until an operator loads the slot by hand. Clients that re

agent_prs.title: feat(openwebui)!: Open WebUI images through /v1, and image mode only while an image renders (image-gen overhaul 2b)

issues.body:
## What happens

Open WebUI renders a fixed-step model such as SDXL-Lightning (8 steps) at 50 steps, which over-cooks the image. A `/v1/images/generations` render of the same model through hal0 uses 8 steps.

hal0 maps Open WebUI's `steps` parameter onto the workflow's KSampler node (`src/hal0/openwebui/wiring.py:51`, `("steps", "steps", "steps")` in `_OWUI_NODE_TYPES`), but `_image_gen_env_block` (`src/hal0/openwebui/env_writer.py:426`) never emits `IMAGE_STEPS`. Open WebUI then uses its own default of 50 and writes it into the mapped node. ComfyUI's `/history` shows the hal0 render at `steps 8` and the Open WebUI render at `steps 50`, with the same cfg, sampler and scheduler.

Expected: Open WebUI renders each model with the step count the model needs, the same as `/v1`.

## How to reproduce

1. Select `sdxl-lightning` as the img model, so hal0 renders Open WebUI's image env for it.
2. `grep IMAGE_STEPS /etc/hal0/openwebui.env`: no line.
3. Generate an image from Open WebUI (this needs the two connectivity bugs filed alongside this one worked around), then read ComfyUI's `/history`: `steps 50`.

Seen on `origin/main` d6bd52ec (v1.6.5); on main it is hidden behind the other two Open WebUI image bugs. The image-catalog PR #3037 makes it more visible, because its per-model workflows assume each model's own step count.

## If nobody fixes it

Once Open WebUI image generation works, Lightning and Turbo models produce visibly broken images from Open WebUI while looking fine through `/v1`, and every image takes several times longer than it should.

## Fix

Emit `IMAGE_STEPS` in `_image_gen_env_block` from the selected model's step count (the same value `/v1` uses), or drop the `steps` mapping for fixed-step models so the workflow's own value stands. Add a test on the rendered env for a fixed-step model.

Size: XS-S.

agent_prs.title: feat(openwebui)!: Open WebUI images through /v1, and image mode only while an image renders (image-gen overhaul 2b)

issues.body:
## What happens

Open WebUI cannot reach ComfyUI: every image request from Open WebUI fails with connection refused at `http://host.docker.internal:8188`.

hal0 points Open WebUI, a bridge-networked podman container, at the host gateway: `src/hal0/openwebui/env_writer.py:443` sets `"COMFYUI_BASE_URL": "http://host.docker.internal:8188"`. But the ComfyUI img slot runs host-networked (`src/hal0/providers/comfyui.py:326`, `network_mode="host"`), and although its command asks for `--listen 0.0.0.0` (`comfyui.py:271`), the container renderer's loopback fence rewrites the bind of every host-net slot to 127.0.0.1 (`src/hal0/providers/container.py:892-893`, `_loopback_fence_command` defined at `:511`, `_LOOPBACK_BIND = "127.0.0.1"` at `:508`). So ComfyUI listens on `127.0.0.1:8188` only, which the podman bridge cannot reach.

Expected: Open WebUI reaches ComfyUI through a path hal0 controls, without exposing ComfyUI on every interface.

## How to reproduce

1. Load the img slot (ComfyUI) on a box with Open WebUI enabled.
2. `ss -ltn | grep 8188`: `127.0.0.1:8188` only. The slot unit's `Exec=` line has `main.py --listen 127.0.0.1 --port 8188`.
3. From inside the Open WebUI container, connect to `host.docker.internal:8188`: connection refused.

Seen on `origin/main` d6bd52ec (v1.6.5). The image-catalog PRs #3032/#3037 carry the same code unchanged.

## If nobody fixes it

Open WebUI image generation cannot work on any box, independently of the env quoting bug filed alongside this one. Opening ComfyUI's port on all interfaces to work around it would expose an unauthenticated ComfyUI to the LAN.

## Fix

Keep the loopback fence and give Open WebUI a route that reaches the loopback listener. Options: point `COMFYUI_BASE_URL` at a hal0-api proxy route for ComfyUI (Open WebUI already reaches hal0-api through the host gateway), or bind ComfyUI additionally to the podman bridge gateway address only. A test should assert that the URL hal0 writes for Open WebUI is reachable under the

issues.body:
## What happens

With image generation wired to ComfyUI, Open WebUI's `GET /api/v1/images/config` returns 500 and `POST /api/v1/images/generations` returns 400. Open WebUI's log shows a pydantic `ResponseValidationError ... Input should be a valid list` for `COMFYUI_WORKFLOW_NODES`.

hal0 writes `/etc/hal0/openwebui.env` with `write_env_atomic`, which runs every value through `_quote_value` (`src/hal0/config/env.py:31`, quoting branch at `:38-40`, applied at `:94`). A value containing `"` is wrapped in systemd-style double quotes with `\"` escapes. That suits systemd's `EnvironmentFile=`, but Open WebUI is started with `podman run --env-file /etc/hal0/openwebui.env` (`packaging/systemd/hal0-openwebui.service:67`), and podman's `--env-file` keeps the quotes and backslashes literally. Open WebUI's `json.loads` of `COMFYUI_WORKFLOW_NODES` then returns a `str` instead of a list. `COMFYUI_WORKFLOW` is mangled the same way.

Expected: the JSON values reach Open WebUI unchanged, so its image config loads and generation works.

## How to reproduce

1. On a box with the img slot set up (ComfyUI), let hal0 render `/etc/hal0/openwebui.env` with image generation enabled (`ENABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=True`, `IMAGE_GENERATION_ENGINE=comfyui`).
2. `grep COMFYUI_WORKFLOW_NODES /etc/hal0/openwebui.env`: the value starts with `"[{\"type\"`.
3. Sign in to Open WebUI and call `GET /api/v1/images/config`: 500.

Seen on `origin/main` d6bd52ec (v1.6.5). The image-catalog PRs #3032/#3037 carry the same code unchanged.

## If nobody fixes it

Image generation from Open WebUI never works on any box, even though hal0 reports it as wired. Users only see a failed request in the chat UI.

## Fix

Render the Open WebUI env file in the format podman's `--env-file` reads (no shell or systemd quoting; one `KEY=value` per line, with values that cannot contain a newline), either with a dedicated writer for this file or a quoting mode on `write_env_atomic`. Add a test that parses the rendered file the way

agent_prs.body:
## Summary

The image starter recommendation now ranks a box by the RAM it can actually use. The rule is unchanged: qwen-image-lightning at ≥96 GB, sdxl-lightning at ≥16 GB, sd-1.5 below that. Only the memory figure it is measured against changes.

That figure is now the pool or the guest's RAM limit, whichever is smaller. The limit is `ram_mb` (lxcfs MemTotal) or `cgroup_max_mb`. Before this change, an LXC guest limited to 48 GiB on a 128 GiB unified-memory host was offered `qwen-image-lightning`. ComfyUI reads that model's weights into guest-charged memory, so the first render was OOM-killed.

```diff
 recommended_for(hw)
-  recommended_model_id(pool_gb(hw))            # unified_memory_mb or ram_mb
+  recommended_model_id(image_pool_gb(hw))      # min(pool, ram_mb, cgroup_max_mb)
```

The shared `pool_gb()` is untouched: the LLM agent ladder and `install.suggest` keep using it. Every caller of the recommendation goes through `recommended_for()`, so they all get the fix:
- the install-time offer;

agent_prs.title: fix(images): rank the starter pick by the guest's RAM limit (#3057)

issues.body:
### What happens

The image starter recommendation ignores the container's memory limit. `recommended_for()` (`src/hal0/comfyui/picker.py:31`) ranks boxes by `pool_gb()` (`src/hal0/install/agent_model.py:76`), which returns `unified_memory_mb or ram_mb`. On a unified-memory host with 128 GiB, an LXC guest limited to 48 GiB reports the host's 131072 MB as `unified_memory_mb`. The ≥96 GB rule then marks `qwen-image-lightning` as recommended in the install-time offer, in `hal0 setup`, and in `GET /api/comfyui/models`.

That model cannot load on such a guest. ComfyUI reads the weights into process memory, and that memory is charged to the guest's memory cgroup. On 2026-10-24 a test guest with a 48 GiB limit OOM-killed the ComfyUI process at 47.7 GB anon-rss, with the guest's cgroup as `oom_memcg`.

Expected: apply the RAM-based rule (qwen-image-lightning at ≥96 GB, sdxl-lightning at ≥16 GB, sd-1.5 below that) to the memory the guest can actually use. Here that gives `sdxl-lightning`. The thresholds stay as they are.

### How to reproduce

On an LXC guest with a memory limit below 96 GiB, running on a 128 GiB unified-memory host:

```sh
curl -s localhost:8080/api/comfyui/models | jq -r '.models[] | select(.recommended) | .id'
# qwen-image-lightning
curl -s localhost:8080/api/hardware | jq '{unified_memory_mb, ram_mb, cgroup_max_mb}'
# {"unified_memory_mb": 131072, "ram_mb": 49152, "cgroup_max_mb": null}
```

`ram_mb` (the guest's MemTotal through lxcfs) already shows the limit. `cgroup_max_mb` is null because `_read_cgroup_memory_max_mb()` (`src/hal0/hardware/probe.py:320`) reads only the guest's own `memory.max`, which is `max` there: the limit is set on the parent cgroup.

### Fix direction

For the image pick, use the smaller of the pool and the guest's RAM limit. `pool_gb()` is shared with the agent-model offer, where GTT allocations are not charged to the guest's cgroup. So either scope the change to `recommended_for()`, or decide on purpose that both offers change.

## Summary

A gated admin MCP call's approval card shows the raw arguments, but the REST URL was built by pasting path arguments in unescaped. After approval, httpx collapsed `.`/`..`, `?` and `#` cut the path short, and the server decoded `%XX`. So an approved call could act on a different resource than the card named.

```diff
 dispatch(tool, args)
+  for each path arg: refuse if not sendable as one literal segment   # mcp.invalid_arg, before any card
   if gated: enqueue approval card
   ...
 _execute_tool(tool, args)
   _split_args(tool, args)
+    same check again (a queued entry can't skip it)
   _format_url(base, template, path_args)
-    template.format(**path_args)
+    template.format(**{k: quote(v, safe="") for k, v in path_args.items()})
```

The check refuses a path argument that is:
- empty, `.`, `..`, or contains `/`;
- not a `str`, except a non-bool integer below 2^53 (JSON and the URL spell those the same);
- contains a control or format character (Unicode `Cc`/`Cf`: C0/C1 controls, zero-width space, bidi overrides, BOM) or a lone surrogate.

Everything else is percent-encoded and reaches the handler literally. That includes `:`, spaces, `+` and non-ASCII (FLM ids like `embed-gemma:300m` are unchanged), and now `?`, `#` and `%` too.

Behaviour change: a gated call with a missing path argument is now refused before a card exists. Before, it was queued, approved, and then failed.

Round 1 added 26 rows for non-string and invisible-character values, which also failed first.

issues.body:
### What happens

Gated admin MCP tools build their REST URL by pasting path arguments into the route template unescaped (`_format_url` in `src/hal0/mcp/admin.py`). The approval card shows the raw argument, but the URL that runs after approval can point somewhere else:

- **Dot segments.** httpx collapses `.` and `..` path segments before sending the request (httpx 0.28.1: `httpx.URL("http://h/api/comfyui/models/../x").raw_path == b"/api/comfyui/x"`). A path argument of `..` climbs out of the tool's route and lands on a sibling route.
- **`?` and `#`.** These end the path. `model_id="junk?x"` sends `DELETE …/models/junk`; `"junk#x"` does the same.
- **Percent escapes.** The server decodes them, so an approved `model_id="%6Dy-model"` acts on `my-model`.

The only path-argument check today is `_split_args` refusing `/`, and it runs after the operator has approved the call.

Expected: the approval card names exactly the resource the call acts on, and an argument that cannot be sent faithfully is refused before the card is shown.

### How to reproduce

`src/hal0/mcp/admin.py`: `_split_args` (~:1726) and `_format_url` (~:1752). Any gated tool with a path argument shows it, for example `comfyui_model_remove`, the `slot_*` tools and the `upstream_*` tools. Building the URL for `{"model_id": ".."}` and reading `httpx.URL(url).raw_path` shows the climb. Combined with a second path segment in a sibling argument, an approved call reaches a different route entirely. A worked example of exactly this, on an unreleased tool, was found during the image-gen overhaul review: an approved "delete file" card ran "remove model".

### If nobody fixes it

A prompt-injected or confused agent can get an operator to approve a destructive call whose card does not name what it deletes, unloads or edits. The operator's approval stops being a reliable control for every gated admin tool that takes a path argument.

### Fix size, your best guess

S. Validate path arguments in `dispatch` before a ga

issues.body:
### What happens

Loading an FLM slot with a model override (`hal0 slot load flm -m gemma3-1b-FLM` on a slot whose `[model].default` is empty or names a different model) runs the one-shot NPU inference gate against the wrong model. On FastFlowLM 1.0.10 (runner pin `1.0.10-r1c3f49e`, #3021) that makes the slot container download a model nobody asked for and leaves the slot stuck in `warming`.

Seen on a v1.6.1 pre-tag smoke (nightly `v1.6.0-nightly.20261024052735`, main 7e4e1b99):

- The container started `serve gemma3:1b` correctly, but the gate's sentinel `POST /v1/chat/completions` asked for `"model": "deepseek-r1:8b"`.
- FLM 1.0.10 auto-pulls a model it does not have, so the container downloaded `Deepseek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B-NPU2` (5.4 GB) into the shared FLM store.
- The gate timed out (`slot.flm_inference_gate_failed`), the slot stayed in `warming`, and the CLI printed `Loaded flm → state=warming`.

Expected: the gate probes the model the slot is serving (`gemma3:1b`), as the docstring of `FLMProvider.verify_inference` says it must (#1171).

### Why

`SlotManager.load(slot_name, model_id)` serves the override, but `_await_ready` (`src/hal0/slots/manager.py`, the FLM block after `wait_ready`) takes `expected_model` from `_model_default(cfg)`, which reads the TOML on disk. With an override, that value is empty or stale. `verify_inference` (`src/hal0/providers/flm.py`) then falls back to `models[0]` from `/v1/models`.

On FLM 0.9.x, `/v1/models` listed only installed models, so the fallback reloaded the wrong weights (#1171). 1. On an NPU box with the 1.0.10 flm runner, set the `flm` slot's `[model].default = ""`.
2. `hal0 slot load flm -m gemma3-1b-FLM`
3. `journalctl -u hal0-slot@flm`: the first chat request after start has `"mo

Both defects came from the CT150 smoke of #3020 and #3022 (nightly 20261024052735). There is one commit per issue.

## #3024: a runtime mask is not seen on a box that has only the suffixed unit

systemd reads `/etc/systemd/system` before `/run/systemd/system`, so `systemctl mask --runtime hermes-gateway.service` holds only while there is no `/etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service`. A box a 1.6.0 nightly installed is in exactly that state. When an `/etc` file does exist, `is-enabled` reports `disabled`, not `masked-runtime`. So the `masked-runtime` handling from #3020 covered a state systemd never reports, and missed the one that occurs.

- `_runtime_masked(run, unit_path)` (new, in `hermes_gateway_regen`) is true when there is no canonical file and `is-enabled` reports `masked*`.
- `migrate_hashed_units` treats it like a persistent mask. It writes nothing to the canonical path (an `/etc` file would shadow the mask), stops, disables and removes the suffixed unit, and never enables or starts the canonical unit. Its rollback does not touch the canonical unit either.
- `install_gateway_unit` leaves the path alone, as it does for a persistent mask.
- `gateway_state_unit` returns the canonical unit in that state. The capture in `hal0 agent install hermes` and in the installer then reads `masked-runtime` instead of the suffixed unit's `enabled`.
- The CLI and the installer handle `masked-runtime` like `masked`: they run the mask-safe move, write no unit and print the left-off note. Before this, the installer ran `install` and the CLI refreshed the unit.
- CHANGELOG: the earlier line about a runtime mask described the `/etc`-file case. It is replaced with the real behaviour. After a reboot the runtime mask is gone, and with no unit file left the gateway stays off until `sudo hal0 agent install hermes`.

After the gateway move runs past a persistent mask (#2950), `hal0 agent install hermes` prints:

```
hermes-gateway.service is masked; left as is (run 'systemctl unmask hermes-gateway.service && systemctl enable --now hermes-gateway.service' to turn it on)

Removed "/etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service".

So every box that reaches this branch ends up with no unit file.

An operator who masked the gateway and later wants it back follows the printed command, gets "Unit file does not exist", and has to work out on their own that `sudo hal0 agent install hermes` must be re-run after unmasking.

### How to reproduce

1. With only the suffixed `hermes-gateway-<hash>.service` installed, enabled and running, and no `/etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service`, run `systemctl mask hermes-gateway.service`.
2. `sudo hal0 agent install hermes`: the mask is kept, and the suffixed unit is stopped and removed (correct).
3. Run the printed remedy. `enable --now` fails.

When the canonical path is a mask, have the remedy text, built from `_gateway_left_off_note` in `src/hal0/cli/agent_commands.py`, say `systemctl unmask hermes-gateway.service && sudo hal0 agent install hermes`. Alternatively, keep a rendered copy of the unit somewhere the unmask restores.

### What happens

The CHANGELOG under [Unreleased] (#2950, #3022) says a runtime-masked `hermes-gateway.service` beside an enabled suffixed `hermes-gateway-<hash>.service` is honoured: the suffixed unit is stopped and removed, and the canonical unit is not enabled or started. On a real box the move instead enables and starts the canonical gateway.

Seen on a v1.6.1 pre-tag smoke (nightly `v1.6.0-nightly.20261024052735`, main 7e4e1b99):

Before `sudo hal0 agent install hermes`:
```
hermes-gateway.service           enabled=masked-runtime  active=inactive   (no file in /etc/systemd/system; /run/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service -> /dev/null)
hermes-gateway-1975ce4b.service  enabled=enabled         active=active
```
After:
```
hermes-gateway.service           enabled=enabled         active=active
hermes-gateway-1975ce4b.service  removed
```
The install printed `hermes-gateway.service: wrote hermes-gateway.service, enabled, started, removed hermes-gateway-1975ce4b.service`.

### Why

A runtime mask only takes effect while no `hermes-gateway.service` file exists in `/etc/systemd/system`, because systemd searches `/etc/systemd/system` before `/run/systemd/system`. That is exactly the state of a box a 1.6.0 nightly installed: only the suffixed unit exists. In that state:

- `gateway_state_unit` (`src/hal0/agents/hermes_gateway_regen.py`) sees no canonical file and returns the suffixed unit, whose state is `enabled`, so `agent install` does not treat the gateway as off.
- `migrate_hashed_units` checks only the `/etc` path for `pre_existing` and `is_masked`, so it sees no mask, writes `/etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service` (which now shadows the `/run` mask), then enables and starts it.

Refs #2950. This is the follow-up to the #3020 review, items (a)–(e) and (h).

- **(b) The installer misreports a finished move.** `python -m hal0.agents.hermes_gateway_regen install|migrate` now exits 3 on `GatewayCleanupError`, which means the gateway moved onto `hermes-gateway.service` and only the old suffixed file is left. ## Summary

FLM model pulls and the NPU model catalogue ran the host `/usr/bin/flm` from the FastFlowLM `.deb`. Only `install.sh` installs that `.deb`, so a box that only runs `hal0 update` kept an old FastFlowLM, and that old binary chose the weights and the tag list for the store a newer `flm` runner image serves. - **`flm pull`** runs in a one-shot `podman run --rm` of the FLM slot's image (honouring `image_pin`, `[slots].default_images` and the runner pin table), with the store mounted where the slot mounts it. There is no host fallback. A missing image fails the pull with "download the flm runner image first".
- **`flm list`** asks the running slot (`podman exec`) first, then a one-shot container, and uses the host binary only as a logged last resort (`flm.cli_host_fallback`).
- **`flm validate`** stays on the host. Setup uses it to gate the NPU lane before any image is pulled.
- **New privileged seam `hal0-flmctl`** (`installer/wrappers/hal0-flmctl`, `packaging/sudoers/hal0-flmctl`). Every podman flag is a literal. Operands (slot token, image ref, store dir, tag) are validated root side.
