Closes #1807.

`deploy/oto-journal-archive.service` était posée à la main et visait `/opt/oto-mcp`, un arbre fixe. L'archive tournait donc sur un script qui pouvait être en retard sur le tag servi. Elle passe à `@ARBRE@`, comme `oto-mcp-maintenance.service`. `install_timers` (`deploy/oto-backend.sh`) la pose avec la maintenance après chaque bascule, sur l'arbre de la couleur en service, et active son timer. Un tag antérieur sans ces fichiers est ignoré, sans faire échouer le déploiement.

## ⚠️ Mise en place : une installation à la main, AVANT le tag

`install_timers` est lu à l'exécution depuis **`/opt/deploy/oto-backend.sh`**, la copie installée sur la box, et non depuis l'arbre du tag. Le workflow appelle `sudo /opt/deploy/oto-backend.sh <tag>`. Le tag seul ne change donc rien : il faut recopier le script avant le tag qui porte cette PR. L'unité d'archive, elle, est lue dans l'arbre du tag.

Geste, une fois la PR fusionnée et avant le tag :
1. Comparer la copie installée à la version fusionnée, et vérifier que seul `install_timers` diffère : `git -C <clone à jour> show origin/main:deploy/oto-backend.sh > /tmp/oto-backend.sh.neuf && diff /opt/deploy/oto-backend.sh /tmp/oto-backend.sh.neuf`. Si la copie installée diverge ailleurs, s'arrêter et le signaler.
2. Comparer aussi l'unité posée à la main, que la première bascule remplacera par celle du tag : `diff /etc/systemd/system/oto-journal-archive.service /opt/oto-mcp-<couleur active>/deploy/oto-journal-archive.service`. Si la copie à la main porte un réglage absent du dépôt, s'arrêter et le signaler.
3. Installer : `install -m 0755 -o root -g root /tmp/oto-backend.sh.neuf /opt/deploy/oto-backend.sh`.
4. Laisser partir le tag. Après la bascule, éprouver :
   - `systemctl cat oto-journal-archive.service | grep -E '^(ExecStart|WorkingDirectory)='` doit nommer `/opt/oto-mcp-<couleur active>`, la même que `cat /etc/oto-mcp/active-prod` ;
   - `systemctl list-timers oto-journal-archive.timer` doit montrer un prochain tir

## Constat

`deploy/oto-journal-archive.service` est posée à la main et nomme l'arbre en dur : `ExecStart=/opt/oto-mcp/.venv/bin/python /opt/oto-mcp/deploy/lanceur_secrets.py --script deploy/archive_tool_calls.py`. Depuis le bleu/vert, `/opt/oto-mcp` est un arbre fixe, pas la couleur qui sert. L'archive tourne donc sur un script qui peut avoir une ou plusieurs versions de retard sur le tag servi.

La maintenance, elle, suit déjà la couleur active. `install_timers` (`deploy/oto-backend.sh`) la réinstalle après chaque bascule depuis l'arbre de la couleur activée, avec `@ARBRE@` remplacé. Sur une instance cible, `amorcer.sh` fait de même pour la maintenance, et pour l'archive depuis oto-backend#1805.

**Conséquence concrète :** un changement du script d'archive n'est servi qu'une fois `/opt/oto-mcp` remis à jour à la main. C'est le cas de la trace par passage de #1806 : tant que l'arbre est en retard, l'alerte `journal_archive_late` sonne alors que l'archive a tourné.

## Correctif proposé

1. `deploy/oto-journal-archive.service` passe à `@ARBRE@`, comme `oto-mcp-maintenance.service`.
2. `install_timers` la pose et active son timer avec la maintenance, après chaque bascule.
3. Le test `tests/deploy/test_maintenance_lanceur_967.py`, qui fige aujourd'hui `/opt/oto-mcp` pour cette unité, est mis à jour.

`deploy/oto-mcp.service` vise aussi `/opt/oto-mcp`. Elle semble antérieure au bleu/vert et n'est plus posée par aucun script de `deploy/` : à confirmer, puis à retirer si elle est morte.

1. **`fix(security): le token-bucket anonyme borne aussi la branche HTML`** — la garde de débit était contournée par le rendu HTML de `subdomain_project.py` sur `access_mode in ("anonymous", "secret")`. Déplacée en tête de bloc, avant le rendu.

issues.body:
Le code lit environ **quatre-vingts** variables d'environnement. `.env.example` en documente **huit**. Il ne peut donc pas servir à monter une instance, et personne ne peut dire ce qu'une machine doit déclarer pour servir correctement.

Le vrai danger n'est pas les variables absentes qui font échouer le boot — celles-là se voient. C'est **celles dont le défaut est une de nos valeurs à nous** : elles laissent l'instance démarrer, l'air de fonctionner, en pointant chez nous.

## Les défauts qui pointent chez nous (mesurés)

| variable | défaut |
|---|---|
| domaine de projet | notre domaine — sert aussi à qualifier une URL de « test » et à en avertir l'utilisateur |
| URL du dashboard | notre dashboard |
| base des liens d'invitation | notre site — **toute invitation émise par l'instance envoie l'invité chez nous** |
| origines CORS | la liste en dur de nos origines (plus celles d'un partenaire) — sans la variable, le dashboard d'un tiers est bloqué par le navigateur et **aucun appel REST n'aboutit** |
| relais d'email | notre relais |
| adresse d'expéditeur | notre adresse |
| destinataire du formulaire de contact | une adresse personnelle chez nous |

À quoi s'ajoutent, hors variables : les contrats légaux (CGU/CGV/DPA) en dur vers notre site, surchargeables seulement par ligne de registre en base — donc pas par instance ; et une quinzaine de liens de marque servis dans des messages d'erreur et des pages publiques.

## Ce qu'on fait

- **l'inventaire complet**, dérivé du code et non écrit à la main : nom, où c'est lu, défaut, et surtout la colonne qui compte — *ce qui se passe si l'instance ne la pose pas* ;
- classer en trois : **requises** (le boot échoue, c'est sain) · **à déclarer sous peine de pointer chez nous** (le vrai sujet) · **réglages** (un défaut neutre est légitime) ;
- faire basculer la deuxième classe vers la première : sur une instance, un défaut qui pointe chez nous doit devenir un refus de démarrer, pas un silence ;
- régénérer `.env.example` depu

- `GET /api/datastores/{datastore}/rows` gagne un `fields` optionnel (comma-separated, même patron que `versions`), **même sémantique que la face MCP `data_rows`** : colonnes gardées + `_id` toujours présent, une colonne déclarée sans valeur rendue `null`. ## Résumé — oto-backend#980, suite

Profil GIL de prod (18/09/2026, oto cd, py-spy --gil 60s) : `_pertinente` dans `_row_to_dict` (`oto_mcp/datastore/core.py`) était **quadratique**. `any(f.startswith(k + ".") for f in fields)` était réévalué pour CHAQUE clé de la ligne, DEUX FOIS (une fois pour les couches, une fois pour les valeurs). Avec `fields` à 144 colonnes (cas réel scout), pages de 50/500 lignes : ~150 clés × 144 champs × 500 lignes. Ce générateur était la première feuille de code applicatif au profil GIL, ~9% du temps — devant `_row_to_dict` elle-même (~5,7%).

## Fait

Les bases de `fields` (`"email.origine"` → base `"email"`) ne changent pas d'une clé à l'autre : `bases_demandees = frozenset(f.split(".", 1)[0] for f in fields)` est maintenant calculé **une fois par appel** (donc une fois par ligne, `_row_to_dict` étant appelée par ligne), puis `_pertinente(k)` teste l'appartenance à cet ensemble (`k in bases_demandees`, O(1)) au lieu de reparcourir `fields` (O(champs)) pour chaque clé. Passe de O(clés × champs) à O(clés + champs) par ligne.

Sémantique strictement inchangée : `k in fields` (le champ nu directement demandé) et `any(f.startswith(k + "."))` (une couche de `k` demandée) sont tous deux couverts par `k in bases_demandees`, puisque `"champ".split(".", 1)[0] == "champ"` pour un champ sans point.

Nouveau test `test_le_balayage_de_fields_ne_depend_plus_du_nombre_de_cles_de_la_ligne` : compare le nombre d'ITÉRATIONS de `fields` (via un `frozenset` instrumenté, `_FieldsCompteIterations`) entre une ligne à 5 clés et une ligne à 200 clés, même `fields`. ## Fait

`datastore_page_with_stats` (`oto_mcp/db/datastore.py`) calcule les trois en **une seule requête**, sur une seule CTE `f` (le jeu mince ET filtré, calculé une fois) :

- `p` : la page (`row_number()` + `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`), sur `f`.

`agg LEFT JOIN p ON TRUE` (jamais l'inverse) : `agg` porte toujours exactement une ligne (`COUNT` sans `GROUP BY` n'est jamais vide), donc le total et les compteurs survivent même quand `offset` dépasse le total (page vide, testé explicitement).

agent_prs.title: fix(datastore): data_claim_next dit quoi faire sans data_release — fermer le run libère, l'intention ne s'écrit jamais dans la fiche (#613)

issues.body:
**État au 05/09/2026 : le point 1 est livré (`5e9deb48`), avec sa règle de rédaction dans `docs/conventions.md`. Seul le point 2 reste — et c'est une décision de conception, pas un correctif.**

## Reste à faire — la décision

Une description servie qui tient compte des outils **réellement servis à la session**. Le jeu est connu au handshake (`mcp_tools` de l'endpoint, inclusion) : une phrase conditionnelle « … then release it (`data_release`) » ne serait rendue que si l'outil est dans le jeu.

**Ce que ça engage, et pourquoi c'est une décision et pas un correctif** : les descriptions deviendraient **par-session**, et l'empreinte servie se mesurerait alors par jeu servi et non plus globalement. L'introspection n'existe aujourd'hui que pour les endpoints publiés. À instruire avant d'être implémentée.

## Le constat qui fonde la question (campagne, 29/08/2026)

`data_claim_next` disait dans sa description : « write your progress via data_write, then RELEASE the row — … Release with data_release… ». Sur une flotte où `data_release` est **filtré à l'inclusion**, les agents lisaient cette prescription à chaque appel sans pouvoir l'exécuter. Résultat sur cent fiches : ils ont écrit leur intention **dans la fiche de l'entreprise**, en fabriquant des colonnes — `_liberation: "run_finish"`, `_action: "release"`, `_run_id: <jeton>` (sur 6 lignes) : des paramètres d'appel dans des données clientes, exportées, dont un jeton. (`_run_id` dans `row` est refusé depuis #602 ; les deux autres sont des colonnes libres.)

**Lecture** : un agent qui a une intention et pas de destination s'en fabrique une. La description est relue à chaque appel, la consigne une fois : **le texte le plus près du geste gagne** (même mécanique que les 37,5 % de `_run_id`).

## Même famille, à noter

Un harnais qui ne passe pas `filter` à `data_claim_next` et l'écrit dans la prose de l'ordre compte sur l'agent pour le recopier — **une contrainte demandée par la prose n'est pas une contrainte**.

issues.body:
Retour d'un **front tiers**, consommateur pur de l'API REST : « un backlink est un `doc_id` entier ; aucun mapping `doc_id → nod_id`. Pour un “qui s'en sert” cliquable : `nod_id`, `type`, et idéalement le verbe de relation (cite / inclut / dépend). »

## Ce que le code fait aujourd'hui

**Un backlink porte trois clés, et pas celles-là.** `db/backlinks.py:122-129` :

```sql
SELECT d.id, d.project_id, d.title FROM doc_links l
 JOIN docs d ON d.id = l.from_doc WHERE l.to_doc = %s ORDER BY d.title
```

→ `id` (l'entier de la page citante — pas `doc_id`), `project_id`, `title`.

- **Pas de `nod_id`.** Il serait dérivable sans jointure — la formule est publique et déjà écrite en SQL : `'nod_' || substr(md5('doc:' || d.id), 1, 24)` (`db/nodes.py:105-121`). Elle n'est simplement pas appliquée ici.
- **Pas de `type`.** Ni le `kind` de la page (`doc|note|source`), ni la nature servie par la surface nœuds.
- **Pas de verbe de relation, et ce n'est pas un oubli : c'est le modèle.** `db/backlinks.py:3-6` : « pas de NER, pas de liens *typés* — seulement `[[…]]` non typé ».

**Le stockage ne peut pas porter un verbe aujourd'hui.** Table `doc_links`, `db/schema/projects.py:159-168` :

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS doc_links (
    from_doc BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES docs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    to_doc   BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES docs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    PRIMARY KEY (from_doc, to_doc)
);
```

**Deux colonnes.** Ni type, ni ancre, ni position, ni horodatage. Ferme #658. Une colonne `readonly: true` protège une valeur posée par une personne
contre son écrasement par un agent — et la fermait à **tout le monde**, y compris celui
à qui elle appartient. La seule sortie nommée était le schéma : lever le cran, écrire,
le remettre.

## Pourquoi un paramètre d'appel, et pas un interrupteur

⚠️ **La manœuvre « lever → écrire → remettre » est le défaut qu'on ferme, pas la sortie
qu'on offre.** Mesurée sur l'autre verrou de la plateforme, celui qui a la forme d'un
ÉTAT (`key_required`, #668) : le 01/09 un agent refusé la retrouve seul et la rejoue
deux fois sur deux tableaux — il referme ; le lendemain un autre passage ne la retrouve
pas et s'arrête. *Il suffit qu'une exécution s'interrompe entre « lever » et « remettre »
pour que le verrou reste ouvert sans que personne le sache* — et une colonne
déverrouillée ne produit aucun signal.

Le forçage vaut donc **pour cet appel et rien d'autre** : rien à rouvrir dans le schéma,
donc rien à refermer, rien à oublier.

## Le nom : `readonly_override`

Il nomme **le cran qu'il lève**, et se lit à côté de lui : la surface existante déclare
`readonly`, `key_required`, `unknown_fields`, `origine` — `<sujet>_<qualificatif>`,
snake_case. `override` dit un ACTE ponctuel là où `readonly: false` dit un état ; les
deux ne se confondent pas à la lecture. Écartés : `force` (ne dit pas quoi), et
`force_readonly` (se lit « force la colonne à être readonly »).

Il ne lève **que** `readonly`. Les deux autres crans de la famille (`origine: "system"`,
`system: "<source>"`) ferment ce que la PLATEFORME pose, pas ce que le client a remis :
il n'y a rien à y corriger de la main du propriétaire.

## Le palier — propriétaire ∪ gouvernant

`ownership.owns` (neuf : la branche owner-match de `can_access`, isolée) ∪
`ownership.can_govern`. **Les deux ensembles se croisent sans s'inclure** — un membre de
l'org propriétaire POSSÈDE sans gouverner, un gérant (`role='manager'`, ADR 0048)
GOUVERNE sans posséder — d'où l

issues.body:
Retour d'un **front tiers**, consommateur pur de l'API REST : « les slots d'une procédure sont écrits par `PUT /api/me/instructions/{slug}`, jamais projetés sur `GET /api/me/guides/{guide_id}` — l'îlot “Équipement” reste fermé. »

## Ce que le code fait aujourd'hui — la prémisse est fausse, le blocage est réel

**Les slots SONT servis.** Branche `guide_id` du handler, `capabilities/orgs/instructions.py:457-462` :

```python
return deprecations.avec_les_deux_noms({
    "org_id": …, "guide_id": int(guide_id), "scope": "org", "slug": …, "title": …,
    "description": …, "version": …,
    "body_md": instr["body_md"], "slots": instr.get("slots") or [],
    "referenced_tools": await tool_registry.manifest_for(instr["body_md"])})
```

C'est bien la même colonne que celle écrite par `PUT /api/me/instructions/{slug}` : validation par `slots.validate_slots` (`orgs/instructions.py:565`), persistance `org_store.set_instruction(…, slots=…)` (`:579-581`), relecture `SELECT … slots … FROM org_instructions WHERE id = %s` (`org_store/instructions.py:263-272`).

**Alors pourquoi l'îlot reste fermé ? Deux raisons, toutes deux dans le contrat.**

### 1. La forme d'un slot n'est déclarée nulle part

`GuideView.slots` est un **`Optional[list]` nu** — `capabilities/orgs/instructions.py:92`. Même chose aux quatre autres endroits où le champ apparaît (`:241`, `:247` `suggested_slots`, `:349`, `:388`). En OpenAPI, ça donne un tableau **sans `items`** : « une liste de n'importe quoi ». Un front qui dérive son formulaire du contrat ne peut rien en faire, alors que la donnée arrive.

La forme, elle, est parfaitement définie — dans le validateur, pas dans un modèle : `{name, type, description?, connector?, schema?}` avec `type ∈ ("tableau", "connecteur", "doc")` (`slots.py:28`), `name` normalisé `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}` (`slots.py:31`, `40-47`), 32 slots max, description tronquée à 500 (`slots.py:37-38`), marqueur en prose `<slot:name>` (`slots.py:34`). Il manque un modèle pydantic qui dise ça
issues.title: Slots d'une procédure : ils SONT servis, mais leur forme n'est pas déclarée (Optional[list] nu) et la fiche ne dit jamais ce qui est branché

agent_prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #767.

`tools/Sign-Authenticode.ps1` discovers `SmartHopper*.dll` recursively but then filters through an explicit `$allowedAssemblies` allowlist. `SmartHopper.Providers.LocalAI.dll` and `SmartHopper.Providers.Ollama.dll` were never added to that list, so both provider assemblies shipped unsigned and `ProviderManager`/`ProviderClassifier` classified them as untrusted, which is why Grasshopper refuses to enable them in `2.0.0-dev.260821`. The hash manifest (`hashes/2.0.0-dev.260821.json`) already contained both DLLs, so only the Authenticode step was out of sync.

```diff
     "SmartHopper.Providers.Gemini.dll",
+    "SmartHopper.Providers.LocalAI.dll",
+    "SmartHopper.Providers.Ollama.dll"
 )
```

Also restructures `CHANGELOG.md`: everything that actually shipped in [2.0.0-dev.260821](https://github.com/architects-toolkit/SmartHopper/releases/tag/2.0.0-dev.260821) was still sitting under `[Unreleased]` (the release did not get its own section), so those entries now live under `## [2.0.0-dev.260821] - 2026-08-21` and `[Unreleased]` holds only this signing fix.

## Breaking Changes

None.

## Testing Done

None locally — Authenticode signing is Windows-only and needs `signtool.exe` plus the signing PFX, and `pwsh` is unavailable in this environment. Verification comes from the next Windows dev build: both provider DLLs should be Authenticode-signed and load without a trust warning in Grasshopper.

- [x] This PR is focused on a single feature or bug fix
- [x] Version in Solution.props was updated, if necessary, and follows semantic versioning
- [x] CHANGELOG.md has been updated
- [x] PR title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) format
- [x] PR description follows [Pull Request Description Template](#pull-request-description-template)

## Goal
Find anything in a trip quickly, above all on phones. For example, "on which day is the temple visit?" is answered by searching "temple".

- **Release:** the search ships in 0.15.0, not 0.14.0.

issues.body:
Wherever Jourfold shows weather or exchange rates, it should say quietly when that data was fetched and offer a way to fetch it again now. This is about the places the data appears, on every platform: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android phones and tablets, iOS and iPadOS.

**Wanted**

1. **When it was fetched.** Visible where the data is, but not prominent and not distracting: a small caption, or a tooltip where space is tight.
2. **Refresh now.** A manual action to fetch again, without going through settings.

**Where the data is shown today**

| Data | Place | Fetch time shown? |
|---|---|---|
| Weather | Desktop inspector | Yes, "as of …" (`InspectorView.cs:474`) |
| Weather | Desktop timetable and list, per day | No |
| Weather | Mobile Today, Plan, item details (`Lines.DayWeather`, `Lines.ItemWeather`) | No |
| Rates | Desktop Costs converter (`CollectionViews.cs:155`) | Only the ECB date of the rates |
| Rates | Mobile converter and its row under More | Only the ECB date of the rates |
| Rates | Desktop expense with a stored conversion | The rate date, which is correct for a stored value and should stay as it is |

There's no manual refresh anywhere. A forced fetch only happens when the feature is turned on or its settings change.

**Notes for the implementation**

- The ECB date and the fetch time are different things: on a Sunday the newest rates are Friday's even if they were fetched a minute ago. Both are useful.
- Weather already carries `Fetched`. `ExchangeRates` only has `Date`, so the fetch time needs storing, or can come from the saved file's time. If it goes into the record, that part belongs in TravelRepo.
- Only offer refresh when the person has turned the feature on, as today, and never fetch without that consent.
- A failed refresh should keep the existing data and its time and say that it failed. Offline is a normal case on the road.
- Refresh should bypass the automatic schedule's waiting periods (`RateSchedule`) while still protecting against repea

issues.body:
Today a long press opens the menu while the finger is still down, 500 ms after it touched the screen (`Menus.OnHold`, `Menus.cs:24`). When a hold turns into a scroll or drag, the menu can still open, and the code carries several checks to reduce that.

**Proposal: open the menu on release instead of on a timer.**

| Finger | Result |
|---|---|
| Released before the threshold, not moved | Normal tap |
| Moved more than the tolerance, at any time | Scroll or drag, no menu and no tap |
| Held past the threshold, then released without moving | Menu opens |

Since nothing happens until the finger lifts, a hold that turns into a move can no longer open the menu, which removes that whole class of edge cases. Much of the timer code can then go, such as the check for a finger captured by a swipe.

**Details to cover**

- Keep a minimum hold (the current 500 ms) so a long press is still different from a tap.
- The menu no longer appears by itself, so people need a sign that the hold has registered: a subtle change of the pressed state at the threshold, and haptic feedback if available.
- Right click and accessibility should keep working through `ContextRequested`, and TalkBack and keyboard clicks must not change.
- `OnHold` also drives long-press copy (`Menus.Copies`), so that would change the same way. Callers: `TimetableView.cs:201` and `:285`, `Lines.cs:118`, `TripListView.cs:81`.
- It's shared code, so Android phones and tablets and the iOS branch all get it.

**Done when:** a test covers the three cases above, plus a hold followed by a move that ends with no menu and no click.
issues.title: Mobile: open the long-press menu on release instead of on a timer

issues.body:
On an emulated Pixel C tablet the sidebar says "Nur auf diesem Handy" (only on this phone).

`MainActivity.Device()` decides between phone and tablet by asking whether the device can make voice calls (`TelephonyManager.IsVoiceCapable`). The emulated tablet reports that it can, so it's called a phone. The `{device}` placeholder is used in 20 strings, so the wrong word can appear in other places too.

A real Wi-Fi tablet should get the right word. A tablet with a SIM and voice support would get the wrong one, and so does this emulator.

**Suggestion:** decide by screen size instead, for example `Configuration.SmallestScreenWidthDp >= 600`, which is also closer to how the layout picks its own breakpoints.
issues.title: Android: tablets with voice support are called a phone

issues.body:
On mobile, an amount typed with a German thousands separator is saved as a decimal, so it ends up a thousand times too small and nothing warns about it.

**To reproduce**

1. Quick Add → Expense (Ausgabe).
2. Enter `1.234` as the amount, currency EUR, and add it.
3. Open Costs.

**Expected:** 1.234,00 EUR. **Actual:** 1,23 EUR, and the total and budget are off accordingly. Confirmed on an Android tablet with the app set to German. `12,50` works correctly.

**Cause**

`QuickAddView.cs:543` swaps comma for dot and parses with the invariant culture:

```csharp
decimal.TryParse(amount.Text?.Replace(',', '.'), NumberStyles.Number, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var value)
```

So `1.234` becomes 1.234, and `1.234,56` becomes `1.234.56`, which is rejected. Booking prices go through the same code. The currency converter on the phone has the same `Replace` at `MorePages.cs:474`.

**Suggestion**

`ExchangeRates.Amount` in TravelRepo already handles this properly, treating a separator as decimal only when one or two digits follow it. Using it in both places would fix this and keep one rule. The placeholder `0.00` could also follow the language.

A test for `1.234`, `1.234,56`, `12,50` and `12.50` would keep it fixed.

issues.body:
On mobile, tapping something on a page that's scrolled down makes the page flash back to the top for a moment before it returns to where it was.

**Confirmed on an Android phone** (emulator, 1440×3040) by recording the screen and stepping through the frames:

| Where | Tap | What the frames show |
|---|---|---|
| More → Costs, scrolled down | Unfold an expense | Scrolled → **top of the page** for ~116 ms → scrolled again |
| Same page, second tap | Fold it again | Same, ~113 ms |
| Plan, scrolled down | Open a plan's details | Same, visible behind the opening sheet, ~122 ms |

It lasts about one or two frames here, so it reads as a flicker. It depends on timing, which fits it being noticed only sometimes.

**Cause**

Every change rebuilds the page. The new `ScrollViewer` starts at offset 0, and the position is restored afterwards through a posted callback, so a frame can be drawn in between:

- `AppShell.cs:215` (Today and More): `after.AttachedToVisualTree += (_, _) => Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(() => after.Offset = offset, DispatcherPriority.Loaded);`
- `PlanView.cs:186` (Plan), the same pattern.
- `TimetableView.cs:110` (timeline), the same pattern. I didn't record this one.

**Suggestion**

The desktop already solved this in `MainWindow.RenderMain`: it lays the new view out and sets the offset before anything is drawn, with a comment describing exactly this flash. The mobile shell could do the same after assigning `main.Child`: call `UpdateLayout()`, then set the offset. I haven't tried this change on mobile.

**Other platforms**

- Tablet and iOS use the same code, so they should behave the same. I didn't record them.
- On the desktop I captured clicks and an edit in a scrolled List and Timetable at about 75 frames per second and saw no jump. Other desktop views weren't tested, so if it shows up there, please add which view.

agent_prs.body:
Refs #67

Okay, so the fork used to hand the hook's detection text to the parent as an `event_description` job. The parent only drains the job pipe once per tick (`event_check_interval`, 5s by default). If the event had already ended, the fork got to its end check about 4s later, didn't see `detected:` in the Notes yet, and wrote the detection itself - then the parent's queued write landed too. `updateEventinZmDB` prepends, so the Notes had it twice.

The fork now calls `updateEventinZmDB` on its own DB handle (it already opens one after fork) for both the start and the end hook results. So the start write is always in the DB before the end check reads it, and the "ZM overwrote" branch only runs when ZM really did.

The parent's `event_description` handler is now unused. Removing it is in a follow-up PR, because proven red can't pass a test file whose only change is deleted tests.

## Acceptance

From #67:

- With hooks and `use_hook_description: yes`, an event that ends before the start hook's result is saved gets the detection in its Notes once, not twice.
- The fork writes the description itself with `updateEventinZmDB($eid, $resTxt)` instead of sending `event_description` to the main process, on both the start and end hook paths.

## Testing

- `t/25-hook-fork-flow.t`: the `updateEventinZmDB` stub now records calls and prepends to the stubbed Notes the way the real `UPDATE` does. The success path asserts one Notes write per hook result and no `event_description` line on the pipe. It fails on master (one write, plus the pipe line) and passes here.
- `make gate` passes. `sh scripts/gates/proven-red.sh master HEAD`: changed tests fail on the pre-change code.

agent_prs.body:
Fixes the ES 6 → ES 7 regression described in #48.

## The problem

Under ES 6, `objectconfig` named a zone and gave it a pattern; ZoneMinder owned the polygon. The two were joined by name after import (`utils.py:500-505` in 6.1.x).

ES 7 dropped that join:

- `process_config` only built a polygon when the config zone had `coords`. A zone declared with a `detection_pattern` and no `coords` was discarded silently — no warning, no error.
- `import_zm_zones` *appended* ZM's zones alongside the config ones instead of onto them. Since `pyzm.client._monitor_zones` never populates `Zone.pattern`, every imported polygon carried `pattern: None` → `.*`, which defeated the real per-zone pattern sitting next to it.

The result was that per-zone patterns and ZM-managed geometry became mutually exclusive: either hand-maintain a duplicate of every polygon in YAML (which goes stale the moment a zone is edited in the ZM web UI), or keep ZM's geometry and lose every pattern.

## The fix

`coords` is now optional.

- Every config zone records its patterns in `g.zone_patterns`, keyed by a normalised name, whether or not it has `coords`. Names are normalised on **both** sides (spaces → underscores, lowercased), so ZM's `My Driveway` joins to a config key of `my_driveway`.
- `import_zm_zones()` stamps those patterns onto the ZM zone of the same name instead of appending a duplicate.
- A config zone that *does* have `coords` still pins its own geometry, and the same-named ZM zone is no longer imported on top of it.

So `objectconfig.yml` expresses intent — which labels matter in which named zone — while ZoneMinder stays the source of truth for geometry, as in ES 6.

Precedence: config `coords` > ZM geometry; config pattern > ZM pattern.

## Zone entries that cannot take effect now say so

- a pattern with no `coords` and no `import_zm_zones` → error
- a pattern that matched no imported zone → error (quiet under `only_triggered_zm_zones`, where an untriggered zone is legitimately absent)

## Summary

Under ES 6, zone **patterns** lived in the config and zone **coordinates** came from ZoneMinder, joined by zone name. Under ES 7 a zone only exists if you write its `coords` into `objectconfig.yml` by hand, and `import_zm_zones: "yes"` appends ZM's zones as *duplicates* with `pattern: None` rather than joining onto them.

The result is that per-zone patterns and ZM-managed geometry are now mutually exclusive. Anyone using per-zone patterns has to maintain a hand-copied duplicate of every polygon, which silently goes stale when a zone is edited in the ZM web UI.

`hook/zmes_hook_helpers/utils.py` in 6.1.x, `process_config`, three steps:

1. `*_zone_detection_pattern` keys were collected into a separate `poly_patterns` list — **name and pattern only**, never into `g.polygons`:

changed, as Finding Diff Any lists changed Types at Library scope, instead of
one transition per member. Type scope keeps its per-member transitions.

## Goal

Make Library-scope `diff --analysis unsafe-code` report the Types whose unsafe
code changed, as Finding Diff Any does at Library scope, instead of one
transition per member. Type scope keeps its per-member transitions.

The operator set the direction on #10881:

- Library summaries list the Types that have a finding, so a Library count is
  the number of Types.
- Library diff follows Finding Diff Any: it lists which Types changed, with no
  per-Type change counts in the primary summary.
- The reasoning is the [no rows within rows](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect/blob/main/docs/design/scope-symmetry.md#no-rows-within-rows)
  rule.

## Shape

| Type | Unsafe code |
| --- | --- |
| A Type with findings at both endpoints that differ | `Changed` |
| A Type that gained its first finding | `Added` |
| A Type that lost its last finding | `Removed` |

## Open question

Should a change in a member's safe-boundary state count as a change?

- Today the state isn't part of `UnsafeMemberFindingSummary`, so a module that
  switches to the updated rules changes no row.
- Under a Types-only Library summary, counting it would flag each affected Type
  once, not every member.

`docs/design/unsafe-code-section.md#diff`. The section's rename to

Closes #11128.

## What changes

`IrFunction.ValidateEliminatedLocalSlots` runs after every pass whenever
semantic checks are armed, which is the default. Before this change it walked
the whole local scope once for each eliminated slot, so the cost grew as
slots times nodes on a large reconstructed body. It now makes one walk that
records the first reference to each eliminated slot, then reports the same
errors with the same messages and exceptions, in slot order.
`NodesSharingLocalScope` now uses an explicit stack instead of nested
iterators, and still skips lambdas and local functions that have their own
scope. One shared matcher, `AnyBoundLocalSlot`, now backs both
`NodeBindsLocalSlot` and the validator, so the two cannot drift apart.

Normative owner: [`IrNode.CheckInvariant`](../blob/main/src/ILInspector.Decompiler/Pipeline/Ir/IrNodes.Function.cs).
The claim is unchanged: no eliminated local slot is referenced in the
function's shared local scope. Only the cost of checking it changed.

## Evidence

- No-corpus gate: 8274 passed, 5 failed, 7 skipped. All five failures
  were already known on base: the custom event accessors filter, the
  field-like event render, and three AuthoredRebuildFidelity PDB
  acquisition tests.

issues.body:
The eliminated-local invariant check walks the whole tree once per eliminated
slot, so it scales badly on large spilled bodies.

## Cost

`IrFunction.ValidateEliminatedLocalSlots` (added in #9567, in
`src/ILInspector.Decompiler/Pipeline/Ir/IrNodes.Function.cs`):

- It iterates every eliminated local slot.
- For each slot, it calls `LocalSlotReferencesInScope(this, index)`.
- That walks the whole tree through `NodesSharingLocalScope`, a recursive
  `yield` iterator. Each node therefore passes through one enumerator per tree
  level.

The cost is O(eliminated slots x nodes x depth). `IrNode.CheckInvariant` runs
it after every pass while semantic checks are armed, which is on by default
since #3302, and the pipeline has about 200 passes.

## Evidence

From the #11093 measurement on CoreCLR (an investigation probe, not a NativeAOT
claim):

- A classic async method returning
  `await F(0) + await F(1) + ... + await F(499)` reconstructs Full, but spends
  about 132 s in passes under the tracer, and 91 s untraced.
- Only about 19 s of that is the classic async pass.
- Ordinary passes each take about 6 s: slot materialization, producer-only
  slot retirement, short-circuit ternary, increment/decrement and others.
- The hottest decompiler frame in the sample is `NodesSharingLocalScope`, under
  `ValidateEliminatedLocalSlots`.
- The 2,000-term version did not finish within 300 s.

The body is a left-deep binary tree about 500 levels deep, with hundreds of
spill locals.

## Suggested direction

Make the check one pass over the tree:

1. Collect the set of local slots that scoped nodes bind or read.
2. Intersect that set with the eliminated set.
3. Report the first offending node.

Separately, flatten `NodesSharingLocalScope` to use an explicit stack. That also
benefits `PdbLocalScopePass` and `LocalSlotReferencedInScope`.

This should change no output; the invariant's semantics stay the same.

Related to #11093 and #4472.

agent_prs.body:
Part of #10706, the first slice of Finding Diff Any adoption step 7.

## Claim

Normative owner: `docs/design/finding-diff-any.md#contract`, together with the paragraph under it on one-sided bodies. At the Library level, a Type's Body is `Changed` when "a method of it with a body is present on one side only", and "a method with a body present on one side only, public or not, is a Body difference without reading its IL; a public one is an API difference too."

The code didn't do this for public methods. `BodiesEqual` still carried the older rule: "A public method on one side only is an API fact; its body is not compared". #10195 replaced that rule in the design but kept it in the code. So a paired Type that gained a public method with a body reported API `Changed` and Body `Unchanged`. The Type level that step 7 adds requires this fix. Its partition claim makes such a Member Body `Changed` (`#type`, rules 2 and 3), and that holds only if the Library level agrees.

## Change

- **`BodiesEqual`.** Once the Body censuses are equal, one pass over the before side's methods collects the paired methods and returns at a before-side method with a body that has no pair. The after side is searched only when some method went unpaired. Paired IL is read after that, so a body that can't be decoded never hides a presence difference. The pair list is reused across units.
- **`FindingDiffAnyTypePairing.Inventory`** folds the same rule into the Type's Body state, and **`Explain`** reports the method as `- body …` or `+ body …`.
- A non-public one-sided method already differed in the Body census, so in practice the change only affects public methods.
- **Design.** The Type inventory paragraph now states the rule.

## Gates

- **Fixture expectations.** Three Types gain a public method with a body and now read Body `Changed`: `PublicMemberAdded`, `InterfaceAdded` (its `Dispose`), and `Generic<T>` (`Other`). A new fixture, `AbstractMemberAdded`, adds a public abstract method with no body

Follow-up to the CLI adoption of Finding Unsafe Any (#5254).

The CLI `Unsafe Code` section's Library scope now lists Types through
**Finding Unsafe Any**, the census's visit settled at each Type's first
finding. The producer (`FindingUnsafeAny` in `ILInspector.Analysis`) is
host-neutral and runs under Browser/Wasm.

The Inspect Web Library **Unsafe** tab still runs the Library census and
shows per-Type counts. Its
[scope-of-work rule](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect/blob/main/docs/design/inspect-web-surface-composition.md#unsafe)
reuses a loaded Library census so a drill from the Library starts no new
census.

Adopting Finding Unsafe Any there is a design decision for the web owner:

- Library rows would list Types (no counts), as the CLI does.
- A drill to a Type would run the Type-scope census instead of selecting from
  a loaded Library census.
- The Library cost on large libraries drops (CoreLib census about 2.0 s vs about
  0.9 s, JIT, CLI measurement).

Closes #11093. Part of #4472.

The classic async general inverse now counts branch targets once per method,
instead of rescanning the whole body for every await it splices. Output does
not change. Large classic async methods decompile 2-4x faster under NativeAOT.

## Design basis

The normative owner is
[`docs/design/classic-async-reconstruction.md#domain-and-failure-semantics`](docs/design/classic-async-reconstruction.md#domain-and-failure-semantics):
the inverse has no planning budget or tree-depth admission of its own. This PR
keeps that claim and records the measurement that justifies it.

## Changes

- `ClassicGeneralInverse.SpliceSuspensions`:
  - Before splicing, it counts the transfers into each offset once: `Branch`,
    `ConditionalBranch`, distinct `SwitchBranch` targets and `Leave`.
  - `SpliceOne` decrements the counts for the IsCompleted test and the
    suspension and resume blocks it detaches.
  - The two `_work.Body.Descendants.Any(TargetsOffset ...)` scans that ran for
    every suspension are now count lookups.
  - Splicing only removes transfers, so the counts answer the same "is this
    block still entered" question as the old scans.
- The design document records the #11093 measurement: generated methods with
  4,000 awaits, a 500-term spilled expression, 300 nested try/finally levels
  and a 1,000-case switch all reconstruct Full without unbounded recursion. A

issues.body:
The classic async general inverse has no depth or work limit of its own.

## Context

PR #11079 retired the classic async recipes. The recipe core had a planning
budget and a tree-depth gate, and both failed visibly when exceeded. Those
gates covered only the recipe path, which ran after the inverse had already
declined.

`docs/design/classic-async-reconstruction.md#domain-and-failure-semantics`
now states that the inverse has no planning budget or tree-depth admission.

## Question

Can a supported, Roslyn-lowered classic async `MoveNext` drive the inverse into
unbounded or pathological work, or deep recursion? Examples:

- very many awaits;
- deeply nested expression trees spilled across awaits;
- large state dispatch.

If so, the owner should define a bounded admission that fails visibly, rather
than letting the inverse overflow the stack or hang.

## Evidence so far

- The pinned 0.14.0 census corpus shows no problem.
- The pass tests show no problem.
- No exact-head probe has measured worst-case inputs yet.

## Suggested next step

Measure the inverse's depth and work on a generated extreme fixture. Then
decide whether the design needs an admission bound.

Normative owner: `docs/design/classic-async-reconstruction.md`.
Part of #4472 and tracker #10190.

Normative owner: `docs/pdb-acquisition.md#provider-policy`.

issues.body:
Owner: [Type and Member inspection documents](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect/blob/main/docs/design/type-member-inspection-documents.md). Prerequisite for the Library symbol document producer (#11028, design #11030); narrower first step of #11037; fixes the display half of #11033.

## Problem

The Type and Member documents spell a Member's display signature without nullable annotations. `MetadataTypeDeclarationPopulationInspection` and `MetadataMethodGroupInspection` build display text with `MetadataDeclarationQuery.Get*SignatureText`, whose string decoder has no nullable handling. The identity signature beside it is decoded with `typeNullableContext: 0`. Meanwhile the older API surface path (`ApiSurfaceExtractor`, behind `type --json`) applies the Type's and Member's nullable context and prints `TValue? Deserialize<TValue>(System.IO.Stream utf8Json, System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions? options = null)`.

So the same Member has two display spellings depending on the route. The member view also prints `= null` for struct defaults (#11033). The Library symbol document requires each record's `display_signature` to equal the Type document's, and its vectors, built from production's spelling, carry nullable annotations.

## Proposal

The Type and Member documents' display signature for methods, properties, fields, and events becomes the nullable-, tuple-name-, and dynamic-aware spelling that `ApiSurfaceExtractor` already computes from the Type's and Member's nullable context, with correct defaults (`= default` for a struct, `= null` for a reference or `Nullable<T>`). One spelling then serves the Type document, Member overviews and documents, Browser declarations, and the find index.

Evidence: for System.Text.Json 10.0.14, every admitted Member's Type-document display signature equals the API surface signature; the change lands with NativeAOT before-and-after timing for Type and Member document production, because nullable decoding adds work on that path.

The CLI `Unsafe Code` section's Library scope lists the Types that have
unsafe code, through **Finding Unsafe Any**: the unsafe member census's own

Inspect Web gains an **Unsafe** view over the shared unsafe member census. **Analysis** becomes the inspector at Library, Type, and Member scope, and Unsafe is a tab in each. The view uses progressive disclosure, as Compare does:

- **Library:** the Types with unsafe members.
- **Type:** that Type's members.
- **Member:** that member's evidence.

Each scope is a useful answer on its own and leads to the next. This is step 4 of [unsafe member findings](docs/design/unsafe-member-findings.md#adoption-and-gates).

Owner: [`docs/design/inspect-web-surface-composition.md#unsafe`](docs/design/inspect-web-surface-composition.md#unsafe), for the Browser presentation. The census owns admission, attribution, identity, exposure, the new safe-boundary state, Type groups and counts, and completeness ([`unsafe-member-findings.md`](docs/design/unsafe-member-findings.md)).

## Three dimensions

Every scope keeps three separate dimensions and never merges them into one safe or unsafe value:

- **Presence.** The member uses or propagates unsafe code. Propagation is the explicit caller-unsafe contract.
- **Exposure.** Public, non-public, or unknown.
- **Safe boundary.** The member uses an unsafe context without propagating it to callers ([memory-safety models](docs/design/memory-safety-models.md#v2-audit-and-identification-scenarios)). This carries the heaviest audit burden.
  - It's decided only under the updated rules.
  - Under the legacy rules it's shown as **legacy rules** (not applicable), never as a negative.
  - A propagator is never a safe boundary.

issues.body:
Found by the closure-hash prefilter probe, under #10227. This is a real occurrence.

In the .NET runtime pack 10.0.12 → 11.0.0-rc.1, the **setter** of `System.Security.Cryptography.AsnEncodedData.RawData` gained `[Obsolete]` (SYSLIB0065). The property and its getter didn't change.

```text
$ dotnet-inspect diff --library <10.0.12>/System.Security.Cryptography.dll..<11.0.0-rc.1>/System.Security.Cryptography.dll --all -t AsnEncodedData
> No API changes detected.
```

API Declarations spell `public byte[] RawData { get; set; }` on both sides. The accessor-level attribute is neither shown nor compared.

**Expected:** the API status analysis ([`api-status-analysis.md`](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect/blob/main/docs/design/api-status-analysis.md)) reports the obsolete transition on the setter: "Member 'RawData' setter was made obsolete", with the message and diagnostic id. Obsolescence on an accessor is a contract change callers see as a warning, or as an error when `error: true`.

**Likely cause:** status facts are read per member, not per accessor. `ApiAccessor` carries no obsolete fact, and the declaration renderer places attributes only on the property.

## Measurement

`library <assembly> -D` on `dotnet-inspect-perf-3` (NativeAOT, 24 counterbalanced rounds, against main 759d65104):

| Assembly | Head/main | A/A |
| --- | --- | --- |

| System.Private.CoreLib | 0.997 | 0.997 |

| Cost | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Projection load (`PlatformCallerUnsafeContracts.Embedded`) | about 1.2 ms |

`LoadEmbedded` reads the 375 KB, 2,327-entry text resource, then builds three sets: one of identifier strings and two of member and declaring-type names. Slice 5a already parses UTF-8 spans instead of splitting strings. The remaining cost is reading the resource and building the sets.

NativeAOT preinitializes static arrays of string literals, so lookup becomes a binary search with nothing built at run time. Owner: `docs/design/platform-caller-unsafe-contracts.md#data-acquisition`.

- Contract identity, lookup semantics, and contract sources are unchanged.

Explain search now scores a multi-word search text word by word. This is
the ranking change that
[the owner doc](docs/design/capability-catalog-search.md#phrase-search)
had deferred as "a separate ranking change". Fixes #10568.

## Behavior

- **Phrase search.** A search text with more than one segment and at least
  one search word is a phrase. Search words are segments of three or more
  characters that aren't in a fixed list of 24 function words. Each word is
  compared with each term under the existing `StringDistance` rule and its
  0.6 threshold. A word scores its best match times that term's weight, and
  the phrase score is the mean over words. Resources below 0.25 are
  excluded.
- **Heading weights.** A term from the resource's own heading weighs 1:
  owner identity, key, example, name, complete path, or the path's last
  segment. A summary, related route or binding, or a path segment that only
  scopes the resource weighs 1/1.5. This is the H1-to-body ratio from the
  dotnet-docs-llm-tools keyword extractor.
- **A phrase equal to a term matches it whole** (`dependency structure` →
  1.0). Fuzzy whole-text comparison is not applied to phrases: it ranked
  Source Locations first for `boxing allocations` from a shared word ending.
- **Single-word search is unchanged.**
- **`SimilarityThreshold` reports the threshold that applied to the request:**
  0.6 for whole text, 0.25 for a phrase. Every returned result meets it. The
  Document shape is unchanged, and the Browser gets the same behavior from

- Fixes #10577
- Changes `ForeachStatementPass`: a loop whose iteration local is stored
  anywhere outside the header's element or `Current` store keeps its lowered
  form instead of raising to a `foreach` that assigns its iteration variable
- Design owner: `docs/decompiler-architecture.md` (pass layer) with the raise
  contract in `docs/decompiler-raise-discipline.md#raise-acceptance-contract` —
  a raise must emit C# that binds; a `foreach` whose variable is assigned does
  not (CS1656). Unchanged: this fix keeps every owned claim; the record it adds
  is the real witness below.
- Card revision: not applicable (no corpus-visible population change expected;
  the fast suite and the compile-back gates are the evidence)

## Correctness fix

| Obligation | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| False claim | Fidelity Full for a body that does not compile: `foreach (string V_1 in xs) { ...; V_1 = null; }` (CS1656). |
| Root cause | Every `foreach` matcher (enumerator, pattern, array, string, rectangular array, `await foreach`) checked only its scaffold locals (enumerator, array copy, index) and never stores to the item local, in either store form: `StoreLocal`, or `InitObject` on the local's address (`item = default` on a struct or type parameter). |
| Fix shape | One predicate, `IterationVariableOnlyStoredByHeader`, applied in each matcher: decline when the item local has any `StoreLocal` other than the header's or any `InitObject` on its address. The enumerator raise then falls back to its existing inline form with a fresh variable the body copies from; the indexed raises keep the `for` loop. Other address loads stay allowed (a struct item's instance-method receiver). |
| Scope boundary | Passing the iteration variable by `ref` (CS1657) is not checked; no matcher's scaffold rules change; the fresh-variable inline form is the pass's existing behavior. |
| Falsifier | A compiler-produced `foreach` that stops raising after this change, or a raised `foreach` whose body still stores
agent_prs.title: Keep a loop lowered when its iteration variable is stored outside the header

issues.body:
## Problem

`ForeachStatementPass` forms a `foreach` statement when the enumerator local is referenced nowhere else, but it never checks for stores to the iteration local. A body that assigns the iteration variable therefore renders as a `foreach` whose variable is assigned, which is CS1656 (`Cannot assign to 'x' because it is a 'foreach iteration variable'`), and the result is reported at fidelity Full.

## Witness

Found during adversarial review of #10572 (round 6). Compiler-produced probe, built without optimization so the dead store survives:

```csharp
foreach (string s in xs) { Console.WriteLine(s); s = null; }   // as IL: ldnull; stloc at the end of the body
```

The harness `--dump` prints `foreach (string V_1 in xs) { Console.WriteLine(V_1); V_1 = null; }` and `--validity-check` reports CS1656 for the method while its fidelity is Full. `UsingStatementPass` already declines a resource local referenced outside the `using` (`LocalReferencesOnlyWithin`); the foreach pass has no equivalent check on `CurrentStore.Index`.

## Why it matters now

The general classic async inverse (#4472, #10190 slice 2) carries Roslyn's scope-end clear of a hoisted `foreach` iteration variable (`<s>5__N = null` at the end of the loop body) as `s = null;`, because a user's own clear has the same physical form. With the pass as it is, every async `foreach` over a reference-type iteration variable would raise to invalid C# at Full. The design (`docs/design/classic-async-reconstruction.md#general-inverse`) names this pass fix as a stage 2 prerequisite.

## Fix shape

In `TryMatchPattern` and `TryMatchEnumerator`, decline when the iteration local has any store other than the header's `Current` store (or any address-taken use); the loop stays in its enumerator form, which is valid C#. Add a compiler-produced negative (a body that assigns the iteration variable) and an async `foreach` positive once the inverse lands.

Fixes #10372. This is a 1a follow-up under #10227.

## Claim

Owner: [`api-status-analysis.md`, "Status facts"](docs/design/api-status-analysis.md#status-facts).

An `[Obsolete]` is the compiler's compatibility marker, and does not count as obsolete, only when it uses the two-argument form with `error: true` and the exact compiler message, and the declaration matches:
- **Ref structs:** the ref-struct message on a declaration that carries `[IsByRefLike]`. `CompilerFeatureRequired("RefStructs")` is no longer required, because Roslyn doesn't emit it on targets with no `CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute`, such as netstandard2.0 and net4x.
- **Required members:** the required-members message with `[CompilerFeatureRequired("RequiredMembers")]`. This is unchanged; Roslyn refuses to compile required members without that attribute (CS0656).

`AttributeReader.IsCompilerCompatibilityObsolete` holds this one rule. It feeds the status fact, the hidden and suppression readers, and type discovery. `MethodRowGate`'s byte-level copy applies the same rule.

issues.body:
The Markdown Dependency Structure table tags each namespace with a zero-based cycle ordinal: `(108 types, level 0, cycle 0)`. It never states how many cycles there are, or which namespaces form each one. Readers take `cycle 0` to mean "zero cycles".

## Evidence

In the project-analysis question eval (#8516), the question was "How many namespace dependency cycles does the Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 library have?" Haiku 4.5 answered "0 cycles" in two of its first three runs. Both cited the `cycle 0` tags as proof. The library has one cycle of eight namespaces. Opus 5.5 read the same table correctly, but it had to reason from the edges to do it.

```sh
dotnet-inspect library --package Newtonsoft.Json@13.0.4 --namesake-library -S "Dependency Structure"
# | **Newtonsoft.Json (108 types, level 0, cycle 0)** | **Newtonsoft.Json.Converters (42 types, level 0, cycle 0)** | 13 relationships ... |
```

Binary: `0.27.0+bb8df13`.

## Expected

The Markdown section should say the count and the membership outright, for example `Cycles: 1` followed by one row per cycle listing its namespaces. The per-namespace tag should not read as a count. `cycle 1 of 1`, or a named cycle, would do that. JSON already carries a `cycles` array; the Markdown view should match it.

Owner: `docs/design/il-diff-canonicalization.md#census-cursor`; `docs/design/finding-census.md#gates` (cost). Tracking: #10227.

#10477 (Finding census adoption 1a) made `IlCensusCursor` the one producer of canonical IL: `IlFindings.Inspect` drains it and `IlBodyDiff.Compare` canonicalizes through it. It shipped without performance numbers, by operator decision, because step 1's gates are completeness, canonical order, fault order, and bound, and the cost gates belong to step 2. The exhaustive paths did change, so their cost should be measured before step 2 builds on them.

## What changed on the exhaustive paths

- `TargetsMatch` validates branch, switch, and clause targets over precomputed instruction indexes instead of a linear scan of the instruction array per target (expected faster on large bodies).
- `MetadataOperandResolver` memoizes by operand kind and token (expected faster on bodies that repeat callees).
- The image-backed `IlFindings.Inspect(PEReader, …)` runs the raw-IL cursor: a shallow boundary pre-scan, one decode per advance, and `BlockGraph.Build` at the clause stage, so the bytes are read twice; the decoded-body overloads and `IlBodyDiff.Compare` use the existing decode.
- Each branch, switch, or clause atom carries one extra `TargetIndexes` array.

issues.body:
## Summary

`IlBodyDiff` compares the decoded instruction stream (opcodes, operands, branch targets) and never reads `MethodBodyBlock.ExceptionRegions`. Two bodies that differ only in their exception-handling table therefore compare **`Exact`**. That includes a different catch type, a different filter, or a `try` that starts or ends at a different instruction.

This is known and documented: the fidelity report prints "exact (contract v5) … — EH-blind", and `docs/decompiler-architecture.md` says the comparison "is not semantic equivalence". No issue tracks closing it, and it affects more than the fidelity harness.

## Evidence

The probe compiles each pair with Roslyn 5.9.0 in Release and calls `IlBodyDiff.Compare(oldReader, oldBody, newReader, newBody)` at `d93cb58f8`:

```text
catch type             IlBodyDiff=Exact        EH regions old=Catch[0+7]:InvalidOperationException new=Catch[0+7]:Exception
try boundary           IlBodyDiff=Exact        EH regions old=Catch[0+12]:Exception new=Catch[5+7]:Exception
finally vs catch-all   IlBodyDiff=OpcodeDiff   EH regions old=Finally[0+7] new=Catch[0+7]:Object   (control: opcodes differ)
```

The bodies behind those rows:

- **catch type:** `try { Work(); } catch (InvalidOperationException) { Log(); }` vs `… catch (Exception) …`.
- **try boundary:** `try { Work(); Work(); } catch …` vs `Work(); try { Work(); } catch …`.

Both pairs behave differently at run time, and both compare `Exact`.

| Consumer | Effect |

| `FidelityCheck` / native RTS (`ClassifyStatus`, contract v5) | A decompiled body with the wrong catch type, or a statement moved across a `try` boundary, reads as **false `Exact`**. A dropped `try/finally` is still caught, because `leave` and `endfinally` change the opcode stream. |

issues.body:
Operator decision (2026-10-21, after #10399): Fast Diff is renamed **Finding Diff Any** (`FindingDiffAny`). Tracking: #10227.

**Why.** Fast Diff's own Why says it has no equality of its own and answers the Exists scenario with the complete diffs' equality; only the cost of reaching the answer differs. "Fast" names the cost, which is the one thing the design says is not its identity, and "Diff" reads as a fourth kind of diff when it is one scenario (finding-census.md). `Any` is the .NET idiom for Exists (`Enumerable.Any`, `Task.WhenAny`): it names the question, not the mechanism, so it survives Finding census adoption step 4 when the paired walk is replaced by lockstep over cursors. Library Compare already calls the selector **Any Diff**. Rejected: `Census` alone (vague), `FindingWalker` (names the mechanism scheduled for replacement), `FindingDiff` (names the Exhaustive output it never produces; collides with `FindingComparison`), `FindingMatchAny` (wrong polarity: a match is equality; Exists does not run the matcher).

Fixes #10205.

Adds `IlBodyDiffNormalization.NormalizeAssemblyScope` under the [IL diff canonicalization](docs/design/il-diff-canonicalization.md) owner. Under it every type and member reference, including those either compared assembly defines, gets one shared `<assembly>` scope, so operands compare by namespace, name, and signature alone, without their defining or referenced assembly or its version. It subsumes `NormalizeCurrentAssemblyScope` and `NormalizePlatformAssemblyScope`, applies to a module reader as well, and the compiler-generated ordinal correspondence keys under the same rule, so a non-platform reference version change no longer blocks a fold. String literals and member names stay observable.

This is the mechanic Fast Diff's Body policy composes; the Shared Body equality slice (#10196) and Finding census adoption step 1 (#10365) depend on it. No host requests the flag yet, so nothing user-observable changes in this PR.

Gates (ILDiff.Tests):
- `NormalizeAssemblyScope_ToleratesNonPlatformReferenceVersionChanges`: the issue's gate; a pair differing only in a non-platform reference version is `Exact` under the mechanic and not without, including under both narrower scope mechanics together.
- `NormalizeAssemblyScope_ComparesReferencesByNameAlone`, `NormalizeAssemblyScope_SubsumesCurrentAndPlatformScopes`, `NormalizeAssemblyScope_PreservesStringLiteralsAndMemberNames`.
- `NonPlatformReferenceVersion_FoldsUnderAssemblyScope` beside the existing `NonPlatformReferenceVersion_StillDoesNotFold`.
- `EveryDeclaredNormalization_IsAcceptedByCompare` covers the wiring.

issues.body:
## Problem

Canonical IL comparison keeps the assembly identity, including version, of every non-platform reference (`IlMetadataOperandResolver`). A Library that rebuilds only because Dependabot bumped a dependency (for example `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` 8.0.0.0 to 9.0.0.0) is reported with every call into that dependency changed, though no IL changed.

Dependency versions are not an input to body change. Package and Library versions are diff candidates in their own right: for an app whose two dependencies each changed one method, the body diff should find those two methods in the dependencies and report nothing in the app.

## Proposal

Add an `IlBodyDiffNormalization` mechanic, `NormalizeAssemblyScope`, under which every Type and member operand compares by its namespace, name, and signature alone, without its defining or referenced assembly. It subsumes `NormalizeCurrentAssemblyScope` and `NormalizePlatformAssemblyScope`. Owner: `docs/design/il-diff-canonicalization.md`.

## Consumers

- Fast Diff's Body policy (#10195), adopted by the Shared Body equality slice (#10196), which depends on this issue.
- The IL view, so a Body cue opens a view that shows the same answer.

## Gates

A generated pair whose only difference is the version of a non-platform referenced assembly is `Exact` under the mechanic and not `Exact` without it.

Part of #9716.

Fixes #10365.

New owner `docs/design/finding-census.md`: the Finding census as a stream. A **census cursor** yields one row's observations of one kind in a canonical order fixed by that side alone and ends in `Complete`, `Absent(kind)`, or `Failed`; draining it is the kind's `Inspect`. Two scenarios read a pair of cursors:

- **Exists**: lockstep to the first deciding event (`Changed`, `Unchanged`, `Indeterminate`), with the event table and the rule that a fault before any difference is `Indeterminate` and a difference before a fault is `Changed`; builds nothing.
- **Exhaustive**: drain both into sealed censuses and match in the kind's mode (`IlFindings.Compare`; the declaration view's comparison).

The agreement section applies Diff capabilities' Exists contract to the one producer. Fast Diff's paired walk is recorded as an Exists provision kept or deleted by the cost gate. Gates: completeness against `Inspect`, canonical order, Exists agreement (re-basing Body exactness), fault order, laziness by atom count, allocation, cost on the perf hosts, matcher bound. Adoption: IL cursor; Exists over cursors beside the walk; declaration cursor (DV1); Fast Diff as the Exists owner with its types renamed.

Cross-links: Fast Diff Why, Diff system execution modes (depth axis), Finding nomenclature's Census row, declaration view Facts.

Markdown only; markdownlint clean.

issues.body:
Fast Diff, `IlFindings`, and the declaration view each compute one equality per kind with their own producer, held together by gates (Body exactness; the declaration view's emptiness claim). The name Fast Diff reads as a fourth kind of diff when it is one scenario, Exists, over the same census.

Design a **Finding census** owner: a per-row, per-kind **census cursor** that yields observations in a canonical one-sided order with typed terminals (`Complete`, `Absent(kind)`, `Failed`), and two scenarios over a pair of cursors:

- **Exists**: lockstep to the first difference; `Changed`, `Unchanged`, or `Indeterminate`; a fault before any difference is `Indeterminate`, a difference before a fault is `Changed`; builds nothing.
- **Exhaustive**: drain both cursors into sealed `FindingCensus<T>` and match in the kind's mode, which is `IlFindings.Compare` and the declaration view's comparison today.

Agreement by construction, re-basing Fast Diff's Body exactness gate on the cursor; Fast Diff's paired walk becomes an Exists provision kept or deleted by measurement. Adoption: IL cursor, Exists over cursors beside the walk, declaration cursor (DV1), Fast Diff as the Exists owner with its public types renamed.

Parent: #10227.

issues.body:
Normative owner: **Schema Query**, `docs/design/schema-query.md`, with the coordinate sections from `docs/design/library-address-inspection.md`.

Exact `explain` resolves the Library address route's coordinate sections (the `Context:` records and `Metadata: Heap`) through `ExactExplanationRoutes` (`src/DotnetInspect.Cli/Commands/ResourceExplanationCommand.cs`). `CreateCompleteCatalog` omits them because the route shares the `library` root path with the direct-Library catalog, and `ResourceExplanationCatalog.Create` rejects duplicate paths.

**Consequence:** under the proposed root reachability invariant (#10312, `docs/design/resource-explanation.md#routing-declarations`), every resource that exact explanation resolves must be in the host's composed catalog and reachable from the root. Today these sections are resolvable but in neither the catalog nor search, so a reader can reach them only by already knowing their path.

**Expected:** the address route's sections join the complete catalog under one non-colliding canonical registration. That means either one Library catalog that includes them, or a distinct registered root. Exact resolution of their current paths stays unchanged or gains a registered alias.

This is a prerequisite for publishing the root. It is not part of the #10312 design.

Fixes #10347. Part of #10227 (Diff capabilities adoption step 1: "each row gains a declaration view").

## Summary

New owner `docs/design/declaration-view.md`. Its claim:

> For one row of a Type, a Member or the Type's own residual, resolved in one image or in two, the declaration view holds every declaration and implementation fact Fast Diff's census records for that row, on either axis, spelled at the declaration level: decoded rows, named flags, symbolic signatures, typed constants, and attributes with their decoded arguments. One version lists the row's facts. Two versions pair them by fact identity into `Present`, `Changed`, `Added`, and `Removed` transitions, with Fast Diff's census equality, so the view is empty for a row Fast Diff reports `Unchanged` on both axes and non-empty for a row it reports `Changed` by a declaration fact. The view is a representation; every host renders from it.

Design choices:

- **Level.** A new **declaration** level in Diff observability's table, between semantic (C#, API diff) and encoded (tokens, bytes). C# cannot spell `beforefieldinit`, implementation flags, `MethodImpl` rows, or raw attribute blobs; the raw table projection is too low. The view sits where the census compares.
- **Facts are the census.** A declaration fact is one Fast Diff census fact projected to kind, axis, owner, identity, value, certainty. Identity and value are the two halves of the census `SymbolKey`, so equality is the census's; the view adds none. issues.body:
## Summary

[Diff capabilities](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect/blob/main/docs/design/diff-capabilities.md#axes) puts every subject at every accessibility on the Body axis: the IL of every method, the declaration facts of every subject the API axis does not compare (a non-public Member's row, signature, flags, constants, import, and attributes; the declaration of a non-public Type), and implementation facts (`beforefieldinit`, inlining and `InternalCall` flags, compiler-emitted attributes such as `Intrinsic`). It states that those facts "are shown by a **declaration view**, part of each row's rung-4 diff", and that the residual's rung-4 view includes "the Type's declaration view for its Body declaration and implementation facts".

No owner defines that view. Fast Diff's Body census already compares non-public declaration facts and `beforefieldinit`, so a Body `Changed` decided by one of them alone (an added private field, an attribute added to an internal method) opens the IL view with no difference. Fast Diff's Observability section records that as a known divergence under rule 4 of Diff observability until this view exists.

## Scope

- An owner design for the declaration view: a Member- or Type-scope diff of metadata declaration facts at any accessibility, at the level the Body axis compares them, with the facts it presents named kind by kind so the Fast Diff census and the view agree.
- The view in both hosts: CLI `diff` and Inspect Web, entered from a Body cue the way the IL view is.
- The Expansive gate of Diff capabilities: a private field, a changed inlining flag, and a gained `Intrinsic` attribute shown in the view.
- Once the view exists, the uncertain-kind rows for implementation flags and compiler-emitted attributes can move from the API census to the Body census (adoption step 2 of Diff capabilities).

## Owner

Diff capabilities, adoption step 1 (axes), sub-slice 1b: "Each row gains a declaration view". Tracking: #10227.

issues.body:
Part of #10227 (slice 1a, PR 2 of 3). Decision record:
https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect/issues/10227#issuecomment-6278953821

## Problem

`IsHidden` on `ApiType` / `ApiMember` / accessors folds `EditorBrowsable(Never)`
and `[Obsolete]` into one flag (`AttributeReader.HasHiddenAttribute`). The
Public scope suppresses both, so Visible -> Hidden and a newly obsolete Type or
Member show as **Removed** today. The API axis (`ApiSurfaceExtractionScope.ApiAxis`)
admits hidden and obsolete subjects. However, the comparison has no rows for
their status transitions: when hosts switch to the API axis (#10227 PR 3),
these changes would go silent (D1).

## Owner

A new design document, `docs/design/api-status-analysis.md`, owns API status:
hidden (`EditorBrowsable(Never)`) and obsolete (with message and error flag)
as two separate facts per subject, and their transitions as rows.
`api-population-scope.md` and `diff-capabilities.md` already point to "a
separate API status analysis".

## Change

- Split the hidden and obsolete facts. Public-scope admission keeps
  suppressing both, so default output is unchanged.
- Add the `TypeHiddenChanged`, `MemberHiddenChanged`, `TypeObsoleteChanged` and
  `MemberObsoleteChanged` change kinds in a new `ApiChangeCategory.Status`,
  emitted between API axis or include-all surfaces.
- Classification:
  - Hidden <-> visible is NonBreaking (D2).
  - Obsolete added or removed as a warning is NonBreaking.
  - Obsolete becoming an error, or added as an error, is Breaking, because
    callers stop compiling. Error -> warning or removed is NonBreaking.
  - A subject outside the API axis is NonBreaking (#10339).

issues.body:
Owner: `docs/design/fast-diff.md#type`. This is a scope proposal: it extends Fast Diff's Type-level contract. Tracking: #9716. Consumer: the Type findings map (#10222).

## Problem

Fast Diff's Type level does not run for a Type present in one image only. `fast-diff.md#type` says: "the Type level is not run for it … it has no per-Member rows".

A consumer that lists the Members of an added or removed Type needs the same Member partition Fast Diff uses for paired Types. For example, the Type findings map wants to list an added Type's Members as `Added`. The partition means:

- identity by census key;
- accessors raised into their property or event;
- generated code attached to its owner;
- residual facts owned by the Type.

There is no owner for that partition over one side today.

## Proposal

Extend the Type level with a one-sided form. For a Type present in one image, return the present side's Members, partitioned by the same ownership rules, each one-sided, plus the residual. Every state is then a one-sided change, so no IL is read for state.

## Gates

- On a one-sided fixture Type, the Members returned equal the Members of the same Type's two-sided Type level against itself.
- The one-sided form reads no IL.

issues.body:
Slice 1 of #10190.

## Claim

The census card and baseline report a method-count-weighted "fully raised"
aggregate. Of 89,065 real-world corpus methods, 34,842 are constructors,
static constructors, or accessors that raise at 92.3%; the remaining 54,223
raise at 86.3%. The idiom scorecard is 76 of 76 recovered and no longer
generates work. Neither number tells a reviewer whether a body a reader
would open renders well.

## Change

Add three measures to `tools/DecompilerHarness` census output, the
real-world baseline `metrics` block, and the quality diff card:

1. **Branch-weighted raised.** Fully raised basis points over methods whose
   imported CFG has at least one conditional branch.
2. **State-machine raised.** Over methods whose MethodDef carries
   `AsyncStateMachineAttribute` or `IteratorStateMachineAttribute`: the share
   whose rendered body contains no generated type name (`DEC0009` absent) and
   is fully raised. This is the number the classic state-machine corpus
   already approximates at 16.0%; the real-world corpus should carry it too.
3. **Reader-facing target set.** Public API bodies of the pinned corpus
   rendering `Full` with no `goto` and no generated name, reported as a count
   and basis points.

Add drop tolerances for all three to `tolerances` matching the existing
10 bps convention. Retire the scorecard as a work generator in
`docs/decompiler-quality.md`; keep `IdiomShapeScorecardTests` as a regression
pin.

## Evidence

issues.body:
`StateMachineSourceResolver.IsCurrentAssemblyStateMachineType` (`src/ILInspector.Analysis/StateMachineSourceResolver.cs:2120`) splits the `[AsyncStateMachine]`/`[IteratorStateMachine]` serialized Type name at the first `,` with `IndexOf(',')`. It does not honour serialization escaping.

**When it happens:** an async method or iterator explicitly implements a generic interface with two or more Type arguments. Its state-machine name then contains an escaped comma, for example `<…IObjectCreator<…ContainerExec\,…EmptyCreationContext>-CreateObjectAsync>d__19`.

**What goes wrong:**
- The resolver reads the text after the escaped comma as an assembly name.
- It decides the claim points to another assembly, and marks the attribute `Ignored`.
- MoveNext → kickoff returns None, and kickoff → MoveNext returns false.
- Nothing throws. Only `ResolveUltimateDeclaredMethod` reports `Unresolved`.

`StateMachineRelationshipIndex` decodes the escape and resolves the same Types.

**Evidence:** `exp/state-machine-owner-check` `0b544816c`, `eng/check-state-machine-owners.cs`.
- Aspire.Hosting 13.6.0 and 13.6.1: `ContainerCreator+<…IObjectCreator<…ContainerExec,…EmptyCreationContext>-CreateObjectAsync>d__19`.
- Fixture `ExplicitGenericStateMachines`: `GetAsync` and the iterator `get_Items`.
- No other disagreement with the index across 3,045 async state machines in six Library pairs and the state-machine fixtures.

**Consequence:** generated code for these methods is not attributed to its owning Member. That affects Library Body Analysis attribution, and it would affect Fast Diff's Type level and the Annotated Type Map's Member grain.

**Direction:** take the async (and iterator) kickoff → state machine → MoveNext identity from `StateMachineRelationshipIndex`'s certificate, as recorded on #10227, rather than re-parsing the attribute. If a local fix comes first, decode the escape, and add the fixture's two cases as a gate.

## Change

> Should we accept this declaration-spelling fix?

**Conclusion:** **REVIEW**.

Both Metadata declaration paths spelled any by-ref parameter that has the raw `In` flag (and not `Out`) as C# `in`. That flag is the interop marshalling direction, not the C# modifier.

- C# `in` is identified by `IsReadOnlyAttribute`.
- C# `ref readonly` is identified by `RequiresLocationAttribute`.
- `[In] ref` is an ordinary mutable `ref`.

So two kinds of parameter came out wrong:

issues.body:
## Summary

`ApiSurfaceExtractor` spells a parameter `in` whenever the raw
`ParameterAttributes.In` flag is set. That flag is not the C# `in` modifier -- it is
also the interop `[In]` marshalling attribute, which is routinely applied to a
**mutable** `ref` parameter. C# `in` additionally requires readonly-ref metadata
(`IsReadOnlyAttribute`, or `RequiresLocationAttribute` for `ref readonly`).

Found by adversarial review (GPT) of #3528.

## Observed

```console
dotnet artifacts/bin/dotnet-inspect/release/dotnet-inspect.dll member \
  System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.IConnectionPointContainer FindConnectionPoint \
  --all --library <System.Private.CoreLib.dll> -v:d
```

```csharp
FindConnectionPoint(in System.Guid riid, ...)
```

The runtime declares it as a mutable `ref`:

```csharp
void FindConnectionPoint([In] ref Guid riid, out IConnectionPoint ppCP);
```

So the rendered declaration changes the parameter''s meaning, and a caller
copy-pasting it cannot assign through `riid`.

## Relationship to #3528

#3528 fixed the mirror-image defect on the **`out`** side: `ApiSurfaceExtractor` was
testing `Out` without `&& !In`, so an interop `[In, Out] ref` was spelled `out` and
broke definite assignment (CS0269). That fix makes `[In, Out] ref` render as `ref`,
which is correct.

This issue is the remaining half: `[In] ref` (In set, Out clear) still renders as
`in`. It is **pre-existing and unchanged** by #3528 -- that PR neither introduced nor
worsened it -- so it was deliberately left out of scope rather than folded into a
gate-restoration PR.

## Proposal

Emit `in` only when readonly-ref metadata is present, not from the raw `In` flag:

- `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsReadOnlyAttribute` on the parameter -> `in`
- `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RequiresLocationAttribute` -> `ref readonly`
- otherwise a byref parameter is `ref`, regardless of `[In]`

Apply the same correction in `MetadataDeclarationQuery`, which carries its own copy
of the rule.

Before this change, an application-authored direct reference stopped at `NotEvaluated` / `ApplicationAuthoredExemption`. As a result, a `net10.0` app that references System.Text.Json 8.0.5 got no signal that the platform already supplies a newer version. An agent comparing that reference against the newest System.Text.Json release would upgrade it, which gives up pruning for no benefit.

## Change

- **Comparison input:** an application-authored declaration is compared with the target platform using its restored resolution. That is the version the project's restore resolved, matched through the relationship's declaration association. The comparison runs only when the root's processing and restored relationships are both complete.
- **Who decides:** the comparison goes through `PlatformPrunePolicy`, which owns platform supply decisions.
  - When the platform supplies the package (`Subsumed`), the row reports `PlatformDelegation`.
  - Otherwise the row reports `PackageRetained`.
  - Both carry reason `ApplicationAuthored` and keep applicability `ApplicationAuthoredExemption`. PackageHouse's exemption and its precedence are unchanged.
- **Evidence:** these rows carry a new typed result, `DependencyInspectionPruningResult.RestoredResolution` (`kind: restored-resolution`). No PackageHouse receipt is issued and the graph is unchanged. The JSON fields `subsumption` and `delegates_to_platform` now come from the typed result, so they also cover these rows.
- **Shared inventory read:** these rows share the request's single inventory read with candidate-bound rows, including the existing inventory-failure path. They do no package-source work, because project roots don't accept source options.

Make `depends -S Pruning` evaluate every direct declaration against the
target platform inventory, as library pruning does, including declarations
authored by a project. A platform-supplied declaration reports

A `net10.0` app that references `System.Text.Json` 8.0.5 today reports:
