The Rails 8.1 schema dumper writes columns in database order, so columns added by later migrations end up at the end of their table. When two branches add columns to the same table, both append at the end and their `db/schema.rb` changes conflict. This PR adds `alphabetical_schema` so schema dumps are sorted again.

### Changes
- **`Gemfile` / `Gemfile.lock`:** adds `alphabetical_schema` (0.1.3) to the `:development, :test` group. It hooks into `ActiveRecord::SchemaDumper` and sorts each table's columns by name. Production doesn't need it because it never dumps the schema.
- **`db/schema.rb`:** regenerated with `bin/rails db:schema:dump`. The diff only reorders columns (44 lines). Types, defaults, indexes, foreign keys and constraints are unchanged.

Example (`articles`):
```diff
   t.datetime "created_at", null: false
+  t.string "slug"
   t.string "title"
   t.datetime "updated_at", null: false
   t.bigint "user_id", null: false
-  t.string "slug"
```

### Note
The gem requires `rails < 8.2`. Upgrading to Rails 8.2 will need a newer release of the gem, or removing it.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #465

When a participant's EGD pin is changed, their rank and rating are now updated from the EGD lookup. Before this, a new pin kept the old rating. While a pin is present, `normalize_rating` keeps the stored rating, so the stale value stayed until the next daily sync.

### Changes

- **`EgdSyncJob#perform(participant_id = nil)`**: with an id, only that participant is refreshed. With no id it refreshes everyone, as before, so the recurring schedule and the admin "sync EGD" action are unchanged.
- **`Participant` after-commit hook**: when a save sets or changes `egd_pin` to a non-blank value, it queues the job for that participant.
  ```ruby
  after_commit :sync_from_egd, on: [:create, :update], if: -> { saved_change_to_egd_pin? && egd_pin.present? }
  ```
  - It is a model hook, so admin edits, new registrations and console changes all trigger it.
  - Clearing the pin queues nothing; the rating then comes from the rank again, which is existing behaviour.
  - The job's own save doesn't change the pin, so it can't re-trigger itself.

### Review notes

- **Async**: the admin edit page shows the old rank and rating until the job runs. I chose a background job so a slow EGD API can't block saves; a synchronous lookup is the alternative if immediate feedback matters more.
- **EGD wins**: if an admin changes the pin and rank in the same save, the job then overwrites the rank with the EGD value.
- **Runs on registration**: the registration form currently accepts the client-submitted `rating` whenever a pin is present. Running the lookup on create corrects that value against EGD.
- **No match, no change**: if the lookup finds nothing, returns a different pin, or `EGD_API_TOKEN` isn't set, nothing is updated. This is the existing job behaviour.

agent_prs.body:
Participants registered with an EGD pin keep the rank and rating they had at registration time. This adds a background job that refreshes those values from the European Go Database, scheduled daily and manually triggerable by admins.

### `EgdSyncJob`
- Iterates participants with a non-blank `egd_pin`, skipping pins that are not 8 digits.
- Resolves each pin through the existing `EgdLookupService` (which already handles pin queries and swallows network failures), and only applies a result whose `egd_pin` matches the participant's — a mismatched or empty response leaves the record untouched.
- Persists via `save`, so model normalization, validations and PaperTrail versioning apply; validation failures are logged per participant rather than aborting the run. Returns the number of updated participants.

### Admin endpoint
- `POST /admin/participants/sync_egd` (collection route in the `admin` namespace, so the existing `require_admin!` filter covers it) enqueues the job and redirects back with a notice.
- "Sync EGD data" button added to the admin participants index header.

```ruby
# config/recurring.yml (production/staging)
sync_egd_data:
  class: EgdSyncJob
  schedule: every day at 4am
```

### Tests
- `test/jobs/egd_sync_job_test.rb`: update on match, skip participants without a pin, no-op on empty lookup, ignore results for a different pin.
- `test/controllers/admin/participants_controller_test.rb`: admin enqueues the job and gets the notice; a regular user is redirected and nothing is enqueued.

Note: when EGD returns a rank but no rating, the existing `Participant#normalize_rating` behaviour keeps the previously stored rating rather than re-deriving it from the rank — consistent with admin edits today, but worth a look if a different rule is preferred.

agent_prs.body:
Mollie settlements aren't scoped to a profile. As a result, the sync also imported settlements from other profiles and from before we started taking payments. This PR adds a date cut-off and an optional balance filter.

### Date cut-off (`MollieSettlementSync`)
- Settlements whose `created_at` date falls before the date of the earliest **Mollie** payment are skipped. Settlements created on that same date are kept.
- Only Mollie payments count toward the cut-off. Manually recorded payments are ignored, so a backdated cash or bank-transfer entry doesn't widen the range.
- If there are no Mollie payments yet, `call` returns an empty result without calling the Mollie API.
- A settlement without a `created_at` is skipped, because the cut-off can't be checked. Mollie should always send one.
- Settlements are filtered on our side because the Mollie API has no date filter for settlements.

### Optional balance filter
- New env var `MOLLIE_SETTLEMENT_BALANCE_ID`. When set, it is sent as Mollie's `balanceId` query param. When unset or blank, all balances are fetched as before.
- Unlike the organization token, it is read only from ENV, not from credentials.
- It can also be passed directly for testing: `MollieSettlementSync.new(balance_id: "bal_…")`.

```ruby
options = { limit: PAGE_SIZE, api_key: @token }
options[:balance_id] = @balance_id if @balance_id.present?   # → ?balanceId=…
```

### Admin UI
- The settlements index page now has a short note describing both limits.

### Tests
- Existing tests: payment fixtures are pinned to 2026-09-01, and test settlements get a default `created_at` of 2026-10-01 so they pass the cut-off.
- New tests: the cut-off boundary (day before vs. same day), manual payments being ignored, no API call when there are no Mollie payments, the balance param being sent or omitted, and reading the balance ID from ENV.

Mollie pays out weekly or monthly. Each payout ("settlement") contains the payments from that period, minus fees. This PR syncs settlements from the Mollie API and links each payment to the settlement it was paid out in, so admins can see which payments are in which settlement.

**Requires config:** the Settlements API rejects the regular payments API key. It needs an **organization access token** with `settlements.read` and `payments.read`. Set it as the credential `mollie_organization_token` or as `MOLLIE_ORGANIZATION_TOKEN`. Until it is set, the settlements page shows setup instructions and hides the sync button.

### Data model
- New `settlements` table: `mollie_settlement_id` (unique), `reference`, `status`, `amount_cents` (net payout), `settled_at`, `mollie_created_at`.
- `payments.settlement_id` is a nullable FK. `Payment belongs_to :settlement, optional: true`. `Settlement has_many :payments, dependent: :nullify`.
- `Settlement#deductions_cents` is the gross total of our payments minus the payout. That is mostly Mollie fees, but refunds and chargebacks settled in the same period are deducted too.

### `MollieSettlementSync` (`app/services`)
- Walks `Mollie::Settlement.all` and each `Settlement::Payment.all`, following pagination at 250 per page. Every call passes the org token as `api_key:`.
- Links payments by `mollie_payment_id` using `update_all`, inside a transaction together with the settlement upsert. Mollie payments we don't know about are ignored.
- Settlements already stored as `paidout` are not re-fetched, so repeat syncs stay cheap.
- Settlements with an unknown status are skipped and logged.

### Admin UI (`require_admin!`)
- `GET /admin/settlements`: list with payment count, payments total, deductions and paid-out amount, plus a **Sync with Mollie** button (`POST /admin/settlements/sync`).
- `GET /admin/settlements/:id`: summary plus the payments in that settlement.
- The payments overview gets a **Settlement** column. The dashboard and payments

agent_prs.body:
`/payments/success` requires no login and found payments by their sequential `id`. Anyone could step through `?payment_id=1,2,3…` to read every payment's status and harvest participant UUIDs from the "Try again" link. Each request also made a live `Mollie::Payment.get` call.

### Changes

- **Signed return token (`Payment`)**
  - `#return_token` creates the token with `signed_id(purpose: :payment_return, expires_in: RETURN_TOKEN_EXPIRY)`; `RETURN_TOKEN_EXPIRY` is 1 week.
  - `.find_by_return_token` looks it up with `find_signed`. A blank, tampered, expired or wrong-purpose token returns `nil`.
- **Controller (`PaymentsController`)**
  - `success` finds the payment only through `params[:token]`. `payment_id` is ignored.
  - The Mollie `redirect_url` and the dev-only simulation redirects now carry `token:`.
  - If no payment is found, the existing generic "Return from Payment" page is shown: no status, no participant UUID, no Mollie call.
- **Rate limiting (`rack_attack.rb`)**
  - New throttle `payment_success/ip`: 20 `GET /payments/success` requests per minute per IP. This limits both enumeration and calls to Mollie.

```ruby
# before
@payment = Payment.find_by(id: params[:payment_id])
# after
@payment = Payment.find_by_return_token(params[:token])
```

### Notes for review

- **Existing return links stop working.** URLs with `payment_id`, including those already handed to Mollie for open checkouts, now land on the generic page. Status still reaches payers by email and is still recorded by the webhook.
- **The token is not secret.** `signed_id` shows the record id in readable form, but the signature stops anyone forging or changing it, so it can't be used to enumerate payments.
- **A valid token still shows the participant UUID.** The token reaches only the payer through the Mollie redirect, so the "Try again" link is shown as before.

issues.body:
**Source:** pentest finding 1 — verified in code.

## Verification
`PaymentsController#success` (`app/controllers/payments_controller.rb`) skips authentication and looks up the payment purely by a guessable sequential primary key:

```ruby
skip_before_action :authenticate_user!, only: [:new, :create, :success, :webhook]

def success
  @payment = Payment.find_by(id: params[:payment_id])
  ...
end
```

There is no ownership check, so anyone can enumerate `/payments/success?payment_id=1,2,3,…` and read the status of every payment. Worse, for a non-paid payment the view renders:

```erb
<%= link_to "Try again", new_participant_payment_path(@payment.participant), ... %>
```

which embeds the participant UUID, giving an attacker the UUIDs needed to reach the per-participant endpoints (see the related finding about UUID-only access).

Additionally, `success` triggers a live `Mollie::Payment.get` call for every request, so enumeration also produces unauthenticated outbound API traffic to Mollie.

## Impact
- Unauthenticated disclosure of payment status of all registrations.
- Disclosure of participant UUIDs (capability tokens for `/participants/{uuid}` and `/participants/{uuid}/payment/new`).
- Enumeration of the total number of payments/registrations.

## Suggested remediation
- Look the payment up by an unguessable identifier (e.g. the participant/payment UUID or the Mollie payment id) instead of the numeric `id`, and/or
- Bind the returning payer to the payment (signed session value or signed/expiring token in the redirect URL), and
- Never render the participant UUID for a payment the requester is not entitled to; show a generic "return from payment" page when the payment cannot be attributed to the requester.
- Consider rate-limiting `/payments/success` in `config/initializers/rack_attack.rb` to blunt enumeration and Mollie API amplification.
issues.title: Security: /payments/success leaks payment status and participant UUID via unauthenticated payment_id (IDOR)

agent_prs.body:
The Mollie sync only read the status and refunded amount, so a charged-back payment stayed `paid`. The participant stayed on the public list and counted as paid in bookkeeping.

### Detection (`Payment`)
- `sync_from_mollie!` now reads `amount_charged_back`. Any positive amount maps to a new `charged_back` status, which takes precedence over `refunded`:
  ```ruby
  def mollie_status(mollie_payment)
    return "charged_back" if mollie_amount_positive?(mollie_payment.try(:amount_charged_back))
    return "refunded" if mollie_amount_positive?(mollie_payment.try(:amount_refunded))
    mollie_payment.status
  end
  ```
- `charged_back` is in `UNSUCCESSFUL_STATUSES`, so it no longer blocks a new payment.
- New scopes: `charged_back`, `reversed` (refunded + charged back) and `for_bookkeeping` (paid + charged back).
- No webhook changes. Mollie calls the payment webhook on a chargeback, and the webhook already re-fetches the payment.

### Participant
- `not_refunded` (public list) now excludes charged-back participants too; a later successful payment brings them back.
- New `charged_back?`. `registration_status` returns `"Chargeback"` (after Paid, before Refund). Charged-back participants are not deletable.

### Admin
- Participants: new "Chargeback" filter, sort position and red badge. The Refund, Confirmed and Pending filters now exclude chargebacks.
- Payments overview: lists `for_bookkeeping` payments, and charged-back rows get a "Charged back" badge. They can still be marked processed.
- **Semantics change to review:** when a payment becomes `charged_back`, `processed_in_bookkeeping` is reset to `false`. This puts it back in the unprocessed count so the bookkeeping gets corrected.

### Minor
- Statuses are now shown humanized ("charged back") on the payment result page and the per-participant payments table.

### Not covered
- Partial chargebacks are treated as full ones, the same as partial refunds.
- The separate Chargebacks API is not used.

agent_prs.title: Detect Mollie chargebacks and record them as a `charged_back` payment status

issues.body:
**Source:** pentest finding 3 — verified in code.

## Verification
`PaymentsController#sync_from_mollie` only maps Mollie's status plus the refunded amount:

```ruby
def mollie_status(mollie_payment)
  return "refunded" if mollie_refunded?(mollie_payment)
  mollie_payment.status
end

def mollie_refunded?(mollie_payment)
  mollie_amount_value(mollie_payment.try(:amount_refunded))&.positive?
end
```

A repo-wide search for `chargeback` / `amountChargedBack` returns no hits: chargebacks are never read from Mollie, and `Payment::STATUSES` has no chargeback state. The Mollie webhook (`PaymentsController#webhook`) only re-fetches the payment; Mollie's chargeback notifications (and the `amountChargedBack` field) are ignored.

## Impact
A participant can pay (e.g. by credit card or direct debit), receive a paid registration and confirmation email, then request a chargeback. The payment stays `paid` in our database, so the participant remains on the participant list and in bookkeeping as paid, and the loss is likely to go unnoticed until manual reconciliation with Mollie.

## Suggested remediation
- Read `amountChargedBack` when syncing a payment, and/or use the [Chargebacks API](https://docs.mollie.com/reference/chargebacks-api).
- Add a `charged_back` status (analogous to the existing home-grown `refunded` status) and include it in `UNSUCCESSFUL_STATUSES` so the participant drops off the public list and can pay again.
- Handle the chargeback webhook events so the status is updated without manual action, and surface charged-back payments in the admin payments overview for follow-up.
- Add tests covering a Mollie payment that is `paid` with a non-zero charged-back amount.

agent_prs.title: Send a real Content-Security-Policy header

issues.body:
## Current state
`config/initializers/content_security_policy.rb` is still the untouched Rails generator stub — the entire policy block is commented out, so **no `Content-Security-Policy` header is sent at all**. `csp_meta_tag` is present in `app/views/layouts/application.html.erb`, but without a policy (and without a nonce generator) it emits nothing useful.

This means the only defence against XSS is our own sanitization (`EditorsHelper#render_html_content`), which is deliberately liberal (it allows `style`, `class`, `bgcolor`, `bordercolor` … on TinyMCE-authored HTML per our design preferences). A CSP would give a genuine second layer.

## Proposed policy
Inventory of what the app actually loads (so the policy does not break anything):

| Source | Used for |
|---|---|
| `self` | importmap JS (`app/javascript`), Propshaft CSS, self-hosted TinyMCE (`/tinymce/js/tinymce/tinymce.min.js`), images/blobs via Active Storage |
| `https://ga.jspm.io` | `intl-tel-input` + its utils, pinned in `config/importmap.rb` |
| `https://challenges.cloudflare.com` | Turnstile `api.js` (script + iframe) |
| `data:` | inline SVG/font data URIs, TinyMCE icons |
| inline `<script>` | one small inline script in the layout (`egc27TurnstileOnLoad`), plus the importmap/`<script type="importmap">` JSON emitted by `javascript_importmap_tags` |
| inline `style="…"` | ~17 occurrences in ERB (including the body background image) plus TinyMCE-authored content |

Suggested starting point:
- `default-src :self`
- `script-src :self, :https` narrowed to `:self`, `https://ga.jspm.io`, `https://challenges.cloudflare.com` + nonce
- `style-src :self` + `'unsafe-inline'` initially (needed by TinyMCE and existing inline styles); track removal separately
- `img-src :self, :data, :https` (article/page/sponsor images, Active Storage blobs)
- `connect-src :self`, `font-src :self, :data`
- `frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com` (Turnstile renders an iframe)
- `object-src :none`, `base-uri :self`, `form-act

agent_prs.body:
`PaymentsController` carried nearly all payment behaviour — pricing, Mollie API calls, status mapping, refund detection and refresh loops — making none of it reusable outside a request (e.g. from a job). This moves that logic into `Payment` and `Participant`, leaving the controller with routing decisions only.

### `Payment`
- `Payment.build_for(participant)` — unsaved payment at the current congress pass price
- `Payment.sync_from_mollie_webhook(mollie_id)` — fetch + apply a webhook status update
- `#sync_from_mollie!`, `#refresh_from_mollie!` (raises) and `#refresh_from_mollie` (logs and returns nil)
- `#resume_mollie_checkout!` — refreshes from Mollie and returns the checkout URL only when that checkout can still be completed
- `#start_mollie_checkout!(redirect_url:, webhook_url:)` — creates the Mollie payment, validates the checkout URL, stores the Mollie id
- `#price_valid_until`, `#simulate_mollie_status!`, and `RETRYABLE_MOLLIE_STATUSES`
- Mollie status/refund/payment-method mapping moved in as private methods

### `Participant`
- `paid_payment`, `pending_payment`, `current_payment` replace the repeated `payments.completed.order(...).first || ...` chains
- `refresh_paid_payments!` — refreshes locally paid Mollie payments until one is still paid there, so refunds are picked up

### `PaymentsController`
Roughly halved; `create` reads as the flow it is:

```ruby
@participant.refresh_paid_payments!
return redirect_to success_payments_path, notice: ALREADY_PAID_NOTICE if @participant.paid_payment.present?

@payment = @participant.pending_payment || start_new_payment_attempt

checkout_url = @payment.resume_mollie_checkout!
return redirect_to success_payments_path, notice: ALREADY_PAID_NOTICE if @payment.paid?

if checkout_url.blank?
  @payment = start_new_payment_attempt if @payment.mollie_payment_id.present?
  checkout_url = @payment.start_mollie_checkout!(
    redirect_url: success_payments_url(payment_id: @payment.id),
    webhook_url: webhook_payments_url
  )
e

Printed flyers advertise `/cns`, `/cnt`, `/jp` and `/kr`, omitting the `/pages` prefix, so those URLs currently 404. This adds permanent redirects to the corresponding page URLs.

### Changes

- **`config/routes.rb`**: register the four flyer slugs as top-level `GET` routes redirecting (301) to `/pages/:slug`.

```ruby
# Flyers were printed with URLs missing the /pages prefix, so keep those
# shortcuts working by redirecting them to the real page URLs.
%w[cns cnt jp kr].each do |slug|
  get slug, to: redirect("/pages/#{slug}")
end
```

- **`test/integration/flyer_shortcut_routes_test.rb`**: asserts each shortcut responds `301` and points at the matching page path.

The list is explicit rather than a catch-all `/:slug` route, so it cannot shadow future top-level routes or leak page existence for arbitrary slugs.

agent_prs.body:
`config/importmap.rb` pinned `intl-tel-input` and its `utils` bundle directly from `ga.jspm.io`, with no SRI. A compromise of that CDN would execute arbitrary JS on the public registration form — the page where participants enter name, email and phone and where the payment flow starts. It also makes the form dependent on a third-party's uptime and exposes every visitor's IP.

The library is now vendored and served from our own origin, consistent with how TinyMCE is already self-hosted.

### Changes

- **`vendor/javascript/`** — `intl-tel-input@25.12.2` added verbatim from the npm registry tarball: `intl-tel-input--umd.js` (`build/js/intlTelInput.js`) and `intl-tel-input--utils.js` (`build/js/utils.js`).
- **`.gitignore`** — `vendor/` → `vendor/*` with a `!vendor/javascript/` exception, so vendored JS is committed while `vendor/bundle` stays ignored.
- **`config/importmap.rb`** — pins resolve to the local assets. The trailing `# @25.12.2` comments are the form `bin/importmap audit` uses to resolve a version for vendored pins, so the package stays covered by the CI audit.
- **`app/javascript/lib/intl_tel_input.js`** — the npm bundle is UMD, not ESM: in module scope it assigns `window.intlTelInput` and exports nothing (jspm was silently converting it). A four-line wrapper re-exports it, leaving `phone_input_controller.js` untouched.
- **`test/system/participants_phone_input_test.rb`** — covers both pins: the field is enhanced by the main bundle, and a typed number normalizes to E.164, which only succeeds once the lazily imported `utils` module has loaded.

```ruby
# intl-tel-input ships a UMD bundle, so it is vendored and re-exported as an ES module
pin "intl-tel-input", to: "lib/intl_tel_input.js"
pin "intl-tel-input/umd", to: "intl-tel-input--umd.js" # @25.12.2
pin "intl-tel-input/utils", to: "intl-tel-input--utils.js" # @25.12.2
```

### Notes for review

- Once merged, the forthcoming CSP can drop `https://ga.jspm.io` from `script-src`, leaving `self` + Cloudflare
agent_prs.title: Self-host intl-tel-input instead of loading it from ga.jspm.io

issues.body:
## Current state
`config/importmap.rb` pins two modules from a third-party CDN:

```ruby
pin "intl-tel-input", to: "https://ga.jspm.io/npm:intl-tel-input@25.12.2/build/js/intlTelInput.js"
pin "intl-tel-input/utils", to: "https://ga.jspm.io/npm:intl-tel-input@25.12.2/build/js/utils.js"
```

These are loaded as ES modules on the participant registration form (phone input). There is no Subresource Integrity, and importmap-rails does not add SRI for pinned remote URLs by default.

Cloudflare Turnstile (`https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js`) is also loaded from a third party, but that one cannot be pinned/self-hosted — it is inherent to the product and the vendor is trusted.

## Impact
If `ga.jspm.io` is compromised or DNS-hijacked, arbitrary JavaScript executes on the public registration form — the exact page where participants type name, email, phone and where the payment flow starts. This is the classic supply-chain/Magecart scenario.

Secondary concerns: an outage at the CDN breaks the registration form, and every visitor's IP is exposed to a third party.

## Recommendations
1. **Self-host `intl-tel-input`** with `bin/importmap pin intl-tel-input --download` (vendors the files under `vendor/javascript` and pins them locally). This removes the third-party dependency entirely and is consistent with how TinyMCE is already self-hosted (`/tinymce/js/tinymce/tinymce.min.js`). Note `intl-tel-input` also loads a `utils.js` at runtime — check that the vendored setup points at the local copy.
2. If self-hosting is not desired, at minimum add **Subresource Integrity** hashes for the pinned URLs and pin an exact version (already the case: `@25.12.2`).
3. Once self-hosted, the CSP (see the related CSP issue) can drop `https://ga.jspm.io` from `script-src`, leaving only `self` + Cloudflare Turnstile.
4. Keep `bin/importmap audit` in the CI pipeline (it already runs via `config/ci.rb`) so known-vulnerable pinned packages are flagged.

agent_prs.body:
`POST /rails/active_storage/direct_uploads` was reachable by anonymous visitors (it inherits from `ActiveStorage::BaseController`, so our global `authenticate_user!` never applies), allowing arbitrary files of arbitrary type and size to be uploaded and then served from our domain. The endpoint is unused: no `direct_upload: true` forms, no `@rails/activestorage` pin, and TinyMCE uploads go through the guarded `Tinymce::ImagesController`.

### Changes

- **`config/application.rb`** — `config.active_storage.draw_routes = false`, so the engine no longer draws its default route set.
- **`config/initializers/active_storage_routes.rb`** (new) — also sets `ActiveStorage.draw_routes = false` directly. The engine only applies the config flag in an `after_initialize` hook, which can run *after* the route set has been loaded; without this the engine routes were still drawn at boot (and collided with ours).
- **`config/routes.rb`** — redraws the Active Storage routes we actually use, mirroring the engine defaults minus `direct_uploads`:

  ```ruby
  scope ActiveStorage.routes_prefix do
    get "/blobs/redirect/:signed_id/*filename" => "active_storage/blobs/redirect#show", as: :rails_service_blob
    # ... proxy, representation and disk routes ...
    put "/disk/:encoded_token" => "active_storage/disk#update", as: :update_rails_disk_service
  end
  ```

  The `direct`/`resolve` helpers are kept so `rails_blob_path`, `url_for(attachment)` and variants continue to resolve.
- **`test/integration/active_storage_routes_test.rb`** (new) — asserts the direct-uploads path 404s and that `rails_direct_uploads_path` no longer exists, plus a positive check that blob serving still redirects.

### Out of scope

No Rack::Attack throttle was added for `/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads` since the route no longer exists; it would be needed again only if direct uploads are reintroduced. Purging the PoC and other unattached blobs from the staging bucket remains an operational task.

agent_prs.title: Remove unauthenticated Active Storage direct uploads endpoint

issues.body:
**Source:** pentest finding — verified in code.

## Verification
The Active Storage engine is loaded (`config/application.rb`: `require "active_storage/engine"`) and its routes are drawn with the defaults, so `POST /rails/active_storage/direct_uploads` exists. `ActiveStorage::DirectUploadsController` inherits from `ActiveStorage::BaseController` (not our `ApplicationController`), so our global `before_action :authenticate_user!` does **not** apply — only Rails' CSRF token and a session cookie are needed, and both are trivially obtained by visiting any public page.

The endpoint is also unused by this application:
- `config/importmap.rb` does not pin `@rails/activestorage`, and there is no `activestorage` import in `app/javascript` — the client-side direct-upload JS is not even loaded.
- No form uses `direct_upload: true` (repo-wide search returns no hits); the only attachments are `has_one_attached :main_image` (Page, Article) and `has_one_attached :logo` (Sponsor), all uploaded through normal authenticated form posts.
- Rich-text image uploads go through `Tinymce::ImagesController#create`, which *is* properly guarded (`authenticate_upload_user!`, `require_upload_role!`, content-type allowlist, 10 MB limit). Direct uploads bypass every one of those checks.
- `config/initializers/rack_attack.rb` has no throttle for any `/rails/active_storage/*` path.

So an anonymous attacker can upload arbitrary files of arbitrary content type and size and then serve them from our domain via `/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/{signed_id}/{filename}`, exactly as demonstrated in the PoC.

## Impact
- **Malware / phishing hosting on our domain** — attacker-controlled content served from the congress domain lends it credibility and may get the domain blocklisted.
- **Unbounded storage abuse / cost** — no size limit, no rate limit; blobs are unattached so they are only cleaned up by the `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob`/unattached purge if that is scheduled (it is not, as far as the code show

agent_prs.body:
Devise allowed 6-character passwords with no other strength validation on `User`, leaving little resistance to offline cracking or targeted guessing. Per the issue instruction, the minimum is raised to 12 (NIST SP 800-63B favours length over complexity rules).

### Config
- `config/initializers/devise.rb`: `config.password_length = 6..128` → `12..128`.

```ruby
config.password_length = 12..128
```

Existing users keep their current password until they change it; no forced reset.

### View

Fixtures set `encrypted_password` directly and sign-in does not re-validate length, so they were left unchanged.

agent_prs.title: Security: raise minimum password length from 6 to 12

issues.body:
**Source:** pentest finding 7 — verified in code.

## Verification
`config/initializers/devise.rb`:

```ruby
config.password_length = 6..128
```

There are no additional password strength validations on `User` (no complexity, no breached-password check). A six-character password is the only requirement.

## Impact
Weak passwords are permitted, offering little resistance to offline cracking (if the hash database ever leaks) and to targeted online guessing. Note that online brute force is partly mitigated already: Rack::Attack throttles the sign-in path and Turnstile is on the login form.

## Suggested remediation
- Raise the minimum length to at least 8, preferably 12 (NIST SP 800-63B recommends length over complexity rules).
- Optionally reject passwords from known-breached/common password lists.
- Existing users are unaffected until they change their password; consider prompting on next password change rather than forcing a reset.
- Update any tests/fixtures that rely on short passwords.
issues.title: Security: minimum password length of 6 is too weak

agent_prs.body:
Refunded payments were indistinguishable from paid ones: Mollie keeps a refunded payment in the `paid` status and only reports the refunded amount separately, so refunded participants still showed as "Paid" in the admin dashboard and remained on the public participant list.

## Payment model
- New `refunded` status (ours, not Mollie's) with a `refunded` scope and `#refunded?`.
- `refunded` added to `UNSUCCESSFUL_STATUSES`: the money went back to the payer, so it no longer blocks recording a new payment or deleting the participant.

## Mollie sync
- `sync_from_mollie` maps a payment with `amountRefunded > 0` (full or partial) onto `refunded`, covering both the webhook and the redirect/retry paths.
- The "already paid" short-circuit in `create` now checks the synced local payment rather than the raw Mollie status, so a refunded payer can start a new payment instead of being told they already paid.

```ruby
def mollie_status(mollie_payment)
  return "refunded" if mollie_refunded?(mollie_payment)

  mollie_payment.status
end
```

## Admin dashboard
- `Participant#registration_status` returns `"Refund"` (red badge), unless a later payment succeeded.
- Status filter gains a `Refund` option; Confirmed/Pending filters exclude refunded participants; status sorting `CASE` extended with `Refund` after `Paid`.

## Public participant list
- New `Participant.not_refunded` scope, applied in `ParticipantsController#index`. A subsequent successful payment reinstates the participant.

Tests cover the model behaviour, webhook refund detection (including a zero-amount refund staying `paid`), the public list exclusion, and the admin filters/sorting.

agent_prs.body:
Previously, a guest could register a participant with any email address; if a `User` already existed for that address, the new participant was silently attached to that account. This let anyone add registrations to someone else's account. Registrations under an existing account now require being signed in as that account.

### Controller (`ParticipantsController`)
- New `refuse_registration_for_existing_account` before_action on `create`, declared **after** `verify_turnstile` so the response cannot be used to probe for account existence.
- Guest + email belongs to a **confirmed** account → redirect to sign-in with an alert to log in first.
- Guest + email belongs to an **unconfirmed** account → redirect to the confirmation resend page (that account cannot sign in yet), mirroring the existing `alter_registration` EGD-duplicate flow.
- Signed-in users are unchanged: `build_participant` already locks the email to `current_user.email`, so their additional registrations still link to their own account and confirm immediately.

```ruby
def refuse_registration_for_existing_account
  return if user_signed_in?

  email = normalize_email(@participant.email)
  return if email.blank?

  user = User.find_by(email: email)
  return if user.nil?

  if user.confirmed?
    redirect_to new_user_session_path, alert: "An account with that email address already exists. Please log in first to register another participant."
  else
    redirect_to new_user_confirmation_path, notice: "An account with that email address already exists. Please confirm your email address to continue."
  end
end
```

### Tests
- The two tests covering the old "guest registration links to existing user" behaviour are replaced by refusal tests (no participant created, no mail sent, expected redirect + flash) for the confirmed and unconfirmed account cases.
- Linking behaviour is still covered, now via the signed-in owner path.

Open point for review: the alert confirms that an account exists for the submitted addr

agent_prs.body:
Upgrades the app to Ruby 4.0.6 and fixes the Codespaces error where ruby-lsp could not activate the Ruby environment:

```
rbenv: version `ruby-3.4.5' is not installed (set by /workspaces/egc27/.ruby-version)
```

Two things caused that: `.ruby-version` carried a `ruby-` prefix (version managers expect a bare version), and the devcontainer image's Ruby did not match the declared version.

### Ruby version bump
- `.ruby-version`: `ruby-3.4.5` → `4.0.6`
- `Dockerfile`: `ARG RUBY_VERSION=4.0.6`
- Version references updated in `config/deploy.yml` comment and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

### Devcontainer
- Base image switched from `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/ruby:3-4-trixie` to `ghcr.io/rails/devcontainer/images/ruby:4.0.6`, which ships exactly the Ruby declared in `.ruby-version` (matching the `ghcr.io/rails/devcontainer/*` features already in use)
- Dropped the rvm-specific `gem install rails webdrivers` and `rvm fix-permissions` steps — rvm is absent from this image, and gems come from the Gemfile; apt install now wrapped in `USER root` / `USER vscode` since the image runs as `vscode`
- `devcontainer.json` pins the LSP's version manager instead of letting it guess rbenv:

```jsonc
"customizations": {
  "vscode": {
    "settings": {
      "rubyLsp.rubyVersionManager": { "identifier": "mise" }
    }
  }
}
```

Inside the built image, `mise ls` resolves `ruby 4.0.6` from `/workspaces/egc27/.ruby-version`. No Gemfile changes were needed; the existing lockfile installs cleanly and the suite passes on 4.0.6.

Note: the production image build could not be exercised end-to-end in the sandbox (TLS interception breaks `bundle install` inside Docker), so CI is the first real check of that path.

Admins had no way to remove a participant registration. Deletion should be blocked once a payment succeeded, and when the participant is the last one under their user, the admin should be warned and able to delete the user account as well.

## Changes

- **Route**: `DELETE /admin/participants/:id` (`admin/participants` now includes `:destroy`).
- **`Admin::ParticipantsController#destroy`**: refuses with an alert when the participant has a completed payment; otherwise destroys the participant (payments and event registrations cascade through existing `dependent: :destroy`). The user is destroyed in the same transaction only when the `delete_user` checkbox is submitted, a user exists, it is not the signed-in admin's own account, and no other participants remain for that user.
- **`Participant`**: `deletable?` (`!blocking_payments?`) and `only_participant_for_user?` express the two rules in the model.
- **Admin edit view**: new "Delete participant" section with a Turbo confirm dialog. Shows the warning plus "Also delete the user account" checkbox for a user's last participant, or an explanation when a successful payment blocks deletion.
- **Tests**: authorization, payment block, checkbox on/off, non-last-participant case, and the rendered edit-page states.

```ruby
delete_user = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(params[:delete_user]) &&
  user.present? && user != current_user && @participant.only_participant_for_user?

ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  @participant.destroy!
  user.destroy! if delete_user
end
```

Deletion is exposed on the admin edit page rather than the index row actions, since the last-participant warning and checkbox need the space; the index can be extended later if admins want a one-click path.

Participants whose payments are all canceled, expired or failed had no way to get a manual payment recorded: the admin UI only offered the record-payment link when a participant had *no* payments at all, so a single dead Mollie attempt permanently blocked manual registration.

### Changes

- **`Payment`** — added `UNSUCCESSFUL_STATUSES` (`canceled`, `expired`, `failed`), an `unsuccessful?` predicate and `unsuccessful` / `blocking` scopes.

<% elsif !participant.blocking_payments? %>

Pages were all publicly readable. This adds a per-page access level so some pages require a signed-in user, and hides restricted pages from menus, listings and search for anonymous visitors.

### Data model
- Migration adds `pages.access_level` (string, `null: false`, default `"public"`).
- `Page` enum with `prefix: :access_level` (avoids clashing with `Module#public`), plus `Page.readable_by(user)` scope and `Page#readable_by?(user)`.

```ruby
enum :access_level, { public: "public", authenticated: "authenticated" }, prefix: :access_level

scope :readable_by, ->(user) { user.present? ? all : where(access_level: :public) }

def readable_by?(user)
  access_level_public? || user.present?
end
```

### Access enforcement
- `PagesController#show` falls back to `authenticate_user!` when the page is not readable (visitor is redirected to sign-in and returned after login).
- `PagesController#index` scopes to `Page.readable_by(current_user)`; `access_level` added to strong params.

Admins had no way to see all completed payments in one place, nor to track which ones had been entered in the bookkeeping. This adds a `processed_in_bookkeeping` flag on payments, an overview of completed payments, and actions to toggle that flag.

def mark_processed

end

  payment.update!(processed_in_bookkeeping: processed)

  redirect_to admin_payments_path(processed: permitted_processed_filter), notice: notice
end
```

Toggling the flag does not touch `status`, so it never triggers the payment confirmation email.

agent_prs.body:
Participants sometimes pay in cash or by bank transfer, which previously had no way to be reflected in the app — registration status stayed unpaid because every `Payment` originated from Mollie.

### Schema
- `payments.provider` (`mollie` | `manual`) default `mollie`, NOT NULL — existing rows keep Mollie semantics.
- `payments.payment_method` (`mollie` | `cash` | `bank_transfer` | `other`) or values from Mollie
- `payments.reference` (optional) for a bank transaction or receipt reference.

### Model
- Inclusion validation on `payment_method`, plus `manual?` and `payment_method_label`.
- Confirmation email callback moved from `after_update_commit` to `after_commit on: [:create, :update]`, so a payment created directly as paid also notifies the participant. The `confirmation_sent` check-and-set guard against duplicate mails is unchanged.

```ruby
after_commit :send_payment_confirmation, on: [:create, :update], if: :became_paid?
```

### Admin flow
- `Admin::PaymentsController#new/#create`, admin-only, nested at `admin/participants/:participant_id/payments`.
- Form is prefilled from `CongressPassPricing` for the participant; amount is entered in euros and converted to cents.
- `mollie` is not offered and is rejected server-side, and `mollie_payment_id` is always left blank, so manual records can't collide with or masquerade as Mollie transactions.

**Alvorlig, og ikke udgivet:** kom med #80. På butikker med WooCommerces egne ordretabeller (HPOS) blev et tillægs varer taget af leveringen igen, et øjeblik efter de var lagt på. Gaardmester kører HPOS. Fundet af #87's HPOS-kørsel og forklarer #89.

## Hvad skete der

1. Tillæggets skrivning sender varelisten med tillægget og optegner den bagefter med `save_meta_data()`.
2. På HPOS gemmer en meta-skrivning hele ordren, når ordrens "ændret"-tid er et sekund eller mere gammel (`OrdersTableDataStore::after_meta_change`). Den gemning udløser `woocommerce_update_order` og dermed den første ordres genafsendelse.
3. Genafsendelsen kørte, før tillægget var skrevet på ordrens liste. Den byggede derfor varelisten uden tillægget, så en forskel fra optegnelsen og sendte listen uden tillægget.

I en butik er ordren altid mere end et sekund gammel, så det ville ramme næsten hvert tillæg. I testsuiten er ordren sjældent et sekund gammel, så det viste sig kun af og til: #89 og `TwoAdditionsAtOnceTest` "after an earlier addition" på HPOS, 4–6 ud af 10 kørsler før denne rettelse. På posts-lageret gemmer en meta-skrivning ikke ordren, så det gamle lager var ikke ramt.

## Rettelsen

- Holdes ordren af en tillægsskrivning i samme request, sender genafsendelsen intet. Skrivningen sender varerne og fører selv optegnelsen. En 1.5.2-ordre får stadig sin optegnelse, og den sender intet.
- Når skrivningen har sluppet holdet, kører genafsendelsen én gang. Det, den første ordre selv har at sende, går så med tillægget på listen og i optegnelsen: en rettelse, der ikke nåede frem, eller en 1.5.2-ordre, der har flyttet sig.
- Det samme gælder, når et tillæg tages af.
- Genafsendelsens eget hold fra #81 er uændret.

## Test

- Ny test `test_the_earlier_order_saved_during_an_addition_keeps_its_goods` med og uden et tidligere tillæg. Den fremprovokerer gemningen hver gang: på posts-lageret ved at gøre det, ordretabellerne gør, og på HPOS med en ordre, der sidst blev ændret for en time siden.
- Uden
agent_prs.title: Et tillæg mister ikke sine varer, når HPOS gemmer ordren midt i skrivningen (#89)

issues.body:
To tests fejler af og til, når hele wpunit-suiten kører, men aldrig alene:

- `UpgradeFrom152Test::test_an_addition_to_a_1_5_2_order_does_not_send_it_whole` fejlede én gang på HPOS i CI på #87 (run 40494018540): "Only the write that puts the addition on the shipment. Failed asserting that actual size 2 matches expected size 1".
- `AnAdditionsRefundReachesTheDeliveryTest::test_putting_an_addition_on_sends_its_goods_once` fejlede én gang i en lokal kørsel af hele suiten på HPOS: "actual size 2 matches expected size 1" (linje 153).

**Symptom, begge gange:** efter den PUT, der lægger tillægget på, sender den første ordres egen genafsendelse (`oko_resend_shipment_on_update`, udløst af gemningen i `oko_remember_addition`) én PUT til. Den har altså set en forskel mellem ordren og optegnelsen af, hvad Økoskabet har.

**Hvorfor det betyder noget:**
- For en ordre med optegnelse (`OKO_SENT_META`) er den ekstra PUT de samme varer igen. Det er uskadeligt.
- For en åben 1.5.2-ordre uden optegnelse betyder et manglende fingeraftryks-match, at **hele ordren** sendes, oven i rettelser fra backoffice.

**Ikke reproduceret:**
- 25 kørsler af `UpgradeFrom152Test` alene på HPOS.
- 10 kørsler af hele suiten på HPOS (PHP 8.3, WooCommerce 11.2.1) efter #80 og #88.
- Agenten på #87 kørte 11 lokalt.

Fejlen afhænger derfor sandsynligvis af rækkefølgen af tests eller af tilstand, der lever på tværs af tests i samme PHP-proces. Kandidater:
- `oko_merchant_configuration_memo()` og andre statics, som `Merchants::purge_config_cache()` ikke rydder mellem tests
- `static $seen` i `oko_resend_shipment_on_update`
- WooCommerces ordre-cache på HPOS

**Næste skridt, når den viser sig igen:** gør de to assertions mere sigende, så de udskriver den ekstra PUT og optegnelsen. Så kan forskellen ses direkte. #87 kører suiten i CI ved hver PR, så den bliver fanget.

issues.body:
## Hvad sker der

`uninstall.php` er plugin-skabelonens: `o_uninstall()` indeholder kun en udkommenteret `@TODO`. Afinstallation fjerner derfor intet: hverken indstillinger, merchant-konti, de options #80 tilføjer (`okoskabet_line_totals_last_said`, holdene `_oko_addition_lock_*`), migreringslisten (`okoskabet_completed_migrations`) eller ordre-meta.

## Beslutning

WordPress-konventionen er, at afinstallation rydder op. En butik, der afinstallerer og geninstallerer, mister så sin opsætning (API-nøgler, merchants). Ordre-meta bør nok blive stående under alle omstændigheder, fordi ordrerne findes videre.

Forslag: slet pluginets egne options og transients, behold ordre-meta. Men det er jeres valg.

`oko_order_line_items()` trækker refunderede antal fra og springer linjer med antal under 1 over. Hvad skal en fuldt refunderet ordre gøre hos Økoskabet?

issues.body:
Fundet i gennemgangen før 1.6.0 (#80). Ikke rettet der.

## Hvad sker der

#80 lægger et hold pr. ordre (`oko_lock_additions_to`) om den skrivning, der lægger et tillæg på en levering, så to tillæg på samme tid ikke taber det ene. Men forældreordrens egen genafsendelse, `oko_resend_shipment_on_update()`, skriver også hele varelisten (`oko_lines_with_additions`), og den tager ikke holdet.

Overlapper de to, kan en af PUT'erne lande sidst:

- Forælderens PUT lander sidst og er bygget, før tillægget blev husket. Så mangler tillæggets varer hos Økoskabet, mens ordren siger, at de er med. Ingen senere gemning retter det, for genafsendelsen sammenligner med sin egen optegnelse, ikke med Økoskabet.

#80 får genafsendelsen til at køre oftere end før: en rettelse eller delvis refusion af et tillæg sender nu forælderen igen.

## Set

Ved at læse koden på #80's gren (`oko_resend_shipment_on_update` kalder ikke `oko_lock_additions_to`). Ikke afprøvet med en probe. Probe-mønstret fra `TwoAdditionsAtOnceTest` (et `pre_http_request`-filter, der kører den anden anmodning midt i den første PUT) kan genbruges.

## Mulig rettelse (~15 linjer)

Kun når `line_items` er blandt ændringerne:

1. Tag `oko_lock_additions_to($order_id)`.
2. Er holdet optaget: send intet, og sæt ikke `$seen`. Optegnelsen er urørt, så næste gemning prøver igen.
3. Byg `line_items` fra en frisk indlæst ordre inde i holdet, PUT dem, og optegn de byggede linjer.
4. Slip holdet i `finally`.

agent_prs.body:
Closes #19

## Contexte

Sur la page Tarifs « Écoles », le nombre d'enseignants choisi au curseur ne correspondait pas aux graduations ni à la pastille de palier allumée dessous.

Cause, mesurée dans le navigateur (1280 px) : le calcul du palier (`indexPalier`) est juste, mais le curseur allait de 1 à 40 **de façon linéaire**, alors que les graduations « 1 5 10 15 20 40 » et les pastilles étaient réparties **à intervalles réguliers**. À 20 enseignants, le curseur était au milieu (49 %), la graduation « 20 » à 78 % et la pastille « 20 et + » allumée entre 67 et 85 %. L'écart venait déjà de la maquette.

## Ce qui change

- **Le curseur suit l'échelle des paliers** : chaque palier en occupe un cinquième (1 → 0 %, 5 → 20 %, 10 → 40 %, 15 → 60 %, 20 → 80 %, 40 → 100 %), linéaire entre deux repères. Le palier 20–40 garde donc un cinquième du curseur au lieu de la moitié. Fonctions pures `CRANS`, `positionCurseur`, `enseignantsCurseur` et `largeursPaliers` dans `assets/js/tarifs-ui.js`. Le curseur va maintenant de 0 à 100 et se cale sur la position exacte du nombre affiché.
- **Graduations** placées sous la position exacte du centre du curseur (même repère, demi-pouce de 8 px compris).
- **Pastilles** : même ligne de cinq, chacune dimensionnée pour que le curseur soit toujours au-dessus de la pastille allumée. Les frontières tombent à mi-chemin entre deux nombres, par exemple entre 4 et 5.
- **Clavier** : les flèches ajoutent ou retirent un enseignant. Début, Fin, Page préc. et Page suiv. gardent leur comportement natif.
- **Petit écran** : des espaces insécables font que les pastilles ne se coupent qu'après « : » (« 10–14 : » / « −19 % »), avec un rembourrage réduit.
- **Inchangés** : les prix, les règles de remise, les libellés et l'annonce du lecteur d'écran (`aria-valuetext` = « N enseignants »).

## Summary

Moves an embargo's status, revision link and termination onto the `EmbargoEvent` itself and makes the case's `embargo_register` its ordered list of whole embargoes, deleting the register-entry type (ADR-0202). Every reader of an entry's `status`, `replaces` or `termination` now reads the embargo's own field.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Motivation

Every fact about an embargo belongs on the embargo, so a later message about its status can be an `Update` of the embargo itself (#6625, #6482). Pre-1.0, stored cases are not migrated (ADR-0175).

**Decision — the stored termination's cause is required.** ADR-0202 gives a terminated embargo "the cause kind, the act that caused it when known, and a human reason"; only the act is qualified by "when known", and ADR-0203 makes end time reached "a cause like the others". So `EmbargoTermination.cause` is now required. The `Remove(EmbargoEvent)` wire form keeps its optional `terminationCause` until #6482 retires it: a `Remove` that names no cause ends the embargo early for an unnamed reason, which is what `OTHER` means, so `EmbargoTermination.from_cause(None)` records `OTHER`. That one mapping is used by the CASE_MANAGER's teardown and the replica's ledger copy, so every node stores the same termination. EMB-13-011 is amended to say so. Refusing a no-cause `Remove` instead would have broken the participant's threat-signal ask, which sends no cause (EMB-13-005).

CM-17-024 (the register never holds an embargo by id) follows from ADR-0202, which the maintainer decided in planning; the refusal the old rule asked for cannot arise once the register holds

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — every fact about an embargo is on the embargo, so a message about its status can be an Update of the embargo itself.

## Summary

`EmbargoEvent` holds only its terms. Its status, the embargo a revision replaced and how it ended are on the case's register entry `(embargo, status, replaces, termination)` (`vultron/core/models/embargo_register/entry.py`). ADR-0202 (proposed in the docs PR) moves all three onto the embargo and makes the register the case's ordered list of embargoes. ADR-0122's statuses, triggers and invariants stand, now over the embargoes' own fields. This is a stored-schema change, decided by the maintainer in planning. Pre-1.0, there is no migration of old stored cases (ADR-0175).

## Summary

Call-outs (`SynchronousCallOut`, ADR-0183, `vultron/core/behaviors/call_out/`) write their answers through their own blackboard client, not through a port binding. `BTBridge` restores none of these keys after a run, and the managed-keys check from #6771 (PR #6787) cannot see them, because it reads port bindings. So a call-out's verdict or refusal reason can stay on the blackboard into the next act's run.

## Evidence or Context

Across all call-out contracts there are about 60 such keys.

This is a design choice; re-survey first. Two examples, not prescriptions:

- The bridge finds every call-out in the tree it runs and restores the keys each declares.
- Each call-out seam restores its own keys when its tick ends, as `ActKeyScope` does.

Listing about 60 keys by hand in `managed_keys` is the wrong fix: it would drift as contracts are added.

A note's body, title and audience travel as `content`, `name` and `intendedAudience`, an identifier's value as `identifier`, and the item's notes as `vulNotes`. Each name was checked against the AS2 Vocabulary definition first. An AS2 term is used only where it means the same thing (VM-10-009). Every other name is a new Vultron term with its own definition (VM-10-012).

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — an AS2 reader sees the Case Owner's removal or reinstatement as the Owner's own act, naming the actor, which the CASE_MANAGER admits and announces.

## Summary

Today the Owner sends `Remove(CaseParticipant)[target=VulnerabilityCase]` or `Add(CaseParticipant)[target=VulnerabilityCase]`, which names the CASE_MANAGER's record instead of the actor the Owner decided about. ADR-0199 revision 2 (PR #6624) keeps the decision the Owner's own act and changes what it names:

- The Owner sends the CASE_MANAGER `Remove(<Actor>, origin=<case>)` or `Add(<Actor>, target=<case>)`. The act names the actor as a typed reference (`id` + `type`), not the `CaseParticipant`.
- The CASE_MANAGER refuses an act that breaks the existing rules with a refusal notice. Otherwise it admits the Owner's act as the one ledger entry. It sends no `Accept` and makes no act of its own.
- The named actor receives the CASE_MANAGER's `Announce(<the Owner's act>)`, with an id derived from the act. That replaces the separate unledgered notice. Replicas apply the change only from the entry.

Revision 1 of ADR-0199 had the Owner offer the act and the CASE_MANAGER accept it and make it. That is withdrawn, and so is the Offer form this Task first described. The participant record, its removal fact and the reinstatement semantics are unchanged (ADR-0116). There is no shim for the old form (pre-1.0).

## Summary

Plans #6748: participants need a way to share their local tracking IDs with a case. This PR specifies the behavior in a new group, CM-35. Task #6762 implements it, and the CM-35 tests stay strict `xfail` until it lands.

The decisions from the planning interview:

- A participant status carries a list of tracking IDs. Each entry has a required `value` and an optional free-text `tracker`. Neither field is interpreted or checked against a fixed list of names. The field isn't called `id`, because AS2's context maps `id` to `@id`.
- The list is a set keyed on `value`: a status with two entries that share a `value` is refused.
- A status that leaves the list out keeps the previous set, a list replaces it, and `[]` clears it. The set exists to route inbound messages to the participant's tracker, so it must show the current set. A case-file update merges its lists (CM-34-011), but the participant is the only author of its own tracking IDs, so it doesn't have that problem.
- The whole case sees the set, so participants can name each other's tickets when they talk outside the case.
- When a received status leaves the list out, the CASE_MANAGER records the participant's previous set. This is the one exception to recording a status as received (RSH-09-001, RSH-09-010). The ledger then shows the participant which IDs the case holds for it, so it can correct a wrong set with a new status. Replicas copy the recorded set.
- A tracking ID is its own type. It never parses as a vulnerability's `ids` entry, and an `ids` entry never parses as a tracking ID.

issues.body:
Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — a fresh actor's store opens reliably, so creating an actor never returns 500 from a schema-creation race.

## Summary

`POST /api/v2/actors/` on a demo container returned 500 with
`sqlite3.OperationalError: table vultron_objects already exists`. The call path is
`create_actor` (`vultron/adapters/driving/fastapi/routers/actors/_routes/registry.py`)
→ `get_datalayer` (`vultron/adapters/driven/datalayer_sqlite/__init__.py`)
→ `SqliteDataLayer.__init__` → `SQLModel.metadata.create_all(self._engine)`
(`vultron/adapters/driven/datalayer_sqlite/datalayer.py`).

`create_all` checks for each table, then creates it. `session_guard` serialises that
inside one engine, but `get_datalayer`'s `_actor_instances` check-then-set has no lock,
and another engine or process opening the same database file at the same moment can
create the table between the check and the `CREATE TABLE`.

## Evidence or Context

- PR #5997, run 42165051821, job `rvcv-handoff Demo Integration`: `actor2` returned
  500 on the seeding step "Seeding the Coordinator and Vendor2 containers with actor
  records". `rvcv-handoff Invariant Harness` and `CI gate` failed as a result.
- The PR changes only embargo Reject ids; the same workflow passed on `main` at
  `8f07421ab`. So the failure is intermittent and not caused by that diff.

## Fix or Approach

Make opening a store safe when two openers race: serialise `get_datalayer`'s
instance creation with a module lock, and treat "table already exists" from
`create_all` as success (or create tables with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`
semantics), so a concurrent opener does not fail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two threads that open the same new actor's file-backed store at the same time
  both succeed, and a test pins it.
- [ ] `get_datalayer` returns one instance per (actor, URL) under concurrent calls.

Governing specs: DL-07-004

| Mark | Icon | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| best | ⭐ | layer 1 in the highest band with any moves |
| good | 👍 | harm-free, not best |
| sub-optimal | ⚠️ | trade-off band, not best |
| neutral | ➖ | unhelpful band, every shift zero (advice-only moves included) |

- A trade-off move with no harm-free move open at that point is ⭐.
- A ⚠️ move that a harm-free move dominated also says "a harm-free move did as well".

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — the `caseEngagement` key either gets a writer and survives each status, or stops travelling on the wire.

## Summary

`ParticipantStatus.case_engagement` (wire `caseEngagement`, default `True`) is a self-reported claim that no trigger, node or message ever sets. `CreateParticipantStatusNode` builds each new status without it, so any value but the default would be lost on the participant's next status. Planning #6748 found this: `tracking_id` had the same gap.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

The surface reading is "a field is missing a setter". The underlying question is whether "engaged" means anything apart from the participant's RM state. `Engage` already moves RM to ACCEPTED, and `Defer` moves it to DEFERRED. If the flag repeats what RM says, it is a dead duplicate and should be deleted, as #6415 deleted `participantCaseName`. If it means something else (for example "still watching but not acting"), it needs a spec, a writer and the same carry-forward rule CM-35-004 gives tracking IDs.

## Category

- [x] Technical debt

## Severity

Low

## Evidence

- `vultron/core/models/participant_status.py` (`case_engagement` field)
- `vultron/core/behaviors/case/nodes/participant/status.py` (`_build_status` does not pass it)
- `vultron/core/use_cases/triggers/case/engage.py` (moves RM only)

## Impact if Ignored

A wire key that always reads `true` suggests a meaning no implementation gives it. Another implementation that sets it to `false` would see the value dropped on its next status.

## Suggested Action

Decide whether engagement is anything apart from RM. If not, delete the field and its JSON-LD term (as #6415 did). If it is, specify it and carry it forward through the shared status-write helper #6762 adds.

Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — makes owner-triggered stub invites use the case manager's configured rsvp windows.

## Summary

An owner trigger that stamps a stub Invite deadline uses the default RSVP windows, not the CASE_MANAGER's configured ones.
Triggers have no way to receive `actor_config`, so a re-issue started from the owner's trigger (owner terminate, owner accept of an embargo revision) is stamped with `default_rsvp_window` and `min_rsvp_window` defaults.
Stub Invites and re-issues started by a received message get the manager's configured windows, because #4049 threaded `actor_config` through those use cases and trees.
Two Invites for the same case can therefore carry deadlines computed from different windows, depending on which path produced them.

Found by the pr-ship run on PR #4345 (#4049).
That run found the trigger-side behaviour consistent with how a trigger-side embargo Invite is stamped, so it left it and stated it in the PR body.
Verify the claim in the code before changing anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A trigger-started stub Invite or re-issue is stamped with the same RSVP window the CASE_MANAGER's `ActorConfig` gives a received-message-started one, under the shared deadline rule (CM-28-012, `stamp_rsvp_deadline`).
- [ ] AC-2: The trigger path gets `actor_config` through the same port or factory mechanism the received use cases use. No second deadline calculation and no new setting.
- [ ] AC-3: A trigger-side embargo Invite relay is checked for the same gap, and fixed if it has it.
- [ ] AC-4: Tests show two paths (trigger and received) producing the same deadline for the same `published` time and the same configured window, including a non-default window.

Governing specs: CM-28-012, CM-28-013, CM-28-014, CM-11-014, CM-11-016, EP-07-002, EP-07-006, ADR-0115

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — an AS2 reader sees the Case Owner's invitation as the Owner's own `Invite`, and the invitee answers the CASE_MANAGER's stub Invite made from it.

## Summary

ADR-0199 revision 3 (#6626, PR #6696): the decider sends its own act, and when that act needs an answer, the CASE_MANAGER makes the ask. The ask is its own `Offer` or `Invite` with the decider's `object` and `target`, `attributedTo` naming the decider and `inReplyTo` naming the decider's act. An `Announce` never asks.

The Case Owner decides whom to invite, but its direct-invite trigger sends a recommend-actor `Offer(Actor)[target=VulnerabilityCase]` (CM-17-007), which is an `Offer` for a decision the Owner makes itself. This Task replaces that with the Owner's own `Invite(<case preview>)[target=<invitee>]`, carrying the roles, sent to the CASE_MANAGER only. The CASE_MANAGER records the Owner's Invite in the ledger and sends its own stub Invite to the invitee.

The suggestion path keeps its shape. A participant's `Offer(Actor)` is a suggestion the Owner decides, the Owner's `Accept` is its decision, and the stub Invite's `inReplyTo` names that `Accept` (#6464).

## Summary

Let a `VulnerabilityItem` embed or link a CSAF or CVE document as its content, with a `mediaType` that identifies the format.

## Motivation

This is #5132's original second half. An item could carry the issuer's record for its vulnerability (a CVE record, or a CSAF document for that vulnerability). - Content plus `mediaType` on the item.
- The CVE JSON schema check for CVE content (CM-05-010).

- A CSAF document in an item is a projection of the case, never a source (CSAF-02-002).

## Summary

When the CASE_MANAGER makes an act another actor asked for, it credits the asker in `attributedTo` (CM-24-002, CM-24-012) but does not name the request. Theme: theme:test-and-ci — makes the demo placeholder-sentinel ratchet model guards and bindings the way Python runs them, so it neither fails correct code nor passes a leak.

## Summary

The pre-push review of #5904 found three mis-models in
`test/architecture/test_demo_step_no_unbound_ratchet.py` that sit outside that
issue's seven gaps. They are fixed in the same PR, which closes this issue.

## Evidence or Context

1. `except E as offer` and a match capture (`case Foo() as offer`, `[*offer]`,
   `{**offer}`) bind the sentinel name, but the check did not treat them as
   rebindings: a read in that arm was reported (false positive).
2. A read in the `else` arm of `if offer:`, or in the body of
   `if offer is None:` / `if not offer:`, was treated as defended, although that
   arm is exactly where the name holds a falsy value, maybe the placeholder
   (false negative).
3. A `match` case guard (`case 1 if offer:`) did not defend its own case body.

Where: `test/architecture/test_demo_step_no_unbound_ratchet.py`

## Fix or Approach

Treat handler and capture names as rebindings; give each guard test a polarity
(true proves real vs. false proves real) and scan the arm it leaves undefended,
while the statement still guards the reads after it; treat a case guard like an
`if` test for its own body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `except ... as x` and capture-pattern bindings end the sentinel within their arm.
- [ ] AC-2: the arm a guard proves may hold the placeholder is scanned for reads, and the statement still guards the reads after it.
- [ ] AC-3: a case guard defends its case body.
- [ ] AC-4: each has a test that fails on `origin/main`, and the demo tree still reports 0 leaks.

Governing specs: EDF-06-005, ARCH-18-005

The gate's name describes a protocol ask, which BT-18-014 forbids as a call-out point. Its default is `AlwaysSucceed`, so it never asks anyone. EMB-15-002 and EMB-15-007 justify it by a CASE_MANAGER answering an overture on the owner's behalf, but the CASE_MANAGER never runs this tree: its own consent goes through `record_manager_embargo_consent_tree`, which has no owner gate. `EvaluateEmbargoProposal` already carries the invitee's own policy.

## Evidence or Context

Raised by the #3425 build (Epic run #1147) and investigated with the user. The owner-delegation gate this might be mistaken for is Idea #6045: a CASE_MANAGER sending `Add(EmbargoEvent)` on the owner's standing instruction. That gate belongs on the CASE_MANAGER's activation path, which does not exist yet, so removing this one leaves no hole #6045 needs.

## Fix or Approach

Delete the gate and its bypass Selector. The accept arm becomes `EvaluateEmbargoProposal` then the accept delegate. Amend the two EMB-15 statements to match.

- [ ] AC-1: `create_embargo_response_decision_tree` has no `AuthorizeSelector`, no `CheckIsCaseOwner` arm and no `CaseOwnerApprovesEmbargoResponse` call-out.

## Summary

On Python 3.14, `vultron.wire.as2.signing.load_json` does not always refuse a JSON text that nests too deeply. The refusal depends on the stack size of the host, not on a limit the code sets.

## Evidence or Context

The 3.14 spike (#6053) ran the full suite on CPython 3.14.10 in CI (scratch PR #6345). One test failed, in the `arch` part:

```text
FAILED test/wire/as2/test_signing.py::test_load_json_refuses_text_python_cannot_read[deep-nesting]
  Failed: DID NOT RAISE VultronRefusedJsonError
1 failed, 7408 passed, 4 skipped, 74 xfailed
```

Run: https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/actions/runs/43270317779/job/131364982451

Cause: `load_json` has no depth limit of its own. It relies on `json.loads` raising `RecursionError` for deep nesting and turns that into `VultronRefusedJsonError("JSON is nested too deeply to parse")`. - 3.13, any stack: `RecursionError` (refused).

Theme: theme:adoption-documentation — a reader finds a released draft's frozen pages at `spec/draft-N/` as soon as its release is published.

## Summary

`deploy_site.yml` runs only on its weekday schedule (06:07 UTC) and on a manual dispatch. Nothing starts it when a GitHub Release is published. A released draft's frozen pages therefore stay a placeholder until the next scheduled publish, which can be up to three days later.

## Evidence or Context

Release `v2026.11.0` (Draft 1), 2026-11-13, times in UTC:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 06:22 | The scheduled publish deploys `1ae1bda2c`. Its drafts register already names `draft-1` as released in `v2026.11.0`. |
| 14:45 | The promote creates the draft release with `vultron-spec-draft-1.tar.gz` and its `.sha256`. |
| 15:10 | A maintainer publishes the release. |

The 06:22 publish found the release unpublished and correctly wrote the placeholder (DOCBW-08-032). No publish ran after 15:10, so https://certcc.github.io/Vultron/spec/draft-1/ shows the placeholder. Without a manual dispatch it would stay until Monday 06:07 UTC.

The release procedure has no step that says to publish the site after the release is published.

What is correct and stays:

- The placeholder for an unpublished release (DOCBW-08-032).
- Serving from `main`'s register (DOCBW-08-027).
- The one-publish-at-a-time concurrency group (DOCBW-06-021).

## Fix or Approach

Add `release: types: [published]` to `deploy_site.yml`.

- The run deploys `main`, never the release tag. The workflow already starts every run from `main` (ADR-0171).
- `publish_gate.py` must accept the new event. Decide whether a release-triggered publish keeps the CI gate (recommended: keep it, as the scheduled publish does).
- The `pages` concurrency group already serializes this run with a scheduled or manual one.

The alternative is a documented manual dispatch as the release's last step. It is rejected because a person can forget it.

## Motivation

The promote fixes the pages of one `publish-*` snapshot (DOCBW-07-001). If the entry were added after the promote, the released snapshot would say "not yet released" for good. Theme: theme:adoption-documentation — the promote can release a draft's frozen pages, so the archive adopters cite is actually made.

## Summary

The `frozen-draft` job of `.github/workflows/promote_release.yml` builds the site and checks it, but it never serves `site/spec/`. So once a draft is marked released, its own frozen-copy link fails the job, and the promote makes no tag or release.

## Evidence or Context

Once the drafts register marks a draft released (#6280), the generated Revision Log status table links its frozen copy at `spec/draft-N/` (DOCBW-08-008).

The `frozen-draft` job runs these steps in order:

1. `build-site`
2. `check-site-publication`, which runs `docs-links`
3. `frozen_draft.py build`

It never runs `.github/actions/serve-frozen-drafts`, so `site/spec/` is absent in that job. Two checks then fail on the frozen-copy link:

- `docs-links` reports the link unresolved.
- The archive builder records `'../../../spec/draft-1/' names no file of the site`. This was reproduced locally on the #6280 branch.

The `frozen-draft` job fails, the promote is skipped, and no `v2026.11.0` tag or release is made.

The deploy and the review already serve the frozen drafts before their checks (DOCBW-08-028, DOCBW-08-035). The pull-request check is green only because of that.

## Fix or Approach

Run `serve-frozen-drafts` in the archive job after `build-site` and before `check-site-publication`, with the promoted commit's register. A draft whose release is not published yet gets the DOCBW-08-032 placeholder. The archive builder then writes the link as its live URL (DOCBW-08-016).

Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — a VINCE response added and then deleted on a branch can no longer reach main's history unseen.

## Summary

The committed-data check (#5961) judged only a pull request's final tree. Main merges with merge commits, so a response added in one branch commit and deleted in a later one reaches main's history with CI green. Only pre-commit guards each commit, and a hook can be skipped.

## Evidence or Context

Found by the pre-push review of the #5961 branch (finding `phase8-pr-commits-not-scanned-0`). ADR-0189's threat is permanent git history.

## Fix or Approach

`vince-data check --history BASE` also reads every file each non-merge commit in `BASE..HEAD` added or changed, and the VINCE Data Check workflow runs it with full history. A generator-marked file at a path the generator writes is accepted in an earlier commit without the byte comparison, since it may hold an earlier generator's output; the head tree gets the full check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A VINCE-shaped file added in one branch commit and deleted in a later one fails the check in CI.
- [ ] AC-2: An earlier generation of a generator fixture on the branch passes, and a generator-marked file at a path the generator does not write fails.

Governing specs: VSD-02-001, VSD-02-005.

## Summary

`ConnectorPlugin` requires both a push-in method and a write-out method. So the read-only, polled VINCE shadow connector (#5963) could only satisfy it by carrying a write method it must never have. This plan splits the connector contract by direction: a connector has a name plus only the direction parts it actually implements.

## Changes

- **`specs/architecture.yaml`**: adds three requirements.

  - ARCH-05-005: a connector must not expose a method for a direction it lacks, including a stub that raises, logs or does nothing.
  - ARCH-05-006: the loader refuses an entry point with no direction, and names it.
- **`notes/architecture-hexagonal.md`**: adds a "Connector Directions" section. It defines the three directions (a polled source returns the changes since a bookmark the caller holds), holds the two rules above, says a connector keeps all its directions in one plugin (unlike the driving/driven split), and names which caller uses each direction: a Sentinel polls or receives, an Actuator writes, and a Retriever may read. The note's connector review checklist gains the ARCH-05-005 rule.

`ConnectorPlugin` (`vultron/adapters/connectors/base.py`) requires two methods: `on_inbound_event` (the outside system pushes an event in) and `on_outbound_event` (Vultron pushes an event out). The shadow's VINCE connector does neither. A Sentinel polls it, and it must have no write path (#5963 AC-2). So it cannot satisfy the Protocol without a write method it must not have.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- **Surface symptom:** the example `VinceConnector` (`connectors/example/vince.py`) raises `NotImplementedError` in both methods. It reads as a stub waiting for code.
- **Underlying problem:** the Protocol assumes a two-way, push-driven connector. It has no shape for a read-only source that a caller polls. Even its docstring's example mappings (case created → `create_case`) assume push.
- **Correct, keep:** entry-point discovery under `vultron.connectors` (ARCH-05-003, #5610). Connectors live in adapters, and core never imports them (ARCH-05-001). A connector is any plugin to an outside system, whatever its direction (`CONTEXT.md`).

## Category

Design / architecture.

## Severity

Medium. It blocks #5963, and through it the Epic's finish line.

- `vultron/adapters/connectors/base.py`: both methods are required members of a `runtime_checkable` Protocol.

#5963 either adds an `on_outbound_event` that must refuse every call (a write path in the interface, which AC-2 forbids), or skips the Protocol and so is not discovered as a plugin (AC-3 fails).

Decide the connector shape before #5963. One option: split the Protocol into a rea

Theme: theme:cvd-measurement — readers of the desiderata proposals see that "every vendor aware before any fix is ready" is a weak and sometimes misleading measure, and why move advice leaves it out.

## Summary

`process_model_desiderata.md` proposes `V_i ≺ F_j` for every vendor i whose report reaches Valid and every vendor j. The planning interview for #6450 (2026-11-16) found three objections and dropped it from move advice (ADR-0200). Record the objections on the page, so that no reader takes it as settled.

Governing specs: none; the page is a non-normative research proposal. ADR-0182, ADR-0200.

## Evidence or Context

- It is a proxy for an interest the per-vendor desiderata already measure: the trailing vendor's own `F_i ≺ P` and `D_i ≺ P`. A fix that is ready but not released costs the trailing vendor nothing in itself.
- It is backwards in supply-chain cases: a downstream vendor often cannot fix until the upstream fix exists, and often learns of the vul because of it.
- Its chance baseline is 393/400, so it holds almost always by chance, and its skill coefficient tells little.

## Fix or Approach

Add the three objections under the desideratum in § "Multi-party desiderata", mark it as contested, and link the supply-chain idea that could replace it. Keep its row in the baseline table, because the research may still use it. Follow SG-38 and Simplified Technical English.

## Summary

Plans the move-advice framing from the #6450 planning interviews (2026-11-13 and 2026-11-16). A CVD case is a cooperative game: the participants play against the game and win or lose together. So the case shadow neither picks one best move nor reduces a case to one score. Each open move gets an outcome shift for each vendor against the chance value, and falls in a band set only by its own shifts: **harm-free**, **trade-off** or **unhelpful**. Inside a band there is no order, only a shade by dominance layer and a **top** icon for layer 1. ADR-0200 (proposed) records this, and #6450's spike tests it. No issue closes here: #6450 stays open as the spike that validates ADR-0200.

## Changes

- **`docs/adr/0200-…-not-by-one-case-score.md`** (new, proposed):
  - In this version, a scope is one vendor in the case, notified or not, holding the desiderata about that vendor. There is no case-wide scope. `V_i ≺ F_j` is left out of move advice (#6502).
  - The chance value of each desideratum is the mean over every allowed next step in its smallest model (ADR-0182 rule 2), including events no participant chooses.
  - Each shift has an end part and an embargo part, weighted `1 − f_d`. Bands and dominance both compare every vendor's end parts first; the embargo parts decide only when every end part is zero (bands) or equal (dominance). So a fix beats an embargo extension, and a move that dominates a harm-free move is harm-free. The sign test is strict.
  - Move X dominates move Y when its end parts do at least as well in every scope and better in one, or, with all end parts equal, when its embargo parts do.
  - Bands come from each move's own shifts. Inside a band, the shade is by layer (layer 1 darkest) and top moves get an icon. A trade-off that a harm-free move dominates is not top. The unhelpful band has no shade and no mark. "Leading among yours" marks the coordinator's undominated harm-free or trade-off moves.
  - The limits are stated: rarity weights measure dif
