Theme: theme:cvd-measurement — the desiderata baselines' exact chance model answers "what is this case's expected outcome from here", which is the number every next move is scored against.

## Summary

`vultron/measure/baselines/walk.py` solves the indifference walk exactly, but `_absorption` returns only the start state's expected values. The case shadow scores each next move by how far it changes the case's expected outcome from where the case stands (ADR-0190 rule 5, revision 3). So the walk must solve from any joint state of the multi-vendor model in `vultron/measure/baselines/joint.py`, giving a value per vendor.

Governing specs: CEH-05, CEH-05-006

## Evidence or Context

Planning for #5966 found that ranking a move by the score of the history with that move added credits almost nothing. Most desiderata are orderings that one move does not settle: notifying a vendor makes "vendor aware before public aware" more likely without deciding it. The change in expected outcome does credit it. Each vendor keeps its own value, because CEH-05-006 never combines vendors into one sequence. How the per-vendor values become one case number is #5966's spike.

## Fix or Approach

Let the solver take a start node, or return the value table it already builds for every node, and look up any joint state in it. Expose a move's expected change as the per-vendor difference between a state's values and the values of its successor by that step.

## Summary

Per-test store disposal no longer runs while a sender-sequence hold timer is still running. A timer that a test leaves running is now stopped on its own loop at that test's teardown, the stores are then disposed, and the test fails with `HoldTimerLeakedError`, where before it segfaulted a later test's worker. The demo `client` fixture now also stops the outbox monitor on its loop and finishes the startup replay and position statements, which could race disposal the same way (#6618).

Issues: closed 2, opened 1 (#6618, opened:excursion, found in review)
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Root cause

The segfault in run 42673245636 came from PR #6123's head `9abe694`, which did not yet contain #6124. On that tree the module-scoped demo `client` fixture held the production lifespan open for a whole module, and its hold timer ran the whole time. Every quarter of the hold wait the timer read the actor stores from the app's loop thread. Meanwhile `_dispose_actor_stores_between_tests` closed those SQLite connections after each test. A tick that landed inside a disposal segfaulted the worker. #6124 now stops the timer in that fixture, but nothing pinned that fix and nothing would catch the next leak.

I checked every other place the suite starts the production lifespan: `app_v2`, `main.app`, and `_make_lifespan(configure_globals=True)`. Each one is a function-scoped or in-test `with TestClient(...)`. Its shutdown awaits `finish_sender_sequence_hold_timer` before the autouse disposal runs. The module-scoped demo `client` fixture (`test/demo/conftest.py`) stopped the production `OutboxMonitor` with `monitor.stop()` from the main thread. That is `task.cancel()` off the task's own loop: not thread-safe, and not waited for. The fixture also never waited for the startup inbox replay or the ledger position statements. Any of them could still be reading an actor store when the root conftest's `_dispose_actor_stores_between_tests` closed it after the first test. This is the same disposal-under-read segfault #6148 fixed for the sender-sequence hold timer.

## Evidence or Context

Found by PR #6617's review (the fix PR for #6148). No CI failure attributed to it yet: the window is the startup work and any in-flight monitor drain overlapping the first demo test's teardown.

## Fix or Approach

- Stop the monitor on the portal loop and wait for its task to end.
- Expose the startup replay and the position statements on `app.state`, as the hold timer and monitor already are, and finish them through the portal.
- A demo test asserts no lifespan background coroutine is still running on the portal loop.

Fixed in PR #6617.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The demo client stops the outbox monitor on its own loop and waits for its task.
- [ ] AC-2: The demo client finishes the startup replay and the position statements before any test runs.
- [ ] AC-3: A test fails if any lifespan background task is still running when a demo test runs.

Governing specs: none — test-harness fix, no protocol behavior change

## Summary

Pins `pytest` below 9.2. Under pytest 9.2, pytest-xdist 3.8.0's `--dist loadgroup` ignores every `xdist_group` mark, so the ordered pairs in `test/test_process_global_isolation.py` split across workers. Adds a check that fails the next time a pytest or xdist bump breaks the grouping.

Issues: closed 1, opened 1 (#6228 lifts the pin once a pytest-xdist release fixes it upstream)
Questions: asked 1, filed 0

## Motivation

pytest 9.2 stores a node id in a structured `_id`, and `Node.nodeid` reads it. pytest-xdist 3.8.0 builds `loadgroup` by writing `item._nodeid = "<id>@<group>"` (`xdist/remote.py`), and pytest 9.2 now drops that write. As a result `loadgroup` acts like plain `load` (pytest #15303, pytest-xdist #1386). The upstream fix (#1388) is merged but not released. It also has an open follow-up bug (#1399, fixed by open PR #1402): a hook that drops tests after xdist's own collection hook causes an `INTERNALERROR`. This repo does that: `-m 'not integration'` deselects the tests `test/demo/conftest.py` marks, and on xdist master that crashes the run. So installing xdist from master is not a fix either. CI stayed green by chance: on a large collection xdist hands each worker a block of tests that sit next to each other.

## Changes

- **`pyproject.toml`**: `pytest>=9.1.1,<9.2`, with a comment that names the upstream issues and the condition for lifting the pin.
- **`uv.lock`**: re-locked; pytest 9.2.0 → 9.1.1.
- **`test/test_xdist_loadgroup.py`** (new): runs a real `-n 4` session with this repo's `addopts`. The session has grouped and ungrouped tests, plus a conftest whose `trylast` hook drops a test. The test asserts that the grouped tests ran once each, in collection order, on one worker. It is red on pytest 9.2 (order and worker split) and on xdist master (#1399 `INTERNALERROR`), and green under the pin.
- **`notes/testing-pitfalls.md`** § "Order-Dependent Tests Need an `xdist_group`": adds the rule that the grouping depends on the pi

Theme: theme:test-and-ci — makes the ordered same-worker test pairs that guard process-wide state run as designed again, so their green result means something.

## Summary

Since #6165 bumped pytest from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0 (pytest-xdist 3.8.0), `--dist loadgroup` no longer keeps a module's `xdist_group` tests on one worker in order. `test/test_process_global_isolation.py` relies on that: each `test_2_*` asserts its `test_1_*` writer ran first in the same process, and now fails.

## Evidence or Context

On clean `origin/main` at `2cc89fedb`:

- `uv run pytest test/test_process_global_isolation.py -n 4 -q` fails
  `TestBlackboardIsClearedBetweenTests::test_2_next_test_starts_without_the_stale_key` and
  `TestThirdPartyLogSuppressionIsUndoneBetweenTests::test_2_next_tests_restore_keeps_the_level_it_set`
  with "the 'blackboard' writer test did not run before this one in this process".
- `UV_NO_SYNC=1 uv run --with pytest==9.1.1 pytest test/test_process_global_isolation.py -n 4 -q` passes.
- `-n 0` passes.

Found by the local targeted gate of #6116, whose branch touches neither that file nor any pytest config. #6165's CI passed, so CI's partitioning may hide it; any local `-n` run that selects the module fails. Every module that relies on an `xdist_group` mark for same-worker, in-order pairs is at risk.

## Fix or Approach

Find what pytest 9.2 changed for `xdist_group` / `loadgroup` (the anyio bump in #6165 names a `CallSpec` rename), then fix the grouping (a pytest-xdist upgrade, a pin, or a different mark), rather than weakening the paired tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `uv run pytest test/test_process_global_isolation.py -n 4 -q` passes on the pinned pytest.
- [ ] AC-2: a check fails when an `xdist_group` module's tests are split across workers, so a later pytest or xdist bump cannot silently break the grouping again.

Governing specs: TB-11-002

## Summary

24 modules under `test/demo/` each defined the same autouse fixture: call `reset_demo_failures()`, yield, call it again. The pre-push review of the `coordinated_story` / `vendor_story` package split (#5592, part 1) found the copies when that split added a shared fixture for its new test directories.

## Evidence or Context

`vultron.demo.utils._demo_failures` is process-global, and a gate skips its body once anything is recorded, so every demo test module that observes gates needs a reset around each test. Each module wrote its own (`_fresh_failures`, `_clean_failures`, `clear_failures`, `_reset_failures`, `_clean_accumulator`, `_clean_failure_accumulator`). CS-22-001 asks for one copy.

## Fix or Approach

Define `fresh_demo_failures` once in `test/demo/conftest.py`, not autouse, and opt each module in with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.usefixtures("fresh_demo_failures")`. It stays opt-in rather than autouse for the directory: a test that asserts on failures a module-scoped run recorded must not have them wiped at its own setup. Fixtures that do more than the reset (`test_scenario_harness.py`'s `_devlogs`, the per-scenario `marks` fixtures) keep their own reset.

Governing specs: CS-22-001

- [ ] AC-2: Every module that had one opts in to `fresh_demo_failures`, and the demo integration suite passes.

A received `type` list that names `Page`, `Image`, `Audio` or `Video` together with `Document` now resolves to the subtype. Before this change it was refused as ambiguous. The resolver now reads the AS2 subtype relation where the Python class hierarchy cannot express it.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Root cause

`_resolve_type_term` in `vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/registry.py` picked the known class that is an `issubclass` of every other known class in the list. The core attached-file class `AttachedDocument` owns `Document` (CSAF-01-001, ARCH-25-003). `as_Page` is a wire class, and `AttachedImage`, `AttachedAudio` and `AttachedVideo` are its siblings, not its subclasses. So no class in `["Page", "Document"]` passed the check. This was already true before #6599: the old `as_Page` extended the wire `as_Document`, while `Document` resolved to the core class.

Making the classes inherit was not a clean option. `as_Page` cannot extend a core class. Also, if `AttachedImage` became a subclass of `AttachedDocument`, `isinstance(attachment, AttachedDocument)` in `vultron/wire/csaf/reader.py` would start treating images as CSAF document candidates.

## Changes

- **`vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/registry.py`**: adds `AS2_SUPERTYPES`, which maps wire `type` value to AS2 supertype for the pairs the class hierarchy cannot relate (`Page`, `Image`, `Audio`, `Video` → `Document`). Adds `is_as2_subtype()`, which counts both a subclass and a declared supertype, transitively and through ancestors. The resolver uses it in place of `issubclass`. Supertypes are looked up in `WIRE_TYPE_MAP` only, so the lookup stays wire-only (VM-06-008). No registry key or owner changes, so `_wire_type_alias` stays gone and the collision ratchet is untouched.
- **`test/wire/as2/test_type_list.py`**: adds `TestAs2SubtypeOutsideTheClassHierarchy`:
  - each Document subtype resolves in both orders;

## Summary

AS2 makes `Page`, `Article`, `Image`, `Audio` and `Video` kinds of `Document`. Vultron refuses a received type list that names one of them with `Document`, such as `["Page", "Document"]`, as an unknown type.

## Evidence or Context

- The core attached-file classes own the AS2 type `Document` (ARCH-25-003, ADR-0099, CSAF-01-001). `AttachedImage`, `AttachedAudio` and `AttachedVideo` are not subclasses of `AttachedDocument`. The wire classes `as_Page` and `as_Article` are not related to `AttachedDocument`.
- `_resolve_type_term` in `vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/registry.py` narrows a received type list to the known class that is a subclass of every other class the list names (ADR-0196). For these lists no class qualifies, so it raises `AmbiguousWireTypeError` and the activity is refused as an unknown type.
- To reproduce on `origin/main`: `resolve_wire_type(["Page", "Document"])` raises. The lists `["Article", "Document"]` and `["Image", "Document"]` raise too.
- The bug is already on `main`. The pre-push review of #4119 found it. That PR makes `as_Page` and `as_Article` extend `as_Object` directly, because `as_Document` is now an alias of the core class. It does not change the outcome.

## Fix or Approach

Make the type-list narrowing see the AS2 subtype relation for the file and document types. Two possible ways:

- record each class's AS2 supertype, as `_as2_core_supertype` already does for an extension type;
- make the core file classes and `as_Page`/`as_Article` share a `Document` kind that the narrowing reads.

Keep one owner for each type value (VM-01-013).

## Summary

PR #6437 (#6412) adds HP-08-015 for `Add(ParticipantStatus)` only. The rule: when the activity `context` and the carried status `context` name different cases, refuse before the commit with a reason that names both. That PR's builder searched for a general rule and found none. HP-08-007 and HP-08-013 compare an object's `context` with the target case, never with the activity's own `context`. `resolve_case_context_id` routes by the activity's `context` and never compares it with the object's. MV-10 accepts a case URI in `target`, `context`, `origin` and `object` without relating them. Nothing in the extractor, the parse edge or the inbox compares the two. The maintainer asked for the rule to apply to every message type.

## Evidence or Context

- The single-type instance: `ActivityContextMatchesObjectNode` (`vultron/core/behaviors/case/nodes/activity_context.py`) and HP-08-015 in `specs/handler-protocol.yaml`, once PR #6437 merges.

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — an inline object the parser cannot read as its slot's class is refused, never kept as an empty Link.

## Summary

In an `ActivityStreamRef[X]` slot (`X | as_Link | NonEmptyString | None`, `vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/links.py`), an inline dict without `type` that fails validation as `X` falls through the union to `as_Link`. Every `as_Link` field is optional, `href` included, so the activity parses and the object's content is lost without a trace.

## Evidence or Context

Reproduced on a stub Invite while building #5479:

- An untyped `caseStatus` with no `published` inside a `VulnerabilityCaseStub` target parses, with `target.case_status` an `as_Link` and its `emState` gone.
- The same status with a `type` is refused (CLP-15-008).
- The same untyped status with a `published` parses as a `CaseStatus`.

The fault is general to every Ref slot, not specific to stubs. A fix decides how the parser reads every untyped inline object in a link-or-object slot (MV-04-003, MV-04-004), so it was left out of #5479 with the maintainer's approval (2026-11-03).

## Fix or Approach

Refuse an untyped inline dict that fails the slot's object class instead of letting it validate as a Link. Two candidate seams: require `href` on a Link that arrives as a dict, or decide the member in the parser's slot partition (`vultron/wire/as2/unknown_keys.py`), which already knows the slot's candidate classes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: an untyped inline dict that fails the slot's object class is refused at parse, not read as a Link.
- [ ] AC-2: tests pin the stub `caseStatus` case and one other Ref slot.
- [ ] AC-3: a genuine Link (with `href`) still parses.

Governing specs: MV-04-003, MV-04-004, CLP-15-008, CM-17-013

## Summary

The scenario registry treats a scenario as exactly one file,

story helpers did in #5592. Let the registry accept a `<name_>_demo/` package
as well as a `<name_>_demo.py` module, then split `rcvcv_demo` into one.

The maintainer asked for this as a follow-up to #5592 (decided 2026-11-04).
#5592 itself kept `rcvcv_demo.py` as the one scenario module and moved the
fragments only it tells into a sibling, `vultron/demo/scenario/rcvcv_fragments.py`.
That holds every module under 500 lines and leaves DEMOCI-11-003 untouched.

## Evidence or Context

What assumes one file per scenario today:

- **Specs (ADR-0098).** DEMOCI-11-001's verification compares the registered
  set with the `*_demo.py` modules on disk. DEMOCI-11-002 enumerates the
  package with `pkgutil`. DEMOCI-11-003 (MUST) derives the demo script path as
  `vultron/demo/scenario/<name_>_demo.py`. DEMOMA-19-003 (MUST) names

Theme: theme:full-cvd-scenario-coverage — a demo gate that waits for the pending case inbox to drain reads that record, so it can fail.

## Summary

`wait_for_pending_inbox_quiescent` in `vultron/demo/helpers/polling.py` reports the
pending case inbox drained whatever it holds. It reads
`client.dl_path(VultronPendingCaseInbox.build_id(case_id))` with the key unquoted,
and its `except Exception: return True` turns the failed read into "quiescent".

## Evidence or Context

- `VultronPendingCaseInbox.build_id` stores the row under
  `pending-case-inbox/<percent-quoted case id>`, which holds `%3A` (and `%2F` for a URL
  case id).
- A server decodes the request path once, so the unquoted key reaches the store as
  `pending-case-inbox/<case id>` (or, for a URL case id, as a many-segment key). Neither
  names the stored row.
- For a URN case id the two-segment route used to serve the case itself (no
  `activity_ids`, so the gate passed). Since PR #5718 that route asserts the type
  segment and answers 404, which the `except` also reads as quiescent. The outcome is
  the same: the gate never reads the pending inbox.
- `test_wait_for_pending_inbox_quiescent_exception_treated_as_quiescent` (in
  `test/demo_unit/test_polling_helpers.py`) pins the swallow with a `MagicMock` client,
  so no test reaches the real route.
- No demo calls the helper today; it is exported from `vultron.demo.helpers`. Found
  while reviewing PR #5718. `test_rv_demo.py` had the same unquoted-key defect, fixed
  there.

## Fix or Approach

1. Quote the key for the server's one decode, as `seeding._dl_key` does.
2. Treat only a 404 (row absent) as drained; let any other error propagate.
3. Replace the `MagicMock` exception test with tests that read a real store through the
   datalayer router.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a pending inbox holding activity ids, the gate times out (raises) against a
      real datalayer router instead of passing.
- [ ] With the pending inbox absent or empty, the gate

## Summary

Three helpers in `vultron/demo/helpers/coordinated_story.py` are

`vultron-demo rccv-handoff` and `vultron-demo rvcv-handoff` accept
`--case-actor-id`, and `run_rccv_handoff_demo` / `run_rvcv_handoff_demo`
accept the matching `case_actor_id` parameter. Neither function reads it.
Both read the CaseActor off the case's participant index instead
(`find_case_actor_participant_id`), which is the behaviour their tests assert,
so the option changes nothing a run does.

## Evidence or Context

- `vultron/demo/scenario/rccv_handoff_demo.py` — `run_rccv_handoff_demo`

  not amend an obligation.

  in every scenario, so there is nothing left for the override to select.

Drop the `--case-actor-id` option from both handoff scenarios
(`case_actor_role()` without `has_id`), drop the unused parameter from both
`run_*_demo` functions and both `main()` signatures, and amend `DEMOMA-14-008`
to stop requiring the option.

- [ ] AC-1: Neither handoff scenario declares a `case-actor` role with
      `has_id=True`, and neither `run_*_demo` nor `main()` takes a

issues.body:
Theme: theme:full-cvd-scenario-coverage — write branching demo scenarios as a shared prefix plus one continuation per choice.

## Problem

The scenario tree is declared on `@scenario` as an interim step. The target (maintainer direction, 2026-10-15) is **branches as composition**: a branching story is written once, as shared steps up to a named branch point, then one continuation per choice. Each registered scenario is "prefix plus choice." Ancestry then falls out of the code, and a shared prefix cannot diverge because there is only one copy.

Today sibling scenarios are full copies. For example, `fcv_demo.py` (666 lines) and `fcv_reject_demo.py` (790 lines) differ on only about 560 lines. That breaks DEMOMA-17-001 (Extract Before Reuse).

## Decisions needed (interactive; do not build without them)

1. The composition model: what a "step," a "branch point," and a "continuation" are in code, and how they fit `scenario_harness`, `ActorSession` (DEMOMA-26), and the self-registering `@scenario` decorator.
2. How a composed scenario is registered and named (letter-grammar names as a reviewed convention, DEMOCI-11-015; names are not generated from the path), and how the interim `@scenario` path declarations are retired.
3. How per-scenario spec groups (DEMOMA-09 … DEMOMA-27) and the invariant harness's required event types (DEMOMA-16) follow a composed scenario.
4. The migration order by family, for example `fcv` / `fcv-reject`, then `fvcv-*`, then `fccv-*`, then the root split between vendor-first and coordinator-first paths, and whether each family is one PR.

Planning this Idea produces one Task per family, each blocked by this Idea.
issues.title: Write branching demo scenarios as composition: one shared prefix, one continuation per choice

agent_prs.body:
- Closes #4970

## Summary

Fixes the reporter refusing its CASE_MANAGER's full-case Invite in the exchange demos built on `setup_initialized_case`. Seeding a second case that held the same report moved the reporter's report-to-case link onto that case and kept the first case's CASE_MANAGER on it. The anchored sender check then refused the second case's real CASE_MANAGER (HP-01-006). `link_report_case_links` now binds only a pending link.

Issues: closed 1, opened 2 (#5438 separate-defect, #5444 separate-defect)

## Motivation

In these demos the CaseActor opens a case when the vendor receives the report, and the reporter binds its link to that case, trusting the CaseActor. The vendor then mints a second case holding the same report through `create-case`. When the reporter's copy of the second case was seeded, `link_report_case_links` moved the bound link onto it, CaseActor and all. Two things broke (CBT-02-003): the second case got a CASE_MANAGER it never had, and the first case lost its trust anchor. issues.body:
## Problem

Scenario tests rebuild a whole multi-actor case from nothing for every test.

For example, `test_the_managers_withdrawal_declines_the_revision_it_agreed_to` in `test/core/use_cases/received/test_embargo_proposal_answer_copy.py` takes these steps:

1. It builds a fresh `LedgerNetwork`.
2. A participant proposes a revision.
3. The CASE_MANAGER accepts it.
4. The CASE_MANAGER withdraws.

Only the last step is under test. In a profiled run the test ran its behavior tree 31 times. Afterwards, the autouse rebuild check (`_every_network_rebuilds_from_its_ledger`) replays the whole ledger again.

The slowest tests in that file take 3–6 seconds each, over the TB-12-003 budget of 5 seconds. Sibling tests in the same file rebuild the same first steps.

This is the scenario tree's shared-prefix idea, applied to tests. Many tests share the same steps up to a branch point and differ only in the act after it.

## Idea

Name the case states that many tests start from, for example "participant proposed a revision" or "CASE_MANAGER has agreed". Build each one once per module or session, and give every test its own copy.

Each test still starts from fresh state of its own (TB-06-001, TB-06-003). It just doesn't replay the steps to get there.

## Decisions needed

1. **The copy mechanism.** `SqliteDataLayer.clone_for_actor` exists, and SQLite can copy a whole in-memory database (`sqlite3.Connection.backup`). Neither has been checked for copying a full store, including the actor locks, clock patching, and the `NETWORKS` registry the rebuild check reads.
2. **How the rebuild check treats a copied network.** It could replay from the copy's seed, or from the original's. It could also skip starting points that were already checked once.

issues.body:
## Summary

When several in-process nodes share one process (the demo tests' isolated apps, and the scenario recorder `uv run export-demo-recordings`), `actor_hosts.hosted_actor_ids()` lists the actors of **every** node, not only the node that asks. In memory mode it returns `get_all_actor_datalayers()`, the process-wide store cache, which ignores the `db_url` each node uses. A node that iterates its hosted actors, such as `GET /actors/` (`get_actors`), then opens an empty store for each foreign actor under its own deployment.

## Evidence

One full recording run of the 11 scenarios (#3901) logs about 1,200 WARNINGs of two kinds:

- `Actor 'http://vendor:7999/api/v2/actors/primary' has cached DataLayers under more than one db_url` (`datalayer_sqlite/__init__.py`, `get_all_actor_datalayers`)
- `Store sqlite:///file:node-http_vendor_7999-primary?... is shared by two distinct actor ids` (`datalayer_sqlite/engine.py`)

`create_isolated_actor_app` also opens a placeholder `.../actors/primary` store on every node, which adds to the count.

## Why it matters

The recordings are still correct: `get_actors` reads each actor's record from the store, and a foreign actor's store on this node is empty, so it is not listed. But the noise hides any real warning in a recording run (the recorder defaults to `--log-level ERROR` for that reason), and any future caller of `hosted_actor_ids()` that acts on the list, rather than reading records from it, would act on actors this node does not host. Docker never shows this, because each container has its own process.

## Possible directions

- Let `hosted_actor_ids()` take the node's `db_url` and, in memory mode, return only the actors cached under that URL; pass it from `get_actors`.
- Stop `create_isolated_actor_app` opening a store for an actor that is never created there.

Where: vultron/adapters/driven/actor_hosts.py
issues.title: In process, hosted_actor_ids() lists every node's actors, so each node opens empty stores for foreign actors

issues.body:
## Problem

The 2026-10-15 demo UI planning session settled that the demo scenarios form a **scenario tree** (see the **Demo** section of `CONTEXT.md`):

- The root is a Reporter who has found a vul and must choose whom to tell.
- Every node is a **branch point**: one role facing a decision.
- Every edge is a **choice**: a trigger that role calls.
- A **scenario** is one root-to-**ending** path. Its **recording** is the case ledgers it writes.

Who joins (report to a vendor or a coordinator; invite another vendor or a coordinator) and how a decision goes (validate or invalidate, extend or hand off, revise or terminate) are both just branch points.

Today the tree is implicit. It shows only in scenario names (`fv`, `fvv`, `fvcv-handoff`, `fcv-reject`, `rcv-embargo`, …), and sibling scenarios are full copies of each other. For example, `fcv_demo.py` and `fcv_reject_demo.py` share roughly 450 lines.
The interim plan is to declare branches on `@scenario` (ADR-0098); composition comes later (separate Idea).

## Decisions needed (interactive; do not build without them)

1. The declaration shape on `@scenario`: how a scenario names its parent, the branch point (role and decision), and the choice (trigger) it takes.
2. Where the presenter-facing label of a branch point ("As the Vendor, choose…") and of each choice lives.
3. The order of branch points along each existing path. For example, on the vendor path, does the Vendor validate before or after choosing whether to invite a coordinator?
4. How today's scenarios map onto one tree, including the root choice that `fv*` and `fc*` split on, and where `rcv-embargo` / `rcvv-embargo` sit relative to `fcv`.
5. Path-derived scenario names, folding in the Finder→Reporter rename (ADR-0078 retired `CVDRole.FINDER`): whether names become generated from the path, and the renaming plan for sub-commands, spec groups, and CI matrix entries.
6. The tree index artifact's format, which the UI's offline mode and live mode both read.

## Conte

issues.body:
Theme: theme:standards-engagement — the case inputs read from an attached CSAF vulnerability report can be computed once, by the report receiver, and travel to the CASE_MANAGER on the proposal.

## Summary

Allow the report receiver (the future CASE_OWNER) to run the CSAF case-input helper at its own receipt time and send the results on `CaseProposal`, so the CASE_MANAGER applies them instead of computing them again. This is an optional addition to today's model, not a replacement: "one or both", not "pick one and prohibit the other".

## Motivation

Today (#6091, PR #6189), the CASE_MANAGER reads the CSAF document on the Offer that `Create(CaseProposal)` carries in its `inReplyTo`. It applies `vultron.core.services.report_case_inputs.case_inputs_from_claims` at its own receipt time when the proposal creates a new case. The receiver's claims record stays `display-only`.

The proposer and the CASE_MANAGER are two roles of one coordinating function at a report receiver. When the receiver computes the inputs:

- There is one computation, at one time, so the receiver's record matches the case that is created.
- Facts about the proposer travel on the proposal, as ADR-0133 already does for the receiver's case roles.

## Rough Approach

- The report receiver runs `case_inputs_from_claims` at its receipt time.
- `CaseProposal` gains new optional fields: name, summary, the CSAF-derived proposed embargo end, and the initial P/X/A.
- The CASE_MANAGER applies the carried values when they are present. When they are absent, it keeps today's behavior and reads the carried Offer.

Trade-offs:

- Cost: new wire fields and new CP-01 spec entries.
- Cost: CP-01-021 needs an amendment. Today it says the CASE_MANAGER reads the Reporter's proposed embargo terms only from the Offer in the proposal's `inReplyTo`.
- Gain: one computation at one time, with the receiver's record and the case in agreement.
- Gain: consistent with ADR-0133 (facts about the proposer travel on the proposal).

## Summary

Write an ADR for **action rules** across models (see `CONTEXT.md`): rules over CS × RM × EM × PEC patterns, each naming the desiderata it serves, in two kinds compared against each other.

## Evidence or Context

- `CS_ACTION_RULES` (`vultron/core/states/cs_actions.py`, ADR-0060, CSB-17-001) covers CS patterns only; its reasons are tags ("SA", "exit criteria met") that name no desideratum.

## Decision to record

Both kinds, compared, as the demo stories compare authored narrative with "the story as the code tells it":

Builds on ADR-0060 and ADR-0200.

Design gap (specification).

Medium. It blocks the rest of Focus Task #6372.

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — an AS2 reader sees the Case Owner propose putting an embargo in force and the CASE_MANAGER do it, each message true of its sender.

## Summary

ADR-0180 has the Case Owner put a proposed embargo in force by sending the CASE_MANAGER `Add(EmbargoEvent, target=VulnerabilityCase)`, which is ledgered as the Owner's own act. The CASE_MANAGER holds the case's embargo register and makes the change, so the message states something its sender has not done. ADR-0199 (proposed in PR #6460) rules that out: a request for another actor to act is an `Offer` of the act, answered with `Accept` or a refusal notice, and the actor that holds the record makes the act. ADR-0202 (PR #6479) also moves an embargo's status onto the embargo, so activation becomes a status change of the embargo.

## Motivation

- Found while planning #6246: the Owner's early end of an embargo became `Offer(Update(EmbargoEvent))` under ADR-0199, but the Owner's activation, under ADR-0180, still uses the bare-act form.

## Rough Approach

- The Owner sends `Offer(Update(EmbargoEvent{id, status: active}))` (or `Offer(Add(...))`; decide which verb fits once the embargo carries its own status). The CASE_MANAGER refuses, or sends `Accept` and makes the act with `attributedTo` = Owner and `inReplyTo` = the Offer, committed together.

`origin` means where something comes from or leaves, and `target` where it goes (`notes/activitystreams-semantics.md` § "Choosing AS2 Terms"). ## Summary

An admitted act that someone must answer reaches them as the CASE_MANAGER's `Announce(<the act>)`. Two flows still use the older delegated model, where the CASE_MANAGER makes the act a proposer asked for, with `attributedTo` naming the proposer:

Most tree factories still take per-act values as constructor arguments: `with_case_id(node, case_id)`, `create_*_tree(case_id=...)`, nodes built with a case or actor id. #6551, #6552 and #6553 move the inputs of the subtrees that run nested today; this Concern covers every other tree.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

Surface: constructor arguments look harmless when the tree is built per act (BT-25-005). Underlying: a tree whose shape depends on its data cannot be reused as a subtree without rebuilding it, which is what pushed nodes into nested runs. What stays correct: building a tree fresh per act, and factories choosing *which* nodes an act needs.

## Category

Architecture / behavior trees

## Severity

Low: no defect today, and the nested-run ratchet stops the harmful shape.

## Evidence

`vultron/core/behaviors/case_id_scope.py` (`with_case_id`), and the `case_id=` parameters of the factories under `vultron/core/behaviors/case/`, `report/` and `embargo/`.

## Impact if Ignored

The next subtree someone wants to reuse or loop over needs the same migration first, and two styles of input supply coexist.

## Suggested Action

Decide whether BT-25-003 widens from "a subtree under a work-list loop" to every tree, then plan the migration by tree family.

## Summary

This is part A of the user-approved three-way split of #6476 (`work-epic-tasks` run for Epic #5931). It covers #6476's AC-4, plus the half of its architecture test that this sweep makes pass.

**Rescoped 2026-11-16 (maintainer).** The first plan moved each missing-field refusal from `execute()` into its tree factory as the incomplete-activity guard, which widened each factory's parameters to `X | None`. That puts a validation check at the wrong layer. A slot a message's meaning requires is a required field of that message's event, so a missing one fails when the extractor builds the event (ARCH-10-001, ADR-0032), and the message takes the existing unparseable path. The refusals are deleted, not moved. Draft PR #6519 built the first plan and is on hold until it is reworked against these criteria.

## Evidence or Context

The base `VultronEvent` (`vultron/core/models/events/base.py`) declares `object_`, `target`, `context` and `origin` as `X | None`, and only a few subtypes require the slots their message needs (`ValidateReportReceivedEvent._require_offer_and_report_ids` is one). So an event with no `context` reaches a use case, which then refuses it in `execute()`. PR #6519 counted 28 such checks in 16 received use-case modules (`note`, `actor/{invite,offer_case_participant,suggest,full_case_invite}`, `case/{create,lifecycle,engage_defer}`, `case_proposal/answer`, `report/rm_transitions`, `sync/{replay,announce}`, `embargo/{reject,remove,accept,_embargo_event_frame}`). Each one tests for a missing slot: `case_id`, `invite_id`, `embargo_id`, `report_id`, `offer_id`, the note or the ledger entry.

## Fix or Approach

For each of the 28 checks, make the slot required on that message's event subtype (a non-optional field, or a subtype validator that names the missing slot)

## Summary

In a large local `pytest -n auto -m ''` run on a loaded host, a test in
`test/demo/test_rv_demo.py` either hangs the session or crashes the xdist worker
that runs it. The same tests pass when run alone. Under the default signal
timeout method the session never finishes: the gate's wall-clock ceiling ends it
with exit 124. TB-14-002 and TB-14-008 say a timeout trip fails only its own test
and the session goes on, so this run ends with neither a result nor a named
failure.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- **Surface reading:** a slow demo test outgrew its timeout under load, so give
  it a bigger one.
- **Underlying problem:** the tests already have wide timeouts. Every
  `test_rv_demo.py` item resolves to the 120 s integration tier (TB-14-001), and
  `TestRunRvDemo` carries `@pytest.mark.timeout(180)` (checked by a
  `--collect-only` pass over the module). `test_full_workflow_succeeds` takes
  about 9 s alone, so it needs a 20x slowdown to reach 180 s. Either the in-process
  demo deadlocks under load, or a SIGALRM landing inside the demo's
  BackgroundTasks/RLock path leaves the worker stuck so that xdist waits for ever.
  Both of those are a hang, not honest work. Per TB-14-003, the fix is to find
  and remove the hang, not to raise the ceiling again.
- **Keep:** the signal method (#3603), `--max-worker-restart=0` (#4809) and the
  gate's `timeout` wrapper (TB-14-005). Those did their job: the hang was bounded
  and the dead worker failed the run.

Gathered while building #6091 (PR #6189).

Theme: theme:standards-engagement — projects a CSAF document from a case replica.

## Idea

Any Vultron participant MAY produce a CSAF document from its replica: at
publication (a CSAF document can be an output of the ADR-0030 draft step) and during
coordination, as a bridge to parties that do not use Vultron (for example a
CSAF Vulnerability Report for a vendor or a reporting authority).

Agreed constraints:

- A projection SHOULD NOT include information the recipient is not entitled
  to see.
- A projection states the ledger position it shows.
- Its `involvement` timeline is a filtered view of the case ledger.
- Status values are derived from state at the snapshot: `completed` for
  ledger facts; `outstanding`, `deferred`, `discontinued` where state
  supports them; never `attempted` or `planned`.
- The concept mapping page gives the per-concept rules (for example REPORTER
  maps to `discoverer` only when report metadata names that participant as
  finder; X/A map to the SSVC Exploitation value).

Theme: theme:test-and-ci — a test fails only for its own fault, never because an earlier test on the same worker left an in-memory SQLite store open.

## Summary

A test that leaves a `sqlite3.Connection` open makes a later, unrelated test on the same xdist worker fail. The `ResourceWarning: unclosed database` fires when the garbage collector reaches the connection, and `filterwarnings = ["error"]` escalates the unraisable warning into that test's failure. The failing test is whichever one is running when GC happens to run.

## Evidence

- PR #5908 at head `8de760448`, CI run https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/actions/runs/42213460207, job "Tests (pytest) rest", worker `gw3`:
  `FAILED test/demo/test_rvcv_extension_demo.py::TestRvcvExtensionLedgerDump::test_an_actor_the_run_never_seated_is_left_out - pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning: Exception ignored in: <sqlite3.Connection object ...>`, raised from `ResourceWarning: unclosed database`.
- The warning was raised inside `unittest/mock.py` `__init__`, i.e. during a GC pass, not by anything the test itself opens.
- The same file passes locally: `uv run pytest -n 0 -m '' test/demo/test_rvcv_extension_demo.py`, exit 0.
- PR #5908 changes no SQLite or datalayer code.
- `test/AGENTS.md` § "`filterwarnings = [\"error\"]` Does Not Catch All Warnings": such leaks are bugs, fixed by closing resources in fixtures. Many tests build `SqliteDataLayer("sqlite:///:memory:", ...)` and never close it.

## Fix

Find the leaking test or tests in the rest shard. Run that shard with `PYTHONTRACEMALLOC` so the warning names the allocation site, then close the store in that test's fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The allocation site of the leaked connection is named, and its store is closed in the fixture that opens it.
- A rest-shard run with tracemalloc and `-W error::ResourceWarning` reports no unclosed SQLite connection.

Governing specs: TB-06-001, TB-06-004

## Summary

An in-process demo delivery no longer fails when FastAPI's thread-unsafe suppression of pydantic's alias warning loses a race between `TestClient` portal threads. One narrow `filterwarnings` entry ignores exactly that warning, and a regression test pins the race state.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 1, filed 0

## Root cause

- The emitting call is `fastapi/_compat/v2.py` `ModelField.__post_init__` (FastAPI 0.162.2). It builds `TypeAdapter(Annotated[..., Field(**attributes)])` for every analysed parameter, and the plain `Field()` carries the alias FastAPI sets on every parameter (`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` `analyze_param`). pydantic 2.14.3 warns for it in `_generate_schema.py` `_apply_single_annotation`.
- FastAPI hides that warning with `warnings.catch_warnings()` plus `simplefilter("ignore", …)`. On our interpreter `sys.flags.context_aware_warnings == 0`, so `catch_warnings` saves and restores the process-global filter list and is not thread-safe.
- FastAPI 0.162 builds route parameter fields lazily on the first request (`routing.py` `_build_effective_context` → `_populate_api_route_state` → `get_dependant`), and re-analyses every `dependency_overrides` callable on every request, both on the `TestClient` portal thread. The in-process demo runs several apps on several portal threads at once. One thread's exit restores a filter list without the other thread's `ignore`, and `filterwarnings = ["error"]` escalates the warning into a failed delivery. That fits the evidence: rare, once per run, likelier under host contention.
- Changing the `Path(...)` declarations would not help: the warning fires first from the routes' own `{actor_id}` path parameters in FastAPI's lazy route build, which no declaration in this repo reaches. The maintainer chose the narrow filter over context-aware warnings or pre-warming FastAPI's private route state.

Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — VINCE-derived records cannot outlive the tool's process, because the case shadow tool holds a case only in memory and its container has nowhere persistent to write.

## Summary

The case shadow tool holds a case it read, and its translation, in memory only, and leaves none of either on the host after its process exits. Holding a case across requests while the process runs is allowed, so the tool can follow a live case (#6370). A transient working file is allowed only if it is gone when the process exits. Its Compose service mounts no persistent volume.

Governing specs: SHD-01-003, SHD-02-001

## Evidence or Context

This Task first validated `database.db_url` for a shadow server. ADR-0190 made the shadow a standalone tool with no store, and ADR-0189's storage rule was amended to match: no long-lived copy, no volume. VSD-01-001 and VSD-01-002 are retired in favour of SHD-01-003 and SHD-02-001.

SHD-01-003 was reworded in the planning of #6370 (ADR-0190 revision 5, PR https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/pull/6529): it no longer forbids keeping a case past one request, only leaving it on the host after the process exits. A Streamlit cache or session state holding a case is allowed; writing one to disk is not.

## Fix or Approach

Hold each case and translation in memory. Give any transient working file a directory that is removed before the process exits, including on error. Use no Streamlit cache that persists to disk. Declare no volume on the `shadow` service.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: After the tool reads a synthetic case whose content holds a marker string and its process exits, the marker is in no file under the tool's working and temporary directories or `~/.streamlit` (SHD-01-003).
- [ ] AC-2: The same holds when a read fails partway through translation, and when the process is stopped with SIGTERM while a case is held.
- [ ] AC-3: A test loads the Compose file and asserts the `shadow` service declares no volume

## Summary

A `Tests (pytest) rest` worker died with `Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault`
while the per-test teardown fixture disposed the actor SQLite engines, because the
production sender-sequence hold timer was still mid-read through one of them.

The two stacks in the faulthandler dump are:

- **Main thread** (`test/conftest.py:253` `_dispose_actor_stores_between_tests`)
  → `reset_datalayer()` → `dispose_actor_engines()` → SQLAlchemy pool dispose →
  `sqlite3` connection close.
- **A live `anyio` blocking-portal thread** →
  `sender_sequence_holds._end_holds_on_interval` → `end_hosted_expired_holds` →
  `run_actor_work_then_replay` → `_run_serialised` → `outbox_handler` →
  `datalayer_sqlite/datalayer.py:264 read`.

Closing a SQLite connection out from under an in-flight read on another thread
segfaults the interpreter, which kills the xdist worker. A dead worker fails the
whole run (AGENTS.md § Tests), so the run is red with no assertion behind it.

`end_hosted_expired_holds` is documented production-only: it runs in the
single-node production lifespan, whose shutdown calls
`finish_sender_sequence_hold_timer` and **waits** for the timer to stop
(SYNC-21-011). Production is therefore not exposed. The defect is that in the
test suite the timer outlives the app that started it — either a test starts the
production lifespan without awaiting its shutdown, or the shutdown is not ordered
before the next test's store disposal.

## Problem

PR #4118 (issue #4045, the case stub gets its own wire type) removed the last production class that declared `_wire_type_alias`. The case stub used it to share the `VulnerabilityCase` type value. It now owns the `VulnerabilityCaseStub` key.

## Why it matters

Unused code still has a cost. `AGENTS.md` (the vocabulary-registry row) and `notes/vocabulary-registry.md` still tell agents to declare `_wire_type_alias` when a class shares another class's `type` value. 1. Remove the mechanism, its self-test, and the guidance. A class that shares a type value then fails registration (VM-01-004/008).
2. Keep it as a sanctioned escape hatch, and say in the guidance when it may be used.

Recommendation: option 1, unless a planned class needs it.

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — refuses partial inline objects at the parse edge instead of inventing fields.

## Bug

A partial inline object (`{id, type}`) of a type other than an actor or a case stub is accepted at the parse edge. For `CaseParticipant`, the parser also invents the missing fields. MV-10-001 says a sender that does not inline the full object MUST reference it by URI or `Link`, and that a partial inline object of any other recognised wire type is refused (MV-04-003). ARCH-25-009 says a placeholder object MUST NOT be fabricated for an unresolved reference.

## Reproduce

Parse a `Remove` whose `object` is `{"id": <id>, "type": <T>}` and whose `target` is a case URI (with `published` set):

| `type` | Result |
|---|---|
| `CaseParticipant` | parses as `CaseParticipant` with an invented `ParticipantStatus` (fresh `urn:uuid` id, current timestamp, `rm: START`, `cvd_role: [OBSERVER]`, `case_engagement: True`) and `joined: True` |
| `Note` | parses as an empty `as_Note` (`content: ""`) |
| `Event` | parses as an empty `as_Event` |
| `VulnerabilityReport` | parses as an empty `VulnerabilityReport` |
| `EmbargoEvent`, `VulnerabilityCase` | refused, correctly (required fields missing) |

## Impact

- A receiver acts on participant state nobody asserted: a hollow participant reference is read as a joined `OBSERVER` in RM `START`.
- The hollow objects then satisfy type patterns (`Remove({id, type: CaseParticipant})` → `REMOVE_CASE_PARTICIPANT_FROM_CASE`), so an object the receiver does not hold is routed as if it had been sent in full, without the fetch AKM-05-007 provides.

## Expected

Each such partial inline object is refused at the parse edge (MV-04-003, MV-10-001), as `EmbargoEvent` and `VulnerabilityCase` already are. The actor reference of AKM-05-005 and the `VulnerabilityCaseStub` stay accepted. Defaults that create state (the `CaseParticipant` status factory) don't run for a received object.

Governing specs: MV-10-001, MV-04-003, ARCH-25-009, AKM-05-00

## Summary

Pull-request checks no longer check out every branch's history to find their
base. A pull-request checkout is GitHub's merge commit, whose first parent is
the base tip it merged against, so a depth-2 checkout already holds the base.
A hung full-history fetch had been cancelled by the job cap before any test
ran, which turned the `CI gate` red.

Issues: closed 2, opened 0
Questions: asked 2, filed 0

## Changes

- **`.github/actions/fetch-merge-base/action.yml`** (new): when `HEAD` is a
  merge commit, points `origin/<base>` at `HEAD^1` with no fetch; otherwise
  runs the script below. With no base ref (push, schedule, dispatch) it does
  nothing.
- **`.github/scripts/fetch-merge-base.sh`** (new): for the jobs that need the
  real merge base or every branch commit. In a shallow checkout it fetches the
  base one commit deep and deepens both sides (10, 100, 1000) until
  `git merge-base` resolves, unshallowing only as a last resort, each fetch
  under `timeout` and `retry.sh`. In a full clone (a local run) it only updates
  the base, because its `HEAD` may not be on the remote.
- **`guard-tests.yml`, `adr-lifecycle.yml`, `spec-check.yml` (spec-tests),
  `python-app.yml` (the four-part test matrix)**: `fetch-depth: 0` (and
  `fetch-tags`) become `fetch-depth: 2` plus the action.
- **`demo-verdict.yml`** (head-commit checkout) and **`vince-data-check.yml`**
  (`--history` reads each branch commit): `fetch-depth: 0` removed; each step
  takes its merge base from the script.
- **`python-app.yml` (build)**: full history and tags only on a push, where
  `uv build`'s setuptools-scm version is kept.
- **`vultron/metadata/planning/ci_mirror/_registry.py`**: excludes the new
  action from mirror parity; it readies a CI checkout and is not a check.
- **`test/ci/test_fetch_merge_base.py`** (new): fails any pull-request workflow
  with a literal `fetch-depth: 0`; pins depth 2 plus the action in each
  diff-only job and the build job's pus

## Summary

The `Edited ADRs Match Their Epoch` job (`.github/workflows/adr-lifecycle.yml`) checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`. On one run the full-history fetch hung until the job's `timeout-minutes: 5` cancelled it. The `CI gate` reads the cancelled check as red, so a pull request that touches no ADR was blocked by a transient fetch.

## Evidence or Context

- PR #6389, head `079e27a24`, run 43329598746.
- `actions/checkout` started `git -c protocol.version=2 fetch --no-tags --prune --no-recurse-submodules origin +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* ...` at 23:31:44Z and printed nothing more until `##[error]The operation was canceled.` at 23:36:43Z, the 5-minute cap.
- The previous head of the same PR (`cfbcf20`) ran the same job in 28 s. The job's comment records up to 1.6 min over 15 runs.
- The gate's log: `Red check: Edited ADRs Match Their Epoch: cancelled`, `CI gate: red (1 red, 0 still running)`.
- Reproduction: intermittent. Seen once, on run 43329598746. Re-running the job is the reproduction check.

## Fix or Approach

The check needs only the merge base of `origin/<base>` and `HEAD` and the `docs/adr/` diff between them, not every branch's history. Either:

- fetch only what it needs (the base branch and the PR head, deep enough for `git merge-base`), so the fetch is small; or
- cap the fetch with a step-level timeout and retry it once, so a hung fetch is retried within the job cap instead of cancelling the job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The job no longer fetches every branch's full history; its checkout fetches only the refs `git merge-base` and the ADR diff need, or a hung fetch is retried within the job cap.
- [ ] AC-2: A test under `test/ci/` or `test/metadata/` pins the chosen fetch shape (or the retry), so a change back to an unbounded fetch fails it.

Where: `.github/workflows/adr-lifecycle.yml`

Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — the shadow's handling of sensitive case data can be tried on a test VINCE case treated as if it were sensitive, so a leak shows up before any live case is read.

## Summary

A sanitizer reads one test-instance VINCE case and writes a synthetic case of the same shape: same status, participants and roles, posts and their order, vendor statuses, and timestamp order. Every free-text value, name, contact, organization and id is replaced. Its test treats the source case as sensitive and proves that no source content reaches the output or the logs.

Governing specs: VSD-02-005, VSD-02-006, VSD-02-007, VSD-02-008, VSD-01-003, TB-05-002

## Evidence or Context

The data-handling decision for VINCE-derived data (#5956) clears an unsanitized test-instance case for the repository one case id at a time, through a maintainer. The maintainer also asked for a safe place to try case sanitization: a test instance with no sensitive data, whose data is still treated as sensitive so a leak through sanitization is caught. Sanitizer output counts as synthetic, so it is committed without clearance (#5956).

The connector's fixture directory and the check that guards it are #5961. Test-instance access is #5957.

## Fix or Approach

Map each field of a VINCE API case response (from the API docs linked on #5957) to one of three classes: structural and kept (status values, enumerated vendor statuses, counts, ordering), replaced (free text becomes lorem ipsum; names, emails and organizations become generated fakes; every id becomes a synthetic id, consistent across the case), or shifted (all timestamps move by one offset, so their order and spacing stay). A field the map does not classify is refused, so a new API field fails closed instead of passing through. The output carries the synthetic marker #5961 defines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Given a test-instance VINCE case, the sanitizer writes a case with the same status, the same number of part

Theme: theme:test-and-ci — a process-global registry that only grows, so a seeded id source collides and a long-running container leaks.

## Summary

`py_trees.blackboard.Blackboard.clients` is process-global and nothing ever calls
`Client.unregister()`. Three clients are registered per inbox delivery and never
released:

- `vultron/core/behaviors/bridge.py:331` — one `Client` per `setup_tree`
- `vultron/core/behaviors/inbox/_process_payload.py:91` — `InboxOrchestrator-setup`
- `vultron/core/behaviors/inbox/_process_payload.py:135` — `InboxOrchestrator-result`

`py_trees` offers `Client.unregister(clear=True)` and has no `__del__` cleanup, so
the registry grows monotonically for the life of the process.

Two consequences, of very different weight:

1. **Slow growth in a server.** An actor container's registry gains three entries
   per delivery. Prototype-proportionate: unbounded but small, and no correctness
   effect while ids are random.
2. **An id collision when `uuid4` is seeded.** The demo recorder seeds `uuid4`
   through `deterministic_run`, so a second run in one process redraws the first
   run's client ids and `Client.__init__` raises "this unique identifier has
   already been registered". `vultron/demo/determinism.py`'s `reset_blackboard()`
   works around this by clearing the whole blackboard between runs (#5532), which
   mops up at the recorder's level rather than at the source.

## Why this is separate from #5572

#5572 covers the autouse test fixture in `test/conftest.py`, which clears
`Blackboard.storage` but not the client registry. That is the test-isolation half
of the same omission. This issue is the half inside `vultron/core/behaviors/`: the
code that creates the clients never releases them, in tests and in a server alike.
Fixing this one would make both workarounds unnecessary.

## Fix or approach

Release each client where it is created — unregister it in `execute_with_setup`'s
cleanup and around the two `_process_payload` clients — or hold

Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — no real VINCE case can reach a commit, because every committed VINCE fixture is synthetic and a check refuses anything else.

## Summary

Test fixtures for the VINCE connector are synthetic, produced by a committed generator, and a pre-commit and CI check refuses VINCE API data committed anywhere else or without the synthetic marker.

## Evidence or Context

Recording real API responses is the easy way to get fixtures. One recorded response puts an embargoed case in git history, where removal needs a history rewrite.

## Fix or Approach

The data-handling decision (ADR-0189, #5956) rules that test-instance data is not committable as is. A recorded test-instance response enters the repository only when a maintainer has cleared its VINCE case id on a committed cleared-case list, each entry linking the maintainer's clearance comment. Sanitized output from #6348 counts as synthetic and needs no clearance. A Coding Agent may ask for a clearance and never adds an entry (VSD-02-004).

A generator that writes synthetic VINCE API responses with a `"synthetic": true` marker (or equivalent) into one fixture directory. A check fails on a file that looks like a VINCE API response (by its top-level keys) outside that directory or without the marker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The generator writes the connector's fixtures, each carrying the synthetic marker, into one fixture directory.
- [ ] AC-2: The check fails on a VINCE-shaped JSON file outside the fixture directory, and on one inside it without the marker.
- [ ] AC-3: The check runs in pre-commit and CI, and fails on an empty target set.
- [ ] AC-4: A VINCE-shaped file whose case id is on the cleared-case list passes without the marker; the check refuses an entry with no case id or no clearance link.
- [ ] AC-5: A file carrying the marker passes only when the generator or the sanitizer (#6348) wrote it.

issues.body:
Theme: theme:test-and-ci — makes in-process demo tests give each actor its own config so they catch what Docker catches.

## Summary

Every in-process demo node (the shared `TestClient` app, and every `IsolatedActorApp` in `test/demo/conftest.py`) reads one process-global `get_config()`. So a CaseActor that reads its *own* configuration for a fact that belongs to another actor gets the right answer in process, because "its own" configuration is everyone's. Only the Docker demos give each container its own configuration and expose the bug.

## Evidence

#1876 / PR #4539: the CaseActor seated the report receiver using its own `default_case_roles` (CP-09-007 as it then read). Every in-process test passed, including `TestRunTwoActorDemo::test_full_workflow_succeeds`. In Docker with the dedicated case-actor container, the four vendor-receiver scenarios failed with `CVDRole.VENDOR required for VF state`. Fixed by ADR-0133 (roles ride on the proposal).

This is a second witness for the ISSUE-2655 learning (`plan/incoming/learnings/20260930-2655-…`). That learning found the same class from the payload-completeness side: in-process seeding hides defects that only the Docker topology exposes.

## Why it matters

Any remaining read of `get_config()` or of the local store, on a CASE_MANAGER path, for a fact about a *different* actor is a defect of the same shape. The suite cannot find it, and Docker CI can find it only for the scenarios and configurations it happens to run.

## Possible directions (to plan, not decided)

- A ratchet listing the `get_config()` reads reachable from received-side CASE_MANAGER trees, each annotated as the executing actor's own setting.
- A multi-node in-process topology with distinct per-node configuration (needs `get_config` to be resolvable per app, not per process).

Where: test/demo/conftest.py

ADR-0191's port does not care where a case ledger comes from. A Vultron CASE_MANAGER holds the complete ledger of its case (ADR-0174). Theme: theme:test-and-ci — decides whether in-memory SQLite stores isolate per instance or fail on reuse.

## Scope (narrowed)

Option 1 below (documenting the trap) moved to #5366. This Concern now tracks only the open design question:

- Should in-memory stores be isolated per instance by default (option 2), or should constructing a second in-memory store for an `actor_id` that already has a live engine fail or warn loudly (option 3)?
- Deciding needs an audit first: which tests and harnesses rely on two in-memory stores for one `actor_id` sharing an engine (`get_actor_engine` caches by resolved store URL in `vultron/adapters/driven/datalayer_sqlite/engine.py`).

---

## Summary

Two `SqliteDataLayer("sqlite:///:memory:", actor_id=...)` instances constructed with the same `actor_id` in one process **share state**. A "fresh" store sees the previous one's rows — outbox entries, cases, activities. Nothing raises; the reads simply return another scenario's data.

`test/adapters/driven/trigger_activity_adapter/conftest.py` already works around it (`clear_all()` on setup teardown), but the workaround is undocumented and unenforced, so a test or script that omits it gets silent contamination rather than an error.

## Why this is worth tracking

It produced **two wrong conclusions by two independent agents** inside a single session on #3428:

1. A verification script reported that a declining admission policy emitted `Accept`+`Create` — the outbox rows were leaked from the previous scenario. The real behaviour was correct. I nearly "fixed" a non-bug.
2. An adversarial review agent hit the same trap and had to be explicitly warned about it in its instructions before its measurements were trustworthy.

The failure mode is the worst kind: results that look plausible, are internally consistent, and are wrong. An agent writing a throwaway harness to check protocol behaviour has no reason to suspect the store, and the leaked rows are exactly the type the scenario under test wou

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — a receiver refuses any object that arrives without its time, instead of carrying the gap inward.

## Summary

Make `published` required on every object a receiver accepts, refused at message validation, as CLP-15-006 already does for activities. Today ADR-0103 carries a missing object time as `None` and refuses it only where a decision reads the value (a case with no `genesisHash` and no `published`, an embargo with no `endTime`, a replicated ledger entry, and, per #5479, a `CaseStatus`).

## Motivation

The maintainer, deciding #5300 item 1 on 2026-10-29: requiring `published` on everything received is good practice. ADR-0103's per-decision rule means each new reader of an object's time must first check whether its object type is one of the refused ones, and an absent time travels into core as a `None` that core code must guard (ADR-0032 aims to remove such guards). A conformant sender stamps every object it authors, since locally authored objects keep the `now_utc` default, so the stricter rule refuses only malformed input.

## Rough Approach

- Write an ADR that supersedes the "carry the absent time" part of ADR-0103: a received object with no `published` is malformed. ADR-0103's other ruling stays: a received time is carried as sent, never replaced by the receiver's clock.
- Check what this refuses that is valid today: objects a peer may legitimately send without a time (an inline `Link`, an actor profile, a bare reference that is fetched later) and objects nested inside a ledger entry's `payloadSnapshot`, which are carried as received (ADR-0103, CLP-07-011). Scope the rule to exclude them where needed.
- Then narrow `published` to `datetime` on the affected core classes and remove `carry_absent_times_on_inbound` for `published`. Stored data that lacks the field fails to load, so check the stores first.

## References

- ADR-0103 (object time is carried, never minted), CLP-15-006 (activities), #5479 (`CaseStatus`, the first case deci

issues.body:
Theme: theme:wire-delivery — lets a sender reference any object as typed ID and type for routing.

## Idea

Let a sender reference any object it does not inline as `{id, type}` instead of a bare URI, so a receiver that does not hold the object can still route the activity by type. Today MV-10-001 allows that shape only for an actor (AKM-05-005, ADR-0159); every other object goes inline or as a bare URI or `Link`.

## Why

Without a type, a receiver that lacks the object cannot tell an `Announce` of an embargo from an `Announce` of a case. After #5264 such an activity is `UNKNOWN_UNRESOLVABLE_OBJECT` and is fetched before it is classified (AKM-05-007). A typed reference lets it be classified first. A quick check showed the patterns already route `{id, type: Event}`, `{id, type: CaseParticipant}` and `{id, type: Note}` correctly.

## What it does not replace

- A receiver MUST still cope with a bare URI (SE-01-002), so #5264's strict matching stays.
- The receiver still lacks the object's content. ARCH-25-009 forbids treating a typed reference as the object, so a handler that needs the content still fetches it.

## Questions to settle (ADR)

- Which object types may travel as `{id, type}`, and does it amend MV-10-001 / ADR-0159?
- How a receiver tells a typed reference from a malformed inline object (see #5265, where partial inline objects are wrongly accepted).
- Whether a receiver may route on the type before the fetch and handle it after, or must fetch first.

Source: #5243 (planning conversation), docs PR #5263.
issues.title: Typed {id, type} references for every object type, so a receiver can route an activity whose object it does not hold

Theme: theme:capability-architecture — a VINCE case becomes a Vultron case the shadow's own logic can run on, by mapping rules a person has agreed.

## Summary

Decide how a VINCE case maps onto a Vultron case: VINCE status onto RM, EM and CS states; VINCE participants onto case participants, roles and CVD positions; vuls and CVE IDs onto vulnerability items; posts onto notes. Record each decision in a crosswalk page in the shape of `docs/reference/csaf_crosswalk/`. When the decisions are made, `plan-issue` files the Task that implements the mapping.

## Motivation

No spec governs this mapping. The crosswalk is its first statement. Each row is a protocol-meaning choice, for example which RM state a VINCE "vendor notified" status means. A person decides those before code implements them. The Measuring CVD work later compares one VINCE case measured both ways, and it needs the same mapping.

This issue was a Task. It became an Idea because its first output is decisions, not code.

## Rough Approach

1. Read the VINCE field set from the test instance's API docs and responses (#5957).
2. Draft the crosswalk: each VINCE field read, its Vultron counterpart, or "none".
3. Settle these points in the crosswalk:
   - A VINCE value with no counterpart is reported by name, and the case is not seeded. The mapping never guesses.
   - Times come from VINCE's own timestamps, kept as the times VINCE stated, never a clock read (ADR-0176, Epic #6318).
   - Several vuls and CVE IDs in one VINCE case map onto the vulnerability-item model (Epic #6234).

## Summary

This plans the redaction Idea as a preview-only marker. A sender building a preview, such as the case stub, can mark a field `{"type": "Redacted", "summary": "<reason>"}`: it has a value, and the sender is withholding it. A receiver refuses the marker anywhere else, so a full object, and with it every stored case, never holds one. Anonymity (#2562) is recorded as a separate concept: it gives the others a working alias, not a gap. The implementation is #6372, blocked by #6244 (the case stub becomes the case's `preview`) and #5743 (the rule for declaring an extension term).

It weighs a marker in any field, a marker in preview fields only, no marker at all, and redaction as the way to anonymize. It chooses preview-only, with one choice per field (show, redact, or leave out, the default).

issues.body:
Theme: theme:vocabulary-extensions — lets a sender mark a field redacted rather than absent.

## Idea

Let a sender mark a field as **redacted**: it has a value, but the sender is deliberately withholding it from this recipient. Today a JSON/Pydantic model cannot tell three states apart:

- **Absent**: the sender does not know the value, or it does not apply.
- **`None`**: the field exists but has no value.
- **Redacted**: the field has a value the sender is withholding.

A candidate wire form replaces the value with a small structure, for example `{"type": "Redacted", "reason": "Embargo pending"}`. The same idea must exist in the core domain model, so a handler that receives a redacted field keeps the redaction intent instead of reading `None`. AS2's `summary` can carry a human-readable reason on an otherwise minimal object.

## Why now

The design direction lives in the plan note `notes/selective-disclosure.md`. The notes sweep (#4496) moved it there from `notes/stub-objects.md`. The note's other half, dereferencing a URI reference, is tracked by #3258. No issue tracked the redaction half, and a plan note must track an open issue (NF-08).

## Scope boundary

CM-25-003 currently rules out a reduced delivery tier for Observers. Redaction is the mechanism such a tier would need, so adopting this idea for Observers means amending CM-25-003 first.

Governing specs: AKM-03-001, MV-10-002, CM-25-003

Where: notes/selective-disclosure.md
issues.title: Redaction: let a sender withhold a field's value without implying it is absent

Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — the production VINCE credential arrives only after the rules for live case data are set, so no live case is read under the test-instance rules.

## Summary

Decide, for live production VINCE cases, who and what may read the shadow's store, logs and prompts (in particular whether a Coding Agent may, and on what terms), and how long VINCE-derived data is kept after a VINCE case closes. Record both as amendments to the VINCE data-handling decision record, each naming the Task that enforces it.

## Motivation

The data-handling decision (#5956) set the rules for the test-instance stage: storage outside the checkout, per-case maintainer clearance before anything enters the repository or is published, id-only logs, a runtime-only credential, and sanitized fixtures. The maintainer left two rules open on 2026-11-12 because they were not ready to decide them: the readers of live data, and retention after a case closes. Test-instance data needs no retention rule.

The production account and host (#6338) wait on this decision, so that no live case is read before it is made.

## Rough Approach

Options raised during planning #5956:

- Live data stays on the CERT/CC host and only CERT/CC staff read it there. No Coding Agent session, dev container or CI job gets the production credential or a copy of the store, and bugs are reproduced on the test instance or with sanitized data (#6348).
- A Coding Agent may read a live case after a maintainer clears its case id, as for test-instance examples.

Retention: keep the shadow's copy until the VINCE case closes plus a fixed period, then delete it, or follow VINCE's own retention.

## References

- Epic #5954. Decision record from #5956. #6338 (production account and host). #6348 (sanitizer). #5607 (general log-content rule).
- Docs PR: https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/pull/6352 (ADR-0189 is the record to amend).

issues.body:
Theme: theme:dev-workflow — makes a Markdown lint run change only the files it was given, never another agent's worktree or a write-once history entry.

## Summary

`mdlint.sh` runs `markdownlint-cli2 --fix` over fixed globs (`"**/*.md"` plus exclusions) and drops its arguments. So `./mdlint.sh notes/x.md` rewrites every Markdown file it can reach. That includes the nested agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`, and their `plan/history/` entries.

## Evidence or Context

- `mdlint.sh` ends with `markdownlint-cli2 --fix --config .markdownlint-cli2.yaml "**/*.md" "#node_modules/**" ... "#plan/history/**"`. It never reads `"$@"`. Skills tell agents to run it (`format-markdown`, and `write-docs` step 3).
- `.claude/worktrees/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:177`), but `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`'s `ignores` does not list it.
- The `plan/history/**` entry in `ignores` and mdlint.sh's `#plan/history/**` are anchored at the root, so they do not cover `<worktree>/plan/history/`. Those entries are write-once records (HM-01-005, #2952).
- On 2026-11-10, while working #6181, `./mdlint.sh notes/testing-pitfalls.md` printed `Attempted: 17 fixes in 15 files`. It modified 15 `plan/history/2611/*.md` files in `.claude/worktrees/agent-a06108c3b73c6eed5`, another agent's live worktree, and reported an MD026 error from that worktree.
- Sibling: #6187 (`site/` is also missing from `ignores`).

## Fix or Approach

- `mdlint.sh` lints `"$@"` when it gets arguments, and uses the default glob only when it gets none.
- `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml` `ignores` adds `.claude/worktrees/**` and changes `plan/history/**` to `**/plan/history/**`. mdlint.sh's matching exclusion changes the same way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `./mdlint.sh <file>` lints and fixes only that file.
- [ ] AC-2: a bare `./mdlint.sh` run changes no file under `.claude/worktrees/` or under any `plan/history/`.
- [ ] AC-3: a test pins AC-1 and AC-2.

Governing specs: HM-01-005

Theme: theme:vocabulary-extensions — a refusal and a decline look different on the wire, so no receiver mistakes one for the other.

## Summary

Give the refusal notice its own extension type, `Refuse`, a subclass of `Reject`: `"type": ["Refuse", "Reject"]`.

## Motivation

`Reject` carries 12 semantics with three readings (decline, NAK, refusal). The refusal notice is `Reject(<refused activity inline>)` + `inReplyTo` + `summary` (ADR-0141). A refusal of an `Invite` or `Offer` has the decline's shape and is read by the decline use case (`vultron/wire/as2/extractor/_instances.py`); `Reject(Leave(Case))` reaches `REFUSAL_NOTICE` only because no decline pattern matches. CLP-02-016 already separates *refused* from *rejected* in vocabulary.

## Rough Approach

- `class Refuse(Reject)` in the wire vocabulary; wire type `["Refuse", "Reject"]` (AS2 extension guidance: an overlapping extension type MUST carry the core type; the spec's example is `["Resign","Leave"]`); `vultron:Refuse rdfs:subClassOf as:Reject` in the Vultron context.
- Patterns match `Refuse` before any `Reject` (specific before general).
- Checked and rejected: Ignore (ignoring; our RM defer), Block (actor-level, not delivered), Flag (moderation), TentativeReject (not final; RM invalid), Dislike (sentiment).

## Open questions for planning

- `type` as a list touches the parse layer (today always a string): scope that first.

## References

- Governing section: `notes/as2-vocabulary-alignment.md` § "Refusal Is Its Own Type".
- Cross-cutting rules: `notes/activitystreams-semantics.md` § "Choosing AS2 Terms". Both notes land with the docs PR on branch `docs/as2-vocabulary-alignment`.
- Touches ADR-0141, MSM-05-001, CLP-02-016, `REFUSAL_NOTICE`, #5743 (declaring the term).

Theme: theme:deployable-in-production — the VINCE credential stays off disk in the repository and out of every log and error.

## Summary

The VINCE API credential is read only at runtime from environment variables, never from a committed config file, and never appears in logs, errors or a model's repr.

## Evidence or Context

Config models load YAML that lives in the repository. A credential field there invites a committed secret (CISEC-02).

`AppConfig` (`vultron/config/app.py`) is a pydantic-settings model: environment variables with the `VULTRON_` prefix and `__` as the nesting delimiter override the YAML file, and no `.env` source is read, on purpose. The test-instance values arrive as `VULTRON_VINCE__API_TOKEN` and `VULTRON_VINCE__BASE_URL` (#5957).

## Fix or Approach

Add a `vince` section to `AppConfig` with the credential typed as `pydantic.SecretStr`. Read it from `VULTRON_VINCE__API_TOKEN`, and the base URL from `VULTRON_VINCE__BASE_URL`. Keep the no-`.env` rule. Refuse a YAML config file that carries the credential value.

The credential is a secret kept outside the code, the repository and every configuration file. The first version reads it from the environment only; entering it in the shadow's page is a later feature (ADR-0192, amended 2026-11-13).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The shadow reads the credential from `VULTRON_VINCE__API_TOKEN`, and refuses to read a case without it.
- [ ] AC-2: A config file carrying a credential value is refused at load, with an error that does not echo the value.
- [ ] AC-3: The credential value appears in no log record, exception message or repr during a run (test with a marker value).

Governing specs: VSD-01-004, VSD-01-005, SHD-02-003, CISEC-02, CFG-02.

Decision: ADR-0189, `specs/vince-shadow-data.yaml` (#5956, docs PR https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/pull/6352).

Theme: theme:test-and-ci — makes one received act cheap by reading each record once and indexing the outbox incrementally.

## Summary
One received act costs 1–3 seconds even though every store is in memory. Every test step pays that cost, and so does a real node. In a profile of one received embargo proposal (`_participant_proposes` in `test/core/use_cases/received/test_embargo_proposal_answer_copy.py`):

- The act made 743 store reads of only 73 distinct records. The CASE_MANAGER's case was read 90 times, and two participant records 50 times each.
- `SyncActivityAdapter._pending_announce_index` (`vultron/adapters/driven/sync_activity_adapter.py`) took 1.45 s of 3.25 s. It rebuilds its index whenever the outbox id list changes, which each queued `Announce` does, so it rereads every outbox row on every send. Test outboxes never drain, so the cost grows with the square of the test's length.

Make one act cheap before tests start from named starting points (TB-15): every remaining step still pays this cost.

Governing specs: SYNC-15-012, DL-06-001, DL-06-004, CLP-10-020, TB-12-003, TB-06-001

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-1: `_pending_announce_index` reads only the outbox rows queued since its last snapshot, and drops rows no longer queued, instead of rereading every row. A test queues N `Announce` rows and checks the index reads each row once. SYNC-15-012's duplicate suppression still holds, shown by its existing tests.
- [ ] AC-2: Within one received act, a record read more than once is fetched from the store once, unless it was written in between. A test shows that a read after a write in the same act returns the written version.
- [ ] AC-3: A guard test pins an upper bound on store reads for one received embargo proposal in a `LedgerNetwork`, and fails with the measured count when it is exceeded.
- [ ] AC-4: The PR reports the wall time of `test/core/use_cases/received/test_embargo_proposal_answer_copy.py` and its slowest test, before and after.
