Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — a delivery's verdict stops depending on a blackboard value some previous, unrelated execution left behind.

## Summary
`BTBridge.execute_with_setup` scopes every `context_data` key to one execution, plus a fixed list of hand-off keys. A key a **node publishes through an output port** is not `context_data`, so it gets no entry and its value outlives the execution that wrote it.

PR #5799 added `case_id` to that fixed list after CI caught the live case. The same hazard remains for the other multi-writer output-port keys.

## Evidence or Context
`case_id` was the confirmed case: six nodes publish it as an output port, and both `ReceivedPathNode` and `CheckIsCaseManagerNode` fall back to `/case_id` after their constructor argument. An unscoped key let one delivery's case decide a later delivery's path, so a `Read(Offer(VulnerabilityReport))` whose tree names no case was refused at the path stage as a replica of a case the acknowledgement never named.

Two shared keys are still unscoped:

- `case_manager_id` — 4 writers. Read by `vultron/core/behaviors/sender/nodes/actions.py:107` and `vultron/core/behaviors/embargo/nodes/terminate.py:172`.
- `case_actor_id` — 3 writers. Read by `vultron/core/behaviors/sync/nodes/genesis_announce.py:143` and `vultron/core/behaviors/sync/nodes/replay.py:305`.

All four readers use strict `get_input(...)`. Strict does **not** help here: it raises only when the key is absent, and a previous execution's value makes it present. So a node whose own execution's writer never ticked reads a stale value rather than failing — the silent-wrong-value shape, not the loud one.

In a single-process run — every demo and every in-process integration test — the writer can be a *different actor's* execution, so the stale value can cross the actor isolation BT-09 asks for.

Not reproduced for these two keys; the `case_id` instance is the proof that the mechanism bites, and these two share it by construction.

The index is replica-local state written by three sources: direct Invites, ledger apply (`relay_effect.py`, `overwrite=False`) and case copies. A case copy (`SeedAnnouncedCaseNode._replace`) replaces the invitee's index with the CASE_MANAGER's, which names the proposer's own Invite. ## Summary

Answers the concern by moving the decision on a repeated ask to its effect at the CASE_MANAGER and leaving the participant's pending-assertion window as a traffic saver only. The window can't become an effect check at the participant, because a replica learns its own assertion's effect only from the entry the round trip returns (CLP-07-013). Before this change, embargo proposals were the one repeat whose outcome rested on the window: each proposal mints a fresh embargo id, so a same-terms repeat sent after the window lapsed was registered and relayed again.

Issues: closed 1, opened 1

## Changes

- **`specs/embargo-policy.yaml`**: new EP-09-032 (MUST, protocol). An embargo proposal whose end time equals a pending proposal's is a duplicate; with no revision pending, so is one equal to the embargo in force. Sender and ids don't matter. The CASE_MANAGER changes no state, adds no ledger entry and relays no Invite for it. EP-09-032 `supersedes` EP-09-001 and EP-09-020 in that case, so their commit duties don't contradict it; while a revision is pending, a proposal of the in-force end time is still a counter-proposal under EP-09-020.
- **`specs/sync-ledger-replication.yaml`**: SYNC-11-001's rationale now says the store only saves traffic, each kind of repeat it suppresses needs its own no-op rule at the CASE_MANAGER, and why the window can't be an effect check. Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — a repeat assertion is suppressed or admitted
on its effect, so the decision comes out the same whatever order two threads
reach it and whatever the clock says.

> **Updated 2026-11-03.** This issue was filed while #5591 was still being
> fixed, and two of its three arguments have since been answered by the fix
> that landed (PR #5659). The corrected reasoning is below; the superseded
> claims are named so nobody re-derives them. The remaining question is real
> but smaller than first written, and no longer urgent.

## What #5659 settled

A participant keeps an in-memory pending-assertion store so a near-term repeat
of an assertion whose round-trip has not come back is suppressed
(SYNC-11-001, SYNC-11-002), and it decides by time: an entry suppresses while
it is `pending` and inside a configured window, and a timeout lifts the
suppression so a lost assertion can be made again (SYNC-11-005).

This issue originally argued that deciding by time cost three things. Two are
now paid:

**"It puts a clock on a read path" — fixed.** Every lookup
(`is_suppressed`, `pending_for_subject`, `clear_activity`) now takes the
deciding instant as a required `at` keyword from the caller, which already
holds the instant of the act under decision. The lookup reads no clock and
expiry stays live on it.

**"The timeout needs an evaluator, and every placement is wrong somewhere" —
withdrawn as stated.** The original text claimed that marking an overdue entry
on the lookup "re-creates the clock read" and that no fourth placement existed.
That was wrong: marking on the lookup against a *caller-supplied* instant is
the fourth placement, and it is what shipped. The three dead ends the text
described are still dead ends — marking on a lookup that reads its own clock,
marking only on a write or an explicit sweep (which left `expire_timed_out()`
with no production caller and would have let a lone unanswered ask suppress its
own repeat forever), and sweeping per d

## Summary

Since PR #6000 (#5168), every outbound activity and every nested object sets `@context` to the single string `https://certcc.github.io/Vultron/ns/context.jsonld`. The AS2 URI appears only inside the remote context document. The intended shape is a list with AS2 first:

```json
"@context": [
  "https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams",
  "https://certcc.github.io/Vultron/ns/context.jsonld"
]
```

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- **Surface:** #6000 swapped one context string for another.
- **Underlying:** the spec told it to. VM-10-001, VM-10-002 and ADR-0069 say to "set `@context` to" the Vultron URI and claim citing it alone suffices because the context document imports AS2. That holds only for a receiver that dereferences the document, and VM-10-003 says receivers need not. A non-JSON-LD AS2 receiver, which covers most ActivityPub software, checks for the AS2 URI string and can't find it.
- **Keep:** the Vultron context document itself (`docs/ns/context.jsonld`, AS2 import first, then the term block) is correct.

## Evidence or Context

- AS2 Core §2.1: producers SHOULD include a reference to `https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams` in `@context`.
- The common extension pattern is an array of contexts, for example https://niem.github.io/json/reference/json-ld/context/.
- `context_` is typed `NonEmptyString` in wire `as_Base` (`vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/base.py`) and in `CoreObject` (`vultron/core/models/base/core_object.py`). So an inbound list-form `@context`, the usual fediverse shape, appears to fail validation (unverified; confirm with a test first).
- The field widening (`context_` accepts one IRI or a list) is #5384, in PR #6005, which adds the shared `JsonLdContext` type. This issue builds on it and covers the AS2-first default, the nested-object rule, the spec and ADR

## Summary

`as_Object(name="").to_json()` emits `"name":""`. VM-07-001 requires serialized wire objects to exclude empty-string fields, and that half does not hold.

## Evidence or Context

- `name`, `summary`, `content` and `mediaType` all serialize a blank value, and a core object's `content=""` renders too. No code strips or refuses blanks.
- Docstrings that claim VM-07-001 drops blanks are corrected in the #5662 PR. They were `vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/links.py:56`, `test/wire/as2/test_parser.py:495` and `test/architecture/test_wire_reference_fields_reject_blank.py:27`.
- Related, but a different surface: #3894 covers blank *references* in `Any`-typed fields.
- Found during the #5228 epic run while working #5662, which keeps VM-07-001 whole until this lands.

## Fix or Approach

Type these optional string fields as `NonEmptyString | None` (CS-08-001, CS-08-002), so a blank is refused when the object is built, as #3876 did for blank references. Do not strip blanks at serialization: that would change stored data silently. Add a test that each such field refuses `""` and that no serialized wire object holds an empty-string value. #5662 then splits VM-07-001 with that test as the child's `verification:`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Building a wire object with `name=""`, `summary=""`, `content=""` or `mediaType=""` raises a validation error.
- [ ] A test proves no serialized wire object emits an empty-string field, and it passes.
- [ ] Inbound messages with a blank value in these fields are refused at the parse edge, with a test.

Governing specs: VM-07-001, CS-08-001, CS-08-002

Theme: theme:wire-delivery — makes outbound activities cite the Vultron JSON-LD context.

## Summary

VM-10-001, and §5.2 Serialization of the Protocol Specification, require an outbound message to set `@context` to the Vultron JSON-LD context document, `https://certcc.github.io/Vultron/ns/context.jsonld`. That document imports AS2 and declares every Vultron term.

The code doesn't do that for activities:

- `as_Base.context_` (`vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/base.py`) defaults to `ACTIVITY_STREAMS_NS` (`https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams`). Activity classes such as `Offer`, `Accept` and `Invite` inherit it, so the outer activity carries the AS2 namespace.

A receiver that processes the outer activity as JSON-LD therefore can't expand Vultron terms such as `EmbargoEvent` or `VulnerabilityCase` from the activity's own context. agent_prs.body:
- Closes #5831

## Summary

Stops two writers from adding `plan/history/` files for records kept somewhere else. `spec-retire` no longer writes an implementation entry, because the retired-requirement file is the record. `append-history implementation|idea` now takes a fixed `--source` vocabulary: `ISSUE-N` posts an issue comment, `ISSUE-N-<slug>` and `IDEA-YYMMDDNN` write files, and every other source is refused.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 1, filed 0

## Motivation

AC-2 was reworded by a maintainer decision during the Epic #5829 run: [issue comment](https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/issues/5831#issuecomment-6660263187).
The original AC-2 read any `<PREFIX>-N` as issue N once `gh` confirmed the number exists.
The pre-push review showed this would post records on unrelated issues, because many sources use other numberings: `ADR-0041` would land on PR #41, `VCR-005` on issue #5, and `BUG-2505` is a year and month.
The reworded AC-2 fixes the vocabulary instead of interpreting prefixes.

How the reworded AC-2 is met:

- `implementation`: `ISSUE-N` posts a comment, and `ISSUE-N-<slug>` writes a file (the oversized-PR-body record form in `pr-body-guide.md`).

The `size:` band **thresholds** are now one computed authority (#3536 / #3537), but the **survey statistics that justify them** were duplicated across six long-lived files in the same PR.

## What is duplicated

The 692-PR survey window, `size:S` correct 24% of the time, 40% of PRs unlabelled, findings/kLOC falling 4.5 → 3.5 → 2.7 → 1.5, and the 23.1 / 37.6 / 26.2 / 13.2% band distribution now appear in:

Theme: theme:dev-workflow — makes the survey behind the size bands a command anyone can re-run.

## Summary

The `size:` bands were cut at quantiles of a one-off survey whose script was never committed (#3544). Add a `--calibrate` mode to `pr-size` that recomputes the numbers the bands and the AC rule rest on, from merged PRs and the issues they close.

The 2026-11-03 retrospective (`wip_outputs/issue-sizing-retrospective-2026-11-03.html`) re-derived these by hand: the median merged PR grew from 252 to 739 lines, the old quantile cuts now sit near 210 / 1,080 / 2,700 lines, and estimate accuracy fell to 22% exact. Without a command, the next recalibration repeats that work.

## Fix or Approach

Read merged PRs (additions plus deletions, as `pr-size-label` measures) and their closing issues through `gh`. Keep the arithmetic in pure functions beside `size_bands.py`, so tests feed fixture data and never call GitHub.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-3: `sizing.md` says when to run it (quarterly, and after a workflow change) and what drift warrants recalibrating (lines per AC moves more than about 1.5×, or a band's share more than about 10 points). Tests cover the computations with fixture data.

Routes `SenderIsCaseOwnerNode`'s non-match through `_refuse_by_placement`, the
one rule every other sender kind check records a refusal through, so a side

Root cause, established at runtime on the composed guards before any edit: the
node set `feedback_message` to a reason ending `— REFUSED (HP-01-006)` and

CASE_OWNER for case '…'`) that carried no refusal wording. It never asked the
placement rule. On a lone-`CASE_OWNER` side a refused sender therefore produced
**zero** records at or above WARNING: `BTBridge.get_failure_reason` reported

## Summary

In `vultron/core/behaviors/case/receive_close_case_tree/factory.py`,
`DeclineOwnerCloseIfEmbargoed` is the last child of the `CloseOrDecline`
Selector, and its first child is `CheckIsCaseOwnerForClose` — a
`SenderIsCaseOwnerNode` composed by `owner_close_blocked_by_embargo_guards`.
That check is a *decision* ("is this an owner close an embargo blocks?"), not
a door. But because the arm is the Selector's last child,
`failure_is_the_refusal` answers `True` for it, so now that #5845 routes
`SenderIsCaseOwnerNode` onto `refuse_by_placement`, a non-match there logs at
WARNING carrying the `REFUSED (HP-01-006)` group.

## Evidence

Established at runtime, not read off the source:

```text
uv run pytest test/core/use_cases/received/test_close_case_role_semantics.py \
  -n 0 -k not_the_owner_cannot_leave --log-cli-level=WARNING
```

A CASE_MANAGER that is not the Case Owner sends a Leave (CM-23-010). The
close arm fails at `CaseManagerLeavesOnlyAsCaseOwnerNode`, the decline arm
then ticks, and the run logs two WARNINGs:

- `CaseManagerLeavesOnlyAsCaseOwner: ... — REFUSED (CM-23-010)`
- `CheckIsCaseOwnerForClose: Sender '...' is not the Case Owner of case '...' — REFUSED (HP-01-006)`

The reason the handler reports is the correct CM-23-010 one.

## Why it matters

The second line cites HP-01-006, so a reader — and the demo matcher
`expect_no_sender_refusals`, which keys on a `REFUSED (...)` group naming
HP-01-006 — reads it as a sender-guard refusal. The sender guard admitted
this sender; a later guard refused the delivery.

Does not block: the verdict and the reported reason are correct today, and no
demo drives this path. A demo that did would already fail, because the
delivery is refused and `expect_no_inbox_refusals` catches that.

## Summary

`SenderIsCaseOwnerNode._not_case_owner` records the refusal reason on
`feedback_message` and returns FAILURE without logging it. The only line the
node writes for a non-match is a DEBUG one (`sender '…' is NOT CASE_OWNER for
case '…'`) that carries no `REFUSED` wording. So on a side whose only kind is
`CASE_OWNER`, a refused sender produces no line at or above WARNING anywhere in
the run: `BTBridge.get_failure_reason` reports the reason to the handler, and
the log says nothing.

This is the mirror image of #5786 (a duplicate refusal line) — here the
refusal line is missing. #5786 deliberately left this node alone: its reviewer
judged the `CASE_OWNER` check as having nothing to move, and adding a WARNING
where there is none today is a behaviour change that could surface in the demo
runs guarded by `expect_no_sender_refusals`.

Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — decides how ARCH-24-003's "exactly one authority condition node" applies to the two nodes no declared path can serve, so the inventory of authority askers reaches zero instead of carrying two permanent entries.

## Summary
`test/architecture/test_role_authority_resolver.py` holds `KNOWN_SECOND_AUTHORITY_ASKERS`, the inventory of BT node classes that answer "is the executing actor the case authority" besides the one `CheckIsCaseManagerNode` that ARCH-24-006 sanctions. After #5043 two entries remain that no migration wave reaches:

- `InitializeCreationEmbargoNode` — `vultron/core/behaviors/case/nodes/embargo.py`
- `CaseOpenToExternalWritesNode` — `vultron/core/behaviors/case/nodes/post_close.py`

(The third, `ReceivedPathNode`, is sanctioned until #5044 retires the role gates.)

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem
The surface reading is that both nodes are unmigrated leftovers of ADR-0153. They are not: #5043 changed both to ask through the shared `has_role` predicate, which takes the authority role from the single resolver, so each now satisfies ARCH-24-007 and no longer compares `resolve_case_manager_id(...)` with the receiver inline. The ADR-0153 ratchet recorded that and dropped both modules.

The underlying problem is a mismatch between ARCH-24-003 and how it is measured. ARCH-24-003 says "exactly one authority **condition node**". Neither of these is a condition node: one is an action node asserting a permission rule, the other is a door guard that also reads the ledger. The shared detector in `test/architecture/_authority_question.py` counts any class whose body asks, including one that asks through the sanctioned predicate — which ARCH-24-007 explicitly contemplates as legitimate.

What is correct and should stay: one resolver (ARCH-24-001), one sanctioned condition node (ARCH-24-006), and a detector that reads the resolver, predicate and role names off the live objects so a rename cannot blind it.

Archit

Theme: theme:test-and-ci — GitHub, not agent discipline, refuses a merge to `main` when CI is red or has not run.

## Summary

Human step: create a repository ruleset on `main` that requires the `CI gate` check (#5942). The work is a repository setting, so a person approves and creates it. Agents skip this issue (`ready-for-human`).

## Evidence or Context

- No active ruleset has a `required_status_checks` rule today. The admin role can bypass `main-2 Enforce CI on PRs`, and every agent merges as the admin account. So the new rule must have **no** bypass actors, or agent merges skip it.
- Wait until `CI gate` has run for about a day: green on a code pull request and on a docs-only pull request, and red on a failing pull request.

## Fix or Approach

```bash
gh api -X POST repos/CERTCC/Vultron/rulesets --input - <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "main-3 Require CI gate",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["refs/heads/main"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [],
  "rules": [{
    "type": "required_status_checks",
    "parameters": {
      "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
      "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
      "required_status_checks": [{ "context": "CI gate", "integration_id": 15368 }]
    }
  }]
}
JSON
```

- `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false` keeps the ADR-0126/ADR-0138 rule: being behind `main` alone does not block a merge.
- `integration_id` 15368 (GitHub Actions) means no other app can post the status.
- Emergency: an admin sets the ruleset's enforcement to `disabled`, then enables it again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gh api repos/CERTCC/Vultron/rulesets` lists `main-3 Require CI gate` as active, with the parameters above and an empty bypass list.
- [ ] Every pull request open when the rule goes live gets one new push (an empty commit or `gh pr update-branch`), so it reports `CI gate`.

## Summary

Add `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml`: one job named `CI gate` that runs on every pull request to `main` and passes only when every other check on the pull request's head commit passed or was skipped.

## Evidence or Context

- No active ruleset has a `required_status_checks` rule. Only agents enforce "never merge on red", through `wait-for-ci.sh`. Every agent merges as the admin account, and the admin role can bypass `main-2 Enforce CI on PRs`.

## Summary

Limit how many heavy local checks run at once **on each host**. A shared Python lock gives out a few slots, and `start-dev.sh` sets the number of slots from the host's Docker VM. Every slot container on a host shares the lock; each host has its own.

## Evidence or Context

- One host runs 8–9 slot containers (`start-dev.sh`), each capped at 6 CPUs and 12 GiB, on a 20-core / 128 GB machine. Their caps add up to about 54 CPUs on 20 cores. Each `pytest -n auto` sizes its workers from its own container and cannot see the other containers, so nine concurrent runs start about 54 test workers.
- ADR-0143 (and the comment in `start-dev.sh`) makes the 6-CPU cap a ceiling, not a reserved share: slots split CPU equally under contention. That choice did not foresee 8–9 slots running heavy checks at once. This lock adds the missing limit on concurrent heavy jobs and leaves the cap as it is.
- Measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05, in **one** slot's transcripts only (`wip_outputs/pacman/local-compute-offload-report.html`, change 6): 3,753 memory-limit hits, 58 per-test timeouts, 19 memory kills, 18 hung runs, 8 crashed workers, and 45 h of agent time waiting on local runs. The fleet total is probably about 8× that (an extrapolation, not a measurement).

- **Where the lock lives:** in the named volume that every slot already mounts (`${MAIN_NAME}-data` → `/home/vscode/.data`), under `locks/`. A named volume belongs to one Docker engine, so it is shared by every slot on a host and separate on every other host. No new mount is

Theme: theme:cvd-measurement — lets an ordering measure report a desiderata score for a real case, whose event sequence is almost always incomplete.

## Summary

Decide and build how an incomplete case-state sequence earns a desiderata score. The
existing scorer refuses one, and incomplete is the normal shape for a real case, so
today there is no path from a derived case history to a published ordering measure.

## Motivation

`CVDmodel.score_hist` (`vultron/core/case_states/hypercube/_scoring.py`) routes through
`case_states.validations.is_valid_history`, which admits only a **complete** six-event
history and raises `ScoringError` on anything shorter:

```text
m.score_hist("VFDPXA") -> 7.372685185185184
m.score_hist("VFP")    -> ScoringError: Invalid history VFP
```

Every case-state sequence derivable from the eleven committed recordings under
`ui/src/recordings/` is incomplete — mostly `V,F,P`. So the scorer refuses the whole
corpus. This is not a corpus artifact: many cases never see a public exploit or
observed attacks, and an open case has not closed, which is why CEH-05-005 makes an
incomplete sequence the normal result and CEH-05-008 keeps the event-history layer out
of scoring entirely.

CSB-17-011 is the opening: every accepted prefix has at least one valid completion
among the 70 valid complete histories of CSB-17-004. So a prefix can be scored by
enumerating its completions, rather than by being rejected.

## Rough Approach

Enumerate the valid completions of a prefix and derive a figure from the set, instead
of scoring the prefix directly. What figure is the open question.

## Open Questions

- Report a range, a mean, or a full distribution over the completions? A range states
  what the case cannot do worse or better than; a distribution carries more but needs
  a convention for summarizing it.
- Weight completions by observed frequency, or treat them as equally likely? Equal
  weighting is defensible and simple; frequency weighting needs a corpus larg

issues.body:
Theme: theme:cvd-measurement — generalizes multi-party measurement to shared case-level events.

## Summary

Generalize the original multi-party measurement analysis to the case shape Vultron
implements, where some state is participant-specific and some is participant-agnostic.

## Motivation

`docs/topics/measuring_cvd/benchmarking_mpcvd.md` gives each vendor and product its
own independent six-event history. It then reads the median and spread of the skill
coefficient across them. In a Vultron case:

- only VF (per vendor) and D (per deployer) are participant-specific
- P, X and A are participant-agnostic: every participant shares the case's moment of
  public awareness, public exploit and observed attack

So per-participant histories are not independent. The Measuring CVD restructuring
keeps the original page as a foundation, and describes this generalization as work in
progress in the section's introduction. This Idea is that work.

Questions to settle:

- What unit gets scored: a participant, or a (participant, role) pair? The answer
  needs to work for vendors without deployers and deployers without vendors.
- How do median and spread read when the P/X/A events are shared?
- How does the measure reduce to the two-party special case?
- How does the fairness and equitable-resilience concern carry over? (See the Open
  Questions page.)

## Rough Approach

Do this together with the coupled-state-space baselines in #5072. The skill
coefficient for a shared-event case needs those baselines.

## References

- `docs/topics/measuring_cvd/benchmarking_mpcvd.md`
- `notes/case-state-model.md` § Participant-Specific vs. Participant-Agnostic State
- ADR-0075 (CS split), CSB-15-004 (case-wide deploy gate)

Theme: theme:cvd-measurement — computes baseline frequencies for the extended desiderata.

## Summary

Compute the chance frequency f_d of each extended desideratum by a random walk over the combined report management, embargo management, embargo consent and Case State space, with the coupling rules applied, so the skill coefficient alpha_d can be used for them.

## Motivation

The skill coefficient needs a baseline. The baselines for the original twelve come from a uniform walk over the six-event Case State model (`vultron/core/case_states/hypercube.py`). The extended desiderata involve events from the other models, and the coupling rules change their frequencies: public awareness ends an embargo in force, and fix readiness requires acceptance. A walk that ignores these couplings gives baselines for histories that cannot occur.

## Rough Approach

- Define the joint state and its allowed transitions from the existing state tables (`vultron/core/states/rm.py`, `em.py`, `embargo_register.py`, `participant_embargo_consent.py`) and the composite invariants (`composite_state_invariants.py`), rather than restating them.
- Start with one vendor and a whole-case embargo; add participants once that works.
- Report f_d per desideratum, and check how strongly the desiderata are correlated, which feeds the weighting question on the desiderata page.
- Decide whether a uniform walk is still the right baseline for protocol acts, which are choices rather than chance events.

## References

- PR #5067 (`process_model_desiderata.md` § "Open problems")
- `docs/topics/measuring_cvd/random_walk.md`, `reasoning_over_histories.md`
- `vultron/core/case_states/hypercube.py`

Theme: theme:cvd-measurement — derives a timestamped CVD event history from a case ledger for metrics.

## Summary

Build a translation layer that reads a case ledger and produces the case's event history: each Case State event (V, F, D, P, X, A) and each process-model event (report received, validated, accepted and closed; embargo in force and ended; participant joined and agreed to the embargo), labeled by participant and cause, with its log index, commit stamp and claimed time.

## Motivation

Both proposed measures need this as input. The ordering desiderata need event sequences; the timing metrics need event times. The ledger already holds every state change as its own entry, but nothing turns it into an event history. An archived note (`plan/history/2610/note/NOTES-case-state-model--measuring-cvd-process-quality.md`) named this gap. The existing scoring code in `vultron/core/case_states/hypercube.py` scores histories but has no source of real ones.

The embargo register entries and consent rows carry no timestamps of their own, so their timing has to be joined from the ledger entries that recorded each step.

## Rough Approach

- Map each ledger semantic type to the event or events it records, including the cause split for embargo exit (from the termination record).
- Emit per-participant and per-case event streams; keep log index order authoritative and both clocks available.
- Exercise it on the demo scenario ledgers, which give known histories to check against.
- Keep it read-only and outside the protocol path: an analysis tool, not a case behavior.

## References

- PR #5067 (`timing_metrics.md` § "What the ledger records", § "Data gaps")
- `vultron/core/case_states/hypercube.py`
- `notes/case-ledger-authority.md`

Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — three requirement links on the PCR and HP ends record the relationship their statements actually have.

## Summary

Three `implements` links on the PCR and HP ends look like the wrong type. The builder of PR #5871 (#5866) found them while judging the AKM-01-002 and HP-01-035 links, outside that issue's acceptance criteria.

## Evidence or Context

- **PCR-01-005 and PCR-01-006 `implements` PCR-01-003.** PCR-01-003 says the protocol works the same on one host or many. PCR-01-005 (an Actor does not reach into another Actor's store) and PCR-01-006 (an Actor does not rely on out-of-band communication with a co-located Actor) are prohibitions that follow from it. A prohibition states no mechanism, so SR-13-001's `implements` does not fit. PR #5871 recorded AKM-01-002 `derives_from` PCR-01-003 on the same reasoning; `derives_from` likely fits both PCR links too.
- **HP-01-035 `implements` HP-01-005.** HP-01-035 places the path stage directly after the HP-01-012 addressee check. HP-01-005 requires `REFUSED` for a message the receiver has no role or addressing to act on. The path stage is not the addressee check, so HP-01-035 is not the mechanism that meets HP-01-005. The link may need another type, or it may have no basis (SR-13-018). HP-01-035 `refines` CLP-10-010 was checked in #5866 and stays.

## Fix or Approach

Judge each link by its SR-13 definition and record the result on the owning end, in `specs/participant-case-replica.yaml` and `specs/handler-protocol.yaml`: retype it, keep it with a recorded reason, or delete it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PCR-01-005's link to PCR-01-003 is retyped, kept with a recorded reason, or deleted.
- [ ] PCR-01-006's link to PCR-01-003 is retyped, kept with a recorded reason, or deleted.
- [ ] HP-01-035's link to HP-01-005 is retyped, kept with a recorded reason, or deleted.

## Summary

Adds a per-requirement `see_also: [{spec_id, reason}]` field and makes spec-lint fail on a statement citation that is neither linked nor listed there, or on a stale `see_also` entry (part 2 of #5213, Epic #5226; part 1 was #5909). Every unlinked statement citation in the corpus is listed with a reason, so `uv run spec-lint specs/` exits 0.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Motivation

The #5118 sweep judged every statement citation against SR-13. Many fit no relationship type and stayed in the prose with nothing recorded. Without a check, a new citation lands unjudged and the audit must be done again. A relationship asserts that a change to the target affects the source, and a see-also mention asserts nothing (SR-13-018), so it is a field, not a link type (ADR-0177).

## Changes

Commits are kept apart so a reviewer can tell the mechanical fill from the rule:

Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — remove the 16 deprecated spec entries and retire the deprecated/superseded_by fields.

## Problem

MS-04-005 and MS-09-001 require a superseded requirement to be removed, not marked deprecated (confirmed 2026-10-02 learn session). The spec schema (`vultron/metadata/specs/schema.py`) still defines `deprecated: bool` and `superseded_by`, spec-lint accepts them silently, and 16 entries use them: SE-08-005, DEMOMA-08-002, DEMOMA-08-006, DEMOMA-08-009, ARCH-13-002, ARCH-13-005, IMPLTS-05-007, IMPLTS-07-001, IMPLTS-07-004, IMPLTS-07-007, IMPLTS-07-013, IMPLTS-07-014, CM-24-003 (plus the remaining flagged entries in `tech-stack.yaml` / `multi-actor-demo.yaml` / `architecture.yaml` — re-derive with `grep -rn 'deprecated: true' specs/`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Every `deprecated: true` entry is removed, and its removal recorded in history (MS-09-002).
- [ ] AC-2: Every citation of a removed ID in `vultron/`, `test/` (including `@pytest.mark.spec` markers) and `notes/` is repointed to the replacement (MS-09-003). ADR citations stay (historical).
- [ ] AC-3: `deprecated` and `superseded_by` are removed from the spec schema, or spec-lint reports any use as a hard error.
- [ ] AC-4: A removed ID is never reassigned (MS-04-003): spec-lint or a ratchet keeps a retired-ID list and fails on reuse.

## Decided (maintainer, 2026-10-29, from #5289)

SR-02-021 requires `StatementSpec` to support `deprecated` and `superseded_by`, which exist only for spec-lint to refuse. Decision: drop the fields from the schema (AC-3's first option), and retire SR-02-021 or rewrite it so it no longer names them.

- [ ] AC-5: SR-02-021 no longer requires the `deprecated` or `superseded_by` fields.

Governing specs: SR-02-021, MS-04-003, MS-04-005, MS-09-001, MS-09-002, MS-09-003

## Summary

AKM-02-004 says an object the recipient cannot be expected to hold, such as the proposed embargo of an embargo invitation, MUST travel inline. `parse_activity` does not enforce this for `Invite(EmbargoEvent)`. An `Invite` whose `object` is the embargo's URI parses.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

Surface reading: the activity is harmless, because with an unresolved URI object it matches no pattern (SE-01-006). It is classed `unknown_unresolvable_object`, dead-lettered and refused (`UnresolvableObjectReceivedUseCase`).

Underlying problem: rehydration resolves the URI from the receiver's own store before pattern matching (SE-01-006, "still unresolved after rehydration"). A receiver that already holds the embargo then reads the activity as `invite_to_embargo_on_case`. The parse-edge checks ran before rehydration and saw only a URI. ## Summary

`refuse_misplaced_case_reference` in `vultron/wire/as2/case_reference_placement.py` stopped its walk at any value that is not an `as_Base`. Inline domain objects (a `VulnerabilityCase`, `VulnerabilityReport`, `CaseParticipant` or inline actor) are core models, not `as_Base` (ARCH-25-004), so a case reference nested in one was never seen.

Let the walker descend into any pydantic `BaseModel`, not only `as_Base`. PR #5873 makes this change, since the walker is shared.

- A case reference nested in an inline core object is refused at parse, and the refusal names its path (for example `object.context`).

Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — a receiver admits a case stub only in the activity positions the protocol permits, and MV-10-002 says which positions those are.

## Summary

`MV-10-002` (MUST, `kind: protocol`) says a `VulnerabilityCaseStub` is ONLY permitted in `actor`, `object`, `target` and `origin`. Nothing enforces it. Its `verification:` says "inspection of the inbound message validator confirms that stub detection runs only on `actor`, `object`, `target`, and `origin`", but no stub-position check exists in the parser or the extractor.

Found while reviewing PR #5767, which cites `story_2026_013` on `MV-10-002`. The citation stands; the requirement's text and the code do not agree.

## Evidence

`parse_activity` (`vultron/wire/as2/parser.py`) on an `Announce` with a well-formed stub (`type`, `caseId`, `summary`) in each position, on `main` at 1d325bec4:

| Position | Result |
|---|---|
| `origin` | accepted (`as_VulnerabilityCaseStub`) — permitted |
| `instrument` | accepted — should be refused |
| `result` | accepted — should be refused |
| `context` | accepted — should be refused |
| `actor` | refused (`actor` is `as_ActorRef \| CoreActor`) — the statement *permits* it |

The base `as_Activity` types `target`, `origin` and `instrument` alike as `as_ObjectRef` (`vultron/wire/as2/vocab/base/objects/activities/base.py`), so the field types cannot tell the permitted positions from the others. The wire layer does have an `origin` field; only the pattern objects lack `origin_`.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

Surface: a stale `verification:` clause. Underlying: the statement itself is off — a case stub in `actor` is not a meaningful position and the parser already refuses it, while `instrument`, `result` and `context` are open. ADR-0090 narrowed MV-10-001/002 to the case stub but no check followed. What is right and should stay: the stub is its own pinned `type` (CM-11-013), so a position check can key on the class alone.

## Fix or Approach

Decid

## Summary

The SQLite DataLayer's read path accepts a bare UUID as a lookup key: it retries
the lookup as `urn:uuid:<uuid>`, so `dl.read("<bare uuid>")` returns the object
stored under `urn:uuid:<uuid>`. OID-02-004 says a DataLayer lookup MUST NOT accept
a bare UUID as a lookup key.

## Evidence

- `vultron/adapters/driven/datalayer_sqlite/crud.py` (the read function) calls
  `id_lookup_candidates(object_id)` from `vultron/adapters/utils.py`, which for a

  the forbidden behaviour.
- `test/core/use_cases/triggers/test_actor_triggers.py` passes a bare UUID into a

  the store-level fallback instead of mapping the path segment at the edge.
- `vultron/adapters/driving/fastapi/routers/datalayer.py` already maps a route
  segment with `full_object_id` at the edge, which is the shape OID-02-004 leaves
  room for (ADR-0032: validate at the edge).

Found while building #5311, which touched `vultron/adapters/utils.py`.

UUID into the DataLayer.

issues.body:
Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — the BT node design specs give one answer to where a node's case ID comes from.

## Summary

Three behavior-tree node design requirements give different answers to where a node gets its case ID:

- BTND-01-004 (MUST): a BT node MUST take each value that varies by usage site, a case ID included, as a constructor parameter.
- BTND-01-005 (MUST): a BT node MUST receive each variable input through a constructor parameter or the documented blackboard interface.
- BTND-10-005 (MUST): the ParticipantStatus write node MUST obtain `case_id` from its declared blackboard port, never from a constructor argument.

BTND-10-005 forbids what BTND-01-004 requires; BTND-01-005 permits both.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

Surface: a missing link. The SR-13 link audit (PR #5853, #5212) could have recorded BTND-10-005 `supersedes` BTND-01-004 and moved on.
Underlying: the specs do not say which rule governs, so a link would choose a design. Either the blackboard-port pattern is the exception (BTND-10-005 supersedes BTND-01-004 for that node), or it is the general rule and BTND-01-004 should be reworded to allow a declared port. BTND-01-005's either-way wording looks like the correct general rule and should stay.

## Category

Spec contradiction.

## Severity

Medium. An agent writing a new node can cite either MUST and be right.

## Evidence

- `specs/behavior-tree-node-design.yaml`: BTND-01-004, BTND-01-005, BTND-10-005.
- Recorded as an open question in PR #5853's body; no link was changed on its account.

## Impact if Ignored

New nodes split between the two patterns, and a reviewer cannot say which one is the defect.

## Suggested Action

Decide whether a case ID may come from a declared blackboard port in general. Then either reword BTND-01-004 to allow a declared port (and drop its case-ID example), or record BTND-10-005 `supersedes` BTND-01-004 and say in BTND-10-005 why that node is the exception.

## Summary

Decided in Concern #6041. When the case owner's consent row for a proposed embargo is `DECLINED`, its activation (`Add(EmbargoEvent, target=VulnerabilityCase)` once #6030 lands) is refused before anything is committed, and the owner gets a refusal notice telling it to accept the invitation first. Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — every Accept of an embargo gets one defined answer, so no willing participant's answer is silently dropped and a confused sender learns its view of the case is wrong.

## Summary

Bring the specs and the CASE_MANAGER's Accept handling to the rule decided in Concern #5745: what decides the answer to an `Accept(Invite(EmbargoEvent))` is whether the named embargo is still available, not whether the Accept arrived before its RSVP deadline.

- **Available** (the case's Active Embargo or one of its open proposals, and its end time has not passed): the Accept is honoured, on time or late.
- **Held, but no longer available** (replaced, rejected, cancelled, terminated, or an ACTIVE entry past its end time that the clock has not yet terminated): the Accept is refused uncommitted with the refusal notice (CLP-05-001) that says the answer is moot. When the case holds current terms, the CASE_MANAGER also sends the accepter a fresh `Invite(EmbargoEvent)` to them (EMB-17-003). "The party moved to the 14th; want to come to that instead?"
- **Never held** by the register: the Accept gets a `Create(ProcessingFault)`, not a refusal. The sender is confused, not refused (MSM-05-001: received but not understood). "What party?"

## Evidence or Context

Today a late Accept with no embargo in the case is a silent no-op (EMB-17-004, EMB-17-016), a late Accept of replaced terms gets a re-invite and no refusal, and MSM-07-012 refuses an on-time Accept of a never-held embargo with a refusal notice. The maintainer's rulings are recorded on Concern #5745.

## Fix or Approach

Specs, code and tests move together in this PR, because a changed protocol requirement needs its `@pytest.mark.spec` marker in the same PR (SR-05-004).

The SR-13 link audit of the state-machine and protocol specs (#5210) found three pairs of requirements that state the same rule, and one pair of routing rules that contradicts the RK rule. Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — a late Accept of a live embargo proposal is recorded instead of silently dropped.

## Summary

The CASE_MANAGER's routing of a late `Accept(Invite(EmbargoEvent))` keys on whether
the accepted embargo is the case's Active Embargo. A case in EM `PROPOSED` has an
open proposal and no Active Embargo, so it matches no EMB-17 arm: `late_accept_route`
sends it to `REINVITE`, `ReinviteLateAccepterNode._invite_owed` reads
`case.active_embargo_id` as `None`, logs a WARNING and sends nothing, and because
that arm is a diversion the Accept is never recorded. A willing participant's answer
to a live proposal is lost, and the Case Owner does not see it when deciding the
proposal.

The planning PR amended EMB-17 so the route keys on whether the case can still
answer the named embargo — its Active Embargo or an open proposal, which is what
MSM-07-003 and the Accept tree's own `IsAnswerableEmbargoNode` guard already say —
and so the re-invite names the Active Embargo, or the earliest-expiring open
proposal when none is in force. This issue brings the code to that.

Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — keep the CASE_MANAGER and CASE_OWNER roles off a Coordinator admitted through a suggestion.

## Summary

CM-20-006 says: when the Case Owner approves a Coordinator suggested through the `Offer(Actor, Case)` path (CM-16), the Coordinator's roles MUST NOT include `CASE_MANAGER` or `CASE_OWNER`. The code does not enforce this. If the recorded suggestion names those roles, the Invite the CASE_MANAGER emits when the owner approves carries them unchanged.

## Evidence or Context

- Found while the #5217 bundle split CM-20-002, whose `verification:` claimed `test/demo/` integration tests check this. No test did.
- `test_an_approved_coordinator_is_invited_without_authority_roles` in `test/core/use_cases/received/actor/test_offer_case_participant.py` is a strict xfail that pins the gap. It seeds a recorded `Offer(CaseParticipant)` with roles `[COORDINATOR, CASE_MANAGER, CASE_OWNER]`, runs `AcceptOfferCaseParticipantReceivedUseCase`, and finds both authority roles on the emitted Invite.
- Related: CM-20-004 and CM-20-005 keep `CASE_MANAGER` off a facilitation participant, and CBT-01-014 gives it only to the actor that creates the case.

## Fix or Approach

Two options. The choice is a design decision:

1. Refuse, at intake, a recommendation (`Offer(CaseParticipant)`) or role offer that names `CASE_MANAGER` or `CASE_OWNER` for the invitee.
2. Strip those roles when the CASE_MANAGER builds the Invite from the approved suggestion.

Option 1 fails loudly. Option 2 silently changes what the owner approved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: An approved suggestion never yields an Invite or a `CaseParticipant` holding `CASE_MANAGER` or `CASE_OWNER` (CM-20-006).

Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — the processing-fault requirements agree with each other on whether a fault is ledgered and on when a fault may be answered.

## Summary

Two gaps in the processing-fault requirements surfaced while restating RE/EE/CE as `Create(ProcessingFault)` in #5299:

1. ASK-07-008 says a processing fault that can be attributed to a case MUST be recorded as a canonical `CaseLedgerEntry`. CLP-02-013 says a `Create(ProcessingFault)` NACK is not a case event, because it changes nothing in the case. They cannot both hold.
2. RMB-07-002 (restated from "answer RE with RE+GI") tells a participant in RM Start to answer a fault about an RM activity with another fault. If both sides are in Start, each fault prompts another. ASK-07-015 stops a repeat for the *same* failed activity only, and each answering fault is a new activity.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

On the surface, these are two wording slips. Underneath, nothing in the protocol says whether a fault is a case event, or whether a fault is itself something that can be answered with a fault. Both rules were carried over from the 2022 RE/EE/CE model, where errors were peer messages, and were never checked against the ledger model. The partition of failures into fault, `Reject` and `Add(Note)` (MSM-05-001) is correct and should stay.

Specification consistency.

Low today: CE/EE/RE have no dedicated receive paths, so no code path loops. It becomes real when fault handling is built.

Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — the case owner's personal answer to an embargo proposal and its decision for the case combine in one consistent set of sequences.

## Summary

ADR-0180 separates the case owner's two roles toward a proposed embargo. As a participant it answers the invitation with `Accept`/`Reject(Invite(EmbargoEvent))`, which records only whether the owner finds the embargo acceptable. As the decider for the case it acts on the embargo with `Add` (activate), `Reject(EmbargoEvent)` (decline for the case) or `Remove` (end). The protocol does not yet say which orders of those two answers are consistent:

- **`Add` alone:** allowed. Activation records the owner's `AGREE` if it had not given one. The owner need not `Accept` first.
- **`Accept`, then `Add`:** allowed, and the natural order.
- **`Reject(Invite)`, then `Add`:** allowed today, on purpose: ADR-0122 says an owner whose row is `DECLINED` may still activate, and the activation moves its row straight to `AGREED` as the owner changing its answer. The maintainer's view is that this is odd, and that `Reject`, `Accept`, `Add` may be the consistent sequence. That would make an `Add` from a `DECLINED` owner row a refusal.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- **Surface:** one permitted sequence, `Reject` then `Add`, reads as the owner contradicting itself.
- **Underlying:** nothing states how the owner's consent row constrains its decision for the case, in either direction. The rule is one line of ADR-0122's effects table, carried into ADR-0180, with no requirement saying which combinations are consistent.
- **Correct and to keep:** the split itself (participants answer invitations; the owner acts on embargoes, ADR-0180), and that an owner never has to `Accept` before it may `Add`.

## Background: the owner may let the CASE_MANAGER do the Add

Theme: theme:protocol-correctness — an Accept naming terms the embargo register no longer holds gets one defined answer, not two that contradict each other.

## Summary

`MSM-07-012` (MUST) says an Accept may name an embargo the register does not hold,
or holds in a final status, and that the CASE_MANAGER MUST refuse that Accept
before committing it, with the refusal notice that reports the reason
(`CLP-05-001`). It carries no lateness qualifier, so on its face it reaches late
Accepts too.

`EMB-17` answers the same condition differently. `EMB-17-003` (MUST) relays a
fresh `Invite(EmbargoEvent)` to the accepter. `EMB-17-004` (MUST) says a late
Accept is a no-op when the case holds no terms and that "The no-op is not a
refusal (`HP-01-003`)", and `EMB-17-016` (MUST NOT) forbids sending any activity
in reply to it.

No relationship edge records which requirement governs the late path.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- Surface symptom: `EMB-17-003`'s condition and `MSM-07-012`'s condition now read
  identically, so the pair looks like a drafting slip in one of them.
- Underlying problem: the corpus never says that `MSM-07-012` is about an on-time
  Accept and `EMB-17` about a late one. The ordering that makes them compose is a
  property of the receive tree, not of the requirement text, so the text alone
  does not determine the answer.
- Correct and to keep: both answers are right for their own path. A late Accept
  is never refused on deadline grounds (`EMB-17-001`, ADR-0065), and an Accept of
  terms the register cannot bind records nothing (`CM-18-003`). The defect is
  only that neither requirement says which path it governs.

## Category

Spec conflict: two MUST-tier protocol requirements, same condition, different
obligations.

## Severity

Medium. The prototype behaves correctly, so nothing is broken today. The risk is
to conformance: a second implementation reading the requirements alone can
satisfy either one and violate the other.

Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — the shorter-of-two default-embargo rule is stated once, at one priority.

## Summary

CM-14-006 (SHOULD): when the reporter's `Offer(VulnerabilityReport)` carries an embargo proposal, case initialization SHOULD reconcile the proposed duration against the CASE_OWNER's published policy (its actor default, EP-04-003) and initialize the embargo at the shorter of the two.

EP-04-003 (MUST): where the sender proposes a duration and the CASE_OWNER's profile carries an embargo policy, the CASE_MANAGER MUST make the shorter of the two the active embargo at once.

Same rule, two priorities. CM-14-006 even cites EP-04-003 for the policy it reconciles against.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- Surface: a duplicate requirement.
- Underlying: the priorities disagree, so a conformance reader cannot tell whether the shorter-of-two outcome is mandatory. CM-14-006 also names case initialization (the pre-ADR-0041 CM-14 sequence) as the actor, while EP-04-003 names the CASE_MANAGER.
- Correct and should stay: EP-04-003's MUST, which is what the code implements.

## Category

Spec consistency (duplicate at conflicting priority).

## Severity

Low: the code follows the MUST; the risk is a reader weakening it from CM-14-006.

## Evidence

- `specs/case-management.yaml` CM-14-006; `specs/embargo-policy.yaml` EP-04-003.
- Found by the SR-13 link audit of CM and PRM (#5207, PR #5882).

## Impact if Ignored

Two sources of truth for one rule drift further; the relationship graph records a link between restatements rather than a real dependency.

## Suggested Action

Retire CM-14-006 in favour of EP-04-003 (moving any story or test reference), or rewrite it as a pointer-free narrower case that `refines` EP-04-003 at MUST. Ask the maintainer which priority is intended before changing CM-14-006's obligation.

Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — CBT-04-003's priority and its statement say the same thing, so a reader knows whether the late-joiner Announce is required or permitted.

## Summary

CBT-04-003 (`specs/case-bootstrap-trust.yaml`) has `priority: MUST`, but its statement is a permission: "After the late joiner has accepted the stub Invite (`Accept(Invite(Actor)[target=VulnerabilityCaseStub])`), the CASE_MANAGER MAY send `Announce(VulnerabilityCase)` without a separate `Create(VulnerabilityCase)` bootstrap." A maintainer must decide which one is meant.

## Surface Symptom vs. Underlying Problem

- **Surface:** the priority field and the keyword in the statement disagree, so this looks like a typo.
- **Underlying:** the two readings oblige different things. As a MUST, the CASE_MANAGER is required to seed the late joiner with `Announce(VulnerabilityCase)` and is forbidden a separate `Create` bootstrap. As a MAY, the `Announce`-only path is one permitted option and a `Create` bootstrap stays allowed. The verification test (`test_the_stub_invite_is_the_late_joiners_trust_anchor` in `test/demo/test_pcr_late_joiner.py`) shows that the `Announce`-only path works. It does not show that this path is the only one.
- **Correct and worth keeping:** the rationale. The accepted stub Invite is already the joiner's Trust Anchor (CBT-04-001), so a further `Create` adds a trust step with nothing new to check.

## Category

Specification quality: priority and statement inconsistent (SR-10).

## Severity

Low. The implementation and demo already take the `Announce`-only path. The ambiguity matters to a conformance reader, or to an implementation that bootstraps a late joiner with `Create`.

## Evidence

- `specs/case-bootstrap-trust.yaml`, CBT-04-003: `priority: MUST`, statement "MAY send".
- `spec-lint` does not flag it.
- Found by the SR-13 link audit of the CLP, SYNC, RSH, PCR, CP, TRIG, CBT and SBT families (PR #5863, #5211). It is outside that audit's scope (links only), so t

- `main`: the inbox POST route (`vultron/adapters/driving/fastapi/routers/actors/_routes/mailbox.py:61-98`) and HTTP delivery (`vultron/adapters/driven/http_delivery.py`).
- The WebFinger and HTTP Signatures parts are accurate: `main` has no WebFinger, and its planned signing is FEP-8b32 `eddsa-jcs-2022` proofs, not RFC 9421.
- Kind: **different** (the page contradicts §5.3 and the requirements; code follows §5.3). The likely intent is "full ActivityPub server behavior" (shared inbox, outbox GET, followers).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: §1.3 and §5.3 agree on whether HTTP inbox delivery is a conformance requirement, and the §1.3 text names only behaviors `main` and the requirements leave out.
- [ ] AC-2: `mkdocs build --strict` passes.

Theme: theme:requirements-traceability — the coverage report counts only real test markers, so the coverage figure and the known-gaps page agree with the tests.

## Summary

`spec-coverage` finds `pytest.mark.spec("ID")` by matching source text with a regex (`SPEC_MARKER_RE` in `vultron/metadata/specs/coverage.py`, read through `marked_ids_in`). The same text inside a string literal also matches. A test fixture that writes marker text into a throwaway test file therefore marks those real requirements as tested.

## Evidence or Context

- Found while building the known-gaps page (#5976, PR #6058). The builder had to assemble the marker text at runtime so that its fixtures did not mark real requirements.
- Effect: the coverage figure is inflated, the growth guard in `test/architecture/test_spec_coverage_ratchet.py` can miss a newly untested requirement, and the generated known-gaps page can drop a real gap.
- `vultron/metadata/specs/marked_tests.py` (#5972) already reads markers from the AST to classify xfails; only the marked-ID set still comes from the regex.

## Fix or Approach

Read the marked IDs from the AST: decorators, module and class `pytestmark`, and `pytest.param(marks=...)`, sharing the reader in `marked_tests.py` instead of keeping a second one. Keep the growth guard's meaning: a PR may not add an untested requirement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A spec marker that appears only inside a string literal (including a triple-quoted fixture body) does not count as a marker.
- [ ] AC-2: Real markers given as a decorator, through `pytestmark`, or through `pytest.param(marks=...)` still count.
- [ ] AC-3: The growth guard keeps its meaning, and the committed known-gaps fragment is regenerated if any requirement changes state.

Governing specs: SR-05-005, SR-05-017.

> **Crypto PR (ADR-0164 carve-out): this PR waits for human review before merge.**
> It changes only where the prototype's seeded-key proof gets its `created`
> time, for the outbox signer and for the docs example signer. Keys, the
> cryptosuite, the signed bytes' construction and verification are unchanged;
> production key handling (#1184) is not touched.

## Summary

A proof's `created` time is now the act's instant, carried in the signed activity's `published`, instead of a fresh clock read inside `sign`. So signing reads no clock, one activity seals to one proof on every run, and the `signing.py` `sign` entry leaves `KNOWN_UNSLICED_CLOCK_READS`.

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Motivation

**Decision (AC-1): act-instant, not a bookkeeping or edge exemption (ADR-0176).**

- ADR-0176's bookkeeping port is for adapter times that "do not enter the case ledger" (queued, dead-lettered). A proof does enter it: the signed body is sealed and is the ledger's `payloadSnapshot` (VM-08-003), and its hash covers the proof. A bookkeeping read would put a time the recording clock never sees into every recorded body, so a re-recorded scenario could not equal the committed one (#5676).
- `CLOCK_EDGE_EXEMPTIONS` holds only the wall-clock reads behind the two clock ports and stopwatch reads. A signing time is neither.
- Verification never judges `created` against a window: `verify` (after #6124) checks only that it is a timestamp. So the time has no role of its own that needs a separate read; it is "when the author wrote this", which is the act's instant.
- SIG-05-001's rationale already asks for this: proofs must be the same on every run because tests, demos and docs compare exact wire bodies. A clock-read `created` broke that.
- The recording test (#5760, one clock step per act): the old read ran on every seal, including the write-once re-seal that stores nothing, so it moved the recording clock on a path that commits nothing — ADR-0176

`vultron/wire/as2/signing.py` `sign` calls `now_utc()` when no `created`
argument is supplied, so signing an outbound activity reads the clock outside
the act's single designated read.
This entry appears in `KNOWN_UNSLICED_CLOCK_READS` in

The first AC is a design decision: decide whether the signing `created` time
is an act-instant (the act's edge reads it once and threads it through) or a

## Summary

Rewrites ADR-0176 to the maintainer's postmark rule and builds most of it. The inbox now reads the act clock once when a message arrives, before the message queues for any lock. Every act that processes the message, including a replay, retry or restart re-run, runs at that arrival stamp. Intake and every hold record the stamp as the message's `received_at`. The pre-bootstrap queue window now opens at the first waiter's arrival stamp, and an act judges it at its own instant.

Issues: closed 0, opened 0
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Motivation

Under the old rule, a message was judged at the time it was processed. A backlog at the receiver could then make an on-time answer late: an Accept that arrives at 11:59 against a 12:00 deadline, but is processed at 12:02, was refused. The arrival stamp is the receiver's own clock reading, so the sender cannot set it the way it can set `published`. The receiver's backlog cannot move it either.

**Hold-expiry rule (CBT-03-003, new CBT-03-007).** A case's pre-bootstrap queue window opens at the arrival stamp of the first message that waits on the case. The window has expired once that stamp plus the interval (CBT-03-005) is not after the instant of the act that judges it. That act is a later delivery naming the case or the bootstrap that releases the case's messages, each at its own arrival stamp, or a future sweep (#2887) at its own instant. So a bootstrap that arrived inside the window releases the queue even when a backlog processed it after the window closed. A released message is not judged again at its replay, because the replay runs at its own arrival stamp, which is inside the window the release found open. The window stays per case, as before. Only its two clock reads moved to act instants, so every verdict for the same instants is unchanged.

## Summary

ADR-0176 currently reads "A received activity is judged when it is processed" and gives a held activity the instant of its replay.
This issue revises that decision to a **postmark rule**: the receiver stamps the activity once at the inbox with its own trusted clock, and every subsequent judgment — including replays of held activities — uses that arrival stamp.

## Evidence or context

Found while planning #5651.
This is a maintainer decision of 2026-11-10, made during the #5676 epic run.

A sender's `published` can lag or be deliberately false; the receiver's arrival stamp is trusted and outside the sender's control.
Locking contention can delay processing well past the moment a message arrived:
an embargo Accept that arrives at 11:59 against a 12:00 deadline, but is processed at 12:02 due to backlog, should count as on time.
Under the current rule it would not.

The postmark rule does not change triggers or sweeps, which still read the clock after the tree lock as ADR-0176 specifies.
Recordings continue to read the clock once per delivery, now at arrival.

## Fix or approach

- Rewrite ADR-0176 in place to the postmark rule.
  The ADR is unreleased; the maintainer authorises a `status_override:` reason if adr-lifecycle-check needs one, and no amendment section is needed.
- Update `notes/act-instant.md` to reflect the postmark rule.
- Intake reads the clock once at arrival, before queueing for the tree lock, and carries the stamp with the delivery and with a held activity's stored record.
  Processing passes it as `/at`.
- Settle how a held activity's queue-interval expiry (CBT-03-003) is judged under the postmark rule: compare arrival plus the interval against the releasing or sweeping act's own instant.
  Record the decision in ADR-0176.
- The arrival stamp must go through

## Summary

Slice 1 of ADR-0174 (PR #5755; plan in `notes/act-instant.md`). Builds what every other slice under #5676 uses: an injected clock, one clock read per act at its entry point, the act's instant in the tree run, and the test that keeps new clock reads out.

## Evidence or Context

`now_utc()` is a global any module may call, and the audit after #5591 found clock reads in tree builders, guard nodes, sync predicates and the parse edge (#5649, #5651, #5652). Triggers already read their instant once (`SvcBTTriggerBase._at`), but nothing else does, and nothing enforces it.

## Fix or Approach

- A clock port with one operation, the current time, supplied by the composition root (system clock in production).
- Each act takes the tree lock (`_BT_GLOBAL_LOCK`), then reads the clock once, and holds the lock until it commits (ADR-0174 revision 2). This applies to a trigger invocation, the processing of one inbound delivery (a replayed held activity gets its replay's instant), and each sweep. Queueing for the lock is not decision time.
- A trigger's instant moves from construction (`SvcBTTriggerBase._at`, set in `__init__`) to inside the lock, and the lock covers its whole `execute()`, so checks before its tree such as `_suppressed_repeat` run inside the lock against the act's instant. The lock is re-entrant, so the bridge taking it again is safe.
- `BTBridge.execute_with_setup` takes the act's instant as a required argument and puts it in the tree run's shared state as `/at`. A nested bridge run inherits it the way it inherits `/is_leader`. A node that reads `/at` when it is absent fails.
- An architecture test that fails on a clock read in any module outside an allow-list. Today's sites are recorded item by item as the list to burn down; each later slice removes its own.

Follow-on to ADR-0174 (PR #5755). Generated ids have the same shape as the clock had: a global the recording harness has to replace. Decide whether ids enter the same way, through an injected id-source port, and record that decision.

## Evidence or Context

`deterministic_run()` replaces `uuid4` in every module that bound it by name. A module that imports `uuid4` differently, or a new module the patch does not reach, breaks repeatability silently. ADR-0174 left ids to a later decision on purpose.

## Fix or Approach

- Draft an ADR (or an ADR-0174 amendment) for an id-source port, injected at the composition root, with a seeded source for recordings.
- Decide where ids are minted: at the act's edge, or anywhere through the port.
- Plan the migration slices and an architecture test for direct `uuid4` calls, as ADR-0174 does for the clock.

Governing specs: DEMOCI-11-025

- [ ] AC-1: A decision record states how generated ids enter the application, and which options were rejected.
- [ ] AC-2: The migration is planned as issues under #5676, each with acceptance criteria.
- [ ] AC-3: The plan names the test that will keep direct id generation out of core.

When the case or the actor's own store already holds the fact a Retriever call-out would fetch, the tree reads it there and does not call the Retriever (planned in #3427). - the actor-discovery lookup in `vultron/core/behaviors/call_out/bundles/actor_discovery.py`

A cache of *external* data is out of scope: it belongs to the capability implementation (BT-18-029).

## Summary

Make every Actuator act on one target per call and be safe to repeat (ADR-0183, Concern #3427 question 2). Because an *error* answer leaves a message in holding to be re-run, a tree that acted on some targets before the error acts on them again; each Actuator must therefore be keyed on an id the tree derives from the act, so a repeat is a no-op.

What a tree does after a *no* stays each tree's own logic. Credentials are a deployment matter, and a rejected credential is *error* (ADR-0183).

Build the call-out answer of ADR-0183 (Concern #3446). Every backend gives one answer: a fixed verdict (*yes*, *no*, *error*) and the data its capability declares for that verdict. ## Summary

In `vultron/core/use_cases/triggers/actor.py`, `_record_named_peer` calls `backend = factory('ResolveActorDetails')` then `backend.update()` directly, without calling `py_trees Behaviour.setup()` or `initialise()`. Any real directory-service backend that accesses `self.datalayer` in `update()` will crash with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute ...`.

## Failure scenario

A production deployment replaces `ACTOR_DISCOVERY_DETERMINISTIC` with a bundle whose `resolve_actor_factory` returns a `DataLayerConditionWithPorts` subclass that reads `self.datalayer` in `update()`. `_record_named_peer` calls `backend.update()` directly. `py_trees Behaviour.setup()` (which calls `setup_ports` and wires the blackboard client) and `initialise()` (which assigns `self.datalayer`) are never invoked. `update()` calls `self.datalayer.some_method()` on `None`; `AttributeError` propagates; `dl.create(CoreActor(...))` is never reached; the peer is not recorded. Subsequent delivery to the newly-named actor fails with 'actor not found'.

## File

`vultron/core/use_cases/triggers/actor.py` line 223

## Discovery context

Pre-existing in `origin/main`. Found during code review for PR #2703.

Theme: theme:capability-architecture — removes dead sentinel call-out classes contradicting the capability shapes.

## Summary

Carry the ADR-0097 / BT-18-013 demotion into the code and the fuzzer-node
catalogs. Sentinel is a call-in pattern, not a capability shape, so it has no
shape base class, no bundle field, and no blackboard contract.

## Summary

Holds every call-out backend to a per-actor time budget: the seam each bundle hands out, `TimeBoundedCallOut`, times its backend on a new stopwatch port and, past `ActorConfig.call_out_time_budget`, discards the answer and raises an internal error naming the node and the budget (BT-18-015, BT-18-026, BT-18-027).

Issues: closed 1, opened 0
Questions: asked 0, filed 0

## Motivation

`SynchronousCallOut` refused a `RUNNING` return but nothing bounded a backend that simply blocked, so a slow backend stalled a worker and its answer was still acted on.

**Reconciled with #6226 (ADR-0183).** The issue predates the yes/no/error answer. AC-3 asks for a `CallOutContractError`-family error; this PR raises `CallOutBudgetExceededError`, a subclass of **`CallOutBackendError`**, the error the seam raises for an *error* answer. Both are plain `RuntimeError`s, not `VultronError`s, so `BTBridge` reports `internal_error=True` either way, which is what AC-3 needs. The choice of family follows ADR-0183 § 2, which says an *error* answer leaves the message in holding "as BT-18-027 already requires of a backend that exceeds its time budget": an answer that arrives too late is, like *error*, not one the tree may use. A contract error, by contrast, means the backend is mis-wired.

**Semantics, stated honestly (AC-4).** The seam **detects** an overrun after the backend returns; it does **not** interrupt it. A py_trees tick is synchronous and the backend runs on the ticking thread. So a slow backend still holds the worker for as long as it takes, on every call, and one that never returns is not caught here (BT-18-025's architecture check forbids the blocking I/O that would cause that). What the seam guarantees is that a late answer, whatever its verdict, is discarded and never becomes a decision, and that the operator sees which node was slow and what the budget was. issues.body:
Theme: theme:capability-architecture — bounds call-out backend latency with a configurable timeout at the seam.

## Summary

`SynchronousCallOut` rejects a `RUNNING` return, but nothing bounds a backend that
simply blocks. `docs/howto/wire_capability.md` invites implementers to call a REST
service from `update()`, and the pipeline runs under FastAPI `BackgroundTasks`, so
a slow backend stalls a worker while `BTBridge` ticks toward `max_iterations` and
then fails without naming the node — the same opaque failure BT-18-011 exists to
prevent, reached by blocking instead of suspending. Implements BT-18-015.

The budget is **configuration, not a constant**: it is local to one actor and
observable by no peer, so two deployments choosing different values is not
divergence. Contrast an ask deadline, which travels on the wire in `end_time`
precisely so both parties read the same number (ASK-03-003).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `ActorConfig` gains a call-out timeout as a `timedelta` field with a
      documented default, following the existing `min_rsvp_window` /
      `default_rsvp_window` pattern. No literal duration appears at the seam.
- [ ] AC-2: A `TimeBoundedCallOut` decorator sits alongside `SynchronousCallOut`
      and is applied at the same single point (`CallOutBundle.__post_init__`), so
      no tree-builder call site changes. It is idempotent and name-transparent,
      mirroring `guard_call_out_factory`.
- [ ] AC-3: An overrun raises a `CallOutContractError`-family error — a plain
      `RuntimeError`, **not** a `VultronError` — so `BTBridge` classifies it
      `internal_error=True` (a wiring bug) rather than as a protocol `FAILURE`.
      The message names the offending node and the configured budget.
- [ ] AC-4: **State the semantics honestly in code and docstring.** A py_trees
      tick is synchronous, so a decorator cannot interrupt a blocking child

issues.body:
Theme: theme:capability-architecture — replaces nine CVE criteria nodes with one evaluator call-out.

## Summary

The `IdAssignable` SequenceNode in `assign_cve_id_tree.py` currently exposes
9 individual call-out point nodes (one per CNA Operational Rules criterion).
Per ADR-0070 and BTND-05-007, CVE eligibility checking is one logical
capability — a single `EvaluateCveEligibility` Evaluator call-out that
evaluates all criteria as a unit and returns a verdict.

The current design misrepresents the substitution boundary: when the CNA
Operational Rules are revised, all 9 criteria change together, not
independently. A single Evaluator call-out correctly models the seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Replace the 9-child `IdAssignable` SequenceNode with a single
  `EvaluateCveEligibility` Evaluator call-out point in
  `assign_cve_id_tree.py`.
- [ ] AC-2: Update `AssignCveIdCallOutBundle` to expose one
  `evaluate_cve_eligibility_factory` instead of 9 per-criterion factories.
- [ ] AC-3: The new Evaluator's blackboard contract documents v4.1.0 as the
  reference rules edition, with `output_keys` capturing a verdict and
  rationale.
- [ ] AC-4: Update `notes/bt-fuzzer-rm-id-assignment.md` to reflect the
  consolidated design (replace the 9 individual catalog entries with one
  `EvaluateCveEligibility` entry).
- [ ] AC-5: All existing tests for `assign_cve_id_tree.py` updated to use
  the new bundle shape; no regression.

## Reference

Source: #2108
Docs PR: https://github.com/CERTCC/Vultron/pull/2517
Spec: `specs/behavior-tree-node-design.yaml` BTND-05-007, BTND-05-008

A core-owned projection narrows the case before the port sees it, and the same port serves both an inline call-out wrapper and a call-in Sentinel. issues.body:
Theme: theme:capability-architecture — finds the vendors and stakeholders who should be invited into a case.

## Summary

Determining which vendors/stakeholders should be added to a Vultron case is a non-trivial coordination task. It is not a simple database lookup — it involves multi-source search, supply-chain analysis, and candidate winnowing.

## Workflow

1. **Produce candidates** (Retriever): search CPE data, supply chain graphs, product documentation, GitHub, web sources for indicators that a vendor/product is affected
2. **Winnow candidates** (Evaluator): assess each candidate — is this vendor actually affected? worth notifying? — and produce a ranked notification set
3. **Affinity groups** (memory layer): record which participants were notified for similar cases, so future cases can bootstrap from prior experience. Bias toward overnotification; adds are more important than deletes.

## Key characteristics

- Combines at least Retriever + Evaluator agent types
- Output: a recommended participant set with rationale
- Overnotification is preferred to undernotification (CVD coordination bias)
- Likely a scoped orchestrator: bounded input (case details), bounded output (candidate list), narrow task

## Open questions

- Should affinity groups be a persistent service or case-scoped memory?
- What external sources are in scope? (CPE, EPSS, GitHub, NVD, patch-mgmt APIs, web search)
- How does this interact with the `SvcInviteActorToCaseUseCase` trigger?

## Summary

Answers the three questions #3427 still had open: whether a capability's output is recorded in the case ledger, how Retriever caching and staleness work, and where a Composer sits relative to the note behaviours. ADR-0183 had already answered the other two (Actuator failure and Actuator credentials). The answers follow from existing decisions, so no new ADR is needed.

## Changes

- **`notes/coordination-agents.md`**:
  - A capability's output never enters the case ledger as itself; only the act or case-file change it leads to does (CLP-07-001, CLP-07-004, CLP-07-013). The reasoning stays in the actor's own store unless the actor sends it, for example as a Note.

  - BT-18-029 (MAY): a capability implementation may cache external data; it owns the staleness policy, and the call-out seam provides no cache.

issues.body:
Theme: theme:capability-architecture — settles cross-shape capability semantics for ledger, failure, and caching.

## Summary

Holds the genuine remainders from the four shape Ideas (#1144 Evaluator, #1145
Retriever, #1146 Composer, #2451 Actuator) that ADR-0097 did **not** answer. Those
Ideas close because the contract, the calling convention, and the declaration
format are now settled; these questions are cross-cutting semantics that the
capability layer still owes, and are recorded here so they are not lost.

Filed per the G07 planning protocol rule 5 ("lose nothing") and rule 4 ("a member
with a real remainder ... is re-scoped").

## The five open questions

### 1. Is a capability's output recorded in the canonical case ledger?

Asked by #1144 ("Should the Evaluator output be recorded in the canonical case
ledger?") and #2451 ("Should Actuator side effects be recorded?"). It applies to
every data-producing capability, not just Evaluators.

The tension to resolve: a capability's verdict is a **local operational decision**,
and `notes/call-out-configuration.md` classifies most call-outs that way — no
mechanism to impose canonical state on another party. But CLP-07 says the ledger is
not a process log, so a per-actor verdict arguably does not belong in it at all,
while `CLP-07-004` reserves per-actor observability content. A decision that
*causes* a protocol-visible transition already reaches the ledger through the
transition itself; the question is whether the *rationale* does, and whether
recording it would make an actor's private triage replicate to every participant.

Compare the parallel already decided for asks: the *fact* of an ask is protocol
history, the *diagnosis* is not (ASK-07-008, ADR-0080).

### 2. Actuator failure and partial-success semantics

Asked by #2451. An Actuator returns SUCCESS when a side effect is confirmed and
FAILURE otherwise, but nothing specifies:

- What the tree does on FAILURE — retry, log and continue, or halt. Note
  BT-14-001
